"Absolutely not!" Qin Rong Gong suddenly exploded, his red-rimmed eyes fixing the First Master of the Qin family in a hard stare.

"On what grounds does First Uncle agree? Those are my Second Branch's children!"

"You couldn't possibly be doing this just because your eldest son Qin Rong Cheng still hasn't produced a son—and so you want to claim another man's sons and another man's grandsons for yourself, could you?"

The First Master of the Qin family swept him a cold glance.

And didn't deign to respond.

The old clan leader picked up the teacup beside him and flung it at Qin Rong Gong's feet, bellowing: "You—shut your mouth! What good did reading all those books do you!"

"Your First Uncle thinks of you, thinks of your Second Branch, and never speaks ill of you in public—and what more do you want from him?"

"Clan Leader, please don't upset yourself—it's not good for your health." The First Master of the Qin family only looked at the old clan leader, and said gently: "Old Clan Leader, speaking plainly—the Sun family was actually being very sincere and courteous in what they suggested... They originally proposed entering Zheng'er and Shen'er under the name of my second son Rong Lie, with no wish to take the name of the legitimate eldest grandson of the Qin family Senior Line."

The First Master spoke with increasing clarity and precision, not caring in the least about the expressions around him: "But I thought—Zheng'er is by right the legitimate eldest grandson of this branch of the Qin family. It only makes sense to have him entered under Rong Cheng's name."

At those words, the way the old clan leader and the elders looked at the First Master of the Qin family changed entirely.

Now there was a grandson of the Qin family who truly had the family's interests at heart!

He could even give up the name of the legitimate eldest grandson...

After a pause, the First Master continued: "If our Qin family agrees, then Zheng'er and Shen'er remain sons of our Qin family. But if our Qin family refuses and provokes the Sun family's wrath—they are genuinely capable of having Zheng'er and Shen'er change their surname altogether."

"And can we afford for the bloodline of the Qin and Sun families combined to be severed entirely from our Qin family?"

The old clan leader was so agitated he forgot to stroke his beard and just kept nodding rapidly.

The difference was plain as day!

Absolutely plain as day!

Even two of the elders who had always sided with Qin Mingjie and his son couldn't help but be moved—they had to admire the First Master Qin Mingfeng's tolerance, magnanimity, and the big-picture perspective he brought to the family's interests.

"Mingjie, Rong Gong—have you two heard clearly enough? Have you anything more to say?" The old clan leader snorted coldly, shooting the father and son an irritated look.

Qin Mingjie's face was dark: "Elder Brother is merely seizing the moment to play the good man—just doing this to win the praise of the clan leader and elders."

The old clan leader slapped the table: "Since you say so—then go you and tell the Sun family to leave the children with our Qin family!"

"This..." Qin Mingjie's old face flushed red. He was forced to say: "The two brothers of the Sun family made it plain—if we refused to let the Sun family take the children, they would go before the Emperor to have it adjudicated."

"Then what in the blazes are you even arguing about!" The usually refined and cultivated old clan leader could not restrain himself and let out a crude outburst.

"You two can't do a single thing, you've had your weakness grabbed and exploited by the Sun family, and they've got you completely cornered—and you still have the nerve to criticize your elder brother?"

"If not for Mingfeng's magnanimity, the Sun family wouldn't even leave the children the Qin surname—and our Qin family would lose face utterly and completely, and the Jiangdong Sun family would then be at our throats until one side was destroyed!"

"Agreeing to let the children be entered under the Senior Line—at least the Sun family is still willing, for the children's sake, not to deal with our Qin family in the most extreme way possible."

The First Master of the Qin family pressed home the point: "The clan leader is absolutely right—the Sun brothers also said clearly: for the sake of the children, certain things they could do, they will choose not to."

"There—you see? Didn't old Cheng say as much?" The old clan leader sighed heavily: "That's exactly it! Old Cheng can now see that the Sun family was already going easy on you..."

"Enough of this... since things have come to this pass, don't drag it out any further. Go ahead with the separation as quietly as possible, and get it over with quickly. Ripping the bandage off in one go is better."

"The wedding of the Sixth Young Miss and the Fifth Young Miss is still coming up—there absolutely cannot be any more trouble at this critical moment!" The old clan leader's worried face grew even more deeply lined with wrinkles.

"Our old Qin family has truly had enough..."

The First Master of the Qin family bowed in acknowledgment.

The old clan leader looked at the unwilling, surly Qin Mingjie and his son, and said irritably: "Have you two anything more to say?"

Father and son had no choice but to affirm, with dark faces, that they had nothing more.

The First Master of the Qin family rose with a bow: "Clan Leader, elders—there is one more matter Mingfeng must inform you of."

The old clan leader and the elders all nodded, telling him to proceed.

The First Master of the Qin family then spoke of the matter of adopting the two young ladies from the Third Branch.

The old clan leader silently heaved a long sigh in his heart.

That the Second Branch of the Qin family had pressured the Third Branch daughters into becoming concubines—an affair of that magnitude—even if the Second Branch had concealed it as tightly as they could, he, as clan leader, still knew.

Only these few elders did not know.

It was a disgrace for the Qin family—the old clan leader had not told even his own eldest son, let alone spoken of it with these elders.

The elders were all surprised, and began whispering among themselves.

Qin Mingjie's expression went pitch-black.

This Qin Mingfeng—what a masterful hand!

He had assumed the First Branch was only using the matter of adopting the two Third Branch girls as a pretext—a deliberate ploy to humiliate the Second Branch.

He hadn't expected the man was serious about it!

One of the elders who sided with Qin Mingjie, seeing Qin Mingjie's face turn ugly, looked at the First Master and asked: "Mingjie, why is it that out of nowhere you want to adopt the Seventh and Eighth Girls from the Third Branch?"

The First Master of the Qin family glanced at Qin Mingjie, then told the questioning elder: "You might want to ask Second Brother first."

The elder was startled, looked again at Qin Mingjie, saw his expression turn even more distasteful, and realized inwardly that the Second Branch must have stirred up something again. He dared say no more.

The old clan leader also had no wish for the family's shame to be known far and wide, and directly nodded his approval to the First Master of the Qin family.

"It speaks well of your compassionate heart, Mingfeng. As long as your Third Brother agrees, have the Seventh and Eighth Girls adopted into your household. As they are daughters of a concubine, there is no need for a grand ceremony—just a family feast to mark the occasion is fine."

After a pause, he added: "It will also be those two girls' good fortune!"

The other elders all nodded in agreement, praising the First Master and Madam Li for their kindness and generosity.

The Seventh Young Miss and Eighth Young Miss were daughters born of a concubine of the Third Branch—but once adopted into the First Branch, they would become legitimate daughters of the First Branch's Senior Line.

What else could that be called if not good fortune?

Admittedly, the First Branch, by adopting two daughters, would have to exert effort to arrange their marriages and send them off, and would also need to prepare dowries befitting legitimate daughters.

Strictly calculated, the First Branch was the one at a disadvantage.

But then again, if the First Branch could arrange good marriages for the two girls, that too could prove beneficial to the First Branch.

The old clan leader understood in his heart that Qin Mingfeng was not that kind of calculating man.

He was concerned that the Second Branch, not above any means, would ruin the two Third Branch girls in order to pave the way for their own sons.

Truly worthy of the eldest legitimate son of the Qin Senior Line!

Thinking of the Second Branch's father and son, the old clan leader and several of the elders felt increasingly disappointed in them.

A son born of a concubine was in the end not what a son born of the legitimate wife of the Xianyang Wei family was!

Qin Mingjie and his son plainly felt the disappointment of the old clan leader and the elders, and father and son were both furious and resentful.

All those years of silver spent—and it was all for nothing, as if feeding it to dogs...

The old clan leader, having finished the business at hand, drove Qin Mingjie and his son away in irritation, keeping only the First Master of the Qin family for a private word.

* * *

At first light the next morning, the eldest young master of the Sun family arrived in the capital, dusty from the road.

Without even sitting down for breakfast, he brought the Second and Third Young Masters of the Sun family and Madam Sun and the others to the Qin household.

After the old clan leader had kept the First Master of the Qin family for a long talk the previous night, he had brought several elders early the next morning and taken up position at the Qin household in readiness.

Not to haggle and wrangle with the Sun family—but because, in his long conversation with the First Master, he had learned much information vital to the Qin family's reputation. He had no choice but to bring them all in force and stand watch personally over Qin Mingjie and his son.

To prevent them from stirring up more trouble and provoking the Sun family into a fight to the bitter end, which would destroy both sides...

In truth, once the Qin family had conceded, the Sun family was also quite accommodating.

Before the Qin family clan leader and elders, Zheng'er and Shen'er were formally entered under the name of the Senior Line's eldest son, Qin Rong Cheng.

This matter had also been discussed in advance by the First Master of the Qin family with his son Qin Rong Cheng and his wife Lin Xi.

The young couple had been quite willing to accept this arrangement.

After all, neither of them knew if the next child would be a son, and what if fate had decreed that they would have no sons? If Zheng'er and Shen'er—with the powerful Jiangdong Sun family as their maternal family—became their brothers, it would be a blessing for their own girls.

The young couple thought it a fine thing indeed and felt no resentment.

The Second Branch of the Qin family, covetous as they were of Madam Sun's dowry, had no recourse—they could only watch, helplessly, as dozens of strong servants from the capital's Sun residence carried out every last piece of Madam Sun's dowry, large and small, until not a single item remained.

The separation documents were prepared in four copies.

Madam Sun and Qin Rong Gong each received one copy.

One copy was taken by the old clan leader to be kept in the clan archives. One was submitted to the county office for the official record.

The sons Madam Sun had borne—Zheng'er and Shen'er—were entered under the Senior Line's Qin Rong Cheng, and remained sons of the Qin family.

But the children would be taken back to the Jiangdong Sun household by Madam Sun to be raised there.

The Sun family pledged that the boys' schooling, training, and future marriages upon reaching adulthood would all be handled by the Sun family—not a single coin need come from the Qin family.

With this, the old clan leader and the elders were very satisfied—they felt the Jiangdong Sun family, being a noble clan of several centuries' standing, truly knew how to conduct themselves with decency.

In the end, everyone was quite satisfied with how things concluded—everyone, that is, except the Qin Second Branch, who looked as if they were in mourning at a funeral.

Before the Sun family departed, the eldest Sun sister-in-law brought Madam Sun and the two younger sisters-in-law to pay a final call on Madam Li.

The eldest Sun sister-in-law especially requested to meet the Sixth Young Miss, Qin Rujin.

chapters.title: Rujin—Destined for Joy and Fortune
chapters.content:
The eldest Sun sister-in-law was already thirty-seven. Her face was oval, her brows like crescent moons; she was well-preserved, and one could see at a glance that she had been a great beauty in her youth.

She was the principal wife who managed the Jiangdong Sun family's inner household, and had been doing so for twenty years. She looked soft and pliable, as if she had no temper at all.

But those black, bright eyes of hers gleamed with keen intelligence—one look at them told you she was no one to be trifled with.

When Qin Rujin arrived, the eldest Sun sister-in-law took her hands and praised her effusively.

She praised her until Qin Rujin's face flushed red with embarrassment, and only then relented. She then drew a small, exquisite sachet from the wide sleeve of her robe and pressed it into Qin Rujin's hand.

"Sixth Young Miss, don't take offense—this old-fashioned thing of mine: please accept this sachet as your sister-in-law's gift to you upon first meeting, and as a small addition to your trousseau."

She had brought a sachet, and then called it both a first-meeting gift and a trousseau gift. Madam Li immediately surmised that the eldest Sun sister-in-law had given a bank note.

Qin Rujin looked at the exquisite sachet and happily accepted it at once. But when she felt the sachet—plump and full, with the texture of paper inside—Qin Rujin froze.

The eldest Sun sister-in-law, seeing that little expression on her face, laughed frankly and openly.

The Second and Third Sisters-in-law of Sun also laughed.

Madam Sun also smiled at Qin Rujin, pressing her lips together.

They had all seen it—this silly girl, when she first reached out to take the sachet, had truly liked the sachet for its beauty.

It was only when she felt there were papers inside that she didn't know what to do with herself.

"Sixth Young Sister, just keep it! My eldest sister-in-law is a goddess of fortune—she loves nothing more than showering gifts of money on pretty young girls like you. And especially so, since this is her first time meeting you." Madam Sun smiled as she explained.

Madam Li knew that if the eldest Sun sister-in-law had put her hand to it, the silver would not be small. She also couldn't help saying: "But this—how can we accept?"

The eldest Sun sister-in-law laughed broadly at Madam Li: "Aunt, you mustn't stand on ceremony with our Sun family. Because of Zheng'er and Shen'er, we are as close kin as can be now!"

And then, as if in jest, she added: "Besides—this is the first time I've met the Sixth Young Miss. How could I let myself be outdone by my Second and Third Sisters-in-law?"

The Second and Third Sun sisters-in-law pretended to take offense, shaking their heads: "Eldest Sister-in-law loves to tease us."

The eldest Sun sister-in-law laughed even more openly.

The Second Sun sister-in-law looked at Qin Rujin, and her eyes grew red.

"Honestly—I am grateful to the Sixth Young Miss from the very bottom of my heart! If not for the Sixth Young Miss truly caring for our two eldest nephews' wellbeing... awakening our Wenlan... I fear our Wenlan would have spent a lifetime mired in that rotten pit that is the Qin Second Branch."

She had never stopped carrying a thorn in her heart over what had happened to Madam Sun at her own family home that year.

And later, after she uncovered the truth that Madam Sun had been schemed against by Qin Rong Gong and his mother—one can imagine the pain that caused her.

Now that Madam Sun had formally separated from Qin Rong Gong, that long-buried thorn was finally pulled free.

The eldest Sun sister-in-law also grew serious, and looked at Qin Rujin: "What my Second Sister-in-law says is right. Our Sun family always felt that Qin Rong Gong was never worthy of our Wenlan! But Wenlan's heart was heavy—she thought too much of the family and of those who would come after in the family. Ignoring our urging and our family elders' counsel, she went ahead and married into that household... Now, at last, a weight on our hearts and on our family elders' hearts has been lifted! Wenlan told us herself—the one thing that truly made up her mind was what the Sixth Young Miss did for our two eldest nephews..."

Madam Sun also spoke to Qin Rujin with a face full of gratitude: "Perhaps the Sixth Young Miss herself feels it was merely a small matter—but it made me, as a mother, understand one thing clearly."

"Even you could think so carefully of Zheng'er's and Shen'er's wellbeing, and put yourself in their place—so what have I, their own mother, done for them all these years?"

"Nothing! Beyond giving them life, I did nothing but watch, helplessly, as their father and grandfather wore them down, making them weaker and weaker... and I never even truly fought with their father on their behalf..." Madam Sun spoke, and tears began to stream down her face.

Madam Li quickly rose, went to her, and wiped her tears with a handkerchief, sharing the feeling deeply as a woman who had also been a daughter-in-law of the Qin family.

"Don't blame yourself! It wasn't your fault!" Madam Li patted Madam Sun's shoulder.

She spoke from her own experience to comfort Madam Sun.

"I won't let others say I speak out of turn—I'll just say it directly: your former mother-in-law and that former grand-mother-in-law of yours were truly too formidable."

"If you had fought with Qin Rong Gong for the sake of the children—well, right or wrong aside, what came next would have been no end of unpleasantness, and they might have deliberately tormented the children to get back at you."

"These things—I've been through them too. Only in my case, I wasn't fighting with the children's father over the children—I was fighting with those two women, mother-in-law and grand-mother-in-law."

The three Sun sisters-in-law also comforted her, and Qin Rujin also soothed her. At last, Madam Sun stopped crying.

"Before, I had gone down a dead-end road in my thinking—always telling myself that even for the children's sake, for the family's face, if I could endure it I would endure it... But the truth is, I was only moving myself with my own endurance. The children were small, with no power to resist those who claimed to act in their interest but were in fact harming them. If they could have resisted, they would have."

"My whole family has been worrying about me and suffering on my behalf all these years, all because I had married so unhappily..." Madam Sun raised her eyes and looked at the Second Sun sister-in-law, her face full of remorse.

"Especially Second Sister-in-law—you have worked so hard on my account all these years. The fault was mine, Sister!"

The Second Sun sister-in-law quickly shook her head and stepped forward to take both of Madam Sun's hands: "All of that is behind us now! Nothing but good days ahead!"

Qin Rujin was also deeply moved.

Moved by Madam Sun's awakening. Moved by how every member of the Sun family, from the very first, had stood firmly on Madam Sun's side—not treating her as a daughter spilled from a bucket, never to be retrieved.

And moved by how all of Madam Sun Wenlan's sisters-in-law had stood on the side of women, thinking for their little sister-in-law's sake.

This was a kindred spirit, a mutual support between women.

In this ancient feudal society, it was something rare and precious.

Father had said that the Jiangdong Sun family was the most pragmatic and calculating—siding always with whoever was winning. Yet the Jiangdong Sun family also had within it these wonderfully endearing women.

"Aunt—this is a half-trousseau that our Jiangdong Sun family has specially prepared for the Sixth Young Miss. Here is the trousseau list—please keep it safe!"

The eldest Sun sister-in-law rose to her feet and, with both hands, passed a thick sheaf of papers to Madam Li.

Madam Li was so startled her mind went blank for a moment.

In the great Ying dynasty, a complete trousseau consisted of sixty-four carrying cases. Any family with some means would prepare sixty-four for their daughter—a full trousseau.

Those with more modest circumstances would make do with thirty-two cases—half a trousseau.

But sixty-four cases from a noble family and sixty-four cases from a family of moderate means were two entirely different things.

The Jiangdong Sun family calling this a half-trousseau—its value was something Madam Li didn't dare calculate.

Madam Li also didn't dare accept it.

This was an entirely different matter from a first-meeting gift or even a trousseau addition.

The eldest Sun sister-in-law, seeing she wouldn't take it, immediately became serious: "Aunt—you aren't still standing on ceremony with our Sun family, are you? Even just for the sake of Zheng'er and Shen'er—you ought to accept it on the Sixth Young Miss's behalf!"

The Second and Third Sun sisters-in-law also urged her.

"Aunt, my eldest sister-in-law made a solemn pledge before our family elders—if Yinniang doesn't accept, our Sun family will have no face left."

Madam Sun simply took the half-trousseau list from her eldest sister-in-law's hands and pressed it directly into Madam Li's.

"Aunt, if you don't accept—then I can't very well let Zheng'er and Shen'er be registered under my eldest brother's and sister-in-law's name."

Once Madam Sun had said that, Madam Li had no choice but to accept it on Qin Rujin's behalf.

Qin Rujin was also in a daze.

The eldest Sun sister-in-law, seeing that everything had been settled, and that the afternoon was growing late, rose to make her farewells.

She also told Madam Li cheerfully: "When the day of our Sixth Young Miss's wedding arrives, I shall bring my sisters-in-law and Wenlan early to the household to help!"

Only one's own family would come early to help on the day of a great family occasion.

Madam Li happily agreed.

Zheng'er and Shen'er, though young, had still been told by Madam Sun about the separation from their father.

She also told them that their father was still their father—after coming to the capital from Jiangdong to visit their grandparents in the First Branch, they were also welcome to visit the Second Branch's grandparents and great-grandmother, as well as their father.

Children are the most perceptive of all—from the time they had been old enough to read the expressions on adults' faces, they had known something wasn't right between their mother and father.

Now that Mother had told them she and Father had separated, the children were, in a way, calmer than before—more at ease than they had been when they were still anxious and uncertain.

Mother was not going to stop them from seeing their family in the capital, and that was good.

As for why Mother had separated from Father—clearly Father had done something wrong, something Mother couldn't forgive.

Children still needed their mothers the most at this age, and naturally, they were willing to go with her.

When it came time to say goodbye to the children, Qin Rujin gave them the set of over fifty wooden cards she had hastily finished making.

Even the girls from Qin Rong Cheng's and Qin Rong Lie's families each took the half of their own share and gave it to Zheng'er and Shen'er.

The children even made a promise—when Zheng'er and Shen'er came back to the capital next time, they would come back to visit. And when they did, they would see who had learned the most characters, who could recite the most poems...

After seeing Madam Sun Wenlan and her sisters-in-law off, Madam Li let out a long breath of relief.

When she unrolled the half-trousseau list the Sun family had given and read it through, Madam Li nearly cried out loud.

This half-trousseau from the Sun family was worth at least as much as everything the entire First Branch had jointly prepared for Yinniang's dowry!

Madam Li's hands were shaking as she held the half-trousseau list.

"Quick—look at what the eldest Sun sister-in-law gave you in the sachet." Madam Li said to her youngest daughter, her voice trembling.

Qin Rujin handed the sachet to her mother, and asked: "Mother, is the trousseau Wenlan's family prepared for me too generous?"

Madam Li nodded emphatically, then gave the trousseau list to her daughter and took the sachet.

She opened the sachet and saw bank notes, neatly folded in squares.

She spread them open: six of them.

Each bank note was for five hundred taels.

Madam Li drew in another sharp breath.

What an open-handed woman the eldest Sun sister-in-law was!

And that was not counting the separate trousseau gifts the Second and Third Sun sisters-in-law had added for Qin Rujin today.

Each one would be worth at least several hundred taels.

Adding those to the first-meeting gifts they had given previously, together it was quite a lavish sum...

"The Sun family is truly generous!" Madam Li couldn't help exclaiming.

Just at that moment, the First Master of the Qin family, having finished seeing off the eldest Sun brother and his party, came back into the room and heard his wife's exclamation.

He quickly asked what had happened.

Madam Li handed the half-trousseau list the Sun family had given to Qin Rujin over to the First Master: "Have a look yourself, my lord—it's what the Sun family gave Yinniang."

The First Master took it and read it, then was silent.

After a long moment, the First Master couldn't help but exclaim: "This much! At the very least, over twenty thousand taels of silver!"

"Can't it be?" Madam Li looked at him: "Should we really just accept all this on Yinniang's behalf? My lord, I wonder if we ought to think this over."

After a pause, she added: "And that's not all, actually. Adding the trousseau gifts the Sun family gave Yinniang on top of that—I'd say at least this many!" Madam Li held up four fingers.

After all, the jewelry Madam Sun had given Qin Rujin on several occasions was likely worth several thousand taels.

The First Master also felt the heat of it.

He stroked his beard and deliberated for a moment, then gave a small nod: "It has already been accepted—there is nothing more to be said. In future, we will simply treat Zheng'er and Shen'er as our own grandchildren."

Madam Li breathed a quiet sigh of relief.

"That's the way. We'll treat Zheng'er the same as our very own legitimate eldest grandson, and Shen'er the same as our own grandson."

This meant that in the future, when these two boys grew up, the First Branch of the Qin family would also have to give them a generous betrothal gift—just as they would for their own legitimate eldest grandson.

The First Master of the Qin family nodded, then passed the trousseau list back to Qin Rujin with a smile: "This trousseau list—keep it yourself. Rest easy: this was given to you by the Sun family, and so it belongs to you."

Madam Li took over the thread: "As for the matters of returning courtesy and gifts—your father and mother are here for that. You need not worry in the least!"

The First Master then said: "At the root of it, this is also a deal that the Jiangdong Sun family struck with our First Branch of the Qin family. The reason it was given to you in particular, Yinniang, is first: because your great wedding is coming up and the timing fell to you. Second: your Madam Sun sister and the Sun family all privately believe it was you who helped Madam Sun make up her mind to seek the separation. And third: it is, in an indirect way, giving our First Branch and the Jiang family some face..."

Qin Rujin knew her father was right.

Madam Li knew it too.

She then smiled: "Whatever the case—the Jiangdong Sun family's conduct is truly beyond reproach."

The First Master nodded: "Of course. Otherwise, how could they have remained standing firm for several centuries?"

"As for Wenlan, that child—she may well remarry someday. When that day comes, we should prepare a full trousseau for her as if she were our own daughter."

The First Master nodded: "Yes—so preparations should begin now. From what I've seen, Wenlan is no hidebound traditionalist. She has gone through a separation with such clean resolve and decisiveness—remarrying would be no great difficulty."

"I really..." Qin Rujin was still in a daze: "I never imagined—that with Wenlan separating from her husband, I'm the one who ended up with a small fortune!"

Madam Li laughed heartily, full of pride: "When you were small, Mother took you to your maternal grandmother's family at the Liuyuan Temple to pray and burn incense. The abbess at the Liuyuan Temple took one look at you and said you were fated for joy and fortune."

"Back then Mother didn't believe it—I thought the abbess was just saying nice things to please us. But looking at it now—the abbess wasn't wrong in the slightest!" The First Master said with a laugh.

That evening, the Third Uncle of the Qin family returned to the household......

chapters.title: Rujin Confronts Her Third Aunt
chapters.content:
The Third Master of the Qin family arrived home and went straight to the First Branch's Western Courtyard without so much as stepping foot in his own Third Branch's courtyard.

The First Master of the Qin family received him in his study. Seeing him dusty from the road, exhausted and hungry, he felt a pang of concern.

Though they were not born of the same mother, the two brothers had depended on one another through the years. Of all the people in their father's line, the two of them were the only true family left to each other.

"Elder Brother! This time I took those memorials on the repair and dredging of the great and small waterways of the Ying dynasty, written in your own hand, and traveled to many places—leaving a copy with each local official...

Though more than a few didn't pay them much mind, there were also a good many who truly cared about benefiting the people in their regions, and they put those methods to use... with excellent results!"

The Third Master of the Qin family was wildly excited, gesturing with his hands as he spoke.

The First Master patted his arm and looked at him: "You've grown thin, grown thin... You must have suffered greatly out there these past days."

The Third Master gave a laugh, and still couldn't contain his excitement: "Elder Brother! How can you say such a thing to me! That wasn't suffering—!"

"You didn't see the faces of the common people when the waterways had been repaired and the water came rushing through like a silver dragon, winding and pouring! That sight... even now, just thinking of it, I'm nearly moved to tears!"

"Elder Brother, I must thank you!" The Third Master of the Qin family bowed deeply to the First Master.

The First Master quickly stepped forward to help him straighten up, then called out: "Has the meal prepared for the Third Master still not been brought over?"

"Elder Brother—at my age, to still be able to go out and see this vast world, to do something real for the common people of a region, it truly is..."

"I know, I know! Now eat quickly—eat well!" The First Master of the Qin family firmly steered him to his meal.

* * *

At the Jiang residence.

Jiang Jiuxiao had just been summoned by Old Madam Jiang to discuss matters related to the wedding banquet, and had barely left the Old Madam's courtyard when Li Yi arrived with news that the Third Master of the Qin family had returned to the household.

"My lord, your servant has already made inquiries—this time, the Third Master of the Qin family was traveling on behalf of the First Master to visit the lower reaches of the great rivers and waterways across the Ying dynasty. Principally, he was giving local officials—

The First Master of the Qin family had not used his official position to do any of this.

Instead, he had the Third Master present the well-reasoned and practical memorials to those local officials who had long been troubled by flooding—under the guise of a private citizen—helping them to dredge or repair their waterways..."

After hearing this, Jiang Jiuxiao's lips curved with satisfaction.

His father-in-law held a sinecure at the fifth rank in the Ministry of Works and didn't even need to report to the yamen every day.

And yet he had quietly accomplished such remarkable work. A substantive position with real authority was now all but assured.

For several consecutive terms, the chief superintendent of the Bureau of Water in the Ministry of Works had achieved nothing, and every flood season the people's suffering was immense.

The court suffered alongside them, and the Ministry of Revenue suffered most of all.

His father-in-law had an accurate eye—it seemed he had set his sights on the position of chief superintendent of the Bureau of Water long ago.

And fortunately, his father-in-law truly had the genuine ability to merit it.

Given all this, he could now ask Lord Cheng to be a little bolder still...

The following day, happy news arrived from the Qin family's First Branch.

Overnight, the First Master of the Qin family had been promoted from his fifth-rank sinecure to a fourth-rank post as chief superintendent of the Bureau of Water in the Ministry of Works.

A substantive post with real authority.

The former chief superintendent of the Bureau of Water was nominally elevated to a third-rank sinecure—a step up in title but a step down in power.

Every member of the Qin family's First Branch was overjoyed—more festive than the New Year.

At the same time, when news of this reached the Qin Second Branch, not a single face showed a trace of happiness.

In the Qiwu Garden, Qin Ruyue was stunned for a long time when she heard the news.

Of all the times—it had to be right before the Sixth Young Miss's wedding that her father suddenly rose to a higher post, and a substantive one at that!

This would only further elevate the Sixth Young Miss's standing in every way!

And what about herself?

With her own family's father and brother suffering one calamity after another, even the Wang family her fiancé came from had begun to look down on her, deliberately slighting her with their betrothal gifts...

This hadn't happened in her previous life at all!

Where exactly had things gone wrong?

This couldn't go on. She had to find a way to establish a connection with Prince An as soon as possible!

* * *

Taking advantage of this happy occasion of his promotion, the First Master of the Qin family also formally announced his intention to adopt the Seventh and Eighth Young Misses from the Third Branch.

He specifically invited the old clan leader and several elders to serve as witnesses, and formally registered the names of the Seventh and Eighth Young Misses under the First Master of the Qin family's household in the First Branch.

From that day forward, the Seventh and Eighth Young Misses were legitimate daughters of the First Branch.

The Third Master was so overjoyed that day he drank himself into a stupor.

Madam Zhou had someone help him back to his own courtyard.

Thinking about how the Qin First Branch was slapping the Third Branch's face like this—and yet her husband was this delighted about it—she couldn't help but turn sour and start muttering complaints in front of the drunken Third Master.

The Third Master squinted at her, wavering between drunk and sober.

"What's this? You've seen the Second Branch's separation as a precedent, and now you want a separation too?"

Madam Zhou stiffened.

She stared at the Third Master in disbelief.

"I know these years have been stifling for you following a man like me, and I don't blame you—blame me for my own uselessness, for not being able to give you a good life, for not being able to stand up for you...

Because of that, these years you've been suppressing and undermining Concubine Lu and the Seventh and Eighth Girls she bore—openly and behind closed doors—and all I've done is chide you with words. I haven't actually punished you in any real way.

That I've wronged you is my own matter. But how could you also help those brutes of the Second Branch ruin the Seventh Girl? Even if she wasn't born from your body, she has called you 'Mother' for over ten years!"

The more the Third Master spoke, the clearer and more agitated he became.

"I had been thinking—endure, just endure a little longer. When Elder Brother finally stands firmly on his feet, we'll all have better days ahead.

I would make it up to you properly, make it up to Concubine Lu and the two girls... but what have you done? Look at what you've done!"

By the time the Third Master of the Qin family finished speaking, this seven-foot man broke down and wept aloud.

Madam Zhou felt as if she had been plunged into a frozen abyss.

She didn't know how to comfort him... nor did she know how to defend herself.

"Has Concubine Lu not been humble enough in your presence all these years, not respectful enough toward you?

She was bought by the Old Madam specifically to set against you—yet she is perceptive, and she knows that in the end she must live her whole life with our family. She has never once gone to the Old Madam's side to betray us as husband and wife...

And yet it is you—you caused Concubine Lu to lose two male pregnancies in a row!

Even after all that, Concubine Lu has never resented you, never harmed you or your two sons—how could you bring yourself to harm the Seventh Girl she gave birth to! How could you!"

Madam Zhou found her voice at last. Her eyes were red as she snapped furiously: "She's a lowly concubine! Would she dare harm me, the mistress of this household? Would she dare harm my two sons? She wouldn't dare!"

The Third Master of the Qin family shook his head with a look of deep disappointment.

"You are not as good as Concubine Lu—not even close to the 'lowly concubine' you speak of! Look at the two sons you raised. Now look at the two daughters Concubine Lu raised. How can you not be ashamed?"

"Enough. Now that Elder Brother and Sister-in-law have shown their generosity and are willing to adopt the Seventh and Eighth Girls, what right do you have to come and speak sourly of them?" The Third Master of the Qin family looked utterly defeated.

"What you have done is enough cause to divorce a wife. But knowing I was the one who failed first, I won't divorce you. However, you surely have nothing to say against a separation?"

"No!" Madam Zhou screamed. "I won't separate! I absolutely will not separate..."

The Third Master of the Qin family looked at her with total despair and turned to leave.

Madam Zhou collapsed to the floor, tears streaming down her face as she stared at the Third Master's resolute and retreating back.

Where had she gone wrong?

Where had she gone wrong?

Her own mother, her own sister-in-law, her own younger sisters-in-law...

And after marrying into the Qin family—her step-mother-in-law Old Madam Qin, and her second sister-in-law Madam Tong—not one of them had failed to suppress concubines and the children born of them.

They had done it, and no one ever said they were in the wrong. So why—when it came to her—was she being threatened with separation, or even outright divorce?

It's not as if she had done anything serious to the Seventh Girl!

She had only advised the Seventh Girl that becoming the concubine of an imperial prince with a noble title was not a bad lot.

She had merely told the Seventh Girl that for a girl of illegitimate birth, marrying into the household of Prince An as a concubine was the highest branch she could possibly reach...

Where had she gone wrong?

Why had that earned her such contempt from her husband?

* * *

Madam Zhou could neither understand it nor swallow her anger.

She went to find her sister-in-law Madam Li to pour out her grievances.

Madam Li was in the middle of seeing guests off with her two daughters-in-law. Seeing Madam Zhou's swollen red eyes and utterly shattered expression, she turned her mouth aside.

But she had no choice—she sent the two daughters-in-law to see the guests off and received Madam Zhou herself.

On her side, Qin Rujin went to see the Seventh Young Miss, and personally brought her the good news.

But the Seventh Young Miss was still in a daze—and even though today was a good day for her and the Eighth Young Miss, there was not the slightest sign of her coming around.

All that could be done was feed her broth and thin porridge each day, enough to keep a thread of life in her.

But this could not go on—the girl had lost a great deal of weight...

She left the Eighth Young Miss to look after the Seventh, then went to find her mother—she wanted to discuss with her the need to find an experienced senior imperial physician to take a look at the Seventh Young Miss.

The moment she arrived at her mother's courtyard, her mother's maid came to tell her that the Third Mistress had come to pour out her sorrows to the First Mistress.

Qin Rujin wrinkled her brow with distaste.

That Third Aunt of hers—foolish, selfish, and still shameless enough to come crying to her mother?

Crying about what?

Unhappy that the Seventh and Eighth Young Misses had become daughters of their First Branch?

She didn't have anyone announce her.

She just listened as her Third Aunt Madam Zhou sobbed: "Sister-in-law, tell me—what on earth have I done to deserve Heaven's wrath, that my husband would treat me this way?"

"He says he can't go on living with me—it's either separation, or I spend the rest of my life keeping the name of Third Mistress of the Qin family but nothing else..."

"Sister-in-law, is that something a person would say? I've followed him for most of my life without a single day of ease!

Just when I'd finally waited for our Elder Brother to stand on his feet, he does this to me...

How is that any different from crossing a river and kicking away the bridge?"

Madam Li was rolling her eyes inwardly.

When Qin Rujin heard the woman actually implying a grievance against her father, she could listen no more. She reached up, swept aside the bamboo curtain, and stepped into her mother's room.

Giving a perfunctory bow with a cool expression, she turned to Madam Zhou and said: "Third Aunt—what use is it coming to cry to my mother about matters between you and Third Uncle?"

"Besides—you say you haven't had a single day of ease following Third Uncle. But has my mother not suffered her share of grievances from her in-laws?

So why is it that my mother and my father are of one heart, and despite all their hardships they've built a thriving life together, raised six children well—while you cannot?"

"You didn't merely fail to do that—you have also held Third Uncle back! Third Uncle certainly has his own faults, but they are not toward you—they are toward the Seventh Young Miss, the Eighth Young Miss, and Concubine Lu!"

"Sixth Young Miss, you... how could you eavesdrop on your elders?" Madam Zhou was so thoroughly challenged by this junior member of the family that her face burned red, and she spoke without restraint.

Madam Li's expression turned cold at once: "This is my own courtyard—Yinniang can come and go as she pleases. You happen to be here crying out all your complaints, and somehow that becomes my Yinniang eavesdropping?"

"I..." Madam Zhou's face went an even deeper red, so furious her chest ached.

"Even if Yinniang wasn't eavesdropping, how can this child speak to me—an elder—in such a way?"

Madam Zhou dabbed at her eyes, arguing her case: "I haven't been as fortunate as you—your husband only has eyes for you, all your children are legitimate—what do you know of the difficulties of being in my position?"

Qin Rujin looked at her without sympathy and laid bare the truth.

chapters.title: The Fate of a Muddle-Headed Person
chapters.content:
"Fifth Sister told me herself—when the Old Madam forced Concubine Lu into Third Uncle's inner quarters, it was you, Third Aunt, who wanted to be seen as a magnanimous wife. You were the one who accepted her first. Third Uncle had never wanted it, but you pressured him, told him not to make things difficult for you, and practically forced him to go to Concubine Lu..."

Qin Rujin was not making things up. This had indeed come from Qin Ruyue—she had mocked Madam Zhou in front of the original Rujin during a flower gathering, and Rujin had recalled it clearly.

Madam Zhou's face cycled through shades of green and white, and for a long moment she couldn't manage a single word.

Madam Li, seeing her disgraceful state, felt both exasperated and disgusted.

She gave Qin Rujin a glance.

Qin Rujin gave a small shake of her head.

A muddle-headed person like her Third Aunt Madam Zhou would not wake up without a firm word.

This wasn't Qin Rujin being a busybody—she had read the situation clearly. Her father, in fact, cared deeply about the Third Master.

All these years, her father had deliberately kept the Third Master hovering between the First and Second Branches' conflict, so the Second Branch wouldn't target him directly.

Even so, the Second Branch had never fully trusted the Third Branch.

The Third Master hadn't even dared educate his own two legitimate sons too well—for fear that if they became too capable before learning to conceal it, the Second Branch would move against them.

It was the same with her own two brothers—Father had never allowed them to pursue the civil official's path, and had them go into the military instead.

Only with her youngest brother had things changed, because by then the two elder brothers were capable of protecting themselves and the First Branch was growing stronger—only then could her youngest brother devote himself to study and sit the imperial examinations.

While Father drew the Second Branch's attention openly, the Third Master had also done a great deal from the shadows to benefit the First and Third Branches.

Take Father's sudden promotion: the Third Master had played a major part in that.

Going forward, when Father split the clan from the Qin family, he would also bring the Third Master along—brothers of one heart can cut through metal.

"Was I truly wrong? The truth is, I never wanted Third Uncle to take a concubine. But I..." Madam Zhou murmured to herself, her thoughts a tangled mess.

Qin Rujin sighed: "I can understand Third Aunt's feelings. I believe my mother can too—I think any woman in the position of principal wife could understand."

"But Third Aunt—since you were the one who pushed Third Uncle toward Concubine Lu, and Concubine Lu has done nothing to harm the Third Branch's interests, you simply have to swallow down the bitter consequence of Third Uncle having a concubine."

"Yes... I did swallow down that bitter fruit myself. And I haven't done anything to Concubine Lu..." This she said with noticeably less confidence.

Madam Li gave a cold sniff, and Madam Zhou then reluctantly admitted: "Yes... I did harm Concubine Lu..."

Madam Li said: "Concubine Lu saw things clearly. She didn't hold it too much against you. Even I, who personally despise the practice of men taking concubines, can still see that Concubine Lu is a pitiable person who has conducted herself in her position exceptionally well."

"Yes... I know. She was forced to come be a concubine to my husband—if she'd had a choice, she wouldn't have. I didn't want to harm her either, but my husband liked her so much, and I..."

Madam Li, seeing her still so pathetically spineless, was too tired to keep rolling her eyes: "You really are lucky to have encountered such a perceptive and clear-minded woman as Concubine Lu!"

"If she hadn't seen that the Third Master's heart truly lies mostly with you, his principal wife—do you really think that with her intelligence and resourcefulness she couldn't have followed our step-mother-in-law's example and clawed her way up from concubine to wife?"

The truth was, Madam Zhou wasn't even someone the Third Uncle had chosen for himself. She too had been handpicked by Old Madam Qin as the Third Master's principal wife.

In those days, Old Master Qin was still alive—he had been deceived and managed by Old Madam Qin his whole life, and followed her in everything, especially in his old age. The Third Master had been powerless to resist, and the First Master couldn't help him either.

The Third Master had resigned himself—since he had taken a woman as his principal wife, he ought to treat her well. Unfortunately, Madam Zhou had been twisted about by Madam Tong's schemes again and again, letting him down time after time...

"I... I..." Madam Zhou's eyes went wide and she couldn't speak. She was foolish, yes—but in her heart, she knew perfectly well what Concubine Lu was capable of.

All these years of trying to put Concubine Lu down at every turn had been, at its root, fear—terror and jealousy of her.

"Concubine Lu knows her own place. Do you know yours?" Madam Li gave her a sharp rebuke. "You are nothing but a muddle-headed fool! And the worst of it—you actually listened to the Second Branch's goading and ruined the Seventh Girl as you did!"

"If anyone ever reduced one of my children to that state, I couldn't fight them—but I would throw myself at them and bite them to death!"

Madam Zhou looked into her sister-in-law's wolf-mother eyes—cold and vicious—and shuddered with genuine fright.

If she were being fair about it—if someone were to harm her own two sons, she would probably throw herself at them and bite them to death as well...

"Sister-in-law, I... I do regret it in my heart. I couldn't bear it either. I just never expected the Seventh Girl to be so decisive—willing to give up her very life!"

"To begin with, I had already lost all my face over that affair. Then, Sister-in-law, when you said you wanted to adopt the Seventh and Eighth Girls, I thought at first you were just trying to protect them until it all blew over."

Madam Zhou twisted uncomfortably. "But then my husband came back and your First Branch actually went ahead and formalized the adoption—even inviting the clan leader and elders as witnesses... wasn't that slapping me in the face?"

"You deserve it!" Madam Li snapped. "Even now all you care about is your own face! If you truly cared so much about your face, you shouldn't have done those muddle-headed things in the first place—letting Third Brother grow more and more disappointed in you..."

"Waaah..." Seeing Madam Li berate her again, Madam Zhou couldn't hold back and started to cry.

Qin Rujin was lost for words.

Madam Li was exasperated too, and snapped: "What are you crying for! And you have the nerve to cry!"

Madam Zhou sobbed: "How are you even harsher than my own mother? My own mother has never spoken to me like this... waaah..."

At that, Madam Li found herself both furious and amused.

"How old are you, anyway? You're the age of someone who should soon be holding grandchildren—and you're weeping like this in front of young people! How undignified!"

Madam Zhou retorted through her tears: "Sixth Young Miss—that junior family member—is even harsher than you, Sister-in-law. I'm truly frightened of her now... waaah..."

Qin Rujin couldn't stop herself from rolling her eyes.

She finally understood the mix of helplessness and irritation that came over her mother Madam Li whenever she mentioned Third Aunt Madam Zhou.

"Hmph... everyone says I haven't treated the Seventh and Eighth Girls well, but I, as their step-mother, did save up some trousseau money for them..."

Madam Zhou still couldn't let it go and had to make her case.

Madam Li looked at her with contempt: "You—don't I know what you're like? Pinching every copper. You probably haven't set aside all that much for your own sons' betrothal gifts—no one is counting on you for anything regarding the Seventh and Eighth Girls' trousseau!"

Madam Zhou's pale-and-green face turned purple-and-red.

She chewed her lip for a long while, then complained to Madam Li: "How can you say such things to me, Sister-in-law?"

"Enough, enough!" Madam Li waved her off. "From now on, just defer to Third Brother about everything—you can't count on anyone else but him! If you ask him about everything going forward and follow his lead, the two of you won't fall apart!"

Madam Li felt thoroughly drained.

"Really? Sister-in-law, do you mean that? If I follow my husband in everything from now on, he won't be so heartless toward me?"

"He's still heartless toward you?" Madam Li was about to argue, then gave an exasperated nod: "Yes, yes—as long as you follow his lead from now on and don't go acting on your own judgment, he will in time come back around to you..."

After sending Madam Zhou on her way, Madam Li watched her retreating figure, lost in thought.

Qin Rujin refilled her mother's tea and said gently: "Mother needn't worry about Third Aunt. A person like her has the greatest talent for talking herself into a good mood—she'll cheer herself up again very quickly."

She could only hope this muddle-headed Third Aunt truly absorbed what her mother, with such patience, had told her.

Someone who couldn't even bring herself to be generous with her own sons' betrothal gifts—what else could one expect from her?

All she could do was hope she'd follow her mother's advice and defer to the Third Master in all things.

The Third Master took his cues from her father, and with her father looking out for him, things couldn't go too wrong.

"Mother—Concubine Lu once told you she wanted Third Uncle to give her a deed of manumission from her concubine status. Does Third Uncle know about this?"

Concubine Lu was truly a resilient and perceptive woman.

For the sake of her two daughters, she had once made up her mind to endure a lifetime in the Third Master's inner quarters.

But now that both daughters had been adopted by the First Branch, she was at peace.

She had been coerced into becoming a concubine in the first place. Given any choice, how many women would willingly choose a concubine's lot—with no status and no dignity?

Madam Li also had a kind of admiration for Concubine Lu.

"Your father will certainly tell your Third Uncle. Your Third Uncle himself never wanted to take a concubine—he is a son born of a concubine himself, and he knows firsthand how difficult it is for concubine-born children without someone to shelter them."

"Back then, your Third Aunt fell into the Second Branch's mother-and-daughter-in-law trap, and your Third Uncle was deeply disappointed in her then too... Third Uncle certainly has his own fault in it. Your father gave him a thorough scolding as well."

"Now that Concubine Lu wants a deed of manumission, I believe your Third Uncle will agree."

Qin Rujin nodded, and felt a weight lift from her heart.

Concubine Lu was a worthy mother.

She deeply respected the mother's love that had driven Concubine Lu to risk everything for her daughters.

For the Third Master to grant her freedom of his own accord—that was the best possible outcome.

"Concubine Lu said that once your Third Uncle truly gives her a deed of manumission, she'll return to her ancestral home."

Qin Rujin frowned slightly.

"Does Concubine Lu still have family in her hometown?"

"Apparently not." Madam Li answered.

"Then what is there to go back to? A lone woman on her own—even if she registers as an independent household, people will take advantage of her. When that time comes, crying to Heaven won't help, and crying to the earth won't either."

"Besides, the Seventh Young Miss and Eighth Young Miss are still here in the capital..."

Madam Li sighed: "She's afraid that if she stays in the capital, Third Aunt will resent it and cause more trouble. She's also thinking of your Seventh and Eighth Young Misses."

Qin Rujin said: "Once Concubine Lu has the deed in hand, she is a free woman. If Third Aunt dares make life difficult for her after that, it is Third Aunt who will have no ground to stand on."

Madam Li listened to her little daughter's words and smiled again.

"What you've said is much the same as what your father thinks. Your father also doesn't agree with Concubine Lu taking her deed and leaving the capital."

She paused and sighed again: "But we also have no idea how to arrange things for Concubine Lu."

Qin Rujin's eyes turned lightly: "Come to think of it—I heard from the Eighth Young Miss that Concubine Lu is also from the Hedong region, very near Second Aunt's family home. She is skilled at making Hedong-style noodle dishes.

The Eighth Young Miss also told me that Concubine Lu's noodle dishes are both exquisite and delicious—the white-flour master cooks in the Qin household's main kitchen don't even come close to her skill."

Madam Li looked at her little daughter and asked: "Are you suggesting... that Concubine Lu could open a food stall in the capital?"

Qin Rujin smiled and nodded: "Mother—isn't that a good idea?"

Madam Li nodded, then shook her head: "A fine idea—but Concubine Lu has little silver. What she's saved over the years is just her monthly allowance from the Qin family, plus the occasional small earnings from embroidery she's sold...

And even that she was going to leave for the Seventh and Eighth Girls as trousseau..."

Qin Rujin smiled: "Now that the Seventh and Eighth Young Misses are our family's daughters, their trousseau is certainly not Concubine Lu's concern—and besides, there is still Third Uncle.

Concubine Lu's savings could first go toward renting a small shop and getting herself started. Once she earns some money, wouldn't it be even better to supplement the Seventh and Eighth Girls' trousseaus that way?

Perhaps Concubine Lu will even build up a thriving business—and become a real support for the Seventh and Eighth Young Misses in the future?"

Madam Li nodded as she listened: "That makes sense! I'll speak to your father about this, and let him discuss it further with your Third Uncle.

After giving Concubine Lu the deed of manumission, some compensation in silver should be arranged for her as well. Whatever else may be said, Concubine Lu came to your Third Uncle's household and never did anything wrong—and she gave your Third Uncle two daughters."

Then she reached out lovingly and touched her little daughter's face: "They say you take the most after me—but of all six of you children, I think you're the most like your father. Always worrying, always wanting to shelter everyone you care about under your wings."

Qin Rujin grinned: "Isn't that as it should be? The truth is, everyone in our family is like that—even you, Mother."

Madam Li was taken aback, then broke into a smile herself.

Yes—everyone in the family was just like that.

And because of that, the First Branch had not fallen under decades of the Second Branch's suppression—and had at last arrived at this steadily improving moment.

The two of them were still talking when a little maid outside reported that the Fifth Young Miss had come to pay her respects to the First Mistress.

Madam Li's brow creased deeply. She looked at Qin Rujin: "In all these years, this Fifth Sister of yours has never once come to pay her respects to me, her First Aunt by marriage. She doesn't come unless she wants something."

Qin Rujin tilted her head: "Isn't she still under house arrest?"

Madam Li gave a cold laugh: "This Fifth Sister of yours has always been extraordinarily skilled at obeying in appearance while defying in practice—always fond of playing small tricks... Very well. Let her in—let's hear what she has to say."

Qin Ruyue was led in by one of Madam Li's maids and entered the reception room.

She kept her head lowered, but her eyes were quietly taking in everything around her.

In that single glance, she realized—this First Aunt's rooms, which both her grandmother and her mother had always looked down on, were filled with the most fascinating and unusual things.

A telescope. Western-painted enamelware. A self-striking clock...

In her previous life, she hadn't seen these Western novelties until after her second marriage—and only then because her second husband had been a thoroughly dissolute young wastrel, excellent at every pleasure and indulgence.

He had squandered her dowry silver like running water, spending without restraint, hunting down such trinkets...

And yet the First Branch already had all these things now... where had they come from?

After Qin Ruyue greeted Madam Li with a curtsy, she glanced at Qin Rujin standing beside her and let her eyes turn slightly: "Oh—Sixth Sister is here with First Aunt as well?"

Qin Rujin gave a bland "Fifth Sister."

Madam Li had her sit down, had a little maid bring fragrant tea, and then asked: "Fifth Young Miss—you're still under house arrest, aren't you? What brings you to see me today?"

Qin Ruyue bit her lip, her face coloring slightly. She looked at Madam Li and said quietly: "First Aunt, I want to go see the Seventh Young Miss, but the Eighth Young Miss won't let me. I could only come and ask First Aunt to make the decision."

Qin Rujin's brow lightly furrowed. Madam Li asked the question before her: "Fifth Young Miss, why do you suddenly want to go see the Seventh Young Miss?"

Qin Ruyue drew a slow breath, looked at Madam Li, and gave a small smile: "I'm thinking that I'm about to be married off too—I just wanted to go find Seventh Young Miss and have a little chat."

chapters.title: Who Hasn't Got a Secret or Two
chapters.content:
Madam Li glanced at her own little daughter, then looked back at Qin Ruyue and said coolly: "Perhaps Fifth Young Miss doesn't know—your Seventh Young Miss, ever since the day... after being forced to that extremity by your mother, has been in a daze ever since, and has shown no signs of coming around."

Qin Ruyue bit her lower lip, her heart seething with resentment.

Did this Madam Li have to speak so pointedly to an unmarried young girl?

"First Aunt, I mean no harm by it—it's just that Seventh Young Miss and I do share a sisterly bond, after all. Once I've married out, it won't be easy to come back to see Seventh Young Miss whenever I want."

Madam Li arched a mocking eyebrow: "If Fifth Young Miss truly cared about her sisterly bond, she would have come to see Seventh Young Miss before she was placed under house arrest by her father—and it would have served as some small atonement for your mother's sins."

Madam Li despised the hypocrisy of the Fifth Young Miss and hadn't intended to bother with her—but seeing Qin Ruyue's every word so honeyed and evasive, she couldn't restrain herself.

The Fifth Young Miss was, in the end, a person of considerable patience.

She drew a slow breath, then put on the air of a junior who would not stoop to quarrel with an elder.

Her voice became more sincere: "First Aunt—what my elders do is not something I, as a junior and a girl, would have known about. And even had I known, there was nothing I could have done to change it."

"First Aunt—please just do your niece this one kindness and let me go see Seventh Young Miss. As you say, I'll go ask Seventh Young Miss for her forgiveness on behalf of my mother!"

With those words on the table, Madam Li could no longer refuse.

To refuse any further would make Madam Li the one breaking their sisterly bond.

Qin Rujin too was surprised and couldn't help stealing a glance at this Fifth Sister of hers.

What a formidable piece of work.

Exceptionally good at bending and stretching as the situation demanded.

Madam Li frowned and gave a cold laugh: "The way Fifth Young Miss puts it—would First Aunt really have the heart to stop her? Only, your Seventh Young Miss is now my daughter—I care about her!"

"Yes, First Aunt is kind and loving. Fifth Young Miss knows how much you care for the Seventh Young Miss."

Qin Ruyue gave a soft nod, tears wobbling in her eyes.

"Only Fifth Young Miss's mother is now recuperating at a country estate, and in a few days Fifth Young Miss will be married out together with Sixth Young Miss. Fifth Young Miss hopes that First Aunt can spare some care for Fifth Young Miss as well."

Madam Li was frankly disgusted by this performance.

She turned to Qin Rujin: "Yinniang—take your Fifth Sister to your Seventh Young Miss's courtyard yourself.

Once she's been there, she'll understand for herself just how pitiful the Seventh Young Miss is—and know that it's not me, as First Aunt, who is deliberately making things hard for her!"

Qin Rujin nodded and turned to look at Qin Ruyue, saying blandly: "Fifth Sister, after you."

Qin Ruyue breathed in relief, rose to bow to Madam Li, then said to Qin Rujin: "Thank you for the trouble, Sixth Sister."

The moment Qin Rujin led her out of Madam Li's courtyard, Qin Ruyue murmured softly: "Sixth Sister—you truly have good fortune. Not only does the Jiang family value you highly, but even the Sun family has shown such regard for you...

I heard the Sun family gave Sixth Sister a generous half-trousseau. I wonder what Sixth Sister did to earn such regard from them?"

Qin Rujin paused mid-step, turned to look at her, and curved her lips in a smile.

"If I were to say the Sun family values me because of Madam Sun and Zheng'er and Shen'er... would Fifth Sister be regretting that she hadn't treated Madam Sun and the two boys a little better?"

Qin Ruyue narrowed her beautiful eyes and gazed steadily into Qin Rujin's.

"Sixth Sister needn't mock me like that. Elder Brother was the one who was in the wrong—no matter what I might have done for Madam Sun and the two boys, the Sun family would never have looked on me more highly."

Qin Rujin nodded: "Since you understand that, what's there to ask?"

Qin Ruyue played the part of a good-natured elder sister, giving a helpless shake of her head: "You're right—I shouldn't have asked."

"Good that Fifth Sister knows." Qin Rujin's smile deepened, and she turned and walked on.

To any onlooker, the two sisters were getting along in perfect harmony.

"Sixth Sister." Qin Ruyue quickened her steps to walk side by side with Qin Rujin. "You know, you've changed so much recently. How can a person change this much in such a short time?"

"Fifth Sister." Qin Rujin paused again, and smiled as she said the name.

Qin Ruyue also stopped at once, turning her head to look at Qin Rujin.

Qin Rujin said slowly: "Has Fifth Sister not noticed—you yourself have also changed a great deal?"

Qin Ruyue's heart gave a violent lurch. She had her guilty conscience, and naturally feared someone had noticed something.

She quickly lowered her gaze to hide the panic in her eyes.

Deliberately hooking a strand of hair near her temple with her finger, she said: "What is Sixth Sister talking about? Haven't I always been like this?"

"Is that so?" Qin Rujin smiled: "Perhaps only Fifth Sister herself thinks so."

"Then... in what way do you think I've changed?" Qin Ruyue thought for a moment, then raised her eyes to look at Qin Rujin, full of probing curiosity.

"Everything has changed." Qin Rujin's voice was very soft—and hearing it, Qin Ruyue felt another hard blow land within her.

"Everything? Sixth Sister is imagining things!" Qin Ruyue, her composure slightly cracked, turned her head away and quickened her pace as if in flight.

Qin Rujin watched her stumbling, hurried steps and curved her lips in a cold smile.

When they arrived at the courtyard where the Seventh and Eighth Young Misses lived, the Eighth Young Miss heard from a little maid that Qin Ruyue had come again, and her willow-leaf brows shot upward in instant fury.

But the moment the maid added that the Sixth Young Miss had come along too, the Eighth Young Miss transformed completely.

She immediately broke into a little trot to welcome her Sixth Sister.

"Sixth Sister!" The Eighth Young Miss was only thirteen this year, her hair in twin buns, bright-eyed and adorable.

"Eighth Young Sister." Qin Rujin opened her arms and caught the little swallow as she came flying in.

"Eighth Young Sister." Qin Ruyue put on the air of a gentle elder sister and smiled as she called to her.

"Hmph!" The Eighth Young Miss sniffed through her nose. "What are you doing here again?"

Then she turned to Qin Rujin: "Sixth Sister, her brother and her mother hurt my Seventh Sister so badly—I don't want to see her!"

Qin Rujin pulled the little girl out of her arms and leaned close to whisper: "Eighth Young Sister—be good. Trust Sixth Sister. Bad people don't come to good ends..."

At the very least, for anyone in the Qin Second Branch who had done wrong without being punished—she didn't mind stepping in to do the punishing herself.

But for now, she also wanted to know why Qin Ruyue was so insistent on seeing Seventh Young Sister at this particular moment.

Surely she wasn't putting on the sentimental-sisterhood act for nothing.

For someone like Qin Ruyue, she had never stooped to such performances before.

If she was bothering now, she had a purpose.

After all—the woman was a genuine born-again soul.

The Eighth Young Miss knew better than to ignore her Sixth Sister's advice, and said softly: "I'll listen to Sixth Sister."

"Good girl!" Qin Rujin patted the little girl's twin buns.

"Sixth Sister, Eighth Sister—I'd like to speak to Seventh Sister alone for a few minutes." Qin Ruyue looked at the Eighth Young Miss, but directed her words at Qin Rujin.

The Eighth Young Miss immediately panicked and blurted out: "No! I'm afraid you'll hurt my Seventh Sister again!"

Qin Ruyue's strikingly beautiful face darkened—could this wretched girl's words be any more offensive?

"Jiang Yue—you go with Fifth Young Miss." Qin Rujin indicated the second-tier maid who had recently come to serve her, Jiang Yue.

Jiang Yue acknowledged the order and stepped out from behind Qin Rujin.

She was one of the skilled fighters Jiang Jiuxiao had sent for Qin Rujin—the maid with martial skills. There was also a household stewardess by the name of Jiang Feng, whom everyone called Matron Feng; and two men for outside affairs, Jiang Shan and Jiang Chuan.

Qin Rujin was not comfortable letting Qin Ruyue go see the Seventh Young Miss alone, so she sent the martial-skilled Jiang Yue to keep watch.

Qin Ruyue looked at Jiang Yue—short in stature, unremarkable in appearance, the kind of person who would disappear into any crowd.

She turned to look at Qin Rujin: "This maid is quite unfamiliar. How is it I've never seen her before?"

Qin Rujin said blandly: "Fifth Sister seems very interested in my personal attendants?"

Qin Ruyue bit her lip: "I only wanted to look out for Sixth Sister."

"No need." Qin Rujin smiled. "Fifth Sister had better look out for herself."

Qin Ruyue narrowed her eyes and continued: "Sixth Sister is sending someone to follow me in—because you don't trust me alone with Seventh Young Miss?"

"Yes." Qin Rujin nodded.

Qin Ruyue wanted to smile but couldn't quite manage it. She suppressed a dull ache that spread through her chest.

"Why go to the trouble? I'm just a weak girl—surely I'm not actually going to harm Seventh Young Miss? You trust me so little?"

Qin Ruyue looked quietly aggrieved.

The Eighth Young Miss finally lost patience and burst out: "I don't trust you! I don't trust anyone from your Second Branch—young or old! You're all bad people!"

Qin Ruyue frowned. She looked at the Eighth Young Miss, and her beautiful eyes went sharp: "Sixth Sister—is this how the First Branch teaches the Eighth Young Miss?"

The Eighth Young Miss grabbed Qin Rujin at once and planted herself in front of her, arms spread wide, shielding her.

"Stop blackening our First Branch's name! Who doesn't know that I, Qin Eighth Young Miss, was raised by my own birth mother before I was adopted? My heart is red even if I was raised by a concubine—unlike your Second Branch, old and young alike, whose hearts are all black!"

The corners of Qin Ruyue's eyes went red with rage. She flung her sleeve and walked into the Seventh Young Miss's room.

Jiang Yue followed on light feet.

"Sixth Sister—she really won't hurt my Seventh Sister, will she?" the Eighth Young Miss still worried.

Qin Rujin reassured her: "Eighth Young Sister, don't worry—Jiang Yue's martial skills are excellent. With her watching, nothing will happen!"

After entering the Seventh Young Miss's inner room, Qin Ruyue turned, her face cold, and snapped at Jiang Yue who had followed her like a shadow:

"Stop right there! I'm speaking to my Seventh Young Sister—you, a servant, are not to come close!"

Jiang Yue planted her feet and said nothing, not even raising her head.

From this distance, she could control Qin Ruyue entirely if needed.

Even if Qin Ruyue lowered her voice to a near-whisper, it all came through clearly. She had no reason to give Qin Ruyue a second glance.

Satisfied that Jiang Yue hadn't followed her closer, Qin Ruyue let out a quiet breath.

She walked to the Seventh Young Miss's bedside, reached out and brushed away imaginary dust from the edge of the bed, then bent and sat down.

Looking at the Seventh Young Miss—eyes open, unfocused—she said softly: "Seventh Young Sister, I've come to see you. How have you been lately?"

The Seventh Young Miss could not and did not respond.

Qin Ruyue reached out and adjusted the quilt at the corner, her voice dropping to a tone with frost in it.

"I imagine you know what's coming—Sixth Sister and I are soon to be married out." She suddenly bent down and brought her lips close to the Seventh Young Miss's ear, dropping her voice.

"Come back to yourself quickly. Be a good girl and marry into Prince An's household. If not... your Sixth Sister will come to a very bitter end.

Time is truly running short! I admit—the First Branch are kind people. To help you and Eighth Young Sister, they've already adopted you both into the First Branch.

Now you and your sister are both daughters of the First Branch... they've been so good to both of you—can you bear to stand by and watch your Sixth Sister come to such a bitter end in the future?"

chapters.title: The Seventh Young Miss Wakes from Her Nightmare
chapters.content:
Those unfocused eyes of the Seventh Young Miss suddenly changed.

Then her pupils moved rapidly, and Qin Ruyue let out a low cry of fright, every hair on her body standing on end.

She lurched to her feet.

"Se... Seventh Young Sister?" She summoned her courage and called out to the Seventh Young Miss.

Jiang Yue looked over. Seeing that the Seventh Young Miss's expression had changed, but that there was no sign of any danger, she took stock of the situation.

She kept her composure and stayed where she was, taking no action.

Just now, even though this Fifth Young Miss had kept her voice very low, every word had come through to her perfectly clearly.

This was the first errand her Sixth Young Miss had given her. She absolutely could not make a mess of it...

"Sixth Sister... Sixth Sister is about to be married out?" The Seventh Young Miss's voice was strangely hoarse, as if her throat had been scorched by fire.

Only then did Jiang Yue move—darting like a shadow to the small tea table at the side, pouring a cup of warm water with quick, deft hands, and stepping to the Seventh Young Miss's side.

"Seventh Young Miss—don't speak yet. First drink a few sips of water to wet your throat..."

Qin Ruyue snapped: "Who told you to come over? Step back!"

Jiang Yue ignored her and simply helped the Seventh Young Miss drink.

The Seventh Young Miss did indeed feel parched. Since water was being offered, she drank first.

Qin Ruyue had no choice but to stand there, glaring daggers at Jiang Yue.

Like mistress, like maid—both equally infuriating!

"Fifth Young Miss—I belong to the Sixth Young Miss. You have no authority to give me orders. I hope Fifth Young Miss will refrain from ordering other people's servants about in the future."

Jiang Yue said her piece, then stepped back to one side with the empty cup.

Qin Ruyue very nearly lost her composure.

The Seventh Young Miss narrowed her eyes and looked at Qin Ruyue's discomforted face: "Fi... Fifth Sister?"

"It's me." Qin Ruyue saw she was coming around and instantly switched to a smile, taking the Seventh Young Miss's right hand where it lay on the bedside. "You're finally conscious—Fifth Sister came to see you!"

The Seventh Young Miss immediately pulled her hand back.

"You... you just said Sixth Sister is to be married out? Is that true?"

Qin Ruyue frowned. Had the Seventh Young Miss been in a daze these past few days, and had her mind been addled?

She seemed not to remember what had happened before...

If that were the case, it would make things more difficult.

Her original plan had been to exploit the Seventh Young Miss's grateful nature—to use the First Branch's kindness to make her obediently agree to enter Prince An's household as a concubine.

She had also intended to show the same kindness to this foolish girl as the Sixth Young Miss had shown her—and when the moment was right, have this foolish girl carry a few words to Prince An.

Once those words were delivered, she was confident Prince An would find a way to seek her out...

This was the best and least dangerous plan she had been able to come up with.

"Seventh Young Sister—do you not remember anything that happened before?" Qin Ruyue gave a sigh and reached again for the Seventh Young Miss's retreating right hand, her expression full of probing curiosity.

The Seventh Young Miss struggled a few times and couldn't pull free.

She felt Qin Ruyue's hands close around hers like cold, slippery, venomous serpents coiling around her right hand—unbearable.

"Let go of me..." The Seventh Young Miss frowned. Her head was still in chaos, but on one thing she was perfectly clear.

This Fifth Sister of hers was no good person.

She had never been.

"Fifth Sister—is Sixth Sister being married to the Wang family?" The Seventh Young Miss only cared about who her Sixth Sister was marrying.

Qin Ruyue looked at her in surprise: "No—Sixth Sister is being married into the Jiang family. It is I who am being married into the Wang family."

"Sixth Sister is going to the Jiang family?" The Seventh Young Miss was struck as if by lightning. How could her Sixth Sister be marrying into the Jiang family?

In her memory, it was Sixth Sister who had married into the Wang family!

How had this come about?

Oh no!

Sixth Sister absolutely could not marry into the Jiang family!

The Jiang family was heading for terrible misfortune in a few years...

"Sixth Sister? Where is Sixth Sister? I want to see Sixth Sister..." The Seventh Young Miss became agitated.

Qin Ruyue swallowed a mouthful of blood that rose to her throat, unable to go up or down.

Why did everyone care so much about Qin Sixth Young Miss?

What kind of love potion had Qin Sixth Young Miss fed all these people?

* * *

Jiang Yue had already moved to the bead curtain and quietly given instructions to the little maid standing guard there.

The little maid bolted off at a run.

"All right, Seventh Young Sister! You've only just come around—don't hurt yourself. Lie back down. Fifth Sister will sit with you—that's just the same."

"After all—you've been in a daze for days, and today Fifth Sister came to see you, and you've woken up. It was Fifth Sister who called you back." Qin Ruyue had no intention of letting this great credit go to anyone else.

She still intended to use this debt of calling the Seventh Young Miss back to consciousness to demand repayment.
