But the Seventh Young Miss paid her no mind.

This woman was rotten to the core—it was plainly she herself who had married into the Jiang family...

Right!

Jiang family brother-in-law was actually a decent person...

He must have foreseen the Jiang family's impending calamity, and had separated from this woman before the Jiang family fell.

And it wasn't just Lord Jiang and this woman who had separated—several couples in the Jiang family had all parted ways...

My head hurts terribly!

The Seventh Young Miss dared not let her thoughts go any further.

"Seventh Young Sister!" Qin Rujin had heard what Jiang Yue had sent the little maid to tell her, and came rushing over, pulling the Eighth Young Miss along with her.

Seeing the Seventh Young Miss with both hands clutching her head, her own face went white with fear.

The Eighth Young Miss was already weeping as she threw herself forward: "Seventh Sister—Seventh Sister, what's happened? Did that bad woman hurt you?"

Qin Ruyue: "......"

She was going to burst.

"Seventh Young Sister—does your head hurt?" Qin Rujin stepped forward and held the Seventh Young Miss: "I've already sent someone to fetch the physician..."

"Sixth Sister? Is that Sixth Sister?" At the sound of Qin Rujin's voice, the pain in the Seventh Young Miss's head mysteriously vanished.

Qin Rujin quickly nodded: "Yes—it's me, Sixth Sister. I'm here. Don't be afraid! No one can hurt you anymore..."

"Sixth Sister!" The Seventh Young Miss threw herself into Qin Rujin's arms.

Her Sixth Sister was alive and well, right here beside her. Her Sixth Sister had not been—as in that terrible nightmare—caged like a songbird by a beast in human skin for the rest of her life...

Thank heavens!

Thank heavens!

The Seventh Young Miss's mind grew less chaotic.

She understood now—she had spent these past few days trapped in a long and terrible nightmare.

But it was only a nightmare.

Not real!

What was real now was holding her warm, sweet, soft Sixth Sister...

"Sixth Sister—I don't want to see her!" The Seventh Young Miss released Qin Rujin and raised a slender finger at Qin Ruyue, who stood to one side, nearly beside herself with rage.

Qin Ruyue's strikingly beautiful face immediately cycled through every color imaginable, more changeable than a dyer's workshop.

The Eighth Young Miss immediately let go of her Seventh Sister, and like a little firecracker, launched herself at Qin Ruyue.

"Didn't you hear? My Seventh Sister doesn't want to see you! I don't want to see you either—stop putting on this fake sisterly devotion act! You're worse than a stage performer!"

Qin Ruyue nearly stumbled as the Eighth Young Miss barreled into her—she only stayed on her feet because the girl was so small and slight. Even so, Qin Ruyue's ankle turned slightly, and her colorful face went white.

"Eighth Young Sister—why did you deliberately run into me?" Qin Ruyue drew a deep breath and bore the pain, her eyes red as she made her accusation.

But her gaze was fixed only on the Seventh Young Miss: "How could I possibly harm Seventh Young Sister? If I meant to harm her, I wouldn't have woken her up—I'd just have let her stay in her daze, wouldn't I?"

The implication was clear: you owe me for waking you up.

The Seventh Young Miss had only been caught in a long nightmare—she had not forgotten the events before it. Now that her mind was clear again, she remembered perfectly well what the Second Branch had done to her.

Even if Qin Ruyue had not yet been as vicious as in that nightmare, she was still Madam Tong's own daughter!

Madam Tong had hurt her so badly, and not once had this so-called Fifth Sister spoken a word on her behalf...

She was no fool. How could she possibly see Qin Ruyue as some kind of benefactress?

The nightmare had run its course and she had woken up.

She had finished her nightmare, and just happened to hear Qin Ruyue whispering near her ear about Sixth Sister...

Right!

What Qin Ruyue had just whispered in her ear was... Sixth Sister's fate would be very bitter!

In that nightmare, her Sixth Sister had...

Could it be?

Was the nightmare not a nightmare, but something that had actually happened?

But if so—then as things stood now, they were all alive and well, and Sixth Sister was about to marry into the Jiang family—how did any of that fit?

And how could Qin Ruyue know that Sixth Sister's fate ahead would be so bitter?

chapters.title: The Fifth Young Miss Isn't That Kindhearted
chapters.content:
There was definitely something hidden in all of this that she didn't understand...

The Seventh Young Miss steadied herself and stopped trying to drive Qin Ruyue away.

She gave Qin Rujin an apologetic smile: "Sixth Sister, my head is still muddled—I was talking nonsense. Don't worry."

Then she turned to Qin Ruyue: "Fifth Sister, I apologize. Don't hold it against me—I was still confused just now."

Qin Ruyue, seeing her suddenly become soft and yielding, felt a rush of relief.

"What are you saying, Seventh Young Sister? Fifth Sister wouldn't ever blame you." After saying this, she paused.

She looked at the Seventh Young Miss with probing eyes: "Seventh Young Miss is herself now—Fifth Sister can rest easy too."

Then she turned to look at Qin Rujin: "Sixth Sister, you don't know—when I woke Seventh Young Sister just now, she kept saying not to let you marry!"

The Seventh Young Miss had barely registered what was happening before the Eighth Young Miss flared up, baring her teeth at Qin Ruyue: "You bad woman! My Seventh Sister would never say that!"

The Seventh Young Miss called softly, "Eighth Young Sister," and gave her a calming shake of the head.

The Eighth Young Miss puffed out her cheeks in silent fury.

This bad woman was truly rotten! Trying to drive a wedge between Sixth Sister and Seventh Sister like this...

Qin Rujin reached out and gently poked her adorable "puffer fish" face, winked at her, and said "Don't worry, Eighth Young Sister."

Jiang Yue stepped forward at this moment, bowed to Qin Rujin, and said: "Miss—the Seventh Young Miss was only startled that you were being married into the Jiang family. She said nothing about not wanting you to marry."

The Seventh Young Miss also said: "Even in my muddled state, I know that I said no such thing."

Qin Ruyue shot Jiang Yue a glance: "You were standing that far away—how could you possibly have heard clearly?"

Qin Rujin was well aware of Jiang Yue's abilities.

Since Jiang Yue had chosen this moment to speak up, it was because she didn't want Qin Ruyue to drive a wedge between her and the Seventh Young Miss.

As if she could be manipulated in such a way.

"Seventh Young Miss only just woke up—her mind is still muddled. Anything she says in that state should be taken with a grain of salt. And what exactly she said, only Fifth Sister knows in her own heart."

Qin Rujin smiled: "Isn't that right, Fifth Sister?"

Qin Ruyue's beautiful eyes went cold. She replied with bland detachment: "Yes—Sixth Sister is quite right. I know my own heart."

She said no more and simply turned to look at the Seventh Young Miss.

"Seventh Young Sister, don't be upset with me—what I said just now only meant that your feelings for Sixth Sister are so deep, you couldn't bear for her to leave..."

Qin Ruyue had no intention of admitting she had been trying to sow discord. Seeing the opportunity gone, she moved to repair the damage.

But she still managed to get in a shot at the Eighth Young Miss: "Though I did get a rather good dressing-down from Eighth Young Sister—which led everyone to misunderstand me."

The Seventh Young Miss narrowed her eyes. She had always known that Qin Ruyue was the type who would never willingly take any loss.

She also would never stop protecting her own flesh-and-blood little sister.

There was a weight of meaning in her words.

"Fifth Sister, please don't blame Eighth Young Sister either. After what happened to me, she's been terrified—especially wary of anyone from your Second Branch...

I imagine Fifth Sister already knows that in her heart, doesn't she?"

Qin Ruyue was annoyed—but she also understood that the Seventh Young Miss was the protective type, and the most easily exploited because of it.

She had no intention of continuing to spar with her.

"Seventh Young Sister—let's drop all that. What grudge could there be between sisters that lasts past sundown? We were all young and hot-tempered." Qin Ruyue smiled.

"In a few days, Sixth Sister and I will both be married out. Chances to meet again won't be many—shouldn't we all be at peace with one another?"

The Seventh Young Miss heard the meaning beneath those words.

Good. She also wanted to test this strange Qin Ruyue a little further.

"Sixth Sister, Eighth Young Sister—I'd like a few words alone with Fifth Sister. Would you both go have some tea first?" The Seventh Young Miss's gaze was resolute; she didn't want Sixth Sister and Eighth Young Sister to worry.

Qin Ruyue's heart jumped with quiet delight.

Qin Rujin felt a subtle shift in her own heart.

The Eighth Young Miss was anxious. Qin Rujin caught her arm.

She said gently: "It's fine. Your Seventh Sister is a grown young woman—let her have a private word with Fifth Sister about matters only grown girls know. Let's go have tea and cake."

Only then did the Eighth Young Miss calm down and nod obediently.

Qin Rujin gave Jiang Yue a signal with her eyes.

Jiang Yue gave a soft nod and withdrew to an inconspicuous corner to stand quietly.

Qin Ruyue still bore a grudge against Jiang Yue for having spoken up earlier—the way it had made her attempt at sowing discord look foolish. She was about to make a scene.

The Seventh Young Miss reached out and tugged her sleeve: "Fifth Sister—don't worry about that maid. Let's just speak quietly and it's fine."

Qin Ruyue was working hard to win the Seventh Young Miss over right now, and couldn't afford to offend her. She swallowed her anger and let it go.

She made no further attempt to drive Jiang Yue away.

"Please sit, Fifth Sister." The Seventh Young Miss said.

Qin Ruyue gave her a honeyed smile: "Seventh Young Sister gave me quite a fright just now—I thought you were holding a grudge against my mother and brother, and would never speak to me again!"

The Seventh Young Miss suppressed her nausea and looked at Qin Ruyue, shaking her head slightly.

"How could that be? I know that even if Fifth Sister was aware of those things, as a girl in the inner quarters, you wouldn't have been able to do anything to help me even if you wanted to."

The smile on Qin Ruyue's striking face deepened a little, though her eyes held a trace of private satisfaction.

She clasped the Seventh Young Miss's hand and gave it a little shake, sighing: "Yes—I'm glad Seventh Young Sister understands my difficulties."

The Seventh Young Miss stopped herself from shaking her hand free.

"Fifth Sister—earlier I thought I heard you saying to me that Sixth Sister's future ahead would be... not good?"

Qin Ruyue's gaze deepened. This foolish girl—now that she was lucid again, her every thought was still on Qin Sixth Young Miss!

Good!

"Yes." Qin Ruyue nodded and put on a look of worry.

The Seventh Young Miss lowered her eyes and asked: "And... what sort of trouble is it?"

Qin Ruyue had been so consumed by her own bitterness in her previous life that she hadn't paid much attention to what Qin Rujin's life had been like.

She only knew that in her previous life, Qin Rujin had married well—young and already the wife of the Grand Tutor of the Ying dynasty.

The Wang family and Wang the Second had treated her with exceptional kindness and respect.

She had borne Wang the Second three sons and two daughters.

All three sons were accomplished; both daughters had made marriages that others envied...

This was the true reason why—after being reborn—she had staked everything to snatch the Wang family's betrothal away from her.

Wang the Second could have any number of women in the future. But as long as the children she bore were outstanding, that was her greatest security!

Just like her own grandmother, Old Madam Qin.

She had given birth to such a capable and accomplished son, her father—and had lived as a gloriously wealthy senior consort for most of her life.

And yet her grandmother had only started out as a concubine who clawed her way up.

She herself was marrying into the Wang family as a proper daughter of a good family. Under her own scheming, her dowry was already several times larger than what it had been in her previous life.

Wang the Second was pursuing an official career—he would certainly not be able to do without her support.

If she bore Wang the Second three noble sons and two noble daughters—her life would surely exceed even her grandmother's, and surpass the previous life's Sixth Young Miss by far!

"Fifth Sister?" The Seventh Young Miss saw Qin Ruyue's expression—half smiling, half pleased, peculiarly strange—and frowned: "Why have you gone quiet?"

"Oh... nothing. I was thinking about Sixth Sister." Qin Ruyue's face grew a shade more solemn, as if concerned for Qin Rujin.

"You asked why Sixth Sister's future wasn't good. I can't tell you the details—what I can tell you is that my father and my mother's family have broad connections... We have our own methods."

The Seventh Young Miss naturally did not believe her.

Qin Ruyue continued: "The main issue is that the Jiang family's situation isn't looking good in the years ahead... Sixth Sister is marrying into the Jiang family—she will suffer greatly!"

The Seventh Young Miss's heart contracted sharply. Even Qin Ruyue was saying this!

So the part of her nightmare about the Jiang family's calamity... could it truly be coming?

But why? If the nightmare was something that had truly happened, then it should have been Qin Ruyue who married into the Jiang family, and Sixth Sister who married into the Wang family!

Thinking of the Wang family...

The Seventh Young Miss recalled the loathsome and vicious Wang family of her nightmare.

Seeing her complexion worsen, Qin Ruyue gave a cold inward laugh.

But she put on a look of concern: "Seventh Young Sister, there's no need to worry too much on Sixth Sister's behalf... After all, things haven't happened yet—there is still time to make things right."

The Seventh Young Miss came back to herself and followed the thread: "Then... Fifth Sister, tell me how to make it right?"

"I told you before—you must marry into Prince An's household!" Seeing the anger rising in the Seventh Young Miss's face, she quickly moved to soothe her.

"Listen to Fifth Sister—Fifth Sister isn't trying to degrade you by sending you to be a concubine... In truth, you and everyone else have misunderstood my mother and my elder brother."

"They had received advance word that the Jiang family was heading for calamity. But since Lord Jiang was already engaged to Sixth Sister, breaking off the engagement wasn't an option—so there was no other way but to arrange for you to marry into Prince An's household..."

The Seventh Young Miss's face went cold: "What use would my marrying into Prince An's household be? Would it keep Sixth Sister from suffering alongside the Jiang family?"

Qin Ruyue smoothed a strand of hair behind her ear and said earnestly: "Seventh Young Sister, listen carefully! I happened to learn a great secret...

Prince An will definitely rise to great heights in the future! As long as you win Prince An's favor—for Sixth Sister's sake—and speak a few good words on behalf of Lord Jiang to the Prince, the Jiang family's ill fate can be undone."

The Seventh Young Miss nearly couldn't keep herself from laughing in Qin Ruyue's face.

In order to probe out more, she still held herself back, shook her head slightly, and said to Qin Ruyue with a face full of disbelief:

"Fifth Sister speaks in such mysterious riddles. If it were truly that simple, that would be wonderful!

Even as a girl of the inner quarters, I know the present Emperor is a wise ruler who established the Crown Prince early, and that all the princes are wise and capable... How exactly would Prince An rise to such heights?"

And besides—did Qin Ruyue have that kind of good heart?

Their Second Branch had always wanted to see the First Branch come to ruin, always wanted the First Branch to stay forever beaten down.

How could they possibly be forcing her into Prince An's household as a concubine for the purpose of undoing the Sixth Young Miss's ill fate?

Even supposing she went to Prince An's household as a concubine—on what basis did the Second Branch family presume she could win Prince An's favor?

Qin Ruyue was truly treating her like a fool!

No matter.

She didn't mind being treated like a fool.

But the lie Qin Ruyue was spinning had far too many holes...

Qin Ruyue was momentarily at a loss.

She couldn't quite patch up the story anymore.

After all, she hadn't anticipated that the Seventh Young Miss would suddenly become so sharp.

"Right—Fifth Sister. Originally, it was you who were meant to marry into the Jiang family, and Sixth Sister who was meant to marry the Wang family. Why did you switch the engagements?"

"Could it be... that you and your Second Branch had already learned long ago that the Jiang family would soon fall into disaster, while Prince An would rise to great heights?"

"And besides—I don't believe your Second Branch, or you, Fifth Sister, would have any real intention of preventing Sixth Sister from falling into trouble just to force me into Prince An's household as a concubine."

"Your Second Branch has always been suppressing the First Branch—that's been no secret for a long time."

"Fifth Sister—if you don't explain all of this to me clearly and in full, I will never agree to it!" The Seventh Young Miss's brow creased, and the determination in her gaze steadily hardened.

"Besides—I am now a legitimate daughter of the First Branch. By the Qin family's rules, legitimate daughters are not to become concubines. You can no longer coerce me."

chapters.title: So This Was What Rujin's Previous Life Had Been
chapters.content:
Qin Ruyue nearly lost her composure and erupted.

What was happening?!

How was it that once a person became part of the First Branch, even a fool became sharp and difficult to handle?

Qin Ruyue pressed her brows together and drew a slow, deep breath.

She could not tell the Seventh Young Miss that she had been reborn.

Nor could she say she could have prophetic dreams.

All she could do was keep pointing to her father's and brothers' connections and her maternal grandfather's family's extensive network.

The Seventh Young Miss had no way to verify that.

After all, she had only dreamed a long nightmare—she wasn't truly reborn as Qin Ruyue had been.

Since she couldn't extract anything more about Qin Ruyue's strange nature by probing, the Seventh Young Miss no longer wished to waste her energy on the woman.

No matter how earnestly Qin Ruyue tried to persuade her, the Seventh Young Miss simply refused to take the bait.

When pressed too hard, she said: go find the clan council and tell them to change the family rules—let legitimate Qin daughters become concubines.

As for that Prince An...

In her nightmare, he had been a genuine demon—a true monster in human form!

In the nightmare, both she and Sixth Sister had been caged by that demon for the rest of their lives, unable even to die if they wished...

Now, the mere mention of Prince An made her shudder from head to toe. How could she ever agree to become his concubine?

She would sooner die than do it!

Qin Ruyue, rebuffed at every turn by the Seventh Young Miss until she was practically rolling her eyes, felt pain shooting through her chest from every direction.

"Seventh Young Sister—even setting Sixth Sister aside, even just for the sake of the family, for the sake of your Eighth Young Sister, you should enter Prince An's household. After all, the Prince truly has a genuine affection for you!"

"How does Fifth Sister know Prince An genuinely cares for me? I've never even met him. And I'd think the Prince hasn't met me either—it's not as if I'm like Fifth Sister, who never lacked for chances to attend flower gatherings and banquets..."

Qin Ruyue could only say: "Do you remember last year in the eighth month, when our grandmother took all the young ladies of our household to the Dalin Temple for a ritual prayer service?"

"That was when Prince An was also present, and he happened to see all of us Qin sisters..."

The Seventh Young Miss did remember—it had been one of the few times she and the Eighth Young Miss were allowed to go out.

But she didn't believe a word of what Qin Ruyue was saying.

She immediately pushed back: "Prince An is a son of Heaven's own blood—how could he take notice of someone like me? My looks aren't exceptional, my stature isn't striking, and I'm illegitimate-born."

"If he noticed anyone, he would notice a great beauty like Fifth Sister!"

Qin Ruyue nearly choked on something sweet rushing into her throat.

She was nearly spitting blood—but still she had to endure.

Privately, she thought: well, at least you have a little self-awareness.

Of course—she had already extracted the relevant information from her elder brother. On that occasion, what Prince An had taken notice of was indeed not this thin, plain-featured, merely-above-average Seventh Young Miss.

What Prince An had noticed was Qin Sixth Young Miss!

And fate had its ironies—Prince An had hinted to her brother several times that he was interested in the girl in the Qin family with the most beautiful pair of phoenix eyes...

Yet two of the Qin family's young ladies happened to have beautiful upturned phoenix eyes.

Those two were Qin Sixth Young Miss and the Seventh Young Miss.

In terms of the most beautiful phoenix eyes—the Seventh Young Miss's face, nose, and brows were far inferior to those of the Sixth Young Miss. But those phoenix eyes of hers were more steeply upturned than the Sixth Young Miss's.

Which made them more bewitching.

Her elder brother had mistakenly assumed Prince An meant the Seventh Young Miss—creating this enormous misunderstanding, this enormous catastrophe.

One that was then seized upon by Jiang Jiuxiao, nearly destroying the Qin Second Branch entirely...

But she couldn't possibly tell the Seventh Young Miss this truth.

All she could do was let the error stand.

As in the previous life—first get the Seventh Young Miss into Prince An's household.

Then use the Seventh Young Miss to gain access to Prince An. As long as that connection was established, the Second Branch of the Qin family would have nothing left to fear.

In the future, she would also use the secrets she had from her previous life to help Prince An take the path to regency earlier...

Perhaps, with luck on her side, she could even help Prince An take that ultimate seat of power.

If that happened—the merit of being instrumental in a dynasty's founding would be hers!

With a merit that great, wouldn't the Wang family raise her to the heavens?

Her standing in her husband's household would be unshakeable by anyone!

And her own family would raise her to the heavens as well—and meekly serve as her solid backing!

Qin Ruyue creased her brow, looking at the Seventh Young Miss with an air of strong disagreement: "How can Seventh Young Sister speak so poorly of herself? If you're not beautiful, then there aren't many beauties left in the world!"

"Our family does have the rule that legitimate daughters are not to become concubines—but it depends whose concubine one is becoming. To be the beloved concubine of Prince An, with his title and his royal blood—that is far more dignified than being the principal wife of even the greatest noble families!"

The Seventh Young Miss let out a quiet sigh: "Since being Prince An's concubine is so wonderful, let Fifth Sister have that honor."

She seemed calm on the surface, but inwardly she was churning with turbulent feeling.

Some of what Qin Ruyue had said did connect to certain things in her nightmare...

In the nightmare, Sixth Sister had indeed been noticed by Prince An at that visit to Dalin Temple.

Only—the reason Prince An had initially noticed Sixth Sister had nothing to do with her beauty.

It was because Sixth Sister's birth characters were exceptionally propitious for him.

But he could not take Sixth Sister as his concubine. And later, he had developed a twisted and frenzied obsession with Sixth Sister—yet could not make her his woman.

Because an exceptionally powerful and extraordinarily evil daoist sorcerer had calculated that only Sixth Sister, kept in her maidenly purity, could truly bring him good fortune.

If he disregarded that and made Sixth Sister his woman, not only would it break the auspicious fate she held for him—it would trigger a severe spiritual backlash against him, costing him his very life.

That selfish, evil demon could not and dared not risk that!

And in the nightmare, she herself—who shared those same steeply upturned phoenix eyes as Sixth Sister—had become his substitute...

She hadn't dared die, and Sixth Sister equally hadn't dared die.

That man had threatened them both with the lives of every member of the Qin First Branch—dozens of people—and every member of the Qin Third Branch—more than a dozen more...

"Fifth Sister—there's no need to say any more. I've already died once. Dying a second time holds nothing frightening for me."

Qin Ruyue: "......"

She would endure.

There would be time yet.

She simply refused to believe she couldn't get control of a mere little Seventh Young Miss!

* * *

Watching Qin Ruyue fling her sleeve and leave, the Seventh Young Miss immediately called Jiang Yue to her side and asked her to fetch only Sixth Sister.

"Seventh Young Sister—are you all right?" Qin Rujin saw the Seventh Young Miss's small face pale, and took her hand.

She said gently: "You've only just woken up, and you've already been talking with Fifth Sister for so long—you must be tired. Rest first and get your strength back. When you feel better, I'll come and stay with you."

But the Seventh Young Miss gripped Qin Rujin's hand in urgent alarm: "Sixth Sister—don't go! I'm not tired. I have something important to tell you!"

Before Qin Rujin could speak, the Seventh Young Miss launched in at speed.

She told Qin Rujin her long nightmare from beginning to end.

After Qin Rujin heard it all, she sank into a long silence.

"Sixth Sister—the Fifth Young Miss definitely has a very serious problem!"

"What she said to me, though she kept it deeply hidden, I could still feel it—what she said connects to certain things from my nightmare..."

The Seventh Young Miss held nothing back from Qin Rujin.

At this moment, Qin Rujin's own heart was also in turmoil.

What kind of luck did the Qin family have!

One who had transmigrated—herself.

One who had been reborn—Qin Ruyue.

And now a third—the Seventh Young Miss, who had lived through a complete nightmare of her entire previous life.

Of course, she was beginning to understand now why she had transmigrated into Qin Sixth Young Miss's body...

If the original Qin Sixth Young Miss had been reborn, as Qin Ruyue had been, her chances of changing the fate of her previous life were vanishingly slim.

But then she had come here instead. And with Qin Ruyue also reborn, and the Seventh Young Miss having accidentally dreamed a complete version of her previous life through her near-death, things had taken on an exquisitely different shape.

Through the Seventh Young Miss's dream and Qin Ruyue's identity as a reborn soul, Qin Rujin confirmed that the Seventh Young Miss's dream was the true experience of the original Qin Sixth Young Miss in her previous life.

"In my nightmare, the Jiang family was ruined in just a few years—all set in motion by that Prince An, who directed his henchmen to destroy them!

Sixth Sister—you cannot marry into the Jiang family!" The Seventh Young Miss was, after all, a young girl who had lived through little.

The solution she could think of to help Sixth Sister avoid the calamity was simply: Sixth Sister must not marry into the Jiang family.

"Fifth Sister also said the Jiang family would fall into disaster in a few years—at least the part about the Jiang family's impending ruin should be true!"

The Seventh Young Miss was nearly in tears: "Sixth Sister—I'll go with you to find the First Master. No... go find Father. Ask Father to find a way to break off your engagement to the Jiang family!"

Qin Rujin snapped back to herself and placed both hands firmly on the Seventh Young Miss's shoulders.

Her expression was dead serious.

"Seventh Young Sister! Listen to me—do not tell anyone else about this dream of yours. No one—except me. Do you understand?"

The Seventh Young Miss froze: "Not even... not even Father?"

"Not him either. Not now, at least." Qin Rujin was decisive.

Afraid she wouldn't take it seriously enough, she continued gravely: "Right now, if word got out that you'd had a dream like that—if it spread—people might take you for a witch or a demon, and your life would truly be in danger!"

Only then did the Seventh Young Miss feel genuine fear.

"But... but if the dream is real, and what happened in it really does come to pass... what will become of you, Sixth Sister?

And as for me... I would rather die than go be that monster's concubine!"

"Seventh Young Sister—calm yourself! Whether or not events will follow the course of your dream, at least for now you have not been sent to Prince An's household by the Second Branch as in your nightmare."

"And the family I am marrying into is the Jiang family—not the Wang family."

At the mention of the Wang family, Qin Rujin gave a cold smile.

From what the Seventh Young Miss had dreamed—the Wang family had handed the original Rujin over to Prince An.

Prince An had then found a woman who slightly resembled Rujin and sent her to Wang the Second.

And Wang the Second had shamefully and brazenly treated that woman of unknown origin as Qin Sixth Young Miss—and then impudently pressured the Qin First Branch to acknowledge her as such.

The Qin Ruyue of that previous life must not have known about this.

Otherwise, she would not have—after being reborn into this life—made snatching Wang the Second her very first act...

With the Seventh Young Miss's dream about the previous life, many things could be avoided. For what couldn't be avoided, ways could be found in advance.

She was not going to let the Seventh Young Miss tell anyone else about this dream—but she herself needed to tell one person.

That person was Jiang Jiuxiao.

And she also needed to ask Jiang Jiuxiao to send people to protect the Seventh Young Miss.

"Seventh Young Sister—I promise you. I will do everything in my power to make sure neither of us falls into the fate you dreamed."

"First, focus on recovering. After that—I'll handle things!"

* * *

With a plan forming in her mind, after impressing the warning on the Seventh Young Miss three more times, Qin Rujin left Jiang Yue behind to protect her, and returned to her own courtyard with Juhong and the others.

The moment she was back, she called for Matron Feng.

After giving her instructions—

Matron Feng looked at her young mistress in astonishment: "Miss—your great wedding is the day after tomorrow. By custom, in the days before the wedding, the bride-to-be is not to meet with the groom-to-be."

Afraid Qin Rujin had misunderstood her, Matron Feng quickly explained: "Lord Jiang will certainly be willing to see you, Miss—it's just that according to custom... it could disrupt the auspicious energy."

"The matter is urgent—there's no time to worry about rules and customs." Qin Rujin's gaze was resolute.

She had to see Jiang Jiuxiao in person, and as soon as possible!

chapters.title: A Meeting with Lord Jiang Before the Wedding
chapters.content:
Since it was her young mistress's order, Matron Feng dared not be slow about it.

At the Jiang residence.

Matron Feng sent someone in person to see Jiang Jiuxiao.

"The Sixth Young Miss wants to see me again?" Jiang Jiuxiao pressed his fingers to his brow, and the corner of his mouth curved slightly upward. "Has something happened?"

Standing beside him, Li Yi thought: it absolutely cannot have. If anything had happened on the Sixth Young Miss's side, he would have heard about it long ago and already reported it to his master.

The person Matron Feng had sent immediately replied: "In reply to my lord—nothing has happened on the Sixth Young Miss's side. Matron Feng only said the Sixth Young Miss has an urgent matter and wishes to see my lord once!"

"At a time like this..." Jiang Jiuxiao's left hand fingers curved and began tapping the edge of the table, one knock at a time.

"Li Yi." Jiang Jiuxiao spoke.

Li Yi immediately stepped forward with a bow: "Your servant is here!"

"Make arrangements—tonight I'll receive the Sixth Young Miss at the house I recently purchased." Jiang Jiuxiao instructed.

Li Yi's heart gave a start. The house the master had recently bought was a secret even from the Old Madam. Only Xu the eldest young master knew of it—he had personally handled the purchase.

And my lord was going to receive the Sixth Young Miss directly at the new house?

"Go and tell Matron Feng—have her prepare everything carefully and make sure no one learns that the Sixth Young Miss came to see me tonight."

"Yes, my lord!"

Li Yi then stepped forward respectfully and asked: "My lord—you haven't yet taken your evening meal. Shall you eat first and then leave?"

Jiang Jiuxiao gave a small wave of his hand: "No need."

He thought for a moment and added: "Bring along the Yuntian loquats His Majesty bestowed today."

Li Yi froze: "My lord—the Yuntian loquats His Majesty bestowed on you today were all sent to the Old Madam's courtyard."

Jiang Jiuxiao's brow furrowed slightly: "Go to the Old Madam's courtyard yourself and tell her I'm meeting a friend this evening and I'd like to bring half a jin of the Yuntian loquats."

Li Yi: "......"

He rather wanted to say: my lord, these first-ripened Yuntian loquats were sent up to the capital as tribute—there were only so many. His Majesty bestowed just one jin on you... and you already sent them to the Old Madam's courtyard... and now you want to take some back... is that really appropriate?

"Anything else?" Seeing him still rooted to the spot, Jiang Jiuxiao raised an eyebrow with displeasure.

Li Yi's heart clenched. He quickly acknowledged the order.

Old Madam Jiang had just been about to have someone wash the loquats His Majesty had bestowed and bring them out to eat.

With so many people in the household and so few loquats, there was no plan to distribute them. After all—divided unevenly, better not to divide at all.

Then she saw Li Yi come hurrying over, and she was puzzled.

When she heard his reason for coming, she frowned.

"He hasn't even had his evening meal? And he wants to take half a jin of the loquats His Majesty bestowed? Who is so honored?"

Li Yi absolutely dared not say!

His eyes swiveled wildly, not daring to exhale.

But the Old Madam was a very reasonable old woman. Seeing that Li Yi didn't dare speak, she didn't press him.

She smiled: "Well then, take them all. After all, I'm old—my teeth aren't good, and tart and sweet things tend to set my teeth on edge."

Emboldened, Li Yi immediately bowed and said: "Old Madam—my lord said half a jin, so half a jin it is. These were originally given to you. For my lord to ask you to part with them is already embarrassing enough."

The Old Madam gave an amused sound: "You're a clever talker. Very well—just take the half jin then. The rest stays as your master's act of filial devotion to this old lady."

Li Yi successfully made off with half a jin of Yuntian loquats, and breathed a great sigh of relief.

Thinking for a moment, he sent someone to find a beautifully made bamboo-woven fruit basket...

After the evening meal, Qin Rujin—under Matron Feng's careful escort—stepped into a carriage waiting in the back courtyard.

"Matron Feng—did anyone see me leave?" Qin Rujin asked quietly once she had settled into the carriage.

"Miss, rest easy. This old servant made all the arrangements herself. Not even Zisu and the other maids know that Miss has already left the household."

Qin Rujin gave a quiet nod.

She was also deeply grateful that she had not been concerned about the rules and had accepted the people Jiang Jiuxiao had secretly sent her.

Otherwise, slipping out of the Qin household after dinner would have been genuinely difficult.

The carriage was perfectly smooth the whole way—which told Qin Rujin the coachman was also Jiang Jiuxiao's person.

It made her feel even more at ease.

Matron Feng was quietly watching her young mistress.

She saw only a calm and composed bearing, not the slightest hint of anxiety. She felt a quiet admiration.

No wonder her master looked upon this young lady with such regard.

She thought to herself—it seemed that going forward, the four of them who had been sent to serve this young lady would truly be following her lead in all things.

With that thought, the way she looked at this Sixth Young Miss became even more respectful.

"Miss—we've arrived." Matron Feng noted quietly. "This old servant will help you down."

As she spoke, she took the sky-blue cape with white fox-fur trim she had prepared for Qin Rujin and stepped down from the carriage first.

Qin Rujin asked nothing and said nothing. Seeing Matron Feng's hand appear at the carriage curtain, she stood and placed her hand into it.

After helping her down, Matron Feng nimbly fitted the hood on her head and draped the cape over her shoulders.

As she guided her by the hand, Matron Feng said quietly: "Miss, please be at ease. Follow this old servant inside—Lord Jiang is waiting for you within."

Qin Rujin gave a quiet nod.

Her instincts told her—Jiang Jiuxiao was that kind of truly upright gentleman. He would not disappoint her.

She was perfectly at ease.

Matron Feng led her for a long time.

Past the front courtyard, winding and turning—truly nine bends and eighteen curves...

Even Matron Feng was a little worried she'd be too tired to walk.

Matron Feng was quietly muttering to herself.

She had originally assumed the master would receive the young lady in the study in the front courtyard where he saw guests.

She hadn't expected him to be waiting in the rear courtyard's main suite instead.

The house was newly bought, with no servants yet installed inside—otherwise she'd have had a litter chair ready for the young lady.

Qin Rujin didn't feel tired in the slightest.

Women in the Ying dynasty didn't have their feet bound, and ever since she had arrived in this body, she had eaten more generously than the original Rujin.

On top of that, her mother Madam Li had spared no effort preparing nourishing supplements to help her reach her first menstrual cycle before the wedding.

Her blood and vital energy were now in excellent health—and when the vital energy was good, the body was naturally strong.

Unfortunately, her first cycle had not yet come.

That was inherited. Madam Li herself hadn't had hers until she was eighteen—her eldest sister and second sister had both been seventeen. And Qin Rujin was only sixteen this year...

"My lord—Matron Feng has accompanied the Sixth Young Miss here." Li Yi stepped forward to report to Jiang Jiuxiao, who was propping his chin with one hand and deep in thought.

Jiang Jiuxiao glanced outside.

In the warm, amber glow of the red lanterns, Matron Feng supported a girl from a distance—a hood of dusty pink, a cape of sky-blue, strikingly and brilliantly beautiful—as she walked toward him from far away.

"Was the journey smooth?" Jiang Jiuxiao asked.

Li Yi misunderstood, assuming his master was impatient that the Sixth Young Miss had arrived late.

He took it upon himself to explain: "My lord—the house is rather large. The Sixth Young Miss must have grown tired from the walk, which is why she arrived a little late."

Jiang Jiuxiao's brow contracted: "You didn't arrange for a few people to carry a litter chair to meet her?"

Li Yi wished he could give himself a firm slap.

Talk too much!

"Dock three months' wages." Jiang Jiuxiao said, his expression blank. "You're dismissed."

Li Yi felt as though reprieved from execution.

Only three months' docked wages—a lucky escape!

It wasn't as if he lived on his wages anyway.

Besides—last time he had done the Sixth Young Miss a service, she had waved her hand and rewarded him a hundred taels.

It had made all his fellow servants green with envy.

As long as he showed more thoughtfulness on the Sixth Young Miss's behalf in the future, he would earn not only her rewards but occasional ones from his master as well.

Only—this time he had to be sharper!

"My lord—shall your servant take the Yuntian loquats to be washed, to refresh the Sixth Young Miss after her walk?" Li Yi pressed his luck and said one more thing.

"Mm." Jiang Jiuxiao waved him off. "Go ahead."

Seeing his master had agreed, Li Yi knew he'd hit the right note.

Qin Rujin was helped into the room by Matron Feng.

She didn't look around—she only looked at the man sitting upright as a pine in the master's chair.

The original Rujin had very fine manners—but for some reason, when Qin Rujin herself performed a curtsy, it came out rather careless. Not that she did it deliberately.

Jiang Jiuxiao watched her and found it somewhat amusing. He raised a hand to cover his mouth, hiding the upward curve of his lips.

"Please sit. It is my failing—I didn't think the people below would be so thoughtless, and had you walk so far. You must be tired."

The man looked at her with clear, tranquil eyes. His words were considerate, but entirely without romantic intent.

Qin Rujin liked it exactly that way.

This easy, friendly manner of interaction—it kept her from feeling any awkwardness.

"My health is very good. A walk like this is nothing." Qin Rujin smiled brightly at him.

The girl's face was strikingly beautiful—and with that smile, those upturned phoenix eyes became even more bewitching.

Jiang Jiuxiao was caught off guard for a moment.

He thought: this girl truly had an unusual boldness—how could she smile so openly and unguardedly at a man?

Then he caught himself. Hadn't he known all along that this girl had that boldness? She had come to negotiate the betrothal gifts with her own future husband after their engagement.

And now, three days before the wedding, she was coming to see him in person.

He really had no idea what curious ideas she would come up with next...

Li Yi came in personally carrying the washed Yuntian loquats.

At Jiang Jiuxiao's gesture, he respectfully placed them on the small red-sandalwood table beside Qin Rujin.

"These are this year's newly presented Yuntian loquats. His Majesty bestowed one jin on me—I've brought some for you to taste."

Jiang Jiuxiao saw the delight she couldn't hide, and the corner of his lips curved again: "Try one—this variety is more sweet than tart."

He imagined a girl of her age would enjoy that.

Qin Rujin was desperately missing the flavor of fruits—so juicy and wonderfully sweet.

She hadn't expected that in the Ying dynasty, in what was essentially the third lunar month, loquats were already available.

Unfortunately, these were imperial tribute. Apart from the imperial family, no amount of silver could buy them.

She thanked Jiang Jiuxiao and, without any coyness or pretense, actually started eating.

She was already here with Jiang Jiuxiao—having a few good things to eat before getting down to business was surely fine.

She ate five or six in a row before it occurred to her that Jiang Jiuxiao hadn't eaten any.

"That... would you like some, Lord Jiang?"

There were only about a dozen in total.

Clearly she adored them—and yet she was still thinking of him.

Jiang Jiuxiao's eyes softened with a smile: "They're all for you. Eat slowly—there's no rush. Whatever you have to say can wait until you've finished."

Well!

She was an unabashed lover of good food. They would be husband and wife—even if there were no feelings between them, they'd still be seeing each other daily.

There was truly no need to put on any kind of act in front of him.

"I do so love a fruit with plenty of juice—both tart and sweet!" She tilted her head back and smiled at him brightly. "I've made a spectacle of myself before Lord Jiang."

Go ahead and smile.

She didn't mind.

"Mm?" Jiang Jiuxiao looked at her with a faint curiosity: "Fruit?"

Qin Rujin's heart gave a little start. But her mind reacted quickly: "Oh—I like to call juicy fruits 'fruit.' "

"I see..." Jiang Jiuxiao heard her explanation and didn't dwell on it.

This pure and artlessly charming girl—what cunning could she possibly have?

Qin Rujin was nothing if not honest. She actually finished the entire half-jin of Yuntian loquats—fortunately she hadn't eaten much at dinner, or she might have burst.

Li Yi, with his excellent sense of timing, brought in a copper basin of warm water and handed it to Matron Feng.

Matron Feng gave him an approving glance, then drew the snow-white cotton cloth from the basin, wrung it out, and wiped Qin Rujin's hands.

"Lord Jiang." Qin Rujin looked directly at the man sitting upright as a pine before her. "Sixth Young Miss comes to consult you on a truly urgent matter—that is why she has acted so presumptuously tonight..."

Jiang Jiuxiao raised a hand to stop her and said gently: "I know. I don't think the Sixth Young Miss was being presumptuous at all. Please speak freely."

chapters.title: Lord Jiang—Do You Believe What I've Told You?
chapters.content:
An upright gentleman, like the sun high above the clouds.

Not the slightest impatience.

Not the slightest dismissiveness.

Qin Rujin smiled again and said a simple "Good."

"Lord Jiang—you have seen a great deal of the world. Have you ever heard of someone who dreamed of the experiences they lived through in a previous life?"

She needed to first gauge how receptive Jiang Jiuxiao was to things of a mystical nature.

If his threshold was low, she would have to take a more roundabout approach and recount what had befallen the Jiang family in the previous life.

If it was high—so much the better.

Whatever Jiang Jiuxiao had expected her to ask, it was not this.

Thinking about it again, he realized he had once more misjudged her.

A glimmer of interest rose in his eyes. He said calmly: "Speaking of such things, they border on the uncanny and the supernatural—yet the world is full of such things."

"...It is not so strange that someone might have this experience." But the moment those words left him, his handsome eyes narrowed.

Could it be—that the outcome the eminent monk Huiqing had divined was actually manifesting through this young girl?

He immediately grew cautious.

He had Li Yi and Matron Feng withdraw from the room.

Seeing him take such care, Qin Rujin was a little bewildered.

"Sixth Young Miss—is it you who dreamed of your own previous life?" Jiang Jiuxiao's dark eyes were deep and still, like the sea.

Seeing he had misunderstood, Qin Rujin quickly shook her head.

Time was short, and she had no chance to explain further. She simply told him what the Seventh Young Miss had dreamed—what had befallen the Jiang family in the previous life.

After Jiang Jiuxiao heard it, his handsome eyes were as if draped in a fog so deep it would not dissolve.

"Speaking of it—it is indeed very hard to believe. But better to believe it than not... Please, Lord Jiang, be on guard against His Highness Prince An!"

"I cannot linger outside for long. Sixth Young Miss takes her leave, Lord Jiang." Qin Rujin rose, gave a curtsy, and was about to go.

"Wait!" Jiang Jiuxiao also rose and walked to Qin Rujin's side. He pressed one hand to her shoulder, and had her sit back down.

"Trust me—no matter how late you return to the Qin household tonight, no one will ever know."

Qin Rujin looked at him.

Was he saying... he believed what she had told him about the Jiang family's previous life fate?

Just like that, he believed her?

If he truly believed that easily, she found it a little hard to believe.

A thought turning in her mind, Qin Rujin asked him: "Lord Jiang—do you believe what I told you?"

"I do!" He looked at her with absolute certainty, her clear reflection the only thing in his eyes.

How could he not believe her?

The eminent monk Huiqing had divined that the Jiang family faced a great calamity years ago.

For these past years, Huiqing—at the cost of damage to his own spiritual cultivation—had been persistently searching for a way to dissolve the calamity for the Jiang family.

Only a few months ago had he felt his way to a faint and indistinct path...

And now she had come to tell him that someone had dreamed a previous life, and in that dream was a detailed account of how the Jiang family had suffered.

Only now did he understand—this was the true method for dissolving the Jiang family's calamity!

The hidden hand behind the Jiang family's great ruin was Prince An...

From here on, it was a contest of who had the greater skill.

"I've told you everything I know." Qin Rujin, mistaking his silence for wanting more, spread her hands.

"Sixth Young Miss—the dream truly wasn't one you had yourself?"

"If it was you... you need not be frightened..."

"With me here, I absolutely will not let a single thing harm you. Only—besides me, you must never tell another soul!"

Seeing him so grave and earnest in both his promise and his warning, Qin Rujin felt a weight lift from her heart.

"It truly was not my dream." Qin Rujin's expression also grew solemn. "I can tell Lord Jiang who it was—only I also want to ask you to swear an oath: you must not harm this person, and you must send people to protect them!"

"If Lord Jiang cannot promise this..." Qin Rujin gave a cold laugh and pointed upward at the heavens. "Lord Jiang knows the principle that the net of Heaven is vast and its meshes fine—nothing escapes it."

Jiang Jiuxiao nodded gravely, raised his right hand with four fingers pointed to the sky, and swore a clean, unhesitating oath.

If the first time she had risked everything to see him had been for her own sake—this time she had risked everything to see him for him. For the Jiang family.

She was the Jiang family's great benefactress!

And the person she wanted to protect was equally so!

Protecting her and that person was, to begin with, his and the Jiang family's obligation!

This girl—even if he would never come to love her in this life—of one thing he was absolutely certain:

He, Jiang Jiuxiao, would spend this entire lifetime protecting her.

And he would protect that dreamer as well.

And yet—if it had not been for this girl, even had that person dreamed that dream, the Jiang family's calamity would likely still be very difficult to dissolve...

He always knew very clearly what was primary and what was secondary.

Qin Rujin told him who had dreamed the dream.

Jiang Jiuxiao showed no surprise upon hearing it.

The news that the Seventh Young Miss of the Qin family had fallen into a daze after her near-death was naturally known to him.

From a young age, he had followed the eminent monk Huiqing—and not only to study martial arts and Buddhist teachings.

There were many things most people would not believe and had never experienced—but he knew of them...

Otherwise, even if he himself believed Huiqing, his mother would not.

He had also informed his mother in the Jiang household that the Jiang family faced a great calamity...

* * *

That night, Jiang Jiuxiao personally escorted Qin Rujin home.

By the time Qin Rujin stepped out of the carriage, the alley outside the Qin household's back gate was so quiet that not even the shadow of a night watchman could be seen.

After the back gate was knocked and opened, she entered smoothly. Along the entire way back there were only the people Matron Feng had arranged to receive her.

Not until she was back in her own courtyard did Qin Rujin finally breathe easily.

Jiang Jiuxiao had promised her in person: he would send the four most formidable women fighters among his people, disguised as maids and matrons, to serve at the Seventh Young Miss's side.

If the Seventh Young Miss wished to marry in the future, the Jiang family would take responsibility for finding her the most suitable match—one she herself was willing to accept.

However, she had not told him about the original Rujin's experiences in her previous life.

Perhaps the original Rujin's soul was still somewhere, influencing her—not wanting her to speak of what the original Rujin had lived through to too many people...

Of course, he hadn't asked either.

Perhaps it simply hadn't occurred to him.

She could understand that.

As the pillar of a family, what he cared about first and foremost was naturally the family's very survival.

She had people he had arranged to protect her around her already. Three days from now she would be married into his household.

Prince An, however crafty his methods, could not in the current situation seize her and cage her in his household.

After all, the reigning Emperor was still firmly on the Dragon Throne—Prince An did not yet dare show so much as the tip of an ear.

And according to the timeline of the Seventh Young Miss's dream, Prince An at this point still didn't know that it was the original Rujin whose birth characters were auspicious for him.

For now, she was safe.

Jiang Jiuxiao, in order to dissolve the Jiang family's calamity, would certainly move against Prince An. As long as Prince An was brought down, neither she nor the Seventh Young Miss would need to live in constant fear.

With that great worry resolved, Qin Rujin slept exceptionally well that night.

She was still being woken by Matron Feng in the morning.

To keep close watch over her, Matron Feng had taken over the duties of her senior maids and was now attending her side day and night.

"Miss—please get up quickly. The First Master's mother's family have arrived, and the First Mistress has sent word—she asks you to come to her rooms as soon as you're up. Your maternal granduncles' wives... they've all arrived."

Qin Rujin was instantly wide awake.

She sat up in bed in one swift movement.

"The maternal granduncles' wives of the Xianyang Wei family are here?"

Matron Feng smiled and nodded.

Though she had only just recently come to serve beside this young lady and was not yet entirely familiar with the Qin household, she had her own methods for learning a great deal that the Qin family's masters themselves might not know.

For instance—the Xianyang Wei family making such a large show of sending so many people to the capital this time was not solely to see the Sixth Young Miss of the Qin family married off...

Qin Rujin also understood that in an instant.

chapters.title: The Wei Family Mobilizes the Entire Clan to Back the First Branch
chapters.content:
She thought for just a moment, then asked: "Matron Feng—it's not only my granduncles' wives who have arrived in the capital—my granduncles are here as well, aren't they?"

Matron Feng nodded repeatedly: "Miss has guessed correctly—and then some. A great many people have come from Xianyang, Miss. Your great-uncles' wives, your second great-aunt, your third great-aunt, your fourth great-uncle and fourth great-aunt, and your sixth great-aunt as well."

What a turnout!

Qin Rujin asked no more—she quickly got out of bed to wash and dress.

Matron Feng, Juhong, and Banxia all helped her dress and groom.

With so many female elders from the family arriving, Qin Rujin had the maids dress her in festive, cheerful colors.

Elders liked that.

The Wei family's elder generation, the senior generation, and even those of the same generation had all turned out in force—traveling all that distance without complaint. They had come to back the First Branch and take on the Second Branch head-on.

Repaying them was not something that fell to her—a young woman about to be married. But at least she could show them proper warmth.

"Matron Feng—find some way to inquire among the Wei family's servants about everyone's food preferences. Whatever we can make or buy, we'll do our best to see to it."

After she was dressed and groomed, Qin Rujin gave the instructions.

Matron Feng smiled and acknowledged them.

She thought highly of her young mistress's thoughtfulness.

A small matter like this was nothing to her.

She had, after all, grown up as an intelligence operative.

Qin Rujin looked at herself in the bronze mirror, freshly dressed and groomed, and felt something was still missing.

"That's right—I recall that among the trousseau Father gave me, there was a rose-red garnet hairpin left behind by my own grandmother. Please find it."

The red-ruby hairpin already at her bun was lovely—but for this occasion, wearing her own grandmother's jewelry was even better!

Her father had once told her that though this rose-red garnet hairpin had not been of great value, it had been passed down to her grandmother from her grandmother's own mother.

When her own grandmother passed away, her grandmother's trousseau had fallen into her grandfather's hands, and had eventually ended up with Old Madam Qin.

Her grandfather, maintaining at least the pretense of virtue, had not dared keep every piece of grandmother's trousseau—so he had set aside the less valuable items and given them to her father.

When the children had grown up, her father had divided the pieces from grandmother's trousseau and given one portion each to the six of them, brothers and sisters alike.

Banxia was in charge of Qin Rujin's clothing and jewelry.

At those words, she immediately went to find it.

Matron Feng took out the rose-red garnet hairpin from the jewelry case.

It was well-preserved—only the style was of an older fashion from several decades ago.

She recognized at once that this was a piece with some history.

Of course, its monetary value was not especially high—at most worth about one hundred taels of silver.

So she asked with a smile: "Miss—this hairpin holds a special significance, doesn't it?"

Qin Rujin nodded: "It was part of my own grandmother's trousseau—Father gave it to me as a keepsake."

"Then wearing this hairpin today is absolutely the right choice!" Matron Feng smiled warmly in reply.

It was actually a piece from the young lady's own grandmother's trousseau. Those old ladies from the Wei family would likely recognize it the moment they laid eyes on it.

And the young lady's choosing to wear it today showed how much she valued the Wei elders.

* * *

Qin Rujin brought Matron Feng and Juhong to her mother Madam Li's courtyard.

The truth was, it wasn't that the Wei family elders had arrived especially early—she had slipped out to see Jiang Jiuxiao the night before, come back a little late, and gone to bed slightly later than usual. So she had woken later than her ordinary hour.

Going to greet the Wei family elders for the first time, she naturally had to first apologize for rising late.

None of the Wei family's elder women had ever met Qin Rujin before.

Seeing such a cheerfully and beautifully dressed young girl, they all broke into delighted praise at once.

As for her rising late, not a single elder took offense.

The First Mistress of the Wei family's First Branch even laughed and said: young girls should sleep in—it gave them a healthy complexion.

The First Mistress of the Wei family's First Branch was Qin the First Master's eldest maternal uncle's wife.

Qin Rujin was to address her as Great-Granduncle's Wife on the eldest side.

The Wei family elder women who had come this time were: the eldest granduncle and his wife, the second great-aunt, the third great-aunt, the fourth granduncle and his wife, and the sixth great-aunt.

The second granduncle had remained at Xianyang as the family's anchor.

The third granduncle and fifth granduncle and his wife had already passed away.

The sixth granduncle was away on official assignment and could not come.

So it was not an exaggeration to say that nearly the entire Wei clan had turned out.

Not to mention the many great-uncles, great-aunts, cousins, and cousins-by-marriage who had come as well.

The eldest Wei grandmother brought the Wei family women and gave Qin Rujin, the Seventh Young Miss, and the Eighth Young Miss their first-meeting gifts.

Then she took Qin Rujin's hands and looked her up and down with growing satisfaction.

When she noticed the rose-red garnet hairpin tucked beside her bun, the old woman's eyes immediately reddened.

She simply looked at Qin Rujin and said: "Good child! How thoughtful of you!"

The other great-aunts noticed it too. These old women were deeply sentimental.

Seeing this hairpin from their little sister-in-law's trousseau—they felt the pang of missing her, and the comfort of seeing Qin Rujin wearing it to greet them—it was a consolation to their hearts.

And Madam Li was wearing a garment that had also belonged to her own mother-in-law. The old women were comforted by all of this.

It showed them that the First Branch family valued and cherished the Xianyang Wei family—that they were not projecting affection onto people who didn't care.

It was worth every bit of the effort of hauling their aging bodies all the way to the capital.

The eldest Wei grandmother then pointed out the hairpin to the younger-generation Wei women, explaining to them that this hairpin had been passed down from her own mother-in-law to Qin Rujin's grandmother...

After that, the way the younger-generation Wei women looked at Qin Rujin was noticeably warmer than the polite formality of before.

Several of the Wei cousins slightly younger than Qin Rujin all smiled at her and nodded.

Qin Rujin smiled back and acknowledged each of them in turn.

Just as the warm and harmonious gathering was in full swing, a matron came from outside to report that Old Madam Qin had sent an invitation for the Wei family's eldest grandmother and her party to come to the Hall of Longevity and Peace.

Madam Li's brow immediately creased.

The eldest Wei grandmother then said to Madam Li: "Eldest niece-by-marriage, we have come to the Qin household as guests—she is the Qin family's senior grand matron, and we elders ought to go pay our respects to her."

Madam Li was aggrieved on behalf of her great-aunt and the others.

That concubine-turned-wife old woman—wouldn't she be in her element now, putting on airs and lording it over them?

The eldest Wei grandmother read Madam Li's expression and guessed what her eldest niece-by-marriage was thinking.

She smiled and said: "Eldest niece-by-marriage is feeling aggrieved on our behalf—we can all tell!

Only—this time we came not solely to see our Sixth Young Miss married. We were going to meet this woman face to face regardless. Since she's sent someone to invite us, we might as well go and see what she has to say."

Madam Li's face colored slightly in front of these all-seeing elders—but her heart leaped with joy.

At long last—the opportunity had come for the Wei family elders to come and stand behind her husband and herself!

"What Great-Aunt says is right. Only—you've all had a long journey, and you were up late in the inn last night..."

The eldest Wei grandmother waved her off with a smile: "No matter. Our Wei family has long been waiting for this day! Everyone has had their sleeves rolled up and ready—let's go meet that senior grand matron of yours."

The other Wei great-aunts also nodded cheerfully.

They had been waiting a long time for this!

"For now—Sixth Young Miss, take your younger sisters to your courtyard and keep them company for a while. Once we older ones have seen to our business, we'll call you all back for a chat." The eldest Wei grandmother looked at Qin Rujin with warm affection.

Qin Rujin understood—this was not her battlefield. What she could do was look after the Wei cousins, as well as the Seventh and Eighth Young Misses.

Madam Li led the Wei great-aunt party to the Hall of Longevity and Peace.

At the Hall, Old Madam Qin was waiting, battle-ready.

chapters.title: The Fifth Young Miss Resents Her Own Grandmother
chapters.content:
Ever since Madam Sun Wenlan's separation from her eldest grandson Qin Rong Gong, the Second Branch hadn't come out ahead in any way—and had even lost two legitimate grandsons...

It was shameful. It was humiliating!

She had been so furious she had fallen ill.

Even now, she was still feeling poorly.

And to make matters worse, her eyelid had been twitching nonstop since early this morning, and her heart was uneasy.

She had barely touched her morning meal before sending it away.

Not long after, Qin Ruyue came rushing in, white-faced, without even offering a greeting—and told her that a great many people had come from the Xianyang Wei family.

The Wei family had only sent calling cards to the Qin First Branch.

Today was an official day off from court.

The Second Branch was still the one managing the Qin family household.

Strictly speaking, even the Xianyang Wei family ought first to have sent a calling card to them—the Second Branch.

After all, she—as the senior grand matron—was still here.

But the Wei family had not done so!

They had simply treated her and her sons as nothing!

Old Madam Qin was so furious she smashed a set of valuable famille-rose bird-and-flower tea ware.

Qin Ruyue saw her at this moment still fixating on the small matter of the Xianyang Wei family showing her no respect, and was inwardly frantic.

The Xianyang Wei family hadn't had elder members come to visit the Qin household in many years!

Even the annual New Year gifts had been delivered by the younger generation.

For them to come at this moment—and practically the whole clan—it was impossible that it was simply to see Qin the Sixth Young Miss married off.

And what the Wei family cared about most was certainly not a mere Sixth Young Miss.

Then—why was the Xianyang Wei family making such a tremendous display, bringing so many men and women, young and old alike?

The only thing that could make the Xianyang Wei family this invested—that could only be their late grandmother's substantial trousseau!

But—in her previous life, there had been no such episode!

And she suddenly remembered something about the previous life... the most capable sixth uncle from the First Branch's maternal family had died on the road to Mountain River Province, where he had been appointed governor.

But in this life—why was that man still alive?

She had no time to dwell on that now.

But Grandmother... sigh! Grandmother was truly old!

She couldn't even see this much...

She had no choice but to alert her.

Once Old Madam Qin was prompted that the Xianyang Wei family's visit was about the trousseau left behind by the Wei matriarch, her old face instantly went ashen.

Seeing her tremble all over, Qin Ruyue had to step forward to soothe her and coach her on continuing to use the strategy of delay...

As for the Wei family coming as guests to the Qin household without first calling upon her—that too could be used to give the Wei family a show of power and put them on the back foot.

Madam Li led the eldest Wei grandmother and her party into the Hall of Longevity and Peace. Old Madam Qin was seated in the place of honor in the reception hall.

When the eldest Wei grandmother and her party came in, Old Madam Qin didn't stir—she simply sat on in the master's chair.

Qin Ruyue signaled with her eyes until they nearly cramped, but Old Madam Qin didn't see.

Qin Ruyue was inwardly exasperated, and felt a surge of resentment toward Old Madam Qin.

She had been about to use the Wei family's lack of propriety in coming first to the First Branch as a point of leverage.

But now her own grandmother hadn't even bothered to rise from her seat and go down to greet the eldest Wei grandmother and the other elder ladies—that was a breach of courtesy on her grandmother's part!

How could they turn around and find fault with the Wei family?

Madam Li saw Old Madam Qin—face drawn with illness yet sitting in the master's chair with an air of insufferable arrogance—and spat inwardly.

Sure enough—this concubine-turned-wife old woman was deliberately putting on airs!

The eldest Wei grandmother and her party were also astonished. This Old Madam Qin hadn't even risen from her seat.

Let alone come to greet them.

Such behavior was no way to receive guests—it was handing people the perfect pretext to fault her.

And this was not the same as them having gone to the First Branch first.

Setting aside the fact that they and Old Madam Qin were of the same generation—they had been long away from the capital, so of course they went first to see their dear eldest nephew's family.

Had only the daughters-in-law of their generation come—without the elder ladies themselves—Old Madam Qin might have had some ground to take issue.

But all these senior women had come together!

"How have the Madams of the Wei family been keeping? It's been so many years since you've come to the capital, has it not?" Old Madam Qin propped herself up into a forced smile and made conversation, addressing them as peers, without inviting them to sit.

Madam Li was about to speak up, but the second Wei great-aunt stopped her with a firm grip.

She gave Madam Li a smile and a small shake of the head, saying quietly: "Don't fight this battle now."

Several decades ago, she and her eldest sister-in-law had met this old woman once, when their little sister-in-law was already bedridden. This old woman had still been a concubine at that time.

Yet decades had passed, and she had made no more progress in understanding human dealings.

If it hadn't been for the fact that her own husband's generation and her sons' generation had so few men making their way in officialdom, how could their eldest nephew have been made to suffer all these years?

Back then, even if they had staked the entire Xianyang Wei family, they would not have been a match for the Qin Second Branch and the Second Branch's daughter-in-law Madam Tong's family.

Besides, this old woman had other sons aside from Qin Mingjie.

At that time—they could only endure.

It had been unavoidable.

But now, the time had come. Their eldest nephew had been biding his time and accumulating strength; among the younger generation of the Xianyang Wei family, several talented members had emerged.

Furthermore, Wei the sixth—the Wei family's Sixth Uncle—had been rising fast in recent years, and had just last year been promoted to Governor of Mountain River Province—a regional authority with real power, and firmly established.

With the Wei family's Sixth Uncle in place, the already-declining Qin Second Branch was no longer a match.

They had previously worried about the powerful Heshui Tong clan as well.

But now the Second Branch had cut off their own arm by sending Madam Tong to a country estate—could the Heshui Tong family possibly have no objections to that?

And there was the matter of Sixth Young Miss's husband's family being quite respectable...

All these favorable factors had accumulated together. It was only with all this in place that they had chosen the happy occasion of Sixth Young Miss's wedding as the moment to come to the capital and challenge the now-weakened Second Branch...

After all, the Xianyang Wei family never picked a fight without assurance of winning!

"Indeed." The eldest Wei grandmother gave a shallow smile and nodded. "We haven't been here in many years—and we've all grown old."

She then led her party to greet Old Madam Qin, every courtesy perfectly executed, not a single point of protocol missed.

Old Madam Qin made no response—only said "good, good, good" several times.

Treating the Wei family women like juniors. And still didn't offer them seats.

The eldest Wei grandmother and her party did not take such petty tricks and scheming to heart.

After studying Old Madam Qin for a moment, the eldest Wei grandmother suddenly exclaimed in surprise:

"Grand Matron Qin, your complexion looks quite poor—even more haggard than we old bags who didn't get a sip of water after arriving at your hall!"

Old Madam Qin: "......"

Qin Ruyue was already in a state of frantic anxiety, and hearing this vigorous and keen-eyed old woman put her grandmother's face down so blatantly, she had no choice but to step in and play hostess.

"Please, honored elders of the Wei family, be seated and let us talk..."

"And who might this be?" The eldest Wei grandmother looked at Qin Ruyue, cutting her off mid-sentence with a smiling air. "What a lovely young lady! How old are you this year?"

Qin Ruyue had been about to explain on her grandmother's behalf and then introduce herself.

Being cut off by the eldest Wei grandmother—and indirectly being reminded that she was a young junior girl with no standing to be playing hostess to these senior ladies—she dared not say another word. She could only give Old Madam Qin a look.

Old Madam Qin still didn't so much as glance at her.

Of course Old Madam Qin fully understood the pointed meaning behind the eldest Wei grandmother's words.

If she continued to put on airs, she would only look more foolish.

She had no choice but to rise and say: "Look at this old one... being ill for several days has made her befuddled. I quite forgot to ask the honored guests to be seated."

"Oh, you've been unwell? Grand Matron Qin, please do take care of yourself—you're not so young anymore, and your grandchildren are still small!" The eldest Wei grandmother said sincerely, even as she walked toward the guest's first seat.

Madam Li quickly stepped forward to take her arm and help her to her seat.

She then ushered the other great-aunts to their seats as well.

Old Madam Qin's chest was practically ready to explode.

Yet she had no choice but to hold herself in check and smile in return: "We're all getting on in years—we all need to take care of ourselves."

"Grand Matron Qin is ill—why don't we see the Second Mistress and the other close daughters-in-law here to attend her?" the second Wei great-aunt suddenly asked.

Old Madam Qin was ready to simply faint on the spot.

Her second daughter-in-law had already been sent away by her son to a country estate—and now she had to ask!

How was she supposed to explain that?

"Second Great-Aunt, we hadn't mentioned it to the honored elders before—my Second Sister-in-law has also been unwell and was sent by her husband to recuperate at a country estate." Madam Li said with pointed meaningfulness.

The second Wei great-aunt immediately said: "My goodness! Is that so? Grand Matron Qin, you do seem to be having misfortune in the family."

Old Madam Qin nearly vomited blood.

She bit her tongue until it was throbbing, then swallowed down the coppery sweetness.

"Not at all—eating coarse grain, falling ill is common. If that counts as family misfortune, then everyone would have family misfortune."

"Grand Matron, my second sister-in-law didn't mean it that way." The fourth Wei great-aunt spoke up.

"You may not have heard—along our journey, we caught snatches of people talking. They said the Second Branch's eldest young master here had also had a separation, and that both legitimate grandsons were taken away... all of it together does make one sigh."

Old Madam Qin broke into a fit of rapid coughing.

She was beginning to regret not having called her other three daughters-in-law over.

Having let herself end up facing all these sharp tongues alone—a thoroughly disadvantageous situation...

Feeling as if she had been forgotten by everyone, Qin Ruyue bit her lips in humiliation, her eyes nearly red from the effort of holding herself together.

Even her grandmother had forgotten about her—hadn't even introduced her to the Wei family women.

She knew: Qin Sixth Young Miss—along with the Seventh and Eighth Young Misses—had already received a great many valuable first-meeting gifts from the Wei family women!

The Wei family women were meeting her for the first time too. If only her grandmother had introduced her... the Wei family women were all dignified people—she too could have received a good haul of first-meeting gifts.

The Wei family had given Qin Sixth Young Miss a very generous trousseau addition.

They had also given her—Fifth Young Miss—a portion, but it was entirely worthless things like calligraphy rubbings and ink copies...

If they were in a famous master's hand, then of course they'd have value.

But these were just rubbings and copies produced by the Wei family men themselves. What could they possibly be worth?

And yet she couldn't say a word about it.

If it got out, people would praise it as refined and cultured taste—and it would only make her look mercenary...

"Cough, cough... my Sixth Young Miss is indeed fortunate. More so than her two elder brothers and two elder sisters.

Just look—Sixth Young Miss's wedding has brought out such a crowd from the Wei family. So many coming to see her off! How wonderful!"

Old Madam Qin, trying to win back some ground, spoke up in a baiting tone.

The eldest Wei grandmother held her tea cup without drinking. She looked steadily at Old Madam Qin and replied:

"Grand Matron Qin has misunderstood again. We are both women approaching sixty. Old Lady Wei is blunt by nature, so allow me to speak plainly."

Old Madam Qin's old face sank.

Her heart clenched with anxiety—her pulse pounding hard in her chest.

"Aiyo!" She suddenly slumped to one side, one hand pressing her temple, and said weakly: "Why is this head pounding so dreadfully..."

"Honored guests, this old one is not feeling well—I'm afraid I cannot entertain you today.

Eldest daughter-in-law—please take the honored Wei madams back to your side of the household. Once old Qin is feeling better, I shall invite them all again to the Hall of Longevity and Peace for a proper visit."

Old Madam Qin spoke of feeling poorly and having a terrible headache—and yet her words came out perfectly smooth and flowing.

"If that is the case, then we shall not trouble Grand Matron Qin further. Today is a day off from court. Second Master Qin is also at home—it is just as well for us elders to go and find Second Master Qin to have our conversation."

The eldest Wei grandmother rose at an unhurried pace and said calmly.

chapters.title: The Wei Family Demands the Return of the Dowry
chapters.content:
"Wait!" The Old Matriarch's mind fractured with alarm. The Wei family had truly come in force — this was not something that could be easily dissolved.

The Wei family's Grand Maternal Aunt paused, her voice detached. "What more does Madam Qin wish to say?"

"You are all womenfolk, after all, and my son is of a younger generation — I fear he may not have received you properly."

"I feel rather better now. Please, do sit down — I shall keep you company."

The Old Matriarch was shaking with fear within, though she forced herself to appear composed on the surface.

If the Wei family had truly come for the late Madam Wei's dowry, as Fifth Young Miss had said, it was far better to resolve this here in the inner quarters than to let it escalate to the men.

Best to settle it among the womenfolk...

Qin Ruyue looked at her grandmother with anxious eyes, hoping she would follow the plan she had outlined: stall for time.

First delay, then hide the most valuable items. When there was truly no more room to stall, simply say that the old patriarch had lost them.

The Wei family could hardly go chasing after a man who had been dead for decades.

The most worrying thing now was whether her grandmother had already thought to hide the most valuable pieces beforehand.

If she had — things might still be managed.
