If she hadn't — they were in serious trouble.

The Wei family's Grand Maternal Aunt had never truly intended to settle a matter of this magnitude with a concubine-turned-wife anyway.

But if the old woman was willing to come to her senses, return what was not hers to the family of her great-nephew, then all would be well.

What followed — the matters between men, the disputes within clans and between brothers — would be their affair.

At that point, the Wei family need only stand by and lend her great-nephew their weight.

"Since Madam Qin invites me to stay, I shall sit a while longer." The Wei family's Grand Maternal Aunt turned back with unhurried composure.

A flash of venom crossed the Old Matriarch's eyes — quickly masked by a warm smile. "Then please, Madam Wei, do sit down and talk."

Once seated, the Wei family's Grand Maternal Aunt looked at the Old Matriarch with a faint smile.

"Madam Qin — when my sister-in-law passed all those years ago, the greater part of her dowry fell into the hands of the late patriarch's father."

"This matter has yet to receive any accounting from the Qin family. It is time, I think."

The Old Matriarch's heart gave a jolt.

Qin Ruyue, standing behind her with lowered eyes, felt a surge of irritation — just as she had guessed.

A murderous glint flickered in the Old Matriarch's aged eyes.

So they had truly come for the dead woman's dowry.

Years ago, the old patriarch had privately told her that Madam Wei's lavish dowry was rumored to be worth close to a million taels...

Who could look at a sum like that without coveting it?

At the time she had assumed the bulk of it was cash — the wedding-chest silver.

It wasn't until the old patriarch died and the dowry fell into her hands that she discovered the silver was actually the smallest part.

The properties — fields and shops — were not inconsiderable, worth perhaps two hundred thousand taels.

As for the cash in the wedding chest, there were just over one hundred and eight thousand taels, every bit of which her husband had long since diverted for his own use.

Before his death, the old patriarch had warned her that the Wei family of Xianyang might one day come for Madam Wei's dowry. He had told her to use his own private assets — worth over a hundred thousand taels — to make up the shortfall.

How could she bear to part with it? That was over a hundred thousand taels! Not a hundred thousand copper coins!

The most valuable pieces were the antiques and calligraphy and paintings — but those were impossible to convert to cash easily.

The old patriarch had told her that the longer such objects were kept, the more valuable they became. He urged her not to touch them rashly, saying that even if they were returned to the eldest, they were still Qin family property.

He said that when the sons entered officialdom and reached a critical moment, those antiques and paintings would prove most useful.

But how could she possibly hand them over to Qin Mingfeng? He was a Qin family son, yes — but not one born from her own womb.

Of course, the old patriarch had been right in what he said.

That painting — the Spring Equinox Court Ladies — could have been of great use to her son... but that wretched Seventh Young Miss had ruined the opportunity.

"Ah, what is Madam Wei saying?" The Old Matriarch's aged eyes darted rapidly.

She raised her voice: "When my late husband was alive, he declared in the presence of the clan that Madam Wei's dowry had been given to our eldest son!"

Li Shi's eyes went red with anger at once.

Yes, some had been given. But only the least valuable portion of Madam Wei's dowry.

Her husband of course bore no grudge — she and the children bore no grudge either. What they had received of Madam Wei's things, they treasured every piece.

But this old woman was truly too much.

By speaking only half the truth, she was deliberately creating the impression that the late patriarch had returned the entire dowry to their eldest son on his deathbed.

"That is not accurate, Madam Qin!" Li Shi spoke up immediately.

"At the time, the late patriarch did say he intended to return my birth mother-in-law's dowry to my husband. But Madam Qin has not returned a single piece to this day!"

The Old Matriarch frowned at Li Shi, her tone aggrieved. "How can you say such things, First Daughter-in-law? How would I dare involve myself in the dowry of my late husband's first wife?"

"Then what about the Twenty-Four Solar Terms Court Ladies series?" Li Shi gave a cold snort.

"The Twenty-Four Solar Terms Court Ladies?" The Wei family's Grand Maternal Aunt murmured, exchanging a glance with the other women, and then looked steadily at the Old Matriarch. "Madam Qin — that was my sister-in-law's dowry."

The Old Matriarch nodded and gave to the Wei family's Grand Maternal Aunt and her party the same account she had given Qin Mingfeng.

When she finished, she spread her hands with exaggerated helplessness. "That is simply how it is. My late husband fell suddenly and critically ill, and died too quickly — there was no time to settle many things before he was gone."

"He told the children and the clan before his death that everything he owned would go to no one but me, to provide for my old age..."

"Who could have known that mixed in among the things he left me were pieces belonging to Madam Wei?"

Not even a ghost would believe that story.

The Wei women heard her self-assured account and let contempt settle plainly across their faces.

"Madam Qin need not explain further. Our late Madam Wei's dowry has a dowry list." The Grand Maternal Aunt spoke with calm authority.

"Even if some discrepancies have arisen over the years, there are accounts that can be verified."

"Our Wei family asks for nothing else. Simply cross-reference the records — whatever the findings, the truth will speak for itself."

The Old Matriarch knew her only option now was to stall.

Thinking of this, she felt a measure of comfort.

She looked at the Grand Maternal Aunt levelly and said slowly: "But the late patriarch's private treasury and my own are all tangled up in a mess — cross-referencing the accounts is not a matter of one evening."

"Elders, my grandmother has been tallying the accounts since the day she discovered the situation, only it has been so many years and she discovered it rather late..."

The Grand Maternal Aunt's deep-set eyes swept to Qin Ruyue, who had jumped in with some urgency.

She gave a sigh. "Young lady, these are matters of the elder generation. This old woman finds them tiresome enough — you are a young girl who understands nothing of it. Best not to interrupt."

Qin Ruyue's beautiful face went instantly crimson.

The Old Matriarch shot her a sharp look. "Fifth Young Miss! This is not your place to speak."

Qin Ruyue was struck from two sides at once and nearly swayed on her feet.

But no one paid her any mind.

"If Madam Qin is worried about the private treasuries and accounts being in disarray, it so happens that we brought quite a few capable people with us. We have our own accountants ready — assisting your Qin family's clerks in cross-referencing the records would be no trouble at all."

The Grand Matriarch's complexion was now beyond merely unpleasant — it was appalling.

She sat in frozen silence for a long while, at a loss for words.

In the end it was Qin Ruyue at her side who couldn't hold back and spoke up again.

"Madam Wei, do you mean that your Wei family has not come to the Qin household as guests — but has brought your own accountants to audit my grandmother's accounts and search her private treasury?"

The Grand Maternal Aunt looked at this Fifth Young Miss of the Qin family with some surprise.

This was the one who had schemed to steal the engagement that had originally belonged to Sixth Young Miss.

She had a certain quick wit about her.

It was a pity. Her heart was not good, and she had taken the wrong path.

"Madam Qin, you know in your own heart — our Wei family comes only for the dowry of our departed kinswoman. I have said all there is to say. If you are clear-headed, return what does not belong to you and the matter is resolved."

"If you are unwilling to return it, the Wei family has other means. In any case, we shall not have mobilized the entire clan and traveled all the way to the capital for nothing."

The Grand Maternal Aunt finished speaking and smiled with serene composure. "Madam Qin, do as you see fit."

...

In First Master Qin's study.

The Wei family elders and the cousins of the same generation as First Master Qin sat gathered together.

The Wei family's Grand Maternal Uncle — First Master Qin's great-uncle by marriage — stroked his beard. "Now that everything has been laid out plainly, why not strike while the iron is hot? Let us go to Mingfeng's clan today and settle the matter."

All the Wei men nodded in agreement.

They looked toward First Master Qin.

First Master Qin rose and performed a deep bow to the assembled Wei men.

Then he turned to Uncle Ning beside him and instructed: "Ah Ning, go to the clan in person. Make everything clear to the clan elder and the elders. Then ask them to come to the house..."

Uncle Ning acknowledged the order and left.

The Wei Grand Maternal Uncle glanced at the sky and mused to First Master Qin: "It has been some time, and there is no word from your great-aunt's side. I imagine your stepmother is still digging in her heels."

"All these years, she has long since come to consider those things your mother left behind as her own. To have all of it disgorged at once — I suspect it would pain her more than death."

The Wei Grand Maternal Uncle gave a cold snort.

Then he smiled again. "But as the saying goes, the world is unpredictable. Her holding on to your mother's dowry is not entirely a bad thing — it can now be used as leverage to force the clan to agree to the family separation."

The Qin clan would certainly not lightly consent to the First Branch splitting off.

Splitting off had always been the gravest of matters for a family.

If the First Branch had remained weak, they would not even have had standing to raise the question.

But if the First Branch grew strong, the Qin clan would naturally be reluctant to let them go.

Some outside force was therefore needed to bring it about.

The Old Matriarch was not that outside force — but her misappropriation of the original wife's enormous dowry, combined with the deliberate suppression and humiliation of the original wife's legitimate son and his family...

If the original wife's son had not pursued the matter, or lacked the strength to do so, so be it. But if he did pursue it, with his maternal great-uncle's entire clan coming in force from Xianyang to demand an accounting — that was quite another matter altogether.

In Shouhe Hall, the Old Matriarch behaved like a shameless street debtor — no matter what the Wei people said and no matter how Li Shi mocked her, she stubbornly executed one strategy: stall.

Finally, the Wei people ran out of patience. Li Shi ran out of patience.

As they left Shouhe Hall, the Grand Maternal Aunt said to Li Shi: "First great-niece by marriage, send word to your husband. Ask the Qin clan elder and elders to come."

chapters.title: Everyone Has Eyes on That Dowry
chapters.content:
One of the younger Wei women supporting the Grand Maternal Aunt asked: "Great-grandmother, if that Madam Qin can't be reasoned with, why did we bother coming to argue with her at all?"

"The kind of family we are — we do things properly. We present courtesy before force." The Grand Maternal Aunt replied with a smile.

"If she had been frightened by a few words from us and simply returned your great-grandaunt's dowry, wouldn't that have been the ideal outcome?"

If it were truly that easy, the Wei family would never have mobilized so many people to come to the capital.

This visit was not only about reclaiming the late sister-in-law's dowry for the great-nephew — the matter of the First Branch separating from the Qin clan was equally important.

The Second Branch of the Qin family — more precisely, the sons born to the Old Matriarch — had, under Qin Mingjie's leadership, gone fundamentally off course. Left to continue down that road, the entire Qin family wouldn't even know how it had been destroyed.

The great-nephew had seen this early and acted decisively in seeking separation — he was right to do so.

And since he had the courage for it, and the late sister-in-law had left behind only this one bloodline, the Wei family of Xianyang simply had to come and lend him their support.

"Great-grandmother, I'm very simple — I don't understand any of it." The young woman said, embarrassed.

The older Wei women and Li Shi all laughed warmly.

The Grand Maternal Aunt patted the young woman's hand with a gentle smile. "How old are you? You're our family's daughter-in-law now, but still a child! It's perfectly fine not to understand — watch more and it will come."

The young woman gave a bright, cheerful response.

Which drew another round of affectionate laughter from the Wei women and Li Shi.

Li Shi said: "None of you elders need worry about our family's mess. Come with me to the West Courtyard to rest. My daughters-in-law Xixi and An'an and my Ruyin have already been preparing a meal. We'll go back and play a few rounds of Madiao first!"

Madiao was a popular card game currently in fashion in the capital.

It had in fact originated in Chang'an, which was just across the water from Xianyang — practically neighbors.

The Wei women were naturally familiar with Madiao.

Li Shi was catering perfectly to their tastes.

Hearing this, the Grand Maternal Aunt laughed heartily, pointing at Li Shi as she addressed the Wei women: "Look at her — what a wonderful disposition! With such a serious matter at home, she still eats when it's time to eat, drinks when it's time to drink, plays when it's time to play, and receives guests when guests come."

"All of you take a lesson. Don't let any little trouble ruin your appetite and leave you haggard within a few days."

The younger Wei women responded in unison.

They were genuinely impressed.

Li Shi, a little embarrassed by the praise, said: "Grand Auntie-in-law, those words are too kind — I don't know how to respond."

"I was just thinking: my husband does things the same way as our Wei family elders — he never acts without being certain of the outcome."

"This affair is significant, but with so many Wei family kin here to back us up, how could it possibly fail?"

After Li Shi and the Wei party left, the Old Matriarch collapsed into the great chair, too spent even to rise.

She could only pant and instruct Qin Ruyue: "Fifth Young Miss... quickly! Go get your father!"

Qin Ruyue's own heart was churning.

Her grandmother had listened to her advice and deployed the stalling tactic.

But she had watched the entire exchange from the side, even tried several times to interject...

Those Wei aunts were simply too formidable.

Their words were not sharp, yet their composure and intellect far exceeded her grandmother's.

She feared the stalling tactic was utterly useless.

She was angry enough to want several extra brains, trying to think of some way to put the Wei family off the dowry...

And on top of that, seeing her grandmother immediately run to her father every time trouble arose only deepened her dissatisfaction.

Her father...

In her previous life, she had admired him greatly.

Since being reborn, watching with fresh eyes, she had come to see her father for what he was: a man who lusted after beauty and money — essentially a fool.

The Qin family's rise in her previous life had come about entirely through the sale of Seventh Young Miss, through which her eldest brother gained Prince An's favor.

In this life, so much had changed from before.

Neither Sixth Young Miss nor Seventh Young Miss was easy to manipulate anymore... and she still hadn't established a connection with Prince An.

"Fifth Young Miss... why are you still just standing there? Go tell someone to fetch your father!" The Old Matriarch, seeing her most beloved granddaughter still dazed, looked thoroughly displeased.

Qin Ruyue snapped back to herself, quickly agreed, and went out.

After giving the instruction for someone to fetch her father, she came back inside.

The Old Matriarch sat staring blankly.

Qin Ruyue moved to the Old Matriarch's side and asked quietly: "Grandmother — at this point, how much of that first wife's property have you actually accounted for?"

The Old Matriarch's aged eyes immediately sharpened to ice, boring into Qin Ruyue.

"Fifth Young Miss! Why are you asking that?"

Qin Ruyue immediately lowered her gaze. "Grandmother, please trust me — I have no ulterior motive. I think only of Grandmother's welfare, and of Father and Eldest Brother and the family!"

The Old Matriarch's deep-set eyes studied her carefully, appraising. "Fifth Young Miss, if you truly think that way, then nothing could be better. Know this: once a woman is married out, her natal family — her father and brothers — is her greatest pillar of support!"

"Yes, your granddaughter understands!" Qin Ruyue nodded, her expression devoted and earnest as she knelt before the Old Matriarch, looking up at her.

"Grandmother — the Wei family is being so aggressive, and they've come in such force. They are certainly prepared for every contingency and will not easily back down. The most urgent thing now is to hide what we can while we still can."

The Old Matriarch's mind stirred.

She had understood the deeper meaning of what Qin Ruyue was saying.

Seeing her expression waver, Qin Ruyue grew inwardly anxious.

"Just think of your granddaughter as selfish. I was raised by Father and Grandmother, and my only thought is for our own family — I can't concern myself with anyone else..."

"Fifth Young Miss, Grandmother understands your meaning... but now, I fear it's too late!" Understanding what Qin Ruyue intended, she felt deep regret.

Had she known the Wei family would come after all these decades to catch her out, she would have hidden those priceless treasures long ago!

Then she could have simply denied everything to the Wei family — said the long-dead patriarch had lost them. Who could do anything about that?

But she had been too reluctant to move them anywhere else.

She couldn't even bring herself to give them to her own sons...

She had not been born into favorable circumstances — a concubine-born daughter in a large family, unloved by a stepmother who resented her birth mother for stealing her father's affections and had been vicious toward her in turn.

Had she not found her own way to attach herself to the patriarch all those years ago, she would surely have been packed off to some noble household's back court to live and die as someone's concubine.

What she still resented was that she had clearly won the patriarch over, that he had not once but several times promised in moments of deep feeling to marry her as his principal wife...

And yet in the end he had listened to his mother's arrangement and gone to Xianyang... and came back married to a Wei family daughter.

Madam Wei owed her that!

She had stolen her rightful position as principal wife!

Her son had stolen Mingjie's right to be the eldest legitimate son!

Then let the dead woman pay with her dowry...

And yet — why couldn't Madam Wei's ghost just rest?

Dead for decades, and her natal family still came to demand the dowry back!

"If the Wei family comes in such force, they must have prepared for every outcome. There is no time to hide anything now..." By this point, the Old Matriarch had no qualms about admitting in front of her granddaughter that she had indeed coveted Madam Wei's dowry.

"Grandmother, there is still time! If the Wei family asks the clan to go through the dowry list and verify the contents... give the most valuable and easily concealed items to your granddaughter!"

A gleam of sharp calculation flashed across Qin Ruyue's eyes.

"Give them to you?" The Old Matriarch stared fixedly at this most beloved granddaughter.

Qin Ruyue nodded emphatically.

"Grandmother — if you give them to me, I'll put them in my trousseau and take them to the Wang family. Surely they wouldn't search a girl about to be married?"

"Besides, it would all be in my dowry — even if the Wei family suspected and wanted to search, our Qin clan would never allow it!"

"Grandmother, rest easy — even if I carry those things to the Wang family as part of my trousseau first, when the time is right I will bring them back. Those things belong to Father and Eldest Brother. Your granddaughter would not lay a finger on them!"

"Trust me, Grandmother!"

The Old Matriarch saw that her words were earnest and her expression entirely free of greed, and she felt moved.

"Fifth Young Miss — you are a good child... only, the Wei family is obstinate. They care only for their scholars and gentlemen, not for profit. The silver and fields and shops that the first wife left behind are not so many."

"What there is most of are the masterwork calligraphy and paintings from dynasty after dynasty, and some antiques and curios once used by the imperial family!"

Qin Ruyue's heart leapt with joy.

The antiques and curios she could do without.

But masterwork calligraphy and paintings from dynasty after dynasty — those were priceless, not available for any sum of money.

And the Second Wang Son would certainly need them when he entered officialdom.

Of course, even if she did not use them for him, her own sons would need them one day.

"Grandmother — didn't the Wei family send quite a few of their family's own hand-copied paintings and rubbings as trousseau gifts for me?"

"Just pass those priceless masterworks to your granddaughter, and I'll hide them among those ordinary copies and rubbings. Nothing could be better..."

The Old Matriarch turned it over in her mind and had to concede — that really was a sound idea.

Just as she was about to agree, Second Master Qin Mingjie lifted the bead curtain and strode in.

"Fifth Young Miss — what's this about trousseau gifts?" He had arrived in haste and caught only the last few words.

Qin Ruyue's heart lurched.

Her father was petty and suspicious by nature. Though not a man of great wisdom, he was a through-and-through hypocrite, and those were exactly the most difficult kind to deal with.

The Old Matriarch, in the end, trusted her son more.

She recounted the day's events to him, and emphasized Qin Ruyue's suggestion at the end.

"Mingjie, I actually think Fifth Young Miss's idea is quite good — hiding things in her trousseau. Who would dare search a girl about to be married?"

Qin Mingjie regarded this daughter he had once deeply cherished with a long, heavy look.

"Fifth Young Miss, this is not something a girl about to be married should be meddling in." He waved her off. "Your grandmother and I have important things to discuss. Go back to your own courtyard."

Qin Ruyue's heart sank.

She understood perfectly — her father didn't trust her and didn't want her involved.

The hatred coiled and tangled inside her like a skein of tightly wound thread...

Under Qin Mingjie's intimidating manner, Qin Ruyue had no choice but to leave Shouhe Hall.

The Old Matriarch watched her unsteady retreating figure with a slight frown.

"Mingjie — you don't trust Fifth Young Miss?"

Qin Mingjie's expression was dark.

"Mother, I don't want to think the worst of Fifth Young Miss. But — if the items are hidden in her trousseau, there can be no trace of evidence. Once she is married out, she belongs to someone else's family. How can we possibly guarantee she will ever return them?"

"Then what do you propose? You and I are talking — many of the things the first wife left behind are priceless... Mother truly cannot bear to give them all up!"

"If Mother cannot bear it, how can I?" Qin Mingjie said bleakly.

Mother and son stared at each other for a long while, neither able to conceive of a solution.

Then a matron outside reported that the First Master and the clan elder were requesting that the Old Matriarch and Second Master come to the outer court to talk.

Both their pupils contracted instantly, and then both of them swayed on their feet.

chapters.title: The Old Matriarch's Shameful Secret
chapters.content:
"They moved so fast?" Qin Mingjie snarled, already beside himself with anger. "The clan has already been brought in?"

"Calm down first," the Old Matriarch urged. "Think about how to handle this. Being angry now is useless."

"Mother," Qin Mingjie burst out, "since you had already done what you did, why didn't you tell me sooner? Now that it has come to this, our reputation is damaged and we'll likely not be able to hold onto much of it!"

The Old Matriarch, already in the grip of panic and anxiety, looked utterly shocked.

"Ming... Mingjie!"

"Are you blaming your own mother?"

"What use is blame?" Qin Mingjie's face went dark. "If Mother hadn't been so greedy — and hadn't trusted even her own son — how could we have ended up in this embarrassing position?"

The Old Matriarch trembled with fury.

Her lips moved and moved, she muttered for a long time, and still found nothing to say.

If she had felt any remorse before — thinking that had she shared the secret with her sons earlier and had them hide the valuables, this could have been avoided — now, watching this son she had been most proud of, most capable, and most dependent upon grow resentful of her over the dead Madam Wei's dowry...

She felt grief and disappointment — but no regret.

She had done nothing wrong.

"Let's go. To the outer courtyard." The Old Matriarch looked at this son she had once been so proud of. "Anything said now is too late."

"If only Mother hadn't..." Qin Mingjie began furiously.

The Old Matriarch cut him off coldly: "The very reason I never told you brothers about this matter was to prevent exactly this day from coming. If you wish to blame me, I can't stop you — go ahead and blame me."

Qin Mingjie's brows arched in fury, but he was helpless.

Whatever his mother said — whether it was hindsight or not — there was one undeniable truth: the thing had happened. There was nothing to do now but face it.

Mother and son walked in silence all the way to the outer courtyard.

When they arrived and saw the Wei family ranged in dense rows across four generations — elderly, middle-aged, young men and boys — the two of them exchanged a weighty glance.

They then saw the Qin clan elder and several elders sitting with the current Wei family head — Qin Ruyin's Great-Uncle — and barely sparing them a glance as they arrived. The anger in both their hearts deepened.

Especially for Qin Mingjie.

He was, after all, a third-rank official of the court!

And that Wei Great-Uncle was nothing more than a regional clan patriarch — a commoner. He hadn't even stood when he entered. What sense did that make?

"Mingjie is here?" The Qin clan elder had already officially heard from the Wei Great-Uncle about how the Old Matriarch had privately appropriated Madam Wei's dowry, and had been cursing the woman to no end in his heart.

He couldn't even be bothered to greet the Old Matriarch when he saw her.

The Wei Great-Uncle, however, offered the Old Matriarch a cup of his hands in a formal salute.

His etiquette was impeccable.

He then glanced at Qin Mingjie and asked casually: "And how has my young kinsman been keeping?"

He spoke as a senior addressing a junior — to outsiders, this looked like affectionate concern for a younger relative.

Madam Wei was gone, but the Wei family remained the most legitimate in-laws the Qin family had.

The Old Matriarch, who had risen from concubine status, couldn't even have been considered a Qin family relative before she elevated herself.

So the Wei Great-Uncle's gesture was not merely appropriate — from the perspective of the Qin clan elder and elders, it was generous, and showed the Wei family's magnanimity toward Qin Mingjie.

Qin Mingjie had nothing to say to that.

He offered a perfunctory reply and then sat to one side as if facing a great enemy.

Ears sharpened to points, dreading to miss a word between the Wei Great-Uncle and the clan elder.

The Old Matriarch also settled herself into a seat above Qin Mingjie, supported by her senior maid.

"The Wei family head need not concern himself — this matter should be a misunderstanding." The Qin clan elder swallowed his shame, shot the Old Matriarch a hard look, and then turned back to address the Wei Great-Uncle with a tempered breath.

"To speak the family's shame plainly — Mingjie's mother was a concubine elevated to principal wife. In her own natal home she was merely a concubine-born daughter, and her stepmother had no love for her."

"...She never learned much of household management. Fortunately, Mingjie's wife is a proper lady of good family, and since her marriage has helped manage the household..."

"Now that Mingjie's wife has fallen gravely ill and gone to the countryside estate to recover, this household has likely fallen into disorder again."

"You may be assured — though our Qin family may not have the long heritage of your Wei family, we are nonetheless a century-old great clan. We would never do so shameful a thing as privately seizing a daughter-in-law's dowry!"

The Old Matriarch nearly fainted hearing those words.

Qin Mingjie's expression was also terrible.

He wanted to argue back at the old clan elder — but reason told him he must not.

The Qin clan elder had not been obliged to speak so harshly and so thoroughly.

He was doing it for the sake of the Second Branch...

He was furious at the Old Matriarch for her greed — for privately seizing the late Madam Wei's dowry, for causing the Wei family to descend in full force on the Qin household to demand an accounting, and for disgracing their century-old clan.

The Old Matriarch forced herself not to storm out.

"Mingjie's mother — would you care to speak to this?" The Qin clan elder had determined that the Old Matriarch would personally account for this disgrace, surrender everything she had seized from Madam Wei's dowry, and appease the Wei family's fury.

So that he could then shamelessly beg the Wei family head not to spread this shameful business outside.

If it spread, the Qin family's century of good reputation would be beyond saving.

This was not comparable to the divorce of Qin Mingjie's eldest son's wife, or his principal wife being sent to the countryside estate to "recover," or even his keeping and taking in an outside mistress — those were merely private moral failings.

If this matter became public, no male member of the entire Qin family would ever again hope to marry a daughter from a distinguished household.

The Old Matriarch closed her eyes, suppressing the fury within. She was about to nod when she felt, quite suddenly, unbearably reluctant.

She stood and looked at the Qin clan elder: "Old Clan Elder — just because my origins are humble, there is no need to slap me quite so publicly, is there?"

The Qin clan elder was aghast.

This foolish woman!

Was this the time for that? Compared to the enormous sum she had seized from Madam Wei's dowry, what did this small humiliation amount to?

The Qin elders also darkened.

Even one of the elders who had always stood on Qin Mingjie's side could not help but say to him: "Mingjie, shouldn't you speak to your mother?"

Qin Mingjie had no choice but to swallow his resentment and relay to the Wei Grand Maternal Aunt the story his mother had told earlier.

When finished, he added: "All the Wei family elders, Clan Elder and elders — my mother is indeed as the Clan Elder described: unskilled at household management, entirely at sea when it comes to accounts."

"My late father also died too quickly, without time to settle many affairs, and so the late first mother's dowry became entangled with his private treasury."

He paused, then continued: "It was only when my elder brother recently began preparing our Sixth Young Miss's dowry that the matter was discovered, and my mother has had people sorting through it since."

"This will not be resolved in a short time... I hope the Wei family elders will extend further patience."

Then he pivoted sharply: "However, should some items or accounts not reconcile, that can only be attributed to our late father's side of things, and that is... difficult to say."

The Wei Great-Uncle smiled when he heard this. He understood perfectly well the private motives and greed at play.

But his Wei family had mobilized in full force precisely because they had prepared thoroughly for every contingency.

He looked steadily at Qin Mingfeng, the First Master, and spoke with unhurried calm.

"I fear my young kinsman may not know — your late father kept scrupulously detailed accounts of his affairs, especially regarding any use of his wife's dowry."

He said this, then looked toward Qin Mingfeng. "Mingfeng, please bring out the account book copies your late father recorded — regarding the use of your mother's dowry — for the Clan Elder and the elders to examine."

chapters.title: First Master Qin Raises the Question of Separating from the Clan
chapters.content:
Qin Mingjie's mind erupted in a ringing burst.

That darkened face went instantly the color of snow...

Their father's account book copies!

He recalled the day Qin Mingfeng had come to demand the Twenty-Four Solar Terms paintings from their mother, and what he had said.

He had said that the patriarch's old personal attendant, Sun Er-uncle, had given him several account books along with other things...

So Qin Mingfeng really could produce them!

How laughable that he had been waiting and waiting for Qin Mingfeng to come asking their mother for things piece by piece — never imagining that this had merely been a small opening move.

Now they had been dealt a stroke of such devastating magnitude.

The Old Matriarch also went limp in her chair, her limbs trembling.

How could their dead patriarch have done this to her?

If he hadn't recorded so meticulously every time he used Madam Wei's dowry, how could she have ended up in such a position today?

This was her own foolishness, to be fair.

The old patriarch had actually been an extraordinarily self-interested man.

In those days, to win the backing and resources of the Xianyang Wei family, he had not hesitated to break his promise of marrying the Old Matriarch as his principal wife...

And how could such a man be willing to carry the posthumous infamy of having seized his first wife's dowry?

That was precisely why, before his death, he had told her to use his private assets to fill the gap left by his use of Madam Wei's cash dowry.

And that was why — to conceal the fact that he had used his first wife's dowry — he had specifically told his children and clan that he was leaving the bulk of his private property to the Old Matriarch for her old age.

This announcement had been deliberately spread by the Old Matriarch, drawing the envy of many aristocratic women in the capital at the time.

It had also infuriated the always long-suffering First Master Qin so badly he had fallen ill for several days.

He had genuinely thought his biased old father had loved the Old Matriarch so extravagantly.

He never knew that his biased old father had merely been leaving those private assets to the Old Matriarch to use in settling his accounts.

Unfortunately, the Old Matriarch, boundlessly greedy, had withheld the bulk of the private assets the patriarch left her...

Beyond giving a portion to her biological sons, the greater part had actually been lent to her own natal family.

The Old Matriarch's natal mother had been a concubine who bore three brothers for her — two elder and one younger.

Since the Old Matriarch had risen from concubine to principal wife of the Qin patriarch, her standing in her natal home rose enormously.

Her father consequently doted further on her birth mother and the concubine-born sons.

With her money behind them, her natal father and brothers valued her more and more in return.

A concubine-born daughter returning to her natal home for the annual visit was treated as if she were legitimate.

This made her feel ever more strongly that being generous to her natal family was the absolutely right thing to do...

So she had been taken in by their honeyed words and had clutched every coin and every valuable thing tightly in her own hands.

And had concealed it even from her own biological children.

Qin Mingfeng had already prepared several copies of the account book in advance. From the tray Uncle Ning was holding, he took out five copies and distributed them to the Qin clan elder and the elders.

As for the Wei Great-Uncle and his party — they had already seen the original account book that Qin Mingfeng had shown them.

All that remained was to wait while the Qin clan elder and elders read through it.

With each page the Qin clan elder and elders turned, their expressions grew heavier. By the last page, their aged faces were blacker than the bottom of a cooking pot.

What a disgrace. What a thorough disgrace.

To think that a man who had risen to second rank in the court had done this — had...

Ah.

What could they say? What could any of them say?

If they hadn't dipped into some of Madam Wei's dowry in those years, the old patriarch probably wouldn't have climbed to that position.

He was the highest-ranking official the Qin family — a century-old clan — had ever produced.

So be it. So be it.

At least he hadn't been entirely without conscience. He had at least recorded it all, every detail.

And at the end of the account book he had left a note saying he would use his private assets to fill the deficit he had created.

As for the priceless antiques and paintings he had used — those could not be replaced in kind, but he had estimated their value and pledged to make it good from his private assets as well.

"Feng's mother!" The Qin clan elder erupted in a thundering reprimand toward the Old Matriarch. "Qinghu left a note in this account book — he specifically stated he would have you sell his private assets to repay every item and every sum he had borrowed!"

The Old Matriarch's surname was Feng. Qinghu was the old patriarch's style name.

"The accounts are crystal clear, and his instructions were crystal clear. What do you have to say for yourself?"

"Oh dear, oh dear... how could I make sense of any of that, old as I am? Just thinking about it gives me a splitting headache..." The Old Matriarch pressed her temples and groaned.

The Wei men and Qin Mingfeng looked on with cold contempt.

The clan elder and elders were furious, humiliated, and excruciatingly embarrassed — they wished they could find a crack in the earth to disappear into.

But the matter still had to be dealt with.

The Wei family and Qin Mingfeng had more than sufficient evidence. If this was not resolved properly, the consequences for the Qin family would be catastrophic.

"Mingjie, what do you have to say?" The clan elder, unable to watch the Old Matriarch resort to a woman's tricks — cry, make scenes, threaten to harm herself — turned his fury on Qin Mingjie.

Qin Mingjie was also mortified by her.

If only things hadn't come to this.

She had brought complete humiliation on him.

He wiped cold sweat from his brow, rose, and clasped his hands. "Clan Elder — might I examine my father's account book in person?"

The clan elder, in fury, hurled the account book copy in his hand at Qin Mingjie's head.

Qin Mingjie's face burned crimson, but he dared not react. He caught the book in a rush and lowered his gaze to read it.

When he finished, his expression was no better than the clan elder's.

It was worse.

He was a man who had spent over twenty years navigating the court. He knew exactly the weight of this account book in his father's own hand.

It had utterly closed every avenue of manipulation where Madam Wei's dowry was concerned...

How laughable that his mother had hoarded Madam Wei's dowry like a miser for decades without ever breathing a word to him, her own son.

Had it not been for the recent incident with Qin Mingfeng, he would still be in the dark!

Qin Mingjie understood perfectly: with his father's account book as evidence — and with a note left in it no less — he and his mother had not a single chance.

Want to hide Madam Wei's dowry?

And then what?

Even if they hid it, they would have to estimate its value and replace it in cash...

He had already given up.

Seeing his mother wailing away, his temples throbbed. He couldn't hold back a furious bark: "Mother! Stop this!"

The Old Matriarch stared at her son with eyes wide with disbelief.

Qin Mingjie rubbed his aching temples with exhaustion and looked at the Old Matriarch. "Mother, you don't know those accounts — all right. I'll personally have our household accountants help you sort through them. Stop troubling yourself over it."

Without waiting for the Old Matriarch to object, he sharply ordered her people to physically escort her out.

Once the Old Matriarch had left, Qin Mingjie cupped his hands in a general bow to the room.

Then, addressing the Qin clan elder and the Wei Great-Uncle: "Clan Elder, Wei Great-Uncle — this matter is my mother's fault. As her son, I will naturally clean up what she has created."

"Fortunately we have Father's account book. I propose we follow precisely what Father recorded. Would all parties find that acceptable?"

"Mingjie — speak plainly! Some of the lost items must be estimated in value and replaced in silver!" The clan elder snapped in displeasure.

Was he still trying to be clever at this late hour?

Qin Mingjie gritted his teeth and replied with lowered eyes: "Clan Elder need not mention it — I would have done so regardless. Even if Father's private assets are insufficient to fill the gap, I will find a way to make it good."

The clan elder drew a long breath.

Then cupped his hands toward the Wei Great-Uncle. "Wei Elder, does this arrangement sit well with you?"

The Wei Great-Uncle lifted his teacup — but did not drink.

He only said: "This is as it should be. But the bulk of what my sister-in-law brought as a bride were priceless antique calligraphy and paintings. Decades have passed — some of them are now priceless in the truest sense..."

The clan elder immediately understood his meaning, and turned to Qin Mingjie: "Your mother is confused, but you are not! Your father's records are clear — silver and items alike, every detail recorded. Don't you go and get confused as well!"

The message was plain: don't let Qin Mingjie and his mother secretly hold on to the good things, and if anything was already kept, it had to be returned.

Qin Mingjie replied with a flushed face: "Clan Elder can rest easy — I work for the court. I would not stoop to an act that invites the contempt of decent people!"

Even now he could not resist raising his own dignity.

But no one present — from the Wei family or from the Qin clan — held the slightest respect for him.

Even the two elders who had once stood firmly on his side now looked at him with deep disappointment.

The clan elder stared at him for a long moment and sighed: "Knowing that is enough."

In his heart at this moment, he was deeply conflicted.

The Second Branch of the Qin family was finished.

The clan would have to prepare itself to let the Second Branch go.

Even though Qin Mingjie was still a third-rank official, his Second Branch had met scandal after scandal, and especially since losing the Jiangdong Sun family as in-laws, it had lost its vitality.

And now this affair had erupted — capable of shaking the very foundations of the Qin clan...

Mingfeng, though — Mingfeng was excellent.

All these years, suppressed by the Second Branch's mother and sons, he had endured, held his ground, and quietly built his position. He was now a fourth-rank official with real power in his hands.

With his temperament, given an opportunity and the backing of his family, the likelihood of climbing one step further was enormous.

And his three sons and three daughters were all legitimate, all well-raised.

The eldest and second sons had gone to the military — they might still make their mark.

His youngest legitimate son was performing better and better at the family school. Several of the tutors had grown quite fond of him.

He had also inquired, and the word was that with a normal showing in next year's prefectural examination, the boy was certain to pass the first level.

And there was Sixth Young Miss — who by some twist of fate had found such an excellent match.

With the Jiang family holding her in such regard, as long as she bore the Jiang family worthy sons, the Jiang family would certainly support them...

After running through all of this in his mind, the clan elder's gaze on Qin Mingfeng grew more and more satisfied.

He stroked his beard and said to him: "Mingfeng — this is ultimately your affair. In your eyes, is this arrangement acceptable? Do you have any other requirements?"

Qin Mingfeng cupped his hands in a bow.

Then he looked at the Wei Great-Uncle and, with profound sincerity, spoke at length in gratitude to his great-uncle's clan.

The clan elder noticed that he thanked only his maternal great-uncle's clan — and not the Qin clan.

His heart gave a jolt.

Was Mingfeng holding a grudge against the clan? For all those decades in which the clan had never stood up for him and his family?

He didn't have long to dwell on it, because Qin Mingfeng had already turned back to him with a formal bow.

"Clan Elder, elders — the matter of my mother's dowry can be handled as proposed. But Mingfeng requests that the clan assign people to supervise the entire process."

"That goes without saying!" The clan elder nodded at once.

Qin Mingfeng thanked him and the clan.

But then his expression shifted to something grave, and his tone changed entirely.

"There is one more great matter on which Mingfeng asks the Clan Elder and elders to decide. Mingfeng wishes to separate from the clan."

chapters.title: The Qin Clan Has No Choice but to Agree
chapters.content:
"Separate from the clan!" The Qin clan elder rose to his feet in shock, staring with wide eyes. "You want to... separate from the clan?"

"Separate from the clan? How can you say such a thing?"

"Mingfeng, you're not... did this old man's ears fail him?"

"What reason is there for a separation? Mingfeng, this is too reckless!"

"Mingfeng — separation is no trifling matter. We haven't come to that, have we? Surely not!"

The Qin elders, their shock subsiding, rose one by one.

Their gazes burned into Qin Mingfeng — some filled with disbelief, some with anger, some with disappointment.

The Qin clan elder drew a deep breath, and when the fury in his chest had receded, he looked at Qin Mingfeng with gentle eyes.

"Mingfeng, good man — I know these past decades have wronged you." Having said that, his benevolent expression vanished and his heavy gaze swept across the stunned Qin Mingjie.

"All these years the clan too has been remiss in its care of your family. This old man and the elders, thinking back on the past, are deeply regretful. But it will not be so from now on..."

From now on it would not be so?

Qin Mingjie's eyes darkened. What was the old man saying? After taking so many benefits from the Second Branch, was he now going to cross the river and burn the bridge?

Qin Mingfeng kept his gaze lowered, looking at the floor.

So the old clan elder and the elders could actually say those words — acknowledging that his family had been wronged over all these decades.

He had thought the clan elder would never say such a thing.

But what did those words mean now?

The fact that they were said now was because his own family had long been at the mercy of others, and the clan had simply watched.

Whoever was winning — the clan helped that side.

If his daughter Ruyin had not been about to marry into the Jiang family, if he had not gained the support of Jiang Jiuxiao and his third brother to become a fourth-rank official with real power, would the clan have spoken up for him?

No.

If not for the signs of the First Branch rising, and the signs of the Second Branch declining in successive disasters, the clan still would not have stood on his side.

Even with the Old Matriarch's concubine-born son having privately seized his mother's dowry worth a million taels, even with his great-uncle's family making the effort of traveling in full clan force from Xianyang to back him — without those other factors, the clan would have done nothing but smooth things over.

They would never have moved this readily to make Qin Mingjie and his mother return every piece of his mother's dowry.

"Clan Elder, there's no need to say all that. I'm a grandfather already — those years of hardship are behind us." Qin Mingfeng smiled.

Just as the clan elder began to breathe a little easier, his tone shifted.

"Only — the heart died long ago. I hope the Clan Elder and elders will not try to persuade or obstruct me."

The clan elder froze.

"Old Clan Elder — people multiply and branches must divide; trees flourish and limbs must spread. Since Mingfeng wishes to separate, this is a decision made after full deliberation." The Wei Great-Uncle looked at the clan elder with an air of deep significance.

"Is it not better to come to a good agreement and settle matters while we still can?"

The Qin clan elder's grey brows arched.

Now it was clear. The Wei family had not almost mobilized their entire clan simply for that dowry.

They had come to help Qin Mingfeng separate from the clan!

"Wei Elder — that argument has merit in the wrong place." The clan elder glared at the Wei Great-Uncle. "Our Qin family is a century-old great clan — and compared to the Wei family of Xianyang, perhaps not quite as flourishing, but..."

"That is true," the Wei Great-Uncle replied with a smile, "our Wei family is somewhat larger. That is why in recent years, whenever someone among our Wei family has raised the question of separation, the clan has deliberated and permitted it."

This was not untrue.

The Wei family of Xianyang was a great clan indeed — branches thick, people numerous and powerful. Some collateral branches had gone forth and flourished mightily in other regions.

Eggs could not all stay in one basket. For the good of the entire Wei clan, the clan had even proactively offered to let some separate.

Some of the Wei branches that had separated were now more prosperous than the main Xianyang Wei line.

That too was Wei family glory — the main Xianyang line could only be proud of them.

After separation, though it was acknowledged that all shared the same Wei ancestor, some matters had to be clearly delineated as internal or external.

Compared to the Wei family of Xianyang, the Qin family was shallower-rooted and less worldly.

Otherwise they would never have stood by and allowed the Qin Second Branch to oppress the First Branch simply because the Xianyang Wei line had temporarily fallen quiet.

Hearing the Wei Great-Uncle's words, the clan elder froze again.

What could he say to that?

"To speak bluntly, Old Clan Elder — the Qin clan stood by while Mingfeng's family was mistreated. You should have anticipated today."

"Never mock the young for being poor, for youth will one day grow up." The Wei Great-Uncle said with a pleasant smile.

The clan elder felt a mouthful of stale blood forming.

But to simply nod and let a Mingfeng who was beginning to show signs of rising separate from the clan — how could he accept that?

Several elders were also unwilling.

They all looked at the clan elder.

One could no longer hold back. "Clan Elder! A matter as great as separation cannot be agreed to so easily!"

Another looked at Qin Mingfeng with reproach. "Mingfeng, the clan has not treated you badly over all these years. It's just that you and Mingjie have always been at odds — what could we as outsiders do?"

"Helping one would have displeased the other. The clan is in a difficult position too!"

Another said: "Yes, we in the clan haven't done enough — we admit it. Let us old men apologize to you, that's entirely acceptable. But you cannot raise separation at one word of disagreement!"

Qin Mingfeng sighed and looked at the clan elder, then one by one at all the elders.

"My elders — once the heart is dead, it cannot be revived. Let Mingfeng separate."

"We can part on good terms. Even after separation, we cannot write two Qin characters with one stroke of the brush. And if..."

Qin Mingfeng's expression hardened. "If things are forced to end badly, Mingfeng has no objection to saying a few unpleasant things to the elders."

The faces of the clan elder and elders were extremely grim.

Qin Mingjie finally recovered from his shock.

"Elder brother — are you serious? You truly want to separate from the clan?" Qin Mingjie thought Qin Mingfeng had gone mad. "If your family leaves the Qin clan, what are you worth? Who in this capital would still recognize you?"

Yet inside, he was overjoyed.

Was this really happening?

If Qin Mingfeng truly separated from the clan, wouldn't that mean he was no longer in the same line as him?

Wouldn't that make him — Qin Mingjie — the eldest legitimate son of the Qin family in this line?

He had longed to be the eldest legitimate son his entire life, and never imagined there would one day be a way to achieve it like this!

In his heart he was desperate for Qin Mingfeng to actually separate and be gone — but with the clan elder and elders present, he could not show it.

On the contrary, he had to oppose it...

Though his words were too cutting and too cruel, and earned him a reprimand from the clan elder.

That reprimand notwithstanding, the clan elder was satisfied by his opposition to separation.

The clan elder then used Qin Mingjie's words as a basis to further urge Qin Mingfeng to abandon the idea.

The Wei Great-Uncle said calmly from the side: "Old Clan Elder, rest easy — the Xianyang Wei family is here. And the Dongjin Wei family, a branch that separated from us, is not far from the capital."

"We hadn't wished to trouble them before — but for the sake of my great-nephew's family, this old man has already swallowed his pride and written to the Dongjin Wei family patriarch..."

The clan elder and elders looked up in shock.

The Dongjin Wei family was a branch of the Xianyang Wei family?

How had no word of that ever gotten out?

The Dongjin Wei family was a century-old great clan too. They had produced several first- and second-rank officials. Even at present, their clan had quite a few sons posted to key positions across the Six Ministries.

"The Dongjin Wei patriarch has already replied to this old man — they will certainly reach the capital in time for Sixth Young Miss's wedding..."

"Old Clan Elder, with the Dongjin Wei family keeping watch over Mingfeng's household, you need not worry that Mingfeng cannot stand up a separate Qin line."

The Wei Great-Uncle sat with his tea, thoroughly unperturbed.

The clan elder's complexion turned the color of spoiled vegetables.

He had worked it out now.

The Wei family of Xianyang had revealed even the Dongjin Wei family as a trump card in order to help Qin Mingfeng separate from the clan!

It seemed this could not end peacefully...

The Wei Great-Uncle smiled coldly to himself. He had only mentioned the Dongjin Wei family to intimidate the Qin clan. The Dongjin Wei family, having already separated, would not lightly entangle themselves in another family's disputes.

If the main Xianyang Wei line faced a great crisis, the Dongjin Wei would act, out of respect for their shared ancestor.

But for the sake of a Xianyang Wei outsider nephew — that was not possible.

Otherwise he would have sought the Dongjin Wei's help years ago, when his great-nephew was being crushed by the Second Branch.

Great clans operated first for their own interests. This was not children playing games.

His great-nephew understood this too.

Otherwise he would not have quietly maintained close ties with the Wei family all these years — not the superficial relationship the Qin Second Branch mother and sons imagined.

The clan elder was unable to hold back his anger any further. He glared at the Wei Great-Uncle. "Wei Elder — do you truly intend to push this to its limit?"

"Hardly pushing to the limit." The Wei Great-Uncle laughed lightly. "Are we not sitting here discussing this with the Old Clan Elder and the elders?"

"If we truly wanted to push to the limit, my Wei family would have taken our kinswoman's dowry list and our great-nephew's father's own account book to the magistrate's office to charge the Qin family with seizing an original wife's dowry."

The clan elder and all the Qin elders rose to their feet simultaneously. Not one aged face had any color left.

Under the laws of the Great Ying Dynasty, privately seizing a dowry was a litigable offense!

"Old Clan Elder — our evidence is more than sufficient. Physical evidence and witnesses are both in place. Were this truly brought before the magistrate, the Qin clan would lose without question."

"Once the suit is lost, the young men and women of your Qin clan — in their marriages..."

The Wei Great-Uncle let the sentence trail off.

The faces of the clan elder and elders grew even more stricken.

If it truly came to a lawsuit... their combined ages ran to hundreds of years, and they dared not even contemplate the outcome.

That foolish woman Feng!

Her selfishness had placed the entire Qin clan in this helpless position today.

"Mingfeng — truly, is there no room for further discussion?" The clan elder looked at Qin Mingfeng with a beseeching expression, after a long silence.

Qin Mingfeng cupped his hands and replied in a low, resolute voice: "Clan Elder — a melon forced from the vine is not sweet."

The clan elder's aged face filled instantly with defeat.

He had no choice but to acknowledge — however reluctantly — that Qin Mingfeng truly, firmly wanted to separate from the clan. This was not manipulation by the Wei family...

"Old Clan Elder — look at the bright side. Mingfeng's separation may not be a bad thing. It may well be a good one in the end!"

The clan elder had been serving as clan head his whole life — of course he understood the weight of those words from the Wei Great-Uncle.

But if he had a choice, he would far rather have had Qin Mingjie be the one to propose separation today.

A son raised by a concubine truly could not match a son raised by a great family's noble daughter...

"Clan Elder?" An elder, seeing the clan elder's expression waver, called out urgently.

The clan elder waved him silent, his face a picture of grey resignation. "We can hardly bring this to the magistrate's office against Mingfeng..."

That elder furrowed his grey brows and looked at Qin Mingfeng, still wanting to dissuade him. The clan elder stopped him.

The clan elder understood. They had chosen Qin Mingjie in those earlier years, and that had been the wrong choice. Now they must swallow the bitter fruit.

If they pressed Qin Mingfeng further to the point of estrangement, Qin Mingfeng had the right on his side — and the Xianyang Wei family and the Dongjin Wei family behind him.

Could the Qin clan still rely on a Qin Mingjie who was already on a downward slope?

They could not.

Better to settle matters cleanly now, while Qin Mingfeng had not yet become completely cold toward the Qin clan.

While there was still a sliver of warmth left.

Perhaps — if Qin Mingfeng's family soared upward — they might still look kindly on the shared Qin ancestor and be willing to lend a hand to other clan members who had never wronged them...

"Since it is so, let it be as Mingfeng wishes." The clan elder let out a deep sigh.

"Then let it be done today while the day is auspicious. Let the ancestral ceremony be performed." The Wei Great-Uncle said.

The clan elder wrinkled his face in misery. "Surely it need not be... quite so rushed? At least wait until Sixth Young Miss and Fifth Young Miss are married out first?"

chapters.title: Chapter 86
chapters.content:
The Separation Is Complete; Ruyin Will Wed from the New House

"Old Clan Elder — a good day found is better than a good day chosen. Let it be done today." Qin Mingfeng cupped his hands in a bow. "Everything needed for the ceremony has been prepared on Mingfeng's side."

The clan elder drew a deep breath.

Qin Mingjie's eyes narrowed.

What?

The separation today?

Even in the most urgent case, shouldn't he at least wait until his own Fifth Young Miss had been married off?

"Elder brother — are you really this impatient? You don't care about your own niece's face — my Fifth Young Miss — or even your own Sixth Young Miss's face?"

"If you make this separation happen before either of their weddings, how will they explain themselves at their husband's households?"

Qin Mingfeng gave him an indifferent glance.

"My Sixth Young Miss has nothing difficult to explain. She needs only say one thing: her stepgrandmother privately seized her birth grandmother's dowry."

"You—!" Qin Mingjie nearly leapt to his feet, his pale face flushing red with fury.

Qin Mingfeng turned away from him without a second look. For the first time, Qin Mingjie felt a sting of defeat before this elder brother who had spent half his life being made to feel worthless.

This feeling... was truly unbearable.

The clan elder, watching Qin Mingjie at such a critical juncture still daring to be domineering toward his elder brother, almost laughed despite himself — and felt afraid.

He was terrified that this Qin Mingjie, going back to scheme with his greedy and shameless mother Feng, might press Qin Mingfeng until he severed all ties with the Qin clan completely and brought the lawsuit to the magistrate's court. Then everything would be truly finished.

He was not alone in thinking this.

Two elders with particularly clear heads had already seen the same danger. They quickly said to the clan elder: "Clan Elder — since the separation has been settled, let it be as Mingfeng says: let today's auspicious day not be wasted. Let the ceremony be done today!"

As Qin Mingfeng himself had implied — the First Branch's separation had no meaningful impact on the First Branch.

The only First Branch member of marriageable age right now was Sixth Young Miss, and given the Jiang family's regard for her, the separation would change nothing.

The Fifth Young Miss of the Second Branch's husband's family, the Wang family, were a clan that valued propriety extremely highly.

The Fifth Young Miss would likely have a difficult time accounting for herself there.

That was why Qin Mingjie did not want the First Branch to separate before his daughter's wedding.

But the separation of the First Branch would have no material impact on the marriage prospects of other members of the broader Qin clan.

As long as Qin Mingfeng did not bring the case of his mother's misappropriated dowry to the magistrate.

The only ones who would suffer were the Second Branch — it had nothing much to do with the rest of the clan's families. One friend's death does not require another friend to die with him.

The clan elder canvassed the opinions of all the Qin elders.

People are, in the end, selfish.

Even the two elders who had once stood on Qin Mingjie's side had now thought it through.

All agreed that today was the day to complete the separation ceremony.

Since the man had already prepared for it — the sooner the better.

Because he had prepared in advance, all three of First Master Qin's sons were back at the household.

With the Wei family elders as witnesses, the First Branch of the Qin family completed the separation from the clan without incident.

Of course, this was only completing the ceremony within the clan.

What still remained was to determine the clan name, update the clan genealogy, establish an ancestral hall, and register with the authorities.

These things could be done gradually.

For now the property division had to be clearly settled.

Under Great Ying Dynasty law, the legitimate eldest son of the main branch was entitled to retain half of the family's shared resources.

Of the remaining resources, eighty percent was to be divided equally among the legitimate sons.

The remaining twenty percent was divided equally among the illegitimate sons.

But when the legitimate eldest of the main branch voluntarily proposed separation, he was required to yield forty percent of the half he would have been entitled to back to the main clan.

What Qin Mingfeng was entitled to take were the assets accumulated by the Qin ancestors.

As for the old patriarch's own private assets, the bulk of them were in Feng's hands — and filling the deficit from his use of Madam Wei's dowry would not even be enough. There was nothing else to think about.

As for the ancestral legacy, Qin Mingfeng placed no great importance on it. Converted to silver, it would amount to barely ten thousand taels.

Otherwise the old patriarch would never have coveted the enormous dowry of a Wei family bride, and gone against his conscience to marry her.

Of those ten thousand taels, four thousand had to be given over to the Qin clan.

Qin Mingfeng simply donated the remaining six thousand to the Qin clan as well, stating that it was for the education of impoverished clan children.

This gesture moved the clan elder and elders deeply.

And deepened their regret that he had separated.

The Old Matriarch had privately seized Madam Wei's dowry for decades — and for those decades Madam Wei's dowry properties and shops had continued generating income.

The clan elder had already stipulated that the Old Matriarch was to compensate Qin Mingfeng for all of it.

Qin Mingfeng declined to receive it. He told the clan elder and elders: "The shops and fields my mother left were not numerous. Let us calculate the annual income at one thousand taels."

"I will not take that money. I donate it to the clan as well. The clan can use it to buy more ceremonial land — to give better provision to the old, the sick, and the poor."

At that, the clan elder and the elders were moved to tears.

Even if the Old Matriarch had seized Madam Wei's dowry for thirty years — at one thousand taels a year, that was thirty thousand taels.

All thirty thousand taels going to the clan to buy ceremonial land — at current prices of ten taels per mu of good farmland, that was three thousand mu.

For the Qin clan, that was no small benefit.

The Qin clan had never been wealthy. Their elderly, widowed, and orphaned members were numerous, and providing for them was always a struggle.

In all fairness, the clan elder and the elders had indeed accepted many benefits from Qin Mingjie and his mother over the years. But the great majority of those benefits had gone toward the clan — very little had gone to themselves or their children.

That was also why they had dared, this time, not to stand entirely on Qin Mingjie's side.

Only Qin Mingjie leapt up in fury.

He pointed at Qin Mingfeng and roared: "Stop playing the magnanimous one! My mother's shops and fields weren't long since sold by the old patriarch..."

"Silence!"

Before he could finish, the clan elder stopped him with a thundering rebuke.

Qin Mingfeng said calmly: "Second Brother — even if they were sold by Father long ago and converted to silver, what does it matter? Father left a note that he would repay everything with his own private assets, did he not?"

"If Mother followed Father's instructions and used those private assets to buy back fields and shops, then there would have been continued income."

"Mingfeng is right!" The clan elder's sharp eyes fixed on Qin Mingjie. "This is a matter between your father and your mother."

"Even so, the income should only be calculated from the year Father died — that's twenty years at most!" Qin Mingjie argued.

Qin Mingfeng replied without haste: "But Father left instructions that he would bear all responsibility. And his private assets were sufficient at the time to fill the gap. From the time Mother took those assets, responsibility passed to her. The calculation is not difficult."

"Old Clan Elder," he said calmly, completing his thought, "one thousand taels per year is only Mingfeng's estimate. The clan may work out the precise figure directly with Mingjie and his mother."

Qin Mingjie nearly toppled over with fury.

Those old men of the clan were one and all insatiable — he and his mother were about to lose a layer of skin.

The clan elder had the full picture.

He also saw clearly that Qin Mingfeng's gesture was not entirely out of sympathy for the clan's impoverished members — he also intended to set the clan on Qin Mingjie and his mother.

This was understandable.

After being suppressed and humiliated by the Second Branch mother and sons for so many years — could separation alone settle the score in his heart?

Impossible. Not even a saint could manage that.

For the clan's sake, he, these old bones, was willing to serve as the sharp blade with which Qin Mingfeng took his revenge on Qin Mingjie and his mother!

After the proceedings, the Wei Great-Uncle praised Qin Mingfeng. "Mingfeng, you handled that perfectly. Setting the clan to collect that missing money is the best of all possible moves."

"You've earned the clan's gratitude, the clansmen's goodwill, and you don't have to do the dirty work yourself."

The Wei Fourth Grand-Uncle also stroked his beard with a smile. "Even if Qin Mingjie and his mother refuse to acknowledge that sum, it's a difficult situation."

"Mingfeng has separated — he won't have the leisure to wrangle endlessly with Qin Mingjie and his mother. Having the Qin clan wrangle with them is the best possible arrangement."

The Wei Grand-Uncle continued: "And there are even more benefits than that. Having given the clan such substantial gifts, the clan will now be more active than anyone in auditing Mingfeng's mother's dowry."

The other Wei elders nodded in agreement all around.

...

When Qin Ruyin learned that the family had separated from the Qin clan, she was astonished.

Her father and the Wei family elders had truly moved fast!

Not a shred of hesitation or dragging their feet — truly exhilarating.

Her maid Feng Mama said with a smile: "Our First Master is a man built for great things. He'd only been holding himself back all along to protect himself."

Qin Ruyin nodded with a broad grin.

"Oh — by the way, we can't let the Wang family not hear about the separation from the clan, can we?" Qin Ruyin thought of this and blinked with a mischievous gleam.

"Feng Mama, send a quick-witted person to get word to Wang Furen. She's a proud woman — if she hears it from some other lady first, she may well be angry enough to burst."

Feng Mama agreed with a smile.

She had noticed that the Fifth Young Miss had been making quite a few discreet moves lately. She hadn't yet caught anything serious enough to report to Ruyin, and had decided not to bother her — after all, the wedding was so close and there was so much to handle.

She had handled the minor things herself. What she couldn't decide on her own, she passed along to Li Yi.

Feng Mama had barely gone when Banjia came in to report: "Young Miss, the First Mistress is asking for you."

The Wei family womenfolk had enjoyed their midday meal in the Qin family's West Courtyard to their satisfaction and then bid their farewells to go rest at their inn.

Li Shi had made every effort to keep them, but the Wei Grand Maternal Aunt had said with a smile: "Everything for your family has been perfectly resolved — we can rest easy now!"

"Now that the separation is complete, and there are so many of us, we'd rather not stay and invite the contempt of those Second Branch mother and son."

The Wei Second Grand Maternal Aunt had said to Li Shi: "Once your whole family moves into the new house, come to us. We'll stay as many days as you like!"

Li Shi kept agreeing warmly, urging them to definitely come and stay a good long while.

"Mother!" When Qin Ruyin saw her mother, she gave a quick curtsy and pressed close. "You called for me?"

Li Shi's face was radiant with happiness, her eyes bright and shining — she could barely contain her excitement.

"Ruyin! We won!"

"Your mother is overjoyed! How many years has it been — only today does it feel like I've truly lived!"

Qin Ruyin was happy too.

When she had first arrived in this body, she had mistakenly thought her whole family were meek people who would not fight back, and she had steeled herself to fight alone.

But her family were in fact every one of them fighters.

Such major affairs as reclaiming the grandmother's dowry and separating from the clan — resolved just like that, smoothly.

"Oh goodness, look at me, I'm so excited I nearly forgot!" Li Shi took her youngest daughter's hands and looked at her with eyes sparkling. "Your father told me to tell you — you will not be married from this house. We have our own house now!"

"Your father bought it long ago and kept it secret from the whole family..."

"What?" Qin Ruyin was both astonished and overjoyed.

Father had already prepared a new house before the separation was even finalized!

Then she would not be leaving from the West Courtyard of this old Qin household — she would depart from their very own Qin family home!

"Good child — you truly have fortune on your side! On the day you are married, your mother can preside over your wedding rites as the true mistress of the house!" Li Shi said this, and her tears fell.

This was Li Shi's deepest wish.

Her eldest daughter Rujin and second daughter Ruxiu had been married out with Tong Shi presiding as household mistress over their wedding ceremonies.

Now at last, with her youngest daughter, she could fulfill a mother's dream...

Qin Ruyin held her mother and comforted her tenderly.

...

At the Jiang mansion.

Two days hence would be the great occasion of the Fourth Master Jiang's wedding. The Jiang mansion had already begun hanging lanterns and decorations today, dressed in festivity.

Today was a day off from court. Jiang Jiuxiao had just come out from the Grand Matriarch's courtyard when his other personal attendant, Qian Er, came hurrying over.

"My lord, Prince An has arrived — he is already in the outer court..."

chapters.title: Chapter 87
chapters.content:
Prince An Wants to Take Her Away

"Prince An?" Jiang Jiuxiao's refined eyes narrowed slightly.

Feng Mama had recently had word sent to Li Yi about the small private moves the Fifth Young Miss of the Qin family had been making these past days.

She had been doing everything she could to get a message to Prince An.

And now Prince An had arrived in person at his household.

"To the outer court."

Qian Er said with concern: "My lord, Prince An coming to see you at this moment — I fear it cannot be good news."

"Would Prince An go to the trouble of visiting the Jiang mansion for good news?"

Jiang Jiuxiao wore a deep green bamboo-leaf brocade everyday robe. He held his right hand level before his chest and gave his wide sleeve a light shake. "Go personally and select a few capable men — keep a close watch on the Qin family's side these next few days."

Qian Er stiffened and answered with a respectful bow.

Jiang Jiuxiao went to receive the guest in the outer court.

Prince An wore white python-embroidered brocade. He walked with one hand clasped behind his back, his face like jade, his bearing cultured and serene.

Behind him walked two young men in equally splendid dress.

From a distance, Jiang Jiuxiao had already detected that those two elegantly dressed young men were formidable fighters. He glanced at them without expression and then fixed his gaze on Prince An.

He then stepped forward to bow in greeting.

"Your Highness Prince An graces this humble dwelling — we are honored by your presence."

Prince An nodded with a faint smile, his gaze sweeping Jiang Jiuxiao over once, warmly.

He said, as if in jest: "This prince has heard that Lord Jiang's wedding is the day after tomorrow — such a joyful occasion ought to show on his face. Why does Lord Jiang look somewhat displeased?"

Though spoken as banter, these words in the ears of those who knew better would make it sound as though Jiang Jiuxiao, the minister, was displeased at Prince An, a royal of heaven's blood, coming to call.

Jiang Jiuxiao lowered his eyes and said mildly: "Your Highness jests. This minister has been putting things off until this age to take a new wife. The joy is so great I can't sleep for it."

"In the days leading up to welcoming the bride I have been attending to every detail personally. Your Highness sees me looking less than well and thinks my spirits are low — in truth, it is an excess of joy."

He and Prince An had always kept a cool distance. Prince An would appear at private banquets, but Jiang Jiuxiao never cultivated excessive familiarity with him.

The Jiang family were pure ministers — loyal to the emperor alone.

Beyond the reigning emperor and the crown prince, the Jiang family would not grow close with any prince or king.

This was the reason successive emperors had always trusted the Jiang family.

And Prince An had always presented himself as gentle, cultured, and unruffled.

So Prince An opening with words of attack on his very first line — not even bothering to maintain the pretense — was somewhat surprising to Jiang Jiuxiao.

But hearing his answer, Prince An's eyes flashed briefly.

Nonsense.

The information his own people had gathered was nothing like what this man was saying...

"Your Highness comes at this hour — there must be a matter to discuss?" Jiang Jiuxiao's gaze met Prince An's evenly.

Prince An smiled without committing to a reply.

Jiang Jiuxiao said: "May I ask Your Highness to step to the study?"

Prince An nodded and followed Jiang Jiuxiao to his outer-court study.

After they were seated as host and guest, fragrant tea and pastries were brought in order.

Prince An, coming in and seeing the Jiang mansion already decked in festive red and lanterns, and then entering Jiang Jiuxiao's study to see it decorated with many red objects as well, furrowed his brow slightly.

Looking at things this way, the Jiang family truly was lavishing care on this Sixth Young Miss of the Qin First Branch...

This would be somewhat difficult to handle.

Difficult as it was — it still had to be handled.

After a few pleasantries, Prince An's expression settled into gravity.

"Lord Jiang — this prince has never been one for beating around the bush. I come today with a specific request, and I hope Lord Jiang will see his way to granting it."

Jiang Jiuxiao raised his teacup with noble composure and waited.

He had known for a long time that Prince An was not nearly as gentle and unruffled as he appeared.

He went this month to pray for the Empress Dowager's health, and the next month to pray for the Emperor's wellbeing, and occasionally spent half a year praying for the peace of the common people in some temple or monastery — drawing universal praise from court and populace alike.

But those things were only the surface.

This man had very great ambitions.

Recently, with the Emperor's health declining, the imperial princes and kings were all quietly making their own moves in the dark.

Prince An beginning to privately cultivate court ministers at this juncture was hardly impossible.

"Lord Jiang — this prince's inner household still has one vacancy for a side consort."

Jiang Jiuxiao's gaze sharpened in an instant.

Prince An wanted to form a marriage alliance with the Jiang family?
