He told her: "Just prepare whatever you feel comfortable with — what you need to focus on is setting aside more for our two sons' betrothal gifts. The rest is on me."

"I will do whatever you say, my lord! What I had before was... it really was too little. I didn't think they had any hope of marrying into good families..."

Third Master Qin said: "It's not impossible for them to marry well — it all depends on them. Both of them are still young — one is barely past twenty, the other barely seventeen. There is no rush."

"Mm!" Zhou Shi nodded heartily, her eyes shining. "I'm not rushing either — I'm just counting on my two sons to have a change of heart and truly make something of themselves!"

"You won't need to worry about that — Elder Brother has already spoken to me about it, and he wants them to put in serious effort these next two years and try to pass the clerk's examination."

Zhou Shi's eyes lit up, then worry came rushing back. "But... will Rong Guang and Rong Feng agree?"

Third Master Qin nodded. "I talked to them for most of last night — they're both willing."

"Amitabha Buddha! Bless them, bless them, the ancestors bless them!" Zhou Shi rattled off her prayers in a jumble of excitement.

Third Master Qin watched with amusement but did not interrupt her nonsensical chanting and flailing about.

"All right — once everything is packed up, let's go and deliver the house-warming gift to Elder Brother and Sister-in-Law." Third Master Qin said, and Zhou Shi nodded emphatically.

"Oh, and my lord — Yin Niang is getting married tomorrow. Surely our family won't go home tonight? We should stay at Elder Brother's house to help!"

Seeing she had even thought of this, Third Master Qin felt truly comforted, and told her: "Your willingness is the best thing of all."

Zhou Shi immediately said: "Of course I'm willing — as long as Sister-in-Law doesn't find me too much trouble!"

She was now also willing to follow Third Master Qin in calling the First Branch couple Elder Brother and Elder Sister-in-Law.

One thought suddenly struck her, filling her with resentment again.

"My lord, shouldn't we move out soon as well? That old witch Feng Shi is still sick in bed and won't settle down — she sent an old crone over here first thing this morning to sneer and mock and push us out.

"We don't have a house yet, so we could rent a small place to make do for now. After Yin Niang's wedding, I'll take money and go buy ourselves a small house to live in."

Third Master Qin heard this and smiled. "Then after we deliver the house-warming gift to Elder Brother today, we can come back and pack for the move."

Zhou Shi was stunned. "My lord?"

"Before Elder Brother bought his house, he spoke to me... and with his connections, I also managed to buy a small house for our family.

"Let me say first — it really is small. Only three courtyards, since my funds are somewhat limited..."

"My lord! Having a house at all is wonderful! Three courtyards is not small! We are in the capital — finding a three-courtyard residence is already remarkable. I'm not particular!"

Zhou Shi's voice rose several notches, her face alight with excitement.

Heavens above!

Who would have imagined she'd live to see a day like this — not even in her dreams!

"My lord, tell me how much you spent, and I'll make it up to you! Don't refuse — I only just found out from the children that you have actually been quietly doing great things all these years... Going out into the world, you need money too."

Third Master Qin sighed inwardly, but his smile deepened as he held her hands. "Keep your money for yourself and the children. I'm a grown man — I can hardly be spending your money."

"My lord, now you're treating me like a stranger!" Zhou Shi would not hear of it.

Third Master Qin, seeing her insist, conceded at last: "Then set aside some money for Madam Lu — call it compensation from you."

Zhou Shi's face went red at once, and she murmured: "I'm afraid she won't..."

"Don't worry — she understands things more clearly than either of us. If she won't accept the money as compensation, then give it to Ru Yan and Ru He as spending money for their trousseau chests."

In truth, Third Master Qin had already privately given Madam Lu one thousand taels of silver as compensation — in addition to the small shop he had bought for her.

He was not a wealthy man and could only manage one thousand taels for now, intending to compensate her further when his circumstances improved.

But Madam Lu was a woman of firm dignity — after accepting the thousand taels, she had made clear that they were now fully quits, and there was no need for him to give her anything more.

"Then I'll choose a day and go to see Madam Lu myself." Zhou Shi thought it over and said.

Third Master Qin nodded.

This was a matter between his wife and Madam Lu — it was not his place to interfere.

With the Third Branch couple having untied the knot between them, the Second Branch's side of things flared up again.

Old Madam Qin had taken to her sickbed, so Qin Ming Jie had invited the Fourth Branch's wife, Madam Yin, to preside over Qin Ru Yue's wedding ceremonies.

Qin Ru Yue, of course, was not about to accept this quietly.

She wrote a long letter and had it sent to her maternal grandmother.

Her grandmother had known nothing of what her daughter, Tong Shi, had gone through in the Qin household — and when she learned of it, she was so furious she nearly stopped breathing.

Once she had calmed down, she immediately summoned all her sons and daughters-in-law and drove in high dudgeon straight to the Qin compound.

Old Madam Qin was no longer in any condition to receive visitors.

Qin Ming Jie was left to steel himself and receive his enraged in-laws personally.

chapters.title: Qin Fifth Niang Has Finally Gotten to Prince An
chapters.content:
Before Qin Ming Jie could even bow and offer greetings to Tong's Old Grandmother, she pointed a finger at his face and sobbed out a torrent of curses calling him a heartless wretch.

The Tong family had been an eminent clan for hundreds of years, and Tong's Old Grandmother was herself of very distinguished birth.

Qin Ming Jie had never imagined that this high-born mother-in-law of his — once the pride of all well-bred young ladies — would come at him the moment she arrived and berate him to his face without ceremony.

And the Tong family had come in considerable force.

Not a scrap of dignity had been spared for him.

His face darkened immediately, and his acknowledgements of the Tong uncles and others were perfunctory at best.

Tong's Old Grandmother had finished venting and now demanded to see her granddaughter Qin Ru Yue.

Qin Ming Jie had no choice but to send someone to summon Qin Ru Yue.

The moment Qin Ru Yue arrived, Tong's Old Grandmother seized her and wept over her — lamenting her bitter fate: getting married the next day with her mother still locked away in the countryside.

Qin Ru Yue understood inwardly that her grandmother and the Tong party had come to stand up for her mother — not for her.

If they were truly here for her sake, the Tong family would have come long before this, not waited until she had been forced to send that letter herself.

Of course, the Tong family was also standing up for her mother because they had no wish to see that Rui Niang benefiting from the situation.

If that Rui Niang were to have a son in the future, her good father would surely shower affection on the child as well — which would harm her brothers' interests.

The Tong family could disregard her, but they had interests bound up with those brothers of hers.

Qin Ming Jie was making significant gestures from the side, silently urging Qin Ru Yue to quickly find a way to soothe Tong's Old Grandmother.

Qin Ru Yue gave a cold inward laugh — but outwardly she looked gentle and obedient as she said to her grandmother: "Grandmother, please don't grieve. My mother's luck has been poor — she was caught up in trouble because of the matter of that Seventh Sister who left through the clan split.

"My grandmother and my father have spoken of it before — they only wanted my mother to retreat to the countryside for a time...

"It may be that with so many things happening in our family of late, and with Grandmother's health declining, Father has been so overwhelmed that he simply forgot to send someone to bring Mother back to the house."

She needed to use her maternal grandmother's family to bring her mother back home — but she could not afford to offend her own father.

Her paternal family, after all, as long as their interests remained intertwined, would be sure to stand up for her.

Her maternal grandmother's brow furrowed slightly upon hearing her granddaughter speak this way.

Qin Ru Yue's heart lurched — she hurriedly let her gaze fly toward her father with an expression of fear.

Tong's Old Grandmother and Qin Ru Yue's several uncles and aunts-by-marriage all saw it, and they came to understand why she had spoken as she had.

Tong's Grand Uncle wore a cold expression as he regarded Qin Ming Jie. "Brother-in-Law, since Yue Niang has put it this way, our Tong family — out of consideration for her being married tomorrow — will not press the matter with you.

"Brother-in-Law, send someone at once — bring my sister home today! It is only proper that a daughter's mother preside over her own wedding ceremony!"

"Quite! Having an aunt by marriage preside — what kind of arrangement is that?" Tong's Second Aunt-by-Marriage suddenly cut in.

Qin Ming Jie's gaze hardened, and he shot Qin Ru Yue a dark, sinister look.

He had discussed this matter with Old Madam Qin the night before and only reached a decision then.

He had only told the Fourth Branch couple and Qin Ru Yue.

The Fourth Branch couple could not possibly have spoken to the Tong family about it...

Qin Ru Yue was so terrified by that venomous look from her father that her heart nearly stopped — her mind raced frantically for a countermeasure.

She also silently cursed that Second Aunt who had let it slip.

Though Qin Ming Jie suspected his daughter, this was not the moment to make a scene.

He understood: the Tong family still cared about their own dignity. Having allowed the elder of the family — his old mother-in-law — to curse him out thoroughly, they now simply wanted him to capitulate and bring Tong Shi back.

In truth, Old Madam Qin had also pushed herself out of her sickbed the night before to urge him to bring Tong Shi back quickly to manage affairs.

But he was now treating that Rui Niang as though she were his life itself, and she had only recently become pregnant — barely over a month along.

If Tong Shi returned at this juncture, with her methods, that Rui Niang would be no match for her.

The child in Rui Niang's belly would likely not survive Tong Shi's machinations either — and naturally he could not bear that!

He had made his concern clear to Old Madam Qin, and for the sake of the grandchild Rui Niang carried — the child of the son's favourite woman — Old Madam Qin had capitulated.

After all, Qin Ru Yue was just a granddaughter.

Even if she was legitimate-born, that grandchild in Rui Niang's belly had been conceived by the son's most cherished woman!

With his mother agreeing, Qin Ming Jie had naturally not wanted to bring Tong Shi back.

But he had not expected the Tong family, who had said nothing upon learning why Tong Shi was sent to the countryside, to come storming through his door in such force this time.

After the rupture of Lady Sun's marriage and the cold shoulder the Crown Prince's side had given his eldest son, his footing was growing ever more precarious.

He certainly could not afford to fall out with the Tong family right now.

"Grand Brother-in-Law is absolutely right. It had been Ming Jie's intention all along to bring Yue Niang's mother back to preside over her wedding — I was only just sitting here thinking of it...

"It seems your party arrived, Grand Mother-in-Law, before I had a chance to act."

Qin Ming Jie's words sounded fine, but not a single member of the Tong family believed them.

It was nothing more than two families playing a game — and Qin Ming Jie had lost.

......

Zǐ Jǐng Lane.

The Qin Residence.

Third Master Qin, Qin Ming Sheng, brought his whole family with generous gifts to warm his elder brother's new house.

As they arrived, they found the street in front of the Qin Residence already lined with many carriages.

Word had reached well-connected official and noble households that the Jiang family had come early in the morning with generous gifts to warm the Qin First Branch's new home — and so various households had sprung into action.

The Ministry of Works colleagues of the First Elder in particular — led by the Minister of Works himself — had all come to the Qin residence to bring house-warming gifts.

The Minister of Works was in fine spirits about the whole matter.

Because of the First Elder's remarkable achievements while holding a lowly fifth-rank sinecure post, the Emperor had praised him and both his deputies at some length.

The First Elder was also a man who got things done — and the Minister of Works very much liked that.

He was the head of the Ministry of Works, and when he showed esteem for the First Elder, the others naturally had to follow their superior's lead...

Zhou Shi, seeing how the Qin First Branch had suddenly become so sought-after and influential in the capital, was filled with envy.

She tugged at Third Master Qin's sleeve and murmured: "Heavens... Elder Brother has truly become formidable! Just look at all this grandeur..."

Third Master Qin was genuinely happy for his elder brother as well, the smile in his eyes warm. "This is what Elder Brother deserves!"

The women of the inner household naturally knew nothing of the details.

All those years his elder brother had been quietly investing his energy in painstaking work — all of it to arrive at this day!

And even so, it owed something to the future Qin son-in-law, Commissioner Jiang.

Without Commissioner Jiang giving him a hand — what reason would the retired Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, that old gentleman, have had to present before the Emperor's desk all the unrecognised achievements Elder Brother had accumulated over the years, right before his retirement?

The First Elder of the Qin family was very glad to see Third Master Qin's whole family arrive.

With so many guests in the house, he had already drafted even the Wei family cousin-brothers to help him receive visitors.

When Third Master Qin and his two nephews came over, he quickly pressed them into service receiving guests as well.

Qin Rong Guang and Qin Rong Feng, though they were commoners, were the sons of their host's own family — it was perfectly appropriate for them to receive the young gentlemen who had come with their elders.

Zhou Shi watched her two sons, though nervous, muster up their courage and go to help their uncle receive guests, and felt her eyes go hot with emotion.

She herself was leading her maids and servants carrying the gifts to the back courtyard.

Lady Li, seeing her come, was only happy — she had not the slightest expectation of her bringing anything generous.

But when she saw the scale of what Zhou Shi had brought, she was taken aback.

Zhou Shi pulled her aside and offered her an earnest and wholehearted apology...

Lady Li was magnanimous as well. Seeing Zhou Shi acknowledging her wrongs and willing to change, she comforted her: "Our two families are true flesh and blood — what grudge can last past the next morning?

"Say no more of it — today I am dying of busyness; the best help you can give me is to join in receiving the guests!"

Zhou Shi nodded emphatically and agreed with great cheer.

The Wang Residence.

Wang Furen, returning from the Qin compound, got into a blazing row with the Master.

She wanted to dissolve the engagement — the Master was furious and demanded to know whether she wanted to destroy the Wang family's hundred-year reputation.

Wang Furen shot back that it was his insistence on having everything that had destroyed the Wang family's hundred-year reputation.

The husband and wife raged at each other and at last simmered down.

As for the engagement with the Qin family, the Master had come to regret it himself by now.

But calling off an engagement on the very eve of the wedding was indefensible by any measure.

And they had no grounds — no evidence of any misdeed on Qin Fifth Niang's part.

He absolutely could not do something that would so shame the Wang family's name.

Wang Furen said to him in a fury: "Your wanting everything all at once is going to destroy our Mian Er in the end!"

The Master, upon hearing this, immediately called out: "Fine! Let's bring Mian Er here — let Mian Er speak for himself!"

And so Wang Huai Mian was summoned by a servant from Wang Furen's courtyard.

When he heard the cause of his parents' dispute, he frowned and looked at Wang Furen: "Mother, Father is right. Tomorrow is the wedding — going to the Qin family today to call it off is entirely unreasonable on our part."

"Besides, the Qin family's troubles all arose from specific causes — what does any of that have to do with Qin Fifth Niang, a woman of the inner household? She is a good girl!"

Ever since he had investigated through multiple channels and confirmed that the Qin Sixth Niang of the First Branch had nothing remarkable about her origins, he had lost interest in her.

So what if her father had recently been promoted? So what if her father's maternal family had come to the capital to help them preside over the clan split?

The very fact that they had needed the Wei family to come manage the clan split showed that their family was still weak.

The Qin Second Branch was still more than capable of keeping the First Branch firmly in check.

It was just that the Qin Second Branch hadn't bothered.

As for Qin Fifth Niang — not to mention her stunning looks, she had also privately written him a letter full of tender feeling. That foolish girl was willing to tell him anything.

She had even told him beforehand that she was bringing twenty thousand taels of spending money in her trousseau chest...

And had made clear it was for him to use.

He might not care to use it himself, but his children certainly could.

His mother also prided herself on coming from a family of scholars — which sounded well enough, but left her children in threadbare poverty...

He never wanted his own sons to endure the same kind of pinched, meagre life he had lived!

The Qin First Branch had what, exactly?

The Qin Sixth Niang had even needed the Qin Second Branch to supplement her dowry — what kind of family was that!

Wang Huai Mian was, after all, only a scholar — not well-connected enough to catch all the news. And with his wedding the next day he was frantically busy, and no one had thought to pass on to him what had nothing to do with him.

Had he known that the Qin First Branch had just moved the whole family into a spacious house on Zǐ Jǐng Lane the day before, he would certainly not still be thinking of the First Branch as poor and shabby.

"Mian Er? Is that what you truly mean?" Wang Furen was silent a long while, and when she looked at her son again her eyes were full of disappointment.

Wang Huai Mian frowned. "Mother, of course I mean it! And our Wang family's hundred-year reputation cannot be destroyed by my hands!"

The Master was very gratified that his son cared so much for the family's honour — though he had some misgivings as well.

He could only hope that after his son married Qin Fifth Niang, the Qin Second Branch would not cause any more trouble!

Wang Furen drew a slow, deep breath and looked with grave seriousness at the second son she was most proud of. "Mian Er, let Mother ask you one more time — you truly will not regret this?"

As long as her son said he wanted to dissolve the engagement, she would throw her dignity aside and beg the Qin Second Branch to agree to breaking it off.

"I certainly will not regret it!" Wang Huai Mian said without hesitation.

He had one more secret: Qin Fifth Niang was no ordinary girl — she could have prophetic dreams.

This secret he would tell no one!

Just the night before, he had dispatched someone to pass a message from Qin Fifth Niang to Prince An's side. In less than half a month, most likely, his father's position would see a promotion.

And besides — he did want to see what kind of grand affair Jiang the Fourth and Qin Sixth Niang would make of their wedding...

chapters.title: Today She Is Getting Married
chapters.content:
The midday meal at the Qin residence on Zǐ Jǐng Lane was a lively affair.

Fortunately, both of the Qin sons' wives were capable women.

Even when yet more guests arrived after the earlier wave, they managed to prepare a feast that left nothing to be criticized.

After the midday meal, the Jiang family sent someone to the Qin family with news.

That very morning, Jiang Jiuhao had received his official promotion document.

Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

Second rank, first grade.

The highest post in the Ministry of Personnel.

After the previous Minister, Elder Cheng, had retired, the position had sat vacant for several days.

But as far as the court was concerned, the answer had been clear for some time.

Elder Cheng had long admired Jiang Jiuhao.

And in his later years, it was Jiang Jiuhao who had been running the Ministry's main affairs.

The document simply hadn't come down yet — and until it did, there was always a chance of a surprise.

After all, it was not unheard of for the Emperor to issue an edict personally appointing someone to head one of the Six Ministries.

The court had been watching and waiting.

Now the other shoe had finally dropped.

The Qin household was overjoyed without exception.

A future son-in-law receiving a promotion the day before the wedding — what a delightful and unexpected piece of good fortune!

In the eyes of those who believed in fate, this meant the bride, Qin Ru Yin, was born under a prosperous star — a star that brought good fortune and blessings to her husband.

The Wei family was equally happy for Qin Ru Yin.

The guests who had come to warm the house had also brought trousseau gifts for Qin Ru Yin.

Upon hearing the good news from the Jiang family, they all felt as though they had shared in the celebration, and their joy was mingled with envy.

Other households that had been sitting on the fence, upon learning that Jiang Jiuhao's promotion document had officially come through, all sent their stewards hurrying to the Qin residence with house-warming gifts — along with trousseau additions for Qin Ru Yin.

As a general rule, gifts were to be presented in the first half of the morning.

Now that it was well past the midday meal, each of these latecoming households found their own excuse.

Lady Li had no particular wish to accept gifts from those who only came to flatter the powerful — every single one of them was sizing things up before committing.

But the Wei family's Grand Elder Aunt persuaded her.

"Accept all of them. Never mind what those households are thinking — accepting the gift makes no enemies. As for the return of favours, surely you won't have trouble finding opportunities?"

Lady Li knew this was sound reasoning.

Her husband had only just been promoted to fourth rank, and he worked in the gruelling Ministry of Works — she could not afford to make enemies.

As the common saying went: the king of hell may be easy to deal with — it's his imps that are hard to manage.

Fortunately, the Wei family had come in large numbers, with many young women and brides-in-law among them.

Lady Li enlisted their help, and the recording of gifts and arranging of presents was carried out with perfect order.

The most pressing matter for the Qin family at this point was sorting out Qin Ru Yin's trousseau.

When they had moved, Qin Ru Yin's trousseau alone had taken up most of the West Courtyard.

And today had brought in yet more trousseau additions — all of which were placed in the West Courtyard as well.

At the Qin residence on Shun Yi Lane.

Tong Shi had only just returned home when she heard the news of Jiang Jiuhao's appointment as Minister of Personnel.

The Tong family, staying at the Qin compound for Qin Ru Yue's wedding the next day, had not yet departed.

So when Tong Shi returned through the main gate, Qin Ru Yue herself had come with her people to welcome her mother at the gate.

"My child! What fortune has deserted you so completely?"

Tong Shi had grown considerably thinner. But seeing her daughter looking equally haggard, she felt a pang in her heart.

"Jiang the Fourth has received his appointment as Minister of Personnel on the very eve of his wedding...

"That makes him the youngest Minister of Personnel in the entire history of our Great Ying dynasty!"

Originally, this man was supposed to have been her own son-in-law! The husband of her Yue Niang!...

How had every stroke of good luck landed squarely on that Qin Sixth Niang of the First Branch?

It was clearly meant to be her Fifth Niang's good fortune — that Qin Sixth Niang must have stolen it from her Fifth Niang...

Qin Ru Yue burned with hatred deep inside!

She had already been reborn into this life with foreknowledge and had secretly laid plenty of schemes — so why did one piece of good luck after another keep falling into Qin Ru Yin's lap?

Could it truly be that she was unable to change her own tragic and pitiable fate from her previous life?

No!

In this life she absolutely would not end up as tragic and pitiable as she had before!

Prince An's side must surely have already set things in motion!

She would wait.

She would wait and watch Qin Ru Yin make a fool of herself.

Watch her — a woman who should have been a Minister of Personnel's wife — ultimately sink to become a mere concubine in Prince An's household.

A concubine was nothing but a slave.

......

After the evening meal, the Qin residence on Zǐ Jǐng Lane received yet another distinguished guest.

The eminent monk Huì Qīng came with his fellow disciple, the abbess Huì Yuán, to offer blessings to the Qin family — primarily for Qin Ru Yin, who was about to be married.

The reason given was that the methods for repairing and dredging waterways that the First Elder of the Qin family had devised had saved the lives of countless common people...

And so on the occasion of his daughter's wedding, he had come to offer her his blessings.

As for Huì Yuán — she was the most gifted reader of faces among them all.

Having heard that the Wei family had brought many young ladies to see Qin Ru Yin off at her wedding, she divined that one among them had a karmic connection with her.

And so she had come along with her elder fellow-disciple Huì Qīng.

Hearing this, the First Elder of the Qin family at once ordered an incense altar to be set up.

Huì Qīng first blessed the Qin household as a whole, then offered a separate blessing for Qin Ru Yin specifically.

Huì Yuán, meanwhile, read the faces of the young ladies in Lady Li's flower hall.

In the end, she selected one of the Wei family's young ladies to be her lay disciple.

She only needed to observe a vegetarian diet on the first and fifteenth of each month and spend an hour reciting Buddhist scriptures in the shrine room on those two days.

The Wei Grand Elder Aunt was filled with joy — it was her very own little granddaughter, Wei Zi Yi.

The name of Abbess Huì Yuán was known to every family of any standing in the entire Great Ying dynasty.

To have a karmic connection with her, and even to be taken on as her lay disciple — what an honour that was!

A lay disciple only had her name recorded — she was free to marry as she wished.

Now that Wei Zi Yi had become Abbess Huì Yuán's lay disciple, far from affecting her marriage prospects, it would actually enhance them.

Word would likely reach the noble households of the capital before the next day was out — any family with a son of suitable age would be scrambling to send a matchmaker.

Wei Zi Yi herself was delighted as well — she was a clever girl and understood perfectly well what this meant.

She said privately to her grandmother that this was all thanks to her Sister Yin Niang's reflected glory...

After reading the faces of the Wei family's young ladies, Abbess Huì Yuán also mentioned that she had a half-teacher's karmic tie with the Qin Fourth Young Miss.

As it was already growing late, Lady Li invited both masters to stay the night.

Both declined graciously.

Abbess Huì Yuán thought for a moment and expressed her wish to say a few words to the Qin Fourth Young Miss.

Feng Mama, who attended Qin Ru Yin, whispered a few words into her ear.

Qin Ru Yin then had Feng Mama hurry to attend to Qin Ru Yan and tell her not to be afraid — just to speak truthfully.

Feng Mama was inwardly full of admiration for her young mistress's quickness and cleverness, and went to Qin Ru Yan's side and murmured to her softly.

......

Huì Qīng and Huì Yuán spent about an hour at the Qin residence before departing, the fellow disciples going to an inn together.

Jiang Jiuhao was already at the inn waiting for them.

Because Qin Ru Yin's wedding was the next day, the whole Qin household went to bed late.

Qin Ru Jin and Qin Ru Xiu did not go to their own arranged rooms that night — both of them crowded into Qin Ru Yin's room instead.

The three sisters talked for a long while, until at last the eldest, Ru Jin, fell quiet.

Qin Ru Yin considered a moment and then said: "Elder Sister, these past few days you've been home you've only been sharing good news — but I can see something is still not quite right with you."

Qin Ru Jin looked up at her little sister and gave a small shake of her head. "You're overthinking it, Yin Niang — tomorrow is your happy day; you shouldn't be worrying about anyone else..."

Qin Ru Xiu suddenly looked at Qin Ru Yin and asked: "Yin Niang — I nearly forgot to ask — still no sign of your monthly visiting?"

"Which?" Qin Ru Yin was baffled for a moment.

Qin Ru Xiu, seeing her staring back like a goose with its head full of straw, nearly burst out laughing. "What else? That thing — the one that comes every month!"

Qin Ru Yin let out an "oh."

So that was what she was asking about.

She gave a grin and shook her head without a care: "Not the slightest hint of it coming..." She added a moment later: "Which is all for the better!"

Qin Ru Xiu felt almost provoked into laughter by her. "And you don't mind? Ru Yan is younger than you and has already had it for over a year!"

Qin Ru Yin spread her hands. "I can't make it come if it doesn't want to!"

Inwardly she was actually pleased — later it came, the less suffering for her.

This was not the era she had once lived in, and the sanitary products here were genuinely too dreadful to endure...

Elder Sister Qin Ru Jin, hearing this, also frowned with worry.

"Though it's true all of us sisters take after Mother and are late like her, Jiang's family won't know that — I'm afraid your mother-in-law may misunderstand you..."

Ru Jin was a woman of experience — she had been late herself, and with nothing conceived yet, her mother-in-law had scolded her more times than she could count.

Qin Ru Xiu arched her brows, gave a cold snort, and said: "Mother was late too and had six daughters! I've had a son and a daughter both — what of it? Only a petty, narrow-minded mother-in-law with no sense would talk such nonsense!"

She was defending Ru Jin's honour.

Qin Ru Yin caught the meaning and looked at her elder sister with concern.

"Elder Sister, now that Elder Brother-in-Law has returned — are you two all right? Have you discussed the matter of adopting a child?"

Ru Jin had not been willing to bring it up earlier, so she had not pressed. And besides, Ru Jin had been busy helping Lady Li with the wedding preparations — there had been no time for quiet conversation.

Tonight was perfect — three sisters together — now they could have a proper talk.

Her Elder Brother-in-Law had come back today with Elder Sister, and his manner had seemed fine.

He was attentive to her Elder Sister and would not rest until he had taken her arm on the steps to help her along.

"Don't worry about me — my husband and I are perfectly well. After listening to you that time, we had it all out together." Ru Jin smiled a little.

She was speaking the truth, at that.

Though...

"Did Brother-in-Law agree to it? Where is he thinking of finding a child to adopt?" Ru Xiu also immediately asked.

Elder Sister had not told her about this either.

She had wanted to ask, but every time things got busy and she forgot.

Ru Jin nodded. "He did agree to adopt — it's just that... the choice of child is something we're still working out together."

In other words, they had not yet settled on a child.

These things could not be rushed.

Ru Xiu nodded as well. "As long as you and your husband are of one mind, that is what matters most. As for choosing a child, you really cannot rush it — take your time."

Qin Ru Yin had not missed the shadow that flashed and disappeared in her elder sister's eyes.

A pang went through her heart.

Qin Ru Yin was taken aback.

This feeling — it was not hers.

It must be the original soul's emotion.

She must have cared so very deeply for her eldest sister!

This pure and simple sisterhood moved her, and she felt both wistful and grateful.

Grateful that she now had so many such wonderful sisters!

She was not yet married and away from home — even if she was worried about Elder Sister, there was little she could do.

But once she had married Jiang Jiuhao, she would be a lady of standing.

Then, like Second Sister, she would be someone Elder Sister could speak to openly about matters she could not bring up in front of a younger unmarried girl.

There was no hurry.

After the three sisters talked a little while longer, Ru Jin urged the two younger ones to get some sleep.

"Tomorrow is Yin Niang's big day — you cannot stay up too late, or you'll be worn out!"

Qin Ru Yin and Second Sister Ru Xiu were still giggling as they settled down, and Ru Jin carefully tucked the quilt in around Qin Ru Yin, who was sleeping on the innermost side.

The moment the cock crew, Qin Ru Yin was shaken awake by her Second Sister Ru Xiu.

She opened her eyes in a daze — her Second Sister was already fully dressed and groomed, and her Elder Sister was dressed and ready too, at this very moment smiling at her with eyes full of warmth.

"Up now — there is no end of things to do today!"

Qin Ru Yin was still muzzy-headed with sleep, but when she heard Elder Sister's words it finally hit her, a moment behind.

Oh goodness!

Today was her wedding day!

chapters.title: The Wedding is Imminent
chapters.content:
"What do I need to do?" Qin Ru Yin sat up on the bed, somewhat at a loss — and a little nervous.

Twice the soul, first time a bride — the fact that she was holding herself together this well was already quite something.

"You just need to be a good bride today — there's not much you actually need to do." Ru Xiu said with a grin, watching her.

Ru Jin held a handkerchief over her lips and smiled. "Better said: today, whatever you are told to do, you do."

In the middle of the sisters' exchange, Lady Li came in.

She had been too busy the day before — receiving guests bearing gifts, and then accepting the Jiang family's betrothal eve gifts — and had not managed to have a proper word with her little daughter.

"Mother is here? Things are already in full swing outside, I imagine?" Seeing her mother come, Ru Jin quickly led her sisters in a bow, and asked.

Lady Li nodded.

Marrying off a daughter — the daughter was going to someone else's home.

As a mother, her face and eyes were already brimming with reluctance.

"Your two sisters-in-law are outside receiving guests, and your Great Maternal Aunt and your oldest maternal cousin's wife are overseeing the major affairs... so I managed to slip away for a moment to say a few words to Yin Niang."

Qin Ru Yin's heart ached with its own reluctance. She called out "Mother" in her sweetest voice and, still in only her inner garments, pressed over to her mother's side and wrapped both arms around her waist.

"My child!" Lady Li's composure broke in an instant, and Ru Jin and Ru Xiu, watching their mother's grief at parting, felt their own eyes redden.

It took them back to their own weddings, when their mother had been just as loath to let them go.

Ru Jin was the first to collect herself. She dismissed all the attendants to give the four of them a moment alone for private words.

"Yin Niang — whether in public or in private, I've seen that Jiang Taifu Ren is genuinely fond of you — that is a great advantage. Keep it in mind; don't be meek or servile, and don't fight for anything.

"You are blessed — your father and I have done everything we could for your dowry, and the spending money inside the trousseau chest is no small sum!

"With all of this, just settle down and live peacefully at the Jiang family's..."

She glanced at Ru Jin and Ru Xiu. "Both your sisters never even dared dream of what you're getting."

Ru Jin and Ru Xiu both smiled. "Mother, don't worry — both of us are genuinely happy for Yin Niang! We only hope she does better than the two of us put together!"

Lady Li dabbed at her eye and nodded. "You are all good children — your mother knows it in her heart.

"Only — you two also listen today: your father and I have said that as things get better and better at home, we will supplement you two as well."

Ru Jin and Ru Xiu both shook their heads.

"Yin Niang is leaving — there's still Little Brother to think of. Keep it all for him!"

Lady Li shook her head too. "Don't the two of you worry about that — he won't go without! Besides, he's so young — if he sets his heart on studying for the examinations, he likely won't be engaged by twenty.

"Let the older ones have their share first. Even if the family's fortunes are not as bright later on, would your elder brothers and sisters really let him go hungry and cold?"

"Of course not!"

The three sisters spoke in unison.

Little Brother was a good child! As long as they had a bite to eat, Little Brother would have a bite too!

Seeing the three sisters speak so, Lady Li smiled with contentment — a family of flesh and blood ought to be united, each thinking of the others.

Lady Li then looked at Qin Ru Yin again.

"Whatever happens in the Jiang household, do not compete or scramble for anything — only put your heart into caring well for your husband. With your mother-in-law protecting you, the Jiang family will be a comfortable place to live.

"...Your mother has tested her, and I can see that your mother-in-law most dislikes those who are aggressively sharp-elbowed — or stupidly oblivious.

"You mustn't be too meek and biddable either — be too meek and she'll take you for a fool.

"Just be bright and charming — but know where the line is. And be careful and prudent in everything.

"In your husband's home, things are not as they are in your own parents' home — the people there won't always take your side the way family does..."

Qin Ru Yin listened with reddened eyes and nodded at everything.

Lady Li then moved on to speak about the trousseau.

"Between what your father and I prepared for you, and what we managed to wring out of Old Madam Qin and the Second Branch couple, it all amounts to a little under thirty thousand taels' worth.

"On top of that, Sister Sun sent over half a trousseau suite — that added quite a bit more."

When she had finished that sentence, Lady Li added with a smile: "By the way — Sister Sun and cousin-sisters-in-law from the Sun family have already arrived and are helping outside.

"Once Mother finishes talking with you, I'll have someone go invite Sister Sun to come and have a word with you."

Qin Ru Yin was pleasantly surprised — she had not seen Sister Sun in days.

Originally Sun Wen Lan had planned to take the children back to Jiangdong.

But because of Qin Ru Yin's upcoming wedding, she had decided to stay in the capital until the wedding before heading back with the children.

"There is also what Uncle Ning and his family contributed — they put in a trousseau on your behalf as well.

"This part — Uncle Ning only mentioned it to your father later on...

"He made the decision on your behalf to convert it into silver and invest it as a share in the Ning family's business... Uncle Ning will bring the accounts himself to explain it all to you."

Uncle Ning had discussed this privately with Qin Ru Yin before — and at the time she had been embarrassed and told him she couldn't accept something for nothing.

Uncle Ning had told her: it was precisely because of her connections that the great merchant Xu family's eldest son had been willing to come to the Ning family and invite them to participate in overseas trade...

And he had decided on her behalf to convert the trousseau into silver and invest it in that overseas trade.

The goods purchased with that silver were now loaded onto the Xu family's mighty ocean-going merchant ships and had already reached several island nations.

The trading was already half done — the principal had already been recovered.

If the remaining goods sold smoothly, the returns would be several times the original principal!

"Then there are also the trousseau additions received over these past few days — all of it has been recorded on your trousseau list.

"Last of all is the Jiang family's betrothal money — all of that is going back to the Jiang family with you. Our family is keeping not a single coin of it.

"As for the betrothal gifts, we did accept those — the pastries have been distributed among relatives and friends; the mountain delicacies and seafood can be put to good use for your wedding."

Of course betrothal gifts were to be accepted — if the Qin family refused them, the Jiang family would think the Qin family was giving them no face.

Lady Li had outlined everything she needed to convey in simple, clear strokes.

Her little daughter's wedding had come in the midst of so many upheavals in the Qin family — and now the wedding was upon them, and many things had not been said in full.

But her little daughter had already had her awakening, and her spirits had been so much better than before the engagement — she had a clear understanding of so many things in her heart already.

Lady Li was a little comforted, and since things were still to be managed outside, she stepped out first.

Then Ru Jin and Ru Xiu personally attended to helping Qin Ru Yin wash, dress, and groom.

As they helped, they gave her reminders about the small details to be mindful of as a new bride.

The wedding gown was elaborate — she would only put it on just before leaving the house.

Before long, Sun Wen Lan and her three sisters-in-law were led into Qin Ru Yin's room by Bàn Xià, who was dressed in festive colours.

Ru Jin and Ru Xiu were now on sisterly terms with Sun Wen Lan as well, and addressed her sisters-in-law as First Sister-in-Law, Second Sister-in-Law, and Third Sister-in-Law, just as she did.

The Sun family's First Sister-in-Law was the oldest and steadiest of the group.

After the sisters-in-law and little sisters-in-law had all said many propitious words to the bride, she said to Ru Jin and Ru Xiu: "Let's go out while the Full-Fortune Lady has yet to arrive and let the two young ones talk."

Ru Jin and Ru Xiu nodded with a smile and went out arm in arm with the Sun family sisters-in-law.

Sun Wen Lan looked Qin Ru Yin over carefully.

"No wonder you're the one becoming a bride," she said with a smile. "Not yet in your makeup and bridal gown, and already you're blazing with beauty!"

Qin Ru Yin winked at her, playfully teasing: "Sister Sun will be a bride again someday — you've no call to envy me."

Sun Wen Lan's complexion leaned toward cold and striking — should she become a bride again, she would surely be stunning beyond compare.

But at these words of Qin Ru Yin's, that cool and striking face promptly flushed red, making her look even more dazzling and breathtakingly beautiful.

Unable to stop herself, she gave Qin Ru Yin a reproachful look. "So Yin Niang really is a mischievous one — here I am not even teasing you, and you turn around and tease me instead."

Qin Ru Yin grinned.

She wouldn't ask too many questions.

Judging by the look on Sister Sun's face, it would not be long at all before she was a bride again.

She had just overheard a word or two slipping from Third Sister-in-Law Sun's lips.

The Lu Third Young Master of Jiangdong had been in the capital for several days now.

What the Lu Third Young Master had come to the capital for — surely there was no need to spell it out.

And on Sister Sun's cool, striking little face there was that faint, faint shy blush — surely that needed no spelling out either.

"By the way, I've come today also on someone's errand — bringing a trousseau gift for you."

Sun Wen Lan, remembering the errand, quickly beckoned her head maid Lǜ Yi to come forward.

Qin Ru Yin blinked in puzzlement.

She was still receiving trousseau gifts today?

She watched as Lǜ Yi came forward with a smile, dropped a curtsy, then turned and received a tray from the junior maid behind her and brought it over.

Qin Ru Yin could not help but ask: "Sister Sun — who is this trousseau gift from?"

Sun Wen Lan did not keep her guessing. "The Lu family of Jiangdong. Madam Lu Taifu Ren wrote to me personally and had her servants deliver this trousseau gift.

"She is elderly and cannot travel from Jiangdong, and also wished to prepare the gift herself to show her sincerity — which is why it has only arrived today."

She smiled at Qin Ru Yin. "I hope you won't mind that this trousseau gift arrived too late."

Qin Ru Yin quickly shook her head. "I am grateful to Madam Lu Taifu Ren and could not be more so — how could I mind...

"Though — my mother did tell me that the Lu Third Young Master already sent me a trousseau gift."

And it had been sent under the name of the Lu Taifu Ren.

Sun Wen Lan's cool, oval face flushed deeper still.

She glanced at Qin Ru Yin and said in a low voice: "That one... that was Third Young Master's own personal gesture — the one I've brought is the Lu family's gift."

Why had Lu the Third Young Master sent Qin Ru Yin a separate trousseau gift of his own, and one so generous at that?

It was because he believed that the day Sun Wen Lan had summoned her courage and made the leap of going through with the separation was in no small part because of this Qin Sixth Niang.

The Lu Taifu Ren's heartache was actually not so different in nature from the Jiang Taifu Ren's from before.

Both had been worn down by a son of advancing years who simply would not take a wife.

And the Lu Taifu Ren's heartache ran even deeper.

Her third son had his heart set on someone — and even though that woman had long since married another and had children, he would not waver.

How had she not tried to arrange matches for him over these years?

But that wretched little creature of hers would not hear a word of it — the moment the subject was raised he would take himself to bed and refuse to eat or drink for days...

Every single time he would starve himself down to skin and bones before relenting.

Was this not killing his poor old mother?

And then — Sun Wen Lan went and ended her marriage out of the blue!

So what if she had been married before?

So what if she had already had children?

Sun Wen Lan was that little wretch's fate — what could she do about it?

As long as Sun Wen Lan was willing to marry her little wretch, she would not find fault with anything!

Not only find fault — she was grateful to her, and deeply glad of her.

Even if Sun Wen Lan came and had no more children, at least she could accompany her little wretch and help him live properly.

Let her little wretch not die old and alone.

Besides — any children Sun Wen Lan had given birth to, could they be bad children?

Treat them as her own grandchildren — it was the same as giving her little wretch an heir.

And so the Lu Taifu Ren was immensely grateful to that Qin Sixth Young Miss, who had helped Sun Wen Lan resolve her mind to part ways — hence the Lu Taifu Ren's personally prepared trousseau gift for Qin Ru Yin.

"Open it and have a look." Sun Wen Lan herself brought the red sandalwood box from the tray and set it before Qin Ru Yin, smiling and watching her.

chapters.title: Jiang Jiuhao Comes to Collect the Bride
chapters.content:
Qin Ru Yin did as she was told and opened the red sandalwood box.

One look inside — and she immediately stared with wide eyes.

"The Lu Taifu Ren has been far too generous..."

The Lu family's foundations ran as deep as the Sun family's, and the Lu Taifu Ren's gifts were naturally lavish.

Three thousand taels of silver notes were there as spending money for Qin Ru Yin's trousseau chest.

And a set of pigeon-blood red jadeite hair ornaments of exquisite quality...

Qin Ru Yin's first instinct was to decline — but the giver was not here, and she was at a loss for what to do.

Sun Wen Lan clasped her hand and said gently: "Yin Niang, please do accept it!"

"I did nothing for the Lu family — I truly dare not accept such a lavish gift!" Qin Ru Yin shook her head.

If it could be said that the Ning family's involvement was because she had played an indirect part in bringing the eldest son of the great merchant Xu family to the Ning family's door, then the Ning family's trousseau on her behalf was something like a finder's fee.

But even that fee had only come about because she had traded on Jiang Jiuhao's connections.

The Sun family giving her half a trousseau suite was because she had indirectly helped Sister Wen Lan find the courage to end her marriage...

And also because Father had agreed to take Sister Wen Lan's two boys as sons of the Qin First Branch — so that trousseau was given in return for that.

But this trousseau from the Lu family — she really did not dare accept something so generous.

Even if Sister Wen Lan was going to marry Lu the Third Young Master — she was not married yet, was she?

"You silly little sister! You think you've done nothing for the Lu family — but the Lu family doesn't see it that way..." Sun Wen Lan's face reddened again. "Let Sister tell you truthfully then..."

The Sun family patriarch in Jiangdong had written to say that the Lu family had already sent a respected elder of the local community to the Sun family to sound out their feelings.

The Lu family made clear: as long as Sun Wen Lan was willing to remarry, no matter what conditions she put forward, as long as the Lu family could manage it, they would meet every one.

As long as Sun Wen Lan was willing to marry Lu Xun Zhi.

The Sun patriarch had also written a letter separately to Sun Wen Lan, asking whether she was willing...

"So what does Sister Sun think?" Qin Ru Yin was eating up this delicious news and nearly forgot she was supposed to be the bride today.

"I..." Remembering the desperate look in Lu Xun Zhi's eyes that day, nearly unhinged with feeling — Sun Wen Lan's heart ached for him.

"My original plan was to wait until the children were a little older — at least until Shèn Er understood things better — before thinking about marriage...

"But Lu Xun Zhi, he..."

Qin Ru Yin understood in an instant. "He can't wait any longer!"

"Mm." Sun Wen Lan nodded, a little embarrassed.

Then she added: "I don't know what to do now either."

Qin Ru Yin said with a smile: "I know Sister Sun's heart is always full of the children — but you must know that you are your own person first, and a mother second!

"If this mother of theirs is not happy, then growing up under the influence of an unhappy mother, the children will probably not grow up to be happy people either."

Then she held Sun Wen Lan's hands and said earnestly: "Sister Sun — whatever your heart tells you, go and do it.

"Follow your heart, and you won't have regrets in the future.

"If you follow your heart and the children grow up and blame you for it... then it simply means that the blood of the Qin Second Branch runs true — and that is not your problem!"

Qin Ru Yin spoke frankly, and Sun Wen Lan not only did not take offence — she clasped Qin Ru Yin's hands back with gratitude.

Her eyes showed a clear and settled relief. "Yin Niang — I know now what I should do. I truly thank you!"

People said she had a clear and thorough understanding of the world — yet this girl who was eight or nine years her junior was the one who was truly thorough...

If not for her, she might have gone on tangled in doubt for a very long time.

And might have hurt Lu Xun Zhi again.

The Lu Taifu Ren might have looked at her with disappointment yet again...

"Sister Sun doesn't need to thank me — thank yourself. You dared to be your own person, and that is the finest thing."

Qin Ru Yin was genuinely happy for her.

"Since you put it that way, you must absolutely accept the trousseau gift the Lu Taifu Ren has sent!"

Sun Wen Lan smiled brightly. "Consider it the Lu family's matchmaker's fee!"

......

Just as the sky was beginning to lighten at dawn, Lady Li brought the Full-Fortune Lady — the Second Daughter-in-Law of the Cheng family, Second Madam Cheng — to comb the bride's hair.

Second Madam Cheng's parents-in-law and her own parents were all living and well; her sons and daughters were all grown; her grandchildren were clever and delightful.

She was herself the elder of siblings, with brothers and sisters both below her, and her whole family was happy and whole — she was the most renowned Full-Fortune Lady in all the capital.

Of course, most households who wanted her could not get her.

Nor had the Qin family dared to ask her to come as the Full-Fortune Lady for Qin Ru Yin.

It was Jiang Jiuhao who had commissioned Elder Cheng, and Elder Cheng had personally told her to go to the Qin family and serve Qin Ru Yin as the Full-Fortune Lady.

Jiang Taifu Ren had sent word to the Qin family, and Lady Li, overjoyed, had quickly prepared a generous gift and gone to the Cheng residence to extend the invitation to Second Madam Cheng.

Second Madam Cheng had a round, full face, and a slightly plump figure — at a glance, one could tell she was a lady who had lived in comfort and was very blessed.

Today she had worn a dark red brocade cape patterned with ten-thousand-blessing motifs, and had her hair dressed in a neat and tidy coiled bun, with a full set of fine turquoise ornaments.

She carried an air of vitality and dignified composure.

"Third Young Miss — it is time to put on the wedding gown. Put on the gown before the makeup is applied."

Second Madam Cheng smiled and looked Qin Ru Yin over from head to toe, then said many words of blessing and good fortune in her most auspicious voice.

When she had finished, Second Madam Cheng thought to herself: this Qin Third Young Miss really does have exceptional looks!

No wonder the Jiang Taifu Ren is so fond of this girl.

Her late father-in-law had treated that Jiang the Fourth almost like a half-son of his own and placed great importance on him and protected him staunchly.

She could only hope that Jiang the Fourth would, now that he had taken this young woman as his wife, treat her well...

Lady Li had also engaged a makeup artist from the makeup parlour — the most skilled one there was — especially for Qin Ru Yin.

Now that the Qin First Branch's circumstances were better, the makeup artist Lady Li had engaged for Qin Ru Yin was the best in her trade.

Bridal makeup was precisely this makeup artist's most celebrated specialty.

At first the makeup artist had worried a little — Qin Ru Yin's age was rather young, her face not yet fully matured, and she was afraid the girl could not carry such a bold bridal look.

But when she had finished the makeup and looked at the bride reflected in the bronze mirror, she could not help but say: "Miss is truly the most beautiful bride I have ever seen!"

Qin Ru Yin broke into a smile — and she was stunning, brilliantly alive, making even Second Madam Cheng beside her catch her breath.

She laughed and said: "You're too kind — all brides are beautiful!"

That makeup artist had seen more brides than she could count, and not one had been as magnificently lovely as this, or so naturally and easily graceful.

Not flustered or nervous at this moment — but still saying such pleasant, generous things to her...

Second Madam Cheng, listening to her words, was quietly nodding in private agreement.

She had not expected at all that this Qin Third Young Miss had such a charming and delightful nature.

She found herself thinking that perhaps when this Qin Third Young Miss was still the Qin Sixth Young Miss, she had been guarding herself all along, never showing her true face to the world.

With this thought, Second Madam Cheng could not help but sigh — that Jiang the Fourth was a fortunate man. His exchange had brought him home a true treasure.

When it was Second Madam Cheng's turn to comb the bride's hair, she offered especially many words of blessing.

This delighted Lady Li into thanking her over and over again.

When Second Madam Cheng finished combing the bride's hair, Lady Li personally accompanied Second Madam Cheng to have the customary egg wine.

It was the custom in the capital of the Great Ying dynasty, when sending a daughter off in marriage, for the Full-Fortune Lady who had combed the bride's hair to be treated by the host family to egg wine.

It was an expression of gratitude and the highest courtesy toward her.

Because she was the Full-Fortune Lady.

Full of Fortune!

It was the finest blessing one could bestow upon the daughter being married away.

Usually it was the host family's mistress's sisters-in-law or elder sisters-in-law who accompanied the Full-Fortune Lady — the mistress herself was too occupied on such a day.

Having the mistress of the house accompany the Full-Fortune Lady personally was something even Second Madam Cheng had not anticipated.

Of course, at first Second Madam Cheng declined.

Lady Li held her hand and said with a smile: "It doesn't matter — there are plenty of capable kinswomen helping to receive guests at my house today. They're not short of me."

Second Madam Cheng only then set her mind at ease.

And her admiration for this newly split Qin First Branch grew considerably.

When daylight was full, the Jiang family's wedding procession was nearly at the door.

Inside the Qin residence, Qin Ru Yin's brothers, sisters, and sisters-in-law had all set aside whatever they were doing and asked others to cover for them, and had come to bid her farewell and wish her well.

The youngest brother, Rong Jin, and Fifth Sister Ru He had both cried their eyes red.

The three little nieces had their arms wrapped around Third Auntie's arms and legs, not wanting Third Auntie to be married away.

The little nephew from Second Brother's family, held in his nursemaid's arms, saw all the sisters crying and opened his mouth wide and started bawling too.

"Heavens, here the grown ones haven't even started crying yet and the little ones are already at it..." The Wei family Grand Elder Aunt also wiped at her eyes.

The elder came forward one by one and offered Qin Ru Yin words of blessing and good fortune, and the children were each carried out by their nursemaids.

The elders had not yet all had their turn when the sound of firecrackers erupted outside.

Someone called out: "The Jiang family's procession has arrived!"

Sure enough, a little maid came running from the gate to report: "The Jiang family's young master and the wedding procession have arrived at our gate — they're about to come in!"

The Qin residence was hung with lanterns and bright with red decorations — every part of the house that could be decorated had been dressed with red silk and red lanterns and all manner of festive adornments.

The male servants and maids were all dressed in festive colours, weaving busily through every part of the house.

At this moment, the First Elder of the Qin family led the male kinsmen and sons and stood on the front courtyard's steps at the gate.

To his left stood the Wei Grand Uncle and Third Master Qin and the other elders.

To his right stood First Master Qin Brother and the younger generation.

And behind them, a row of Ministry of Works colleagues, and certain members of the Qin clan.

Wearing a new bridegroom's ceremonial hat, dressed in the brilliant red second-rank official regalia emblazoned with the crane motif, Jiang Jiuhao sat erect in the saddle, his right hand light on the reins. The dark chestnut charger gave a soft whinny and came to a smooth, steady halt.

Jiang Jiuhao dismounted with easy grace and walked forward at an unhurried pace.

He stood tall and straight as a pine, polished and noble.

Dressed in the brilliant red, his incomparably handsome face looked several years younger — yet the red only made him appear more cutting.

The First Elder of the Qin family, who was habitually dignified and steady, felt a wave of dizziness wash over him when he faced the unconscious force of presence this third son-in-law radiated without even trying.

He thought to himself: no wonder he is the youngest Minister of Personnel in the entire Great Ying dynasty — this aura is truly not something an ordinary man can withstand.

And yet he felt both proud and elated.

This outstanding and formidable man was the son-in-law of him, Qin Ming Feng!

When he had steadied himself and was about to step forward to receive him — Jiang Jiuhao quickened his pace, and came forward first to greet and bow to him.

Before the First Elder could even react, Jiang Jiuhao said quietly: "Please, Father-in-Law, quickly have someone go set up the incense altar inside.

"In a moment, the imperial cortège sent from the palace to present trousseau gifts to Yin Niang will arrive."

The First Elder's body swayed — he could hardly believe what he was hearing.

The difference in their ranks was so vast that he could not help asking with the deferential form of address: "What did you say?"

chapters.title: The Mother-in-Law Looks at Her Son-in-Law and Loves What She Sees
chapters.content:
Jiang Jiuhao knew he hadn't expected this.

After all, how many daughters of official families had ever received gifts bestowed from the palace?

And the First Elder of the Qin family was no more than a newly appointed fourth-rank official — this was the sort of good fortune he would not dare dream of even in his sleep.

In all the history of the Great Ying dynasty, even daughters of the Three Highest Ministers had not always received honour of this kind.

Even Jiang Jiuhao himself had not imagined the little girl would have such extraordinary good fortune.

It was the Emperor who had specifically sent someone to inform him...

"Father-in-Law, rest assured — this is all true. Please hurry and have preparations made!"

The First Elder turned to look at his eldest son — but he was too moved to speak.

It was Qin Rong Cheng who recovered first and quickly said: "Father, Brother-in-Law, rest easy — I'll go myself!"

No sooner had the Qin family set up the incense altar than the head imperial eunuch arrived, leading a grand procession of palace maids and junior eunuchs bearing trays and making their way toward the Qin residence.

The senior eunuch delivering the edict smiled and told the First Elder to lead the Qin family in receiving the imperial decree — though the bride herself was excused from coming to the front courtyard.

The edict stated that the accomplishments of the First Elder of the Qin family had been thoroughly investigated and verified by the Ministry of Personnel.

Agriculture was the cornerstone of the Great Ying dynasty — all things began with it, for the people depended on food above all else.

What the First Elder had done had in truth saved the lives and property of tens of thousands of common people.

He had protected at least hundreds of thousands of acres of farmland from the devastation of floods.

Yet he had done all of this with bowed head and quiet dedication, never boasting of his merits or broadcasting his deeds to the world.

It was only very recently that the already-retired former Minister of Personnel, Elder Cheng, had come to hear of it and presented it to the Emperor's desk...

From the palace came trousseau gifts: from the Empress Dowager, a pair of jade ruyi sceptres, a pair of red coral ornaments, twenty bolts of imperial tribute silk and brocade, and twenty ingots of five-tael imperial cast gold.

From the Empress, a set of imperially crafted solid gold filigree hair ornaments with kingfisher feather inlay, and ten pairs of perfectly matched freshwater pearls, each the size of a dragon's eye.

After the Qin family received the imperial edict, Qin Rong Cheng immediately took a red cloth pouch and pressed it into the hands of the senior eunuch who had come to read the edict and deliver the gifts.

He invited the senior eunuch to stay and drink at the wedding feast.

The senior eunuch accepted the light little pouch with a smile — knowing full well it contained a bank note — and offered Qin Rong Cheng his congratulations once more.

He declined graciously: "I have to return to the palace to report back, and the young Qin Daren's household is busy with the wedding — please do not see me off!"

Among the wedding guests at the Qin family, there was not one who was not consumed with envy.

Trousseau gifts bestowed by the Empress Dowager and the Empress herself!

In terms of monetary value, that was not particularly remarkable to the noble and powerful households of the capital.

But this was not a matter of how much the trousseau was worth in silver.

This was face — and what an extraordinary face it was!

The most aggrieved of all were the clan elders of the Qin main family who had come to see Qin Ru Yin off on her wedding day.

How wonderful it would have been if the Qin First Branch had never split from the clan!

The glory of the palace's bestowed trousseau would have shed its reflected light on all of the Qin main family too...

All of the unmarried young ladies of the Qin main family would have benefited enormously!

What a pity!

What an utter pity...

And at this moment, in the crowd gathered to watch the excitement beyond the Qin residence, over a dozen men in close-fitting riding clothes were wearing very dark expressions.

They exchanged nods, and one man swiftly threaded through the crowd and disappeared...

At the Qin Second Branch's residence on Shun Yi Lane.

The Wang family's wedding procession had not yet arrived.

Old Madam Qin, forcing herself out of her sickbed, was in Qin Ru Yue's room giving her a lecture.

Tong Shi had no patience for it.

And still burning with resentment toward the Qin Old Madam and her son for the humiliation of being forcibly sent to the countryside, she said to the Old Madam: "Mother — Yue Niang is the most sensible of all the girls! She's getting married today — there's no need to be so strict with her!"

Old Madam Qin gave Tong Shi a cold look.

Today, with her own family here, this daughter-in-law was giving her — her mother-in-law — considerably less deference than usual!

Does this Tong Shi truly think her maternal family can protect her for a lifetime?

"First Branch daughter-in-law — the First Branch and the Third Branch have split from the clan and gone their own way, and we have re-numbered everyone. Ru Yue is now our Second Young Miss — let's not get names wrong again!"

Old Madam Qin's expression was unpleasant.

Tong Shi paid it no mind and said coldly: "Of all the moments to choose from, Mother is still fixating on such small details.

"The Wang family's procession will be arriving any moment — what about the promise Mother made to Wang Furen?

"You promised in front of her that you'd give Ru Yue ten thousand taels of spending money for her trousseau chest — let's have that settled quickly!"

Old Madam Qin was so infuriated she nearly keeled over backwards.

Already fully dressed in her wedding gown, hair done, and bridal makeup in place, Qin Ru Yue sat on the bed and clenched her hands into fists.

What Grandmother had promised in front of her future mother-in-law!

The Wang family had not withdrawn the engagement — yet Grandmother was now dragging her feet over those ten thousand taels of spending money.

She had only just been in here weeping poverty at her...

Wanting to give her only six thousand taels.

Nearly half the original amount!

Even less than she had originally promised her!

Grandmother clearly had money!

She had been managing the Qin family's household accounts for decades.

Even if she had filled the gap of her grandfather's debts to the tune of tens of thousands of taels over the years, that could not have broken her completely.

She could not fathom what her grandmother was playing at, constantly changing her word.

She had already shared so much information that benefited their branch of the family — why was Grandmother still treating her this way?

Was Grandmother just all talk about doting on her, and in reality couldn't care less whether she lived or died in her husband's home?

Her maternal grandmother the Tong matriarch had been less devoted, yet she had managed to squeeze an extra two thousand taels out of her with a single prophetic dream!

"Hmph! At the time I was addled with illness and flustered from trying to stop Wang Furen from calling off the engagement — so I blurted out a number at random...

"First Branch daughter-in-law, you've only just returned from the countryside and don't know the state of affairs in this household — I won't hold that against you. But you shouldn't be demanding that I stick to that figure of ten thousand taels.

"I won't shortchange Ru Yue. Giving her more good things in kind is just as good, isn't it?"

"It's the trousseau chest that matters — the items in the dowry display are already impressive enough. Giving Yue Niang more in spending money is what makes sense." Tong Shi would not yield.

After all, the more the Old Madam gave, the less she herself needed to.

Her silver was being saved for her sons and grandsons!

At that very moment, Old Madam Qin's most trusted old momo came in with an ashen face to report.

She was reporting the news about the palace bestowing trousseau gifts upon Qin Ru Yin...

Even beneath the heavy bridal makeup, it was impossible to hide Qin Ru Yue's pallor.

The palace had bestowed trousseau gifts on Qin Ru Yin!

Why? Why did Qin Ru Yin have such extraordinary luck?

Compared to her own circumstances, how utterly laughable she must seem.

Tong Shi's expression also soured considerably.

But she recovered quickly — and said to the dumbfounded Old Madam: "Mother, look — both setting off on their wedding day, and over there things are glorious, while our Yue Niang —?"

Qin Ru Yue's eyes flashed briefly cold.

She spoke up: "Mother, say no more — your daughter knows Grandmother dotes on her.

"Grandmother has her own troubles too — your daughter doesn't mind how much Grandmother gives."

Then she turned to Old Madam Qin and said: "Grandmother — only it's not easy for your granddaughter in her husband's home, and it's not the same as being at home.

"Even if I want to pass a message in the future, or have Grandmother help me interpret a dream — that will be so much more difficult once I'm in the Wang house."

Old Madam Qin heard Qin Ru Yue's final words and her aged eyes sharpened instantly.

This girl!

This was a threat — that if she was not satisfied, any prophetic dreams she had about the Qin family, she might choose not to share.

Old Madam Qin's head throbbed violently.

She forced herself to calm down, thought it over — and in the end capitulated.

She fixed Qin Ru Yue with a cold look, making no further pretence of grandmotherly love.

"It's good that Yue Niang knows in her heart that Grandmother cares for her! Since you're this sensible, Grandmother also can't bear to see you have a hard time at the Wang family...

"Very well — Grandmother will scrape together eight thousand taels of spending money for you. Beyond that, there truly is no more."

Qin Ru Yue clamped down on her teeth so hard the pain radiated into her jaw.

Still refusing to give her the ten thousand she'd promised to Wang Furen!

At this moment, firecrackers sounded outside, and at once a servant woman came to report that the Wang family's wedding procession had arrived.

That woman's face was full of joy as she reported to Old Madam Qin: "Taifu Ren — wonderful news!"

"Oh?" Old Madam Qin looked at her in surprised inquiry. "Tell me plainly!"

"Taifu Ren — the Wang family's wedding procession is grand and imposing, with many young, strong men come to carry the trousseau..."

By the customs of the Great Ying dynasty's weddings, if the groom's family was very satisfied with the bride, they would send many young men to the bride's home to carry the trousseau.

To show off the bride's dowry to the fullest was a way of giving the bride's family face.

If they were dissatisfied with the bride's family, the carrying party would be meagre, and the procession would be thin and poor.

Even if the bride's dowry was substantial, she would only be able to send it over by carriage from the bride's family side.

In such a situation, the more trousseau the bride had, the more it was the groom's family that benefited — while the bride's family lost face.

The Qin Second Branch cared about saving face — and at least on the surface, the trousseau they would give Qin Ru Yue would not be meagre.

After seeing Wang Furen's attitude, the Qin Second Branch had not dared hope the Wang family's wedding procession would be particularly impressive.

Now, for the Qin Second Branch, this was truly good news.

Even the dark and gloomy look on Old Madam Qin's aged face broke into a thin smile.

Tong Shi's face also brightened, and she said to Qin Ru Yue: "The Wang family still knows how to present themselves — Yue Niang, you don't need to worry...

"What Mother has prepared in your trousseau is impressive — there's plenty for the Wang family's carriers to carry!"

Old Madam Qin, hearing Tong Shi's words, curled her lip — as if those trousseau pieces were all prepared by Tong Shi herself.

Zǐ Jǐng Lane.

After the palace had bestowed the trousseau gifts upon Qin Ru Yin, the Qin residence grew even more lively.

Uninvited guests came in numbers, bearing gifts to share in the wedding wine.

Fortunately, the Wei family had come in large numbers — young women and brides-in-law alike — and whether recording gifts, setting up accounts, or receiving guests to their seats, everything was handled perfectly and without the slightest disorder.

Jiang Jiuhao knelt in the front courtyard and performed the full prostration to the First Elder of the Qin family. The First Elder pulled him up at once, and pressed a thick red packet into his hands.

Then he led the new bridegroom to the back courtyard to perform the prostration to his mother-in-law, Lady Li.

Lady Li, upon seeing her son-in-law in his second-rank crimson official regalia serving as wedding garments, felt the ground tilt beneath her.

This was the first time she had ever set eyes on the court ceremonial dress of a second-rank official!

And this son-in-law — tall and straight, handsome beyond comparison, like some divine celestial descended from the heavens...

And not a day older than he should be!

He looked no more than twenty-three or twenty-four.

The more she looked, the more she liked what she saw.

Seeing this second-rank official of a son-in-law kneel and perform the prostration to her, she panicked and hurriedly bent down to pull him up with both hands.

"Good..."

"Good child! Take this!" Lady Li laughed until she could not close her mouth, and pressed a thick red packet into Jiang Jiuhao's hands as well.

After Lady Li herself helped him to his feet, Jiang Jiuhao made a round of bows to the eldest brothers, eldest sisters-in-law, and others.

Qin Rong Cheng, Qin Rong Lie, and Lin Xi and Meng An all returned the bows in a flurry.

After the exchange of greetings here, Qin Rong Cheng and Qin Rong Lie — the two eldest brothers-in-law — personally accompanied the new bridegroom to take his seat at the feast.

Wang Cheng Bin — Commander of the Five City Regiment, who had come along with Jiang Jiuhao to collect the bride — sent Jiang Jiuhao a meaningful look.

He sidled over and lowered his voice: "Your father-in-law's family are all fine people — respectful toward you and not servile, not fawning and not meek. Truly rare.

"No wonder you broke your own rules... and used your connections to give them a hand..."

Jiang Jiuhao glanced at him with unhurried cool.

Wang Cheng Bin immediately stepped back a pace. "Saying no more, saying no more!"

Then he stepped forward two paces again and caught up with Jiang Jiuhao, lowering his voice to ask: "On the surface everything looks calm — are you being too cautious, Jiang the Fourth?"

chapters.title: The Wang Family's Wedding Procession Comes Charging Through
chapters.content:
"Better safe than sorry." Jiang Jiuhao offered no further explanation.

Wang Cheng Bin shrugged his shoulders. "Hey — you're the wealthy one, and every one of those brothers of mine on rest duty today is short of coin. Just make sure you don't leave them without drinking money."

"They won't go without."

After the wedding feast, one of Wang Cheng Bin's brothers came to find him.

After a murmured exchange, Wang Cheng Bin gave a small nod.

He unfastened the light little pouch at his waist and passed it to that brother.

"Take this and buy the brothers some good wine — it's Jiang Daren treating them to wedding wine, in thanks for their trouble today!"

The brother received it with a broad grin, rubbed the pouch between his fingers — it was a solid stack of banknotes!

So he laughed and said: "Boss, the brothers love a patron like Jiang Daren — make sure to recommend more good work like this to the brothers in future!"

Wang Cheng Bin feigned a kick at him. "Little rat — off with you! Is that all you amount to..."

"Yes, sir! Off I go."

"Pass the word along — every man keeps his mouth sealed tight. Anyone who lets a single breath slip will get himself kicked out of the Five City Regiment!"

That brother's expression sobered at once. "Boss, rest easy! Every man here today helping Jiang Daren is someone you can trust — and His Highness's side knows of it too."

Wang Cheng Bin nodded.

His own family clan and Jiang the Fourth's family clan alike — for generations, both had stood only on the side of the legitimate succession.

The legitimate succession at present was, of course, the Emperor.

The Eastern Palace was the future legitimate succession.

Both of their families had been quietly charged by the current Emperor to stand by the Eastern Palace no matter what...

Regardless of whether the Emperor wavered in his intention to have the Eastern Palace inherit the throne...

At least for now, neither he nor Jiang the Fourth had any choice in the matter.

To put it plainly — they were lashed to the Eastern Palace's mast, and there they would stay.

Jiang the Fourth was more single-minded in his purpose, caring only to ensure the Eastern Palace ascended to the throne without a hitch.

Wang Cheng Bin had a few other considerations — but after casting his gaze around in observation, he had come away only with disappointment.
