In the end, he had found that the Crown Prince was not dangerously compromised — he had simply injured his leg, and as for the calibre of the man, his character and capability and political acumen, he was perfectly suited to be a sovereign who held the gains and consolidated the peace.

From that point on, Wang Cheng Bin had been genuinely and wholeheartedly of one mind with Jiang the Fourth.

......

The crack and pop of firecrackers rang out.

Qin Ru Yin's trousseau began to be carried out from the West Courtyard.

The First Elder had discussed it privately with Jiang Jiuhao beforehand.

Their First Branch had only just split from the clan — at present it was only two households, and within the Qin clan they were a minor branch.

He himself had only just been promoted to fourth rank, and to guard against drawing unwanted envy, they had decided not to make too great a show of Qin Ru Yin's trousseau.

Yet Qin Ru Yin's trousseau still qualified as a "ten-li red parade" in its own right.

He had brought a copy of the trousseau list and intended to let Jiang Jiuhao have a look.

Jiang Jiuhao had declined graciously.

He had no interest in how much his wife's trousseau was worth.

He also understood the First Elder's concern.

He of course agreed with what the First Elder proposed.

They packed the trousseau's original hundred-and-some loads as full and solid as possible and consolidated them down to eighty loads.

Even so — the Qin First Branch's Third Young Miss setting out with such a grand and imposing procession of trousseau absolutely astonished many of the guests.

Several noblewomen who had once considered Qin Ru Yin as a candidate daughter-in-law now felt both their eyes smarting with envy and their hearts aching with regret.

At the time they had worried that the Qin First Branch was being kept under the thumb of the Qin Second Branch, and feared the Qin Sixth Niang's dowry would be thin and meagre...

And now look!

Such a magnificent trousseau being carried out — adding up all her daughters' trousseau together probably still wouldn't match the substance of this one...

After the last load of trousseau had been carried out of the Qin residence, Qin Ru Yin was helped out of her bridal chamber by two cheerfully smiling wedding attendants.

Then her eldest brother, Qin Rong Cheng, carried her on his back to the bridal sedan chair.

"Yin Niang, don't be afraid — Elder Brother's carrying you, steady every step!"

Qin Ru Yin was helped to climb onto her eldest brother's broad shoulders, and she heard his steady, reassuring voice.

"Mm!" She answered obediently, and felt a slight ache in her heart.

Two lifetimes, and she was finally getting married.

She was now living what she had once envied most.

She too had an elder brother to carry her out on her wedding day...

The maids, servants, and attendants who served in her room, as well as the companions who would follow her into her new home, were already seated in carriages following in the wake of the Jiang family's wedding procession.

Jiang Jiuhao sat astride the dark chestnut charger and watched the bride Qin Ru Yin settle herself steadily into the bridal sedan chair. He then gave the head sedan-carrier a look.

Then his sharp gaze swept the surroundings on all sides.

Wang Cheng Bin had just murmured to him: just before the news broke that the palace had bestowed trousseau gifts on the little girl, someone had pulled back the people stationed around the Qin residence.

But he felt things were not so simple.

Yesterday he had asked Huì Qīng to bring Huì Yuán with him to the Qin residence — ostensibly to offer blessings and read faces...

In truth, it was so that Huì Yuán could carefully question the Qin Fourth Young Miss about the dream she had had of her previous life...

After Huì Qīng had heard Huì Yuán's account of everything, he had at last understood why it was that a young Qin miss was able to resolve the curse hanging over the Jiang family.

The one who could resolve the Jiang family's curse was not — as had originally been thought — the former Qin Fifth Niang. It was not even the girl he was taking as his wife.

It was in truth the current Qin Fourth Young Miss.

But he did not see it that way — had he not agreed to the exchange of brides, the Jiang family would have missed the chance to break the curse.

For if there had been no exchange of brides, he would not have taken Qin Ru Yin as his bride.

Without taking Qin Ru Yin, he would never have come to know of the dream the Qin Fourth Young Miss had dreamed of a previous life.

And the Qin Fourth Young Miss — it was clear as day she trusted only Qin Ru Yin.

And so he still believed it was his little girl who was the true key to resolving the Jiang family's curse.

As for what had happened to his little girl in her previous life...

She was his wife now — he would never allow her to go through that again!

Qin Ru Yin felt the sedan chair lift off the ground. The bearers' pace was swift yet extraordinarily smooth — she could not feel the slightest jolt.

She sat up straight inside the sedan chair, the dragon-and-phoenix auspicious red veil draped over her head, the spirit-warding fan held in her hands.

In truth she was a little hungry.

She had been up since the crack of dawn, had been fussed over for a long time, and her sisters-in-law and sisters had all urged her to eat and drink little.

So she had only taken a few bites of half-cooked lotus seed and lily bulb congee.

The symbolism was for a harmonious marriage and many sons.

Being hungry was miserable.

She tried to use the mind-over-matter trick of imagining plums, but when she pictured all the delicious food from her modern life, she only grew hungrier by the moment.

The suona and other instruments played the wedding music around her, and Qin Ru Yin knew she was growing further and further from Zǐ Jǐng Lane.

Right now she only wanted to arrive at the Jiang residence as soon as possible — that way she could have her people quietly bring her something to eat on the sly to tide her over...

She was lost in this chaotic jumble of thoughts when suddenly her ears caught the sound of another lively, festive wedding music procession coming from somewhere nearby.

She was still thinking: today really must be an auspicious day for weddings — there are quite a few people getting married.

Then without warning, somewhere in the crowd a burst of sharp, urgent cries broke out, and the sedan chair gave a sudden lurch.

The fan Qin Ru Yin had been holding upright in front of her nose almost tumbled from her grasp.

Fortunately her hand steadied itself, and the fan did not fall.

And the sedan chair, under the bearers' frantic efforts to correct it, also stopped shaking.

"Which family's wedding procession is this? Utterly rude!"

Qin Ru Yin heard the displeased voices of the two wedding attendants outside calling out on their side.

"Looking at it — how does it look like the crest of the National Academy Rector's family, Master Wang?"

"The Wang family is the most rule-bound family there is — how is it that their wedding procession won't yield on meeting ours here?

"...Master Wang may be of distinguished scholarly repute — but can he be compared to our Jiang Daren?"

"Quite! Truly strange... by rights, the Wang family's procession should not have come all the way around this route and run straight into ours..."

"Oh no — up ahead, why are they fighting?"

"Ah, heavens... there is blood — this... whatever shall we do?"

"Oh goodness! What's gotten into them? Why is the Wang family's wedding procession charging its sedan chair straight toward ours?!"

The two Jiang family wedding attendants had gone white in the face.

chapters.title: Chapter 101
chapters.content:
Wanting to Switch Brides?

"How peculiar — the Wang family used only four bearers when they carried the eldest daughter-in-law's sedan, yet for the second son's bride they've used eight..."

"The second son's bride is the Qin Second Branch's youngest legitimate daughter. After all, the Second Master Qin does outrank Lord Wang by half a grade..."

The two wedding matrons were tense with fear, but that didn't stop them from gossiping.

"Matron, what is happening out there?"

Seated in the bridal sedan, Qin Ruyin had already sensed something was wrong. The commotion outside was such that she couldn't make out what the two matrons were saying.

She called out to the matron outside the sedan.

Even in a capital where a dropped roof tile could hit a noble, Jiang Jiuxiao and the Jiang family behind him were not the sort any ordinary powerful family could afford to provoke. Who would be so recklessly blind as to come crashing into the Jiang family's wedding procession on their very wedding day?

"Yes, yes, I'm here — don't be afraid, new bride!"

"Whatever is happening out there, the men will sort it out. You just sit tight in the sedan!"

The matrons hired by the Jiang family were made of sterner stuff.

Even as they trembled with barely suppressed panic, they hadn't forgotten to reassure Qin Ruyin.

The other matron, hands shaking, still remembered to call out to the eight sedan bearers: "Eight young brothers — you must hold steady, no matter what! A bridal sedan must not be set down before it reaches the Jiang gates — that is the worst of omens!"

The eight bearers needed no such reminder — they already knew the rule.

They were men of the Five City Infantry Command.

Their martial skills went without saying.

To a trained eye, the Wang family's eight sedan bearers had a nimble step and formidable lightness of foot — clearly trained fighters.

The eight brothers feared they were no match.

Yet their commander had such a bond with Lord Jiang — they would rather die than ruin Lord Jiang's happy occasion.

They would fight to the last.

But when the opposing sedan rammed into them, though all eight brothers held the Jiang family sedan steady with desperate strength, each of them spat a mouthful of blood.

Jiang Jiuxiao's sharp eyes went hard. He launched himself from his bay horse in one fluid movement.

"Jiang Sijiu — catch!" Wang Chengbin's sharp cry rang out. He snatched his sword from a retainer's hands and hurled it toward Jiang Jiuxiao.

Well.

Today had truly been an eye-opener.

He had come along to accompany Jiang Sijiu to fetch his bride — and walked straight into someone trying to swap the brides?

No.

Not quite that either.

It looked more like an attempt to exchange brides.

The Wang family would never dare do such a thing.

The Qin Second Branch had already swapped the match between these two cousins once. They couldn't possibly make a second swap on both girls' wedding days.

Then someone else was the hidden hand controlling the Wang family, or using them.

Good thing Jiang Sijiu hadn't listened to him and pulled back all the people he'd placed in the outer ring.

Wang Chengbin, seated on his tall horse, kicked out with one foot and sent a Wang family groomsman flying.

He looked back toward the Jiang family sedan — and saw his eight brothers staggering and swaying, every one of them bleeding.

Clearly they had been hit by hidden weapons.

In that moment, his eyes nearly split with fury.

"Jiang Sijiu! The sedan is going to drop!"

"Brothers — eight of you, go relieve Huang Yun and the others!"

"More men — get the wounded to a physician, quickly!"

"And the rest of you — clear the crowd! Get the people away from here!"

"Neighbors, stop watching! Get home!" Wang Chengbin's hands were full, his mouth even fuller, chaos all around him.

...

Jiang Jiuxiao flew toward his own bridal sedan with sword in one hand.

Just before the eight young bearers staggered and fell, he seized the left front pole of the sedan with his right hand.

With the strength of a single arm, he held the sedan perfectly steady. Qin Ruyin felt only the faintest tremor.

Yet at this moment, her heart was hammering so hard it nearly burst out of her chest.

She forced herself not to scream.

She had no idea what was happening outside — if she cried out, there was no telling what it might draw toward her.

Stay calm. Stay calm.

Qin Ruyin gripped her wedding fan with one hand and lifted the edge of her red veil with it, then with her other hand raised the right curtain of the sedan a crack.

She looked out — and saw utter chaos.

She let the curtain drop at once, frightened.

But in the corner of her eye she had caught a familiar face.

One of the second-tier matrons from Qin Ruyue's courtyard.

She was with the Wang family's wedding procession.

Then the person sitting in that sedan was Qin Ruyue.

And she suddenly understood everything.

The Wang family wanted to swap her and—

No. No, that wasn't right.

The Wang family, so obsessed with their reputation, could never do something like this.

Of course, they wouldn't dare and couldn't manage it.

Then the person behind all of this was obvious.

Prince An!

Qin Ruyin's spine went cold.

She remembered what her Fourth Sister Ruyan had told her — that in the original body's previous life, Prince An had used the ruse of swapping out the bride from the Wang household to bring her to his mansion, where he held her captive for a lifetime.

Could it be that this time Prince An had chosen the same trick — to swap her and Qin Ruyue on their wedding day, then bring her to his mansion just as he had in the original body's past life?

No.

She absolutely could not let Prince An's scheme succeed.

But she also knew clearly: wearing this cumbersome bridal attire, even with nimble feet, there was no escaping in the midst of such enormous chaos.

The only choice was to trust Jiang Jiuxiao and sit in the sedan waiting for her chance.

...

Wang Chengbin stared with wide eyes.

Good lord.

What immense strength Jiang Sijiu had!

No — keeping a sedan of eight poles suspended and perfectly level was not something mere brute strength could accomplish. It required formidable inner force as well.

You remarkable man!

If not for the fact that his little bride had been swapped today, he'd never have seen this trump card Jiang Sijiu had been hiding.

"You there — why aren't you helping Lord Jiang hold the sedan?"

Wang Chengbin snapped back to himself in seconds and shouted for his brothers to go hold the sedan for Jiang Jiuxiao, freeing his hands to deal with those dozen or so black-clad men who were obviously master fighters.

His own martial arts were formidable — but his inner force was somewhat lacking.

Those dozen or so fighters looked to be no inferior to the palace's elite guards.

Against men like those, his inner force was simply not enough.

He'd take a blade for a brother — but throwing his life away was something else. He was only thirty-three.

His Wang family was counting on him.

Besides, he still had to help Jiang Sijiu protect the Crown Prince's ascension.

Jiang Jiuxiao did not hand the sedan over to the men Wang Chengbin sent.

Wang Chengbin's people were better fighters than ordinary officers, but they couldn't protect his Jiang family's bridal sedan.

Whoever was pulling strings behind this would not yield easily.

Having arranged all of this, those formidable fighters he had sent had only one end.

Either succeed or die trying.

Jiang Jiuxiao swept the scene with eyes sharp as a hawk's, then said to Wang Chengbin: "Have your man report to His Highness the Crown Prince."

Wang Chengbin's eyes lit up.

How had he not thought of that?

If Jiang Sijiu judged the person behind this to be that particular prince, then they should let the imperial family fight it out among themselves.

In moments, one of Wang Chengbin's men with exceptional lightness of foot was gone from the scene with a few leaps.

Jiang Jiuxiao gave a sharp whistle.

His own men moved in, surrounding him and the sedan in a protective ring.

A quarter of an hour later, Li Yi and Qian Er had each dealt with a master fighter and came flying back toward the sedan.

Both their faces were grave. They took positions front and back and took over the sedan poles.

"My lord — please go check on the Fourth Mistress. We'll guard the sedan. We will not let the Fourth Mistress come to any harm."

Jiang Jiuxiao tucked his sword behind his back with one hand, then stepped forward and knocked gently on the sedan door. "Ruyin — it's me, Jiang Jiuxiao. Are you all right?"

chapters.title: Chapter 102
chapters.content:
The Wedding Ceremony

Hearing his voice, Qin Ruyin let out a long, shuddering breath of relief.

She immediately called back: "I'm fine!"

Then she asked urgently: "And you? Are you hurt? What's happening out there?"

Jiang Jiuxiao heard that her voice, though trembling, was very much alive and alert, and his own heart eased.

"I'm fine. Just wait a little longer — it will be dealt with shortly. Don't be afraid. I'm here for everything." He kept his voice as free of its usual chill as he could, making it gentle and reassuring.

"All right." Qin Ruyin answered firmly.

He hadn't abandoned her.

She could already guess that there was a powerful figure behind all of this.

Jiang Jiuxiao — who had become President of the Board of Personnel at twenty-eight — would his mind not have worked out the same?

And yet he had chosen to shield her.

That put her at ease, and she suddenly very much wanted to laugh.

In her previous life, Qin Ruyue's eyes must have been broken.

Then again — that girl looked sharp, but was beneath all the cleverness an idiot. Otherwise, why would she have schemed to arrange the match swap herself, handing Jiang Jiuxiao right over to her?

Another quarter of an hour passed, and two companies of the Brocade Guard descended, resplendent in their cloud-brocade flying-fish uniform robes.

Once the Brocade Guard entered the fray, those dozen or so master fighters fell quickly to a disadvantage.

Wang Chengbin personally escorted the Brocade Guard Commander, Li Yongfeng, to the scene.

Li Yongfeng arrived and cast an unhurried glance at Jiang Jiuxiao — standing before the bridal sedan in a protective posture — then cupped his hands.

"Congratulations on Lord Jiang's happy occasion. This commander offers his felicitations. Lord Jiang and his honored wife have had a fright today — please make your way home without delay."

"The auspicious hour must not be missed. Leave everything here to this commander."

Wang Chengbin's eyes went wide.

Li Yongfeng — that man who looked down on everyone — was being this courteous to Jiang Sijiu?

This fellow wore that same expression of a man owed several hundred thousand taels of silver even before the palace's own imperial princes.

Jiang Jiuxiao bowed in return, and said warmly: "Thank you for your trouble, Commander Li, and for the trouble of all your brothers."

He did not invite Li Yongfeng to the Jiang family's wedding banquet.

Unlike him and Wang Chengbin's families — whose loyalty was solely to the rightful line — Li Yongfeng's loyalty would always and only be to the current Emperor.

He was the Emperor's sharpest claw.

A man in his position, above all else, must avoid associating with princes and court officials.

They were all intelligent men — none would put the other in a difficult position.

Not only that, but they would each give the other quiet face.

After all, Jiang Jiuxiao was backing the Crown Prince. And the Crown Prince was the legitimate heir — far more likely to ascend smoothly than all the other princes and kings still bearing lesser titles.

Who knew — one day they might all serve the same master.

...

After Li Yongfeng took over the scene, Jiang Jiuxiao arranged new bearers — his own men this time.

"Ruyin — it's been taken care of. Everything is smooth." Jiang Jiuxiao informed Qin Ruyin where she sat in the sedan before swinging himself back onto his horse with casual ease.

The wedding music started up again.

The procession moved forward once more.

Wang Chengbin nudged his horse up beside Jiang Jiuxiao, keeping half a horse-length back.

"Jiang Sijiu — I didn't realize your new bride was like this!" Wang Chengbin held the reins with one hand and gave a thumbs-up with the other.

"If it were most women, they'd have fainted dead away by now."

"Wang Wu." Jiang Jiuxiao shot him a look. "She is my wife."

"Hey! What kind of person are you — can't even take a compliment?"

"All right, all right! A wife is not to be spoken of — I know, I know! Sorry, sorry!"

"There won't be a next time." Jiang Jiuxiao said seriously.

Seeing his sincerity, Wang Chengbin felt a twinge of regret for his quick mouth. "Right. Absolutely."

Wang Chengbin wasn't wrong, actually.

The other bride, Qin Ruyue, had fainted dead away inside her sedan.

Not only had she fainted — she had done so in the most undignified manner possible, her bridal robes soiled with bile. It was a wretched scene.

The other bridegroom, Wang Huaimian, had been hauled away by his own guards at the first sign of trouble and taken refuge in a shop along the street.

Later, when the fighting between the two wedding processions turned bloody, the spectators who had been watching panicked and rushed into the shop, packing it to the rafters.

The bridegroom's ceremonial cap was now crooked, and his red wedding robes had been trampled somewhere along the way, boot prints stamped all across the hem.

There was no describing the sorry state of it.

"Young master — young master!" His guards saw the Jiang family's procession moving off again and quickly called to him.

"Young master, the Jiang family's sedan is setting off again. Our household's..."

The Wang family's sedan had been set on the ground. After the Brocade Guard dragged away the "troublemakers," the Five City Infantry Command swiftly had the scene cleared.

Now it was only the Wang family's sedan, standing lonely in the middle of the intersection, surrounded by the scattered wreckage of Qin Ruyue's trousseau.

Staring at the mess, at his own sedan sitting forlorn at the roadside, Wang Huaimian's expression was dark enough to drip water.

He hadn't expected things to turn out like this.

Someone had approached him earlier with an offer to arrange eight bearers for him, sedan chair included. He had happily agreed despite his mother's objections — after all, this was surely Prince An showing him face. To refuse would have been to snub the Prince.

Only when his sedan turned out to be identical to the Jiang family's did he realize — he had been used.

No wonder.

No wonder he hadn't been allowed to hang the Wang family crest on the sedan.

One of the lead bearers had icily told him to hang the family crest on the first trousseau carrier instead.

He had originally been looking forward to watching Jiang Sijiu and Qin Sixth Young Miss make fools of themselves. In the end, it was he and Qin Ruyue who were the fools.

He had completely lost the will for this marriage.

Qin Ruyue was jolted awake by the rougher motion of the sedan.

Before the incident, the bearers with their excellent lightness of foot had carried her sedan as smoothly as if gliding on flat ground. She had suffered not the slightest discomfort — and had almost believed that Wang Huaimian cared for her and had specially arranged skilled bearers.

Now that Wang family servants had taken over the carrying, the ride was naturally not so smooth.

She looked down at the stains all over her bridal robes and felt not even the ability to weep.

Just before she lost consciousness, she had understood everything — Prince An had wanted to switch the brides.

He wanted Qin Ruyin. Why would he want to send her to the Jiang family in her place?

And yet — here and now, Qin Ruyue found herself not quite as resentful of Prince An wanting to swap her to the Jiang family as she had been moments before.

She had slowly been thinking: this life had grown so different from the last.

In this life, Jiang Jiuxiao had become President of the Board of Personnel so early — perhaps the Jiang family wouldn't suffer the same tragic fate it had in her previous life.

If that were so, marrying into the Jiang family wouldn't be so terrible.

With the experience of her past life behind her, she would certainly fare better than she had before.

And this Wang family...

Wang Huaimian's scholarship and looks were indeed exceptional. But his character was cause for serious concern.

Qin Ruyue's eyes turned cold and calculating.

She would never forget: when those eight bearers had carried her sedan flying through the air and she had pulled aside the curtain to call to Wang Huaimian for help — he had not looked back once. He had turned and run with his guards.

He had shown complete disregard for her life.

No matter how moving the letters he had written her were — what use were they?

Right now, she only hated Prince An for not completing the job. For not successfully switching her and Qin Ruyin.

She hated herself for being so frightened when she first realized she had been reborn — for being so blind, mistaking Wang Huaimian for gold when he was tin.

But since the swap had failed — her life would have to continue.

At least she didn't love that piece of tin anyway.

Endure the disgust if she must, and push Wang Huaimian up to where he needed to be.

...

The Jiang family wedding procession moved forward through the streets with music playing and the wedding party scattering paper bags of pine candy to children who ran up to block the sedan — joyful and lively.

As if the whole episode of the bride-swapping had never happened.

One of Wang Chengbin's men came to deliver a message.

Wang Chengbin's face went tight after hearing it. He spurred his horse back to Jiang Jiuxiao's side and said quietly: "All the people the Brocade Guard arrested have poisoned themselves."

"Mm?" Jiang Jiuxiao frowned.

The Brocade Guard's methods — they should not have failed to keep live prisoners.

"The poison was hidden in a hollowed tooth. The Brocade Guard was distracted for a moment and the survivors managed it." Wang Chengbin, knowing Jiang Jiuxiao's question, had already answered it.

"Not a single one left?" Jiang Jiuxiao asked.

Wang Chengbin shook his head. "Not one."

"No." The corner of Jiang Jiuxiao's lip curved coldly. "There is still Wang Huaimian."

Wang Chengbin, though he also bore the surname Wang, had already guessed that Wang Huaimian was not innocent in this affair.

He felt a deep irritation at sharing a surname with that dog.

"Then... should we let the Brocade Guard know?" Wang Chengbin asked.

"No need. Do you think the Brocade Guard is incompetent? They can't figure that out on their own?"

"Jiang Sijiu, your mind works better than mine — you're right. But are you willing to just swallow this grievance?"

Jiang Jiuxiao gave him a cool glance. "What's the rush?"

"A certain someone is a whetstone for grinding his own children. Even if I found every piece of evidence, that person would see to it the matter was smoothed over."

"Most likely, a certain someone is already on his way to that person to beg forgiveness right now."

Moments later, another of Wang Chengbin's subordinates came with a message.

Wang Chengbin's face fell after hearing it.

"Jiang Sijiu — you called it exactly!" He urged his horse a step closer to Jiang Jiuxiao and lowered his voice. "Prince An has entered the palace to see the Emperor."

"No matter. With His Highness the Crown Prince to hold him in check. This is no longer something you or I can get involved in — the imperial family must settle their own scores."

Jiang Jiuxiao's voice was calm and low. Yet in his eyes, without his knowing, a flame had ignited.

"Right. Just as long as you know what you're doing. If you have any plans, tell me in advance. You know my brain can't keep up with yours no matter how I try." Wang Chengbin looked at him seriously.

Jiang Jiuxiao nodded. "Don't worry. I'll let you know in advance."

"Good. Now — the Jiang mansion is almost in sight. Get ready to greet your bride!"

...

A burst of firecrackers filled the air. Noise and celebration swelled all around.

Qin Ruyin felt the sedan come to rest on the ground.

Then she heard Feng Mama's voice: "Young Miss — we have arrived at the Jiang family. In a moment, the auspicious matron from the Jiang family and the one from our Qin house will help you down from the sedan. Don't be afraid."

Qin Ruyin called back her assent.

Hearing Feng Mama's voice was deeply reassuring.

It was a pity that Feng Mama, as a servant from her natal home, had come ahead to the Jiang mansion in advance.

If Feng Mama had been at her sedan's side, she would not have been quite so frightened.

But in the end, Jiang Jiuxiao had come to reassure her himself — and now it was all over.

From today on, she would live a proper life with him.

Sure enough, when both auspicious matrons had finished reciting their blessings, they opened the sedan curtain and helped her out.

Then followed a long and elaborate series of wedding rituals.

Jiang Tai-furen was dressed in a mauve dragon-roundel brocade gown, her hair impeccably styled, wearing a matched set of solid-gold red-gemstone jewelry — dignified, composed, and magnificent.

She sat on the seat of honor above, watching the young couple below her, unable to keep the smile from the corners of her mouth.

After the husband and wife had bowed to one another, the chief officiant drew out a long, ceremonious final call: "The rites are complete — escort the couple to the bridal chamber!"

chapters.title: Chapter 103
chapters.content:
Very Pleased with the New Bride

By the customs and etiquette of the Great Ying Dynasty, after the new bride and groom were escorted to the bridal chamber, the groom was to lift the red bridal veil first.

The Jiang family's auspicious matron smiled at Jiang Jiuxiao: "Fourth Master, please lift the veil from the new bride."

The Qin family's auspicious matron, the Second Mistress Cheng, smiled and offered Jiang Jiuxiao a rod of jade green.

Qin Ruyin sat on the wedding bed, and even with the red veil over her head she could feel the overwhelming sea of red around her.

The red veil was lifted.

Qin Ruyin tilted her head slightly and looked up, eyes half-lidded.

Her gaze met the new groom's looking down at her.

He looked so fine in his great red wedding robes.

A genuine feast for the eyes.

And thinking that this man was now hers...

She gave him a radiant smile.

Jiang Jiuxiao was momentarily taken aback.

The two auspicious matrons praised the new bride profusely — what poise and grace, and such remarkable beauty.

The Jiang family women were all rather astonished.

This new bride — wasn't she the least bit shy?

When they had first been brides themselves...

And this bride was so strikingly beautiful. Just as Second Mistress and Third Mistress had said — she truly put all the Jiang family's young mistresses in the shade.

Jiang Jiuxiao hadn't smiled, but the corners of his lips were turned upward.

Next came the drinking of the wedding wine.

The two auspicious matrons each carried a cup of wine — one offered to Jiang Jiuxiao, the other carefully placed in Qin Ruyin's hands.

After the wedding wine, the custom in the capital was for the newlyweds to share a meal of togetherness — braided roll pastries and sweet dumplings, symbolizing a life complete and round.

After the shared meal came the hair-braiding ceremony.

Qin Ruyin was perfectly at ease throughout, doing whatever was asked of her.

When some of the women present made a light show of merry hazing, she kept her smile throughout — neither embarrassed nor impatient.

By showing the Jiang family women and their guests such grace, she earned warm praise from quite a few of the older women.

Qin Ruyin's one rule was: relax and go with it. As long as no one overstepped, she'd simply let it all roll over her.

She also trusted Jiang Jiuxiao.

She trusted he would not let her be wronged.

This trust, for now, had nothing to do with feelings.

True to expectation, the Jiang family women kept the hazing brief and light, and then Jiang Jiuxiao stepped in on her behalf.

The Jiang family women laughed cheerfully, teased the groom a little, and Jiang Jiuxiao bore it without irritation.

The Jiang family women all knew he disliked being teased under normal circumstances, so they knew when to stop.

They turned back to praise the new bride — what vivid beauty, what delightful temperament — and then together they withdrew.

"I need to go to the outer courtyard to toast the guests. I'll be a while before I come back to keep you company." Jiang Jiuxiao unconsciously softened his voice as he spoke gently to her.

"Please go ahead — do what you need to do." Qin Ruyin nodded readily.

Seeing how natural and unruffled she was, he was mildly surprised even though he had learned something about her beforehand.

Still, his brows took on a few shades of cheer — a hint of something bridegroom-like about him.

Shortly after, he spoke again: "Mother cannot come to the bridal chamber today, but she has had her own kitchen prepare food for you."

"When the servants bring it, please eat first. You don't need to wait for me to come back. In the Jiang family — especially in our own courtyard — you do whatever is most comfortable for you."

Qin Ruyin smiled and agreed, saying: "Go on, don't worry about any of this."

Jiang Jiuxiao nodded.

After he left, Zisu and Banjia and the other senior maids came to attend to Qin Ruyin.

The maids saw how considerate and caring the master was toward their young miss and were all delighted for her.

"Young Miss — the master treats you so well! First Mistress back home can rest easy now." Banjia said cheerfully, bringing over a cup of warm water.

Zisu corrected her: "Today there are only our own people in this room, so it's all right. But if there are outsiders, you must not use that title — you must call Young Miss the Fourth Mistress!"

Banjia stuck out her tongue obediently. "Zisu — I've got it!"

Zisu saw she was well-behaved and didn't lecture her further.

She went off to give the other younger maids their reminders.

For Qin Ruyin, this day — aside from the fright on the road — had been a very satisfying wedding.

The Jiang family had done things with real dignity and grandeur.

From the young brides who had come in and out teasing the couple she had heard nothing but admiring murmurs.

Of course, she was even more satisfied with Jiang Jiuxiao's manner.

To say "do whatever is most comfortable" in their own courtyard — that was exactly what she had hoped for.

Her heart was at ease. As long as she didn't act foolishly, life in the Jiang household would not be too difficult.

A quarter of an hour later, a Jiang family matron appeared at the door requesting to see them.

Zisu went and opened the door.

The Jiang family matron beamed at Zisu: "You must be one of the Fourth Mistress's personal maids? This old servant is from the Tai-furen's apartments — you can call me Matron Ding."

Zisu immediately curtsied and smiled warmly: "Matron Ding, good day. I am Zisu, personal maid to the Fourth Mistress."

Matron Ding looked Zisu over carefully and her smile deepened. "What a fine girl! As expected — those who serve our Fourth Mistress are all excellent!"

Zisu humbly returned the compliment.

Matron Ding stated her purpose with a cheerful smile.

"This servant has come to bring the Fourth Mistress her meal. Tai-furen is concerned the Fourth Mistress has been on her feet all day at such a young age and must be hungry — please have the young ladies attend to the Fourth Mistress's meal without delay."

Zisu thanked Matron Ding.

Matron Ding had the little maids carrying food boxes file in one by one.

In short order, a full spread of meat dishes, vegetable dishes, soups, and pastries was laid across the table.

Matron Ding herself then came forward to pay respects to Qin Ruyin.

"This servant greets the Fourth Mistress!"

"Fourth Mistress — Tai-furen says you must not wait for the Fourth Master to return from the outer courtyard before eating. Please eat first; we cannot let you go hungry."

Qin Ruyin expressed sincere thanks to Jiang Tai-furen.

She was genuinely grateful to this mother-in-law of hers.

From her mother and sisters at home, she had heard about mothers-in-law who gave new brides a hard time the very day they crossed the threshold — through subtle little jabs and tests to put them in their place.

Some mothers-in-law were all warmth and graciousness before a bride came through the gate, but showed a completely different face once she had.

She still remembered Qin Ruyue mocking her before — insinuating that Jiang Tai-furen was only showing surface warmth, and that once she was in the door she'd find out just how two-faced the woman was.

But looking at things now, Jiang Tai-furen was nothing at all like the person Qin Ruyue had described.

There was no reason to go through such genuine trouble unless she meant it.

Qin Ruyin's heart was thoroughly settled.

She was still in her bridal makeup, and the elaborate dress and ornaments made eating properly inconvenient.

She had Zisu bring her two pieces of cake.

Matron Ding saw her eat the cake with complete ease, openly and without fuss, and kept nodding inwardly.

Tai-furen had always been fondest of a girl with exactly this kind of character.

Hungry and told to eat — she ate. When something was inconvenient to eat, she didn't push it — she ate what was manageable first.

Wasn't this better than those brides who were famished to the point of their front and back ribs touching yet still insisted they weren't hungry, that they would wait for their husband to come back?

Tai-furen often said that not making oneself suffer was also a sign of a woman's strength.

She hadn't quite understood before.

Not until she saw this new Fourth Mistress.

After all, not just any capital noblewoman could marry into being wife to their Fourth Master without flinching.

Seeing Qin Ruyin eat two pieces of cake and then stop, Matron Ding understood the new Fourth Mistress had measure.

She was not, as Second Mistress had worried, the sort of young and naive innocent who acted on impulse.

"Fourth Mistress — before this servant came, Tai-furen also asked me to share a few things with you clearly."

"Please do, Matron Ding." Qin Ruyin accepted the cup of clear tea Zisu handed her, rinsed her mouth, and nodded to Matron Ding with a smile.

Matron Ding clearly and concisely conveyed Jiang Tai-furen's instructions.

The main subject was staff.

Following Jiang family custom, Qin Ruyin's chamber had been provided with one head management matron, four senior maids, eight second-tier maids, twelve third-tier maids, and various rough servants.

But since Qin Ruyin had brought her own people from her natal home, she was to prioritize using her own people and not feel any pressure otherwise.

Qin Ruyin agreed.

Though she couldn't leave the Jiang family's provided staff entirely unused.

In her natal home, she had only Feng Mama as a first-tier head management matron.

The first-tier head management matron the Jiang family provided from Tai-furen would certainly need to be used.

Feng Mama would then only be responsible for managing the people and matters around Qin Ruyin herself, while the routine household affairs would go to the Jiang family's management matron.

As for senior maids — she currently had three of her own.

After a brief consideration, Qin Ruyin said to Matron Ding: "I have only Feng Mama as a head management matron, so the position is still open for one. As for senior maids — I have room for only one more slot. Matron Ding, whoever you feel is suitable — just let my Feng Mama know."

Matron Ding's eyes crinkled with delight to see her so readily give up one head management matron position and one senior maid position.

When the Fifth Mistress had come through the gate, she hadn't used a single person the household had provided — not the head management matron, not the senior maids.

Even when Second and Third Mistresses came through the gate in their time, pleasant as they were on the surface, they had not used those provided staff either.

Tai-furen had never said a word about it, but it must have stung inside.

"Fourth Mistress — don't worry. Tai-furen specifically had these people trained. They are all capable, and loyal only to the Fourth Mistress!" Matron Ding couldn't help adding this assurance.

Qin Ruyin nodded with a smile. "Then I'm quite fortunate. Matron Ding, when you go back, please thank my mother-in-law on my behalf. Tell her I will come pay my respects to her first thing tomorrow morning."

Matron Ding readily agreed, then took her leave.

The senior maid standing at Qin Ruyin's side, Banjia, immediately stepped forward two paces and pressed a heavy purse into Matron Ding's hand.

"Thank you for the trouble of coming all this way, Matron. This is wedding money from the Fourth Mistress."

Matron Ding accepted it, offered Qin Ruyin a round of thanks, and added many auspicious blessings.

From the moment she walked out of the bridal chamber all the way back to Tai-furen's apartments, the smile never left her lips.

"Young Miss, shall you have a bit more?" Zisu came over with a concerned look.

Qin Ruyin shook her head. "Those two pieces of cake took the edge off — I'm not hungry anymore. I'll wait until the Fourth Master comes back."

Zisu acknowledged and called out quietly to a small maid waiting at the door.

The maid was sharp-witted and immediately set off at a quick trot.

Not long after, she came back.

Zisu heard her report, then relayed it to Qin Ruyin: "Young Miss — His Highness the Crown Prince has come to the outer courtyard in person. The Fourth Master may not be back so soon."

Qin Ruyin was surprised.

Even the Crown Prince had come to drink at the wedding banquet?

Jiang Jiuxiao really did command extraordinary respect.

Qin Ruyin didn't trouble herself with that and simply asked Zisu: "Have my things all been put in order?"

Tomorrow the new bride was to meet and gift the family — there was no small amount to prepare.

Gifts for the Jiang family elders. Gifts for those of the same generation. Gifts for those of the younger generation. And wedding money to distribute to servants.

Zisu immediately answered: "Young Miss, don't worry — all in order. Juhong led the younger ones and handled it personally."

Qin Ruyin nodded.

Jiang Jiuxiao had not yet come back, and she could not remove her makeup or change out of her bridal robes.

Left with nothing to do, a person's mind naturally wandered.

Qin Ruyin found herself with some anxiety about the wedding night.

The original body was still so young — sixteen years old. In the world she had come from, that would still be a minor.

She didn't know how Jiang Jiuxiao would react if she asked him to wait before consummating the marriage.

Just as she was thinking about this, there was a sound at the bridal chamber door, followed by a chorus of respectful greetings.

Jiang Jiuxiao had come back.

Hadn't the Crown Prince personally come to offer congratulations? How had he returned so quickly?

Qin Ruyin felt a flutter of nerves.

"Why are you still wearing the phoenix crown?" Jiang Jiuxiao came striding in.

Zisu and Banjia and the other senior maids quickly retreated outside to wait.

"You weren't back yet." His question had only made her aware of how stiff her neck had become.

"That phoenix crown is quite heavy." Jiang Jiuxiao personally set about removing the crown from her head.

His movements were very gentle — afraid of hurting the delicate girl.

"How do you know the phoenix crown is heavy?" Qin Ruyin had been tense and grasping for something to say, but the moment the words left her mouth she regretted them.

chapters.title: Chapter 104
chapters.content:
Wedding Night

He had been married once before — of course he knew.

She herself had no particular aversion to that thought.

But from what her father and brothers had investigated about the secrets surrounding his first wife — Jiang Jiuxiao had apparently suffered a profound emotional wound.

Bringing it up now — would it remind him of something unpleasant?

Just as Qin Ruyin was feeling uneasy, Jiang Jiuxiao curved his lips.

"How would I not know? I personally chose the design for this phoenix crown and had it made to order by a goldsmith and a jade craftsman."

It had been sent to the Qin family along with the ceremonial dressing gifts.

Qin Ruyin had not known the phoenix crown was Jiang family-made. Her family hadn't thought to tell her, and she had assumed it was prepared at home.

But by Great Ying Dynasty custom, both the phoenix crown and the red bridal veil were sent by the groom's side on the day the ceremonial dressing gifts were delivered.

If the groom held the bride in high regard, the crown would be all the more exquisite and costly.

Seeing the girl in her red wedding robes go blank, Jiang Jiuxiao knew she hadn't realized the crown had been sent to the Qin household by his family.

"Fourth Master — I didn't know you had gone to all this trouble personally." It would have been strange not to be moved.

"Don't say foolish things." Jiang Jiuxiao glanced at her. "Having made up my mind to take you as my wife, how could I be careless?"

A warmth spread through Qin Ruyin's heart.

After Jiang Jiuxiao removed the phoenix crown, Qin Ruyin felt her head grow wonderfully light and free.

She truly wanted to roll her neck around and check whether it still functioned.

Then she heard Jiang Jiuxiao say: "The bridal robes are also heavy and cumbersome. Have your maids help you change into something lighter."

Qin Ruyin had been thinking exactly the same thing.

She quickly called Zisu and Banjia in to support her to the side room next door to change.

The bridal chamber was the main room. The side room on the right was arranged as a wardrobe, and the one on the left as a washroom.

She found this arrangement rather suited to her tastes.

To be honest, it was more spacious and convenient than her room at home.

With better privacy too.

Zisu found her a fresh water-pink long gown to change into, then helped her and Banjia remove the bridal makeup.

The special bridal hairstyle was also undone and replaced with a loose, soft flat bun suitable for resting.

Two ruby-studded hair combs were pressed into the hair at either temple — lending her a hint of the charm of a young married woman.

Jiang Jiuxiao watched Qin Ruyin, supported by her two maids, come out from the side room. The corners of his lips moved slightly.

Stripped of the heavy adornment, she looked even more ravishingly fresh.

And even younger.

"Mother prepared this table of food and you haven't touched a bite — aren't you hungry?" He looked away and walked toward the table spread with dishes.

"As it happens, I had a fair amount to drink in the outer courtyard. Have a meal with me."

Qin Ruyin had actually lost her appetite from going too long without food, and after eating two pieces of cake she no longer felt hungry at all.

But since he had asked her, she went and sat down at the table as well.

Zisu and Banjia moved to serve the two of them.

Jiang Jiuxiao waved them off. "I have never liked being served by others. You need only attend to your mistress."

Zisu and Banjia froze, then looked to their own young miss.

Jiang Jiuxiao hadn't put it entirely plainly. It wasn't that he disliked being served generally — he disliked being served by women.

Qin Ruyin saw the situation and said to her two senior maids: "Do as the Fourth Master says. I don't need to be served either."

She added: "You two have been on your feet all day too, and haven't had dinner yet. Go out and eat something, and then rest properly tonight."

Jiang Jiuxiao found himself taking a closer look at her for looking after her maids with such genuine warmth.

Zisu and Banjia acknowledged and withdrew.

They and the other girls who had come with Qin Ruyin to the Jiang household would naturally have their own meal today — the Jiang family would have kept dinner waiting for them.

Qin Ruyin didn't like cold food, and she knew his digestion was poor.

She said to him: "Your stomach isn't good — don't have anything cold. And one shouldn't eat too heavily in the evening. Perhaps just a warm soup?"

"Yes." Jiang Jiuxiao answered in one syllable and said nothing more.

Qin Ruyin knew he was a man of few words.

She didn't feel there was anything awkward about the two of them sitting in silence.

At a moment like this, actually, not speaking felt more natural.

She wasn't the sort to make conversation for the sake of it either.

After the meal, Qin Ruyin called people in to clear up.

Once the food was taken away, she went to rinse her mouth and bathe.

She thought of what her mother had instructed, and turned back to ask him: "Shall I attend to your washing?"

Every line of her face screamed "please say no."

Her mother had told her before she left: a wife should show deference to her husband. In the presence of others, use respectful forms of address. This was the accepted custom of noble households.

Qin Ruyin had taken her mother's advice.

She and Jiang Jiuxiao were not yet truly man and wife, and he was such a formidable senior court official. She also genuinely respected him.

Using deferential address felt quite right.

Seeing how plainly she hoped he would decline, Jiang Jiuxiao suddenly very much wanted to laugh.

He covered the upward curve of his lips with a loose fist and said quietly: "No need. I don't like being attended to."

Qin Ruyin couldn't have cared less whether this was a brush-off — she was simply happy. She said brightly: "All right! Then I'll go wash up!"

But Jiang Jiuxiao called her back.

"Ruyin — you should change how you address me."

"Oh! Fourth Master?" Qin Ruyin tilted her head.

Right... and yet not quite right.

Let it go.

Jiang Jiuxiao nodded. "That's not entirely wrong."

Qin Ruyin, not troubling herself further, quickly slipped off to the washroom.

There was a little awkwardness there, honestly.

After she had bathed, Juhong — who had already eaten — came with several small maids to help Qin Ruyin towel-dry her hair.

Qin Ruyin had beautiful hair — black, plentiful, thick and lustrous.

Once washed, one person alone was not enough to towel it dry.

Seeing she had even washed her hair, Jiang Jiuxiao paused.

Washing hair in the evening was not easy to dry.

He cast a quiet, suspicious look at this little bride he had just brought home.

Could it be she was stalling for time?

Actually — she only needed to tell him plainly and he would not pressure her.

But then he thought of what his mother had told him privately.

He would broach the subject shortly.

He too had needed to fight today, so he also needed to bathe.

Qin Ruyin saw he was going to bathe and quickly told Juhong to find clothes for him.

"No need — I'll find my own." Jiang Jiuxiao said and went to the right side room himself.

Juhong had no choice but to turn back and help her young miss towel-dry her hair.

They used towels with excellent absorbency.

She was terrified of delaying her young miss and the Fourth Master's wedding night and worked with great diligence.

With Juhong and the others working hard, though the hair wasn't fully dry, it was only barely damp.

Just a little longer and it would be completely dry.

Qin Ruyin: ...

There was really no need to work quite so hard.

Half a quarter of an hour later, Jiang Jiuxiao came in.

At the sound, Qin Ruyin looked over.

He hadn't washed his hair, but it looked clean and fresh — he must have washed it the night before.

He was wearing a new indigo-blue home robe, standing tall and easy and elegant.

Devastatingly handsome.

The little maids Juhong had brought took one look at him, quickly curtsied, and retreated.

Qin Ruyin was sitting sideways on the bed, hair still loose, when she saw him walking toward her. Her heart suddenly thundered.

The dragon-and-phoenix wedding candles burned with a steady hiss and the occasional crackle of a sparking wick.

Qin Ruyin's face had, without her noticing, grown quite warm.

She glanced down again at the vast wedding bed with its great red coverlet embroidered with a hundred children, and her heart beat harder still.

"Is your hair dry? Damp hair will give you a headache." Jiang Jiuxiao spoke.

"Dry? Not dry? It's dry... I think..."

She was talking a little nonsense.

Jiang Jiuxiao silently sighed.

No matter how carefree she was — she was still only a child.

He reached out and felt her hair.

It was dry.

But in the next moment, looking at his own right hand holding a small lock of her hair, he went still.

He — had felt no aversion.

The moment he realized this, he dropped the lock of hair at once and drew his hand back.

"The hair is dry... the hour is late. Let's rest." He said, and moved to climb past Qin Ruyin toward the inside of the bed.

As husband and wife, sharing a bed was only natural.

There was no avoiding it.

He would have her sleep on the outer side — more convenient if she needed to get up in the night.

A rush of warm yet crisp scent swept over Qin Ruyin, and her whole mind went blank.

chapters.title: Chapter 105
chapters.content:
To Consummate or Not to Consummate

Qin Ruyin knew perfectly well, in the rational part of her mind, that this was not the world she had come from.

In this world, the self she now inhabited was considered an adult.

And yet she was a soul that had come from the modern era.

Jiang Jiuxiao noticed her unfocused gaze and felt her body go rigid. He paused.

"I'll sleep on the inner side."

He climbed over and lay down on the inner side of the bed.

Qin Ruyin drew a slow breath, and gave a stiff "mm."

Her mother had told her: a husband and wife usually sleep with the wife on the outer side, so she could more easily rise to serve her husband if he was thirsty in the night.

She had laughed at the idea that ancient women had no rights of their own. But that was all it was — laughing.

She did think, though: he could have climbed into the inner side from the foot of the bed rather than coming from this end.

He had startled her half to death doing it this way.

Qin Ruyin laughed quietly at herself and lay down too.

The moment she was down, she squeezed her eyes shut.

Like an ostrich burying its head in the sand.

Jiang Jiuxiao, however, extended his hand.

The instant Qin Ruyin felt his warm palm settle over her arm, she jolted and her eyes flew open.

But she had already fallen into the shelter of his warm, broad embrace.

Her mind went completely blank. She couldn't think at all.

"Mother said that not consummating on the wedding night would be bad for you..." Lord Jiang — always so composed and steady — spoke with a slight unsteadiness in his voice.

Qin Ruyin couldn't tell if her own heart was pounding, or his.

For Jiang Jiuxiao, this was the first time since the age of three — when his wet nurse stopped holding him — that he had been this close to a woman.

She was his wife.

His one and only, his registered-in-the-clan-record original wife.

If he did not consummate the marriage on their wedding night, the day after it would bring her nothing but criticism.

His mother was right.

Having brought her home with the full ceremony of eight sedan bearers, having given her every reason for joy and anticipation — he should not allow her to face censure in the Jiang family.

Not consummating would also cause unease in her natal family.

He steeled himself. His hand moved, searching for the ties of her robe.

Qin Ruyin instinctively thrust both hands out and seized his.

"Behave..."

Jiang Jiuxiao had only managed that one word before Qin Ruyin's eyes — liquid and wide as a little deer's — looked up at him.

"Fourth Master — my monthly cycle hasn't come yet."

Jiang Jiuxiao: "!"

That poised and scholarly handsome face went scarlet in an instant.

He had never once blushed in his entire life.

Wedding night — he had anticipated many scenarios. This was the one he had not anticipated.

This made him look like a man without a shred of decency — a villain who would take advantage of an underage girl.

While the Great Ying Dynasty's law held that a girl was of age at fifteen after her coming-of-age ceremony, there were plenty of families who kept their daughters until sixteen or seventeen before marrying them out.

Because some girls matured later and were not suited to early marriage.

To think about it — the Jiang family had set the wedding date rather quickly that day. His father-in-law's household had been in the middle of the clan split at the time.

They had probably had no choice but to grit their teeth and agree.

Drawing a slow deep breath, he told the first lie of his life: "That's — fine. I just don't want you catching a chill. I'll hold you while we sleep."

Seeing his face that red and his speech that halting, Qin Ruyin found her fear and tension strangely dissolving. She almost wanted to laugh.

She had lived two lives, and though she had never personally experienced such things, she had at least seen how others went about them.

He had clearly just been about to—

Seeing the little girl say nothing for a long time, Jiang Jiuxiao opened the eyes he had fake-closed.

"On this matter — why didn't your mother's side say anything to my mother?"

Fake-sleeping Qin Ruyin also opened her eyes.

She asked with some surprise: "On this sort of matter — shouldn't the man's side always inquire in advance?"

"At the time — given our circumstances, it wasn't something my mother could bring up on her own initiative."

"And she was probably afraid your mother would misunderstand that our family didn't want to go through with the marriage."

Jiang Jiuxiao assumed she was upset.

He reached out and touched her forehead, and Qin Ruyin's face flushed.

He spoke to reassure her: "It's fine — it's not a serious matter. I only want to tell you — from now on, whatever is on your mind, you can tell me directly."

"I understand." Qin Ruyin, seeing he wasn't angry and had no intention of pressing further, breathed a secret sigh of relief.

It wasn't that she was unwilling.

It was that something in her hadn't quite gotten over that particular hurdle.

Better to wait until her cycle had come at least.

"Are you sleepy?" Jiang Jiuxiao, seeing her composure remained quite steady, also relaxed inwardly.

He didn't want to frighten her and leave a shadow over her heart.

He understood better than anyone the difficulty of carrying a shadow in one's heart.

"Not... not sleepy."

She had been exhausted and drowsy before, but the fright had cleared her head entirely.

"Then shall we talk for a while?" Jiang Jiuxiao asked.

He was a man of few words. If he was suddenly suggesting they talk, it wasn't going to be idle chatter.

Qin Ruyin gave a soft "mm."

Jiang Jiuxiao then told her about that day's bride-swapping incident.

...

"So you have confirmed that the mastermind behind it is Prince An?" Qin Ruyin asked.

"Yes." Jiang Jiuxiao saw no reason to conceal it from her.

"What Prince An's ultimate purpose is remains to be determined. But after what he did today, the Brocade Guard will certainly be investigating him in secret."

Qin Ruyin understood.

The mantis catches the cicada, while the sparrow waits behind.

Jiang Jiuxiao was the sparrow.

He had used the situation to draw Prince An out into the open.

Though it was not an outright victory either.

Because after Prince An's scheme failed, he had acted decisively and immediately gone into the palace to beg the Emperor's pardon.

As for how the Emperor would handle the matter — it was too early to tell.

They would know within a few days.

Hearing all of this, Qin Ruyin was covered in a cold sweat.

"It was never my intention to put you in harm's way. But the enemy was visible while we were hidden — being perpetually on the defensive was no long-term solution."

"At the time I had prepared thoroughly."

"I deliberately brought in the Five City Infantry Command — that way there were official witnesses."

Afraid Qin Ruyin might not fully understand, he explained: "Men of the Five City Infantry Command all hold official ranks. When it comes to a court confrontation, they are far more useful than my private guards."

Jiang Jiuxiao didn't want the girl to think him cold-blooded.

Even if he was, under ordinary circumstances, exactly that.

"Fourth Master, don't worry — I understand all right, and I understand your intentions." Qin Ruyin said sensibly.

What she feared most were people who thought things but didn't say them.

Jiang Jiuxiao, though a man of few words, opened his mouth and spoke. That was excellent.

She felt even more confident about their life ahead in the Jiang family.

"This means you'll need to go out less for the time being." Jiang Jiuxiao looked at her with something apologetic.

Until Prince An was defeated, she and her Fourth Sister would not be safe.

Qin Ruyin gave a quiet "mm."

Then added: "There is at least the return visit home that I must go out for."

"Of course. I've already arranged the men. I'll accompany you myself that day." He gently squeezed her soft hand.

For the first time, he agreed with his mother — she truly was a sensible and well-mannered little girl.

"And — the Jiang family is a large clan and has not yet divided. My brothers are many, and so are my cousins. Life in the inner household will not be quiet for you."

"But don't be afraid. Anyone who dares give you trouble — use my name to deal with them."

"And — Mother is very fond of you and will protect you. If something urgent comes up and I'm not in the household, don't hesitate to disturb her. Be sure to send someone to inform her right away."

Qin Ruyin listened, and listened — and fell asleep.

The dragon-and-phoenix wedding candles were meant to burn until dawn.

After Qin Ruyin had been silent for quite a long time, Jiang Jiuxiao looked over by the soft amber candlelight.

He saw her eyes were tightly closed, her breathing quiet and even, sleeping peacefully.

He propped himself up and looked at her sleeping face for a moment.

How well-behaved she was. He breathed a quiet sigh.

Then he shook his head and smiled faintly — what was wrong with him?

Though they had not consummated the marriage — it felt, in a way, a little like he had a home.

By the middle of the night there had been no call for hot water from the new bridal chamber.

That night, everyone in the Jiang inner household who wanted to know — knew.

Jiang Tai-furen was old and naturally a light sleeper, and on top of that she had one great matter not yet settled, so she went to bed very late.

When midnight had come and gone and still no word came from the bridal chamber about hot water, she was furious and gave her bed frame a sharp slap.

"That fourth boy! Children grow up and stop listening — he's going in one ear and out the other!"

Her personal attendant, Hua Mama, hurried to soothe her.

"Tai-furen, don't fret. That the Fourth Master brought our Fourth Mistress safely home is already the greatest joy!

"Consummation can't be rushed — give the Fourth Master time to gradually see our Fourth Mistress's good qualities."

"Besides, our Fourth Mistress is still quite young, so delicate and tender... you yourself were worried before about her being too young."

"Once you have nurtured and raised our Fourth Mistress a little more, when she's a bit older the consummation will go all the better — and that will be the right time to be expecting children."

"Ah. I suppose you're right."

"These things — it's not that I don't know the reason. It's just that a person is always selfish. One always thinks of one's own children first."

Jiang Tai-furen said ruefully.

"Who doesn't think of their own children first?" Hua Mama laughed.

"You are so good to our Fourth Mistress — she knows it in her heart. Otherwise when Matron Ding went to speak to her about the maids today, the Fourth Mistress would not have so readily accepted the people you sent."

Jiang Tai-furen smiled too. "Ruyin is a sensible girl. From what Matron Ding said, she had a slot open for a head management matron and a senior maid from the very start."

Hua Mama put in a good word for Qin Ruyin.

"Of course! This shows that the Fourth Mistress and you have the mother-and-daughter-in-law bond already — she has made up her mind to live well in this household!"

Jiang Tai-furen brightened. "How could she not?"

Her resentment at her son for not consummating the marriage had already melted away.

She also hadn't placed it on Qin Ruyin's account — she simply assumed it was her son who was unwilling.

Not consummating had its advantages.

Only — she would need to give him a thorough talking-to tomorrow.

"Speaking of childbearing — there's nothing I can do to rush it. I've made peace with it. As long as Old Four lives his life properly with Ruyin, that would be perfect!"

"I hope that today on their wedding day he can let go of that old heartache and be at harmony and happiness with Ruyin."

Hua Mama quickly added: "This servant is certain, Tai-furen — the Fourth Master and Fourth Mistress will have a house full of children and grandchildren!"

"Then let your words be an omen!" Jiang Tai-furen loved to hear such auspicious things.

"The hour is late. Tomorrow Old Four and Old Four's wife still have the tea ceremony to greet the family. I'll go to sleep too."

"Oh yes — have you checked the gifts I've prepared for Ruyin tomorrow?"

"You don't need to worry — they've been checked several times." Hua Mama said, smiling as she attended to Jiang Tai-furen's rest.

"Yes, yes. Speaking of it — it truly wasn't easy for Old Four to be willing to take a new wife. She is our family's precious treasure. We absolutely cannot let her be wronged."

Hua Mama smiled in agreement.

But inwardly she had a small worry.

Including the newly arrived Fourth Mistress, Tai-furen now had five legitimate daughters-in-law.

Aside from the Fourth Mistress who was new and whose true character was not yet fully seen, none of the other four were easy women.

Yet they all kept themselves reined in before Tai-furen.

With Tai-furen above pressing them down, the sisters-in-law didn't dare make too ugly a scene among themselves.

But in private — the undercurrents of competition and jostling for advantage were no small thing.

The household-managing First Mistress was a second wife, and in private had taken no small amount of quiet losses to those sisters-in-law.

And some of the cousins' wives looked like bodhisattvas on the outside but had vicious hands in private.

Everyone was desperate to grab a little more, to pull more advantage toward their own families.

Why did Tai-furen value the First Mistress so highly?

Because under all those hidden currents, the First Mistress still managed to maintain a broad surface of balance and harmony.

Tai-furen's years were increasing, and many things — even if she knew them — what could she do?

Manage them for a while — could she manage them for a lifetime?

Her only hope was that this new Fourth Mistress truly had a quick and perceptive mind — not competing for what shouldn't be competed for, but absolutely winning what needed to be won.

Only then would Tai-furen's remaining years be easier.

...

Due to a condition in her previous life, Qin Ruyin had always slept in one position without moving.

When Jiang Jiuxiao woke, she was still lying in exactly the same position she'd been in when she fell asleep — sleeping sweetly.

The more he looked, the better-behaved she seemed.

Oddly enough — he had never slept particularly well. He typically woke several times a night.

But this night, though he had gone to sleep later than usual and had an extra person beside him, he slept straight through until the third crow of the rooster.

He hadn't even dreamed.

Sleeping this well had improved his color somewhat.

His mood, too, was unusually pleasant.

Looking at the little girl sleeping so sweetly, he was rather reluctant to wake her.

Just as he was hesitating, her attending senior maid arrived.

The familiar one — called Zisu.

Li Yi had mentioned her from time to time.

"Fourth Master — this servant has come to wake the Fourth Mistress..." She was worried her young miss would miss the important tea-and-greeting ceremony today if she slept any longer.

Jiang Jiuxiao had been about to nod, then reconsidered and asked Zisu: "Does your mistress usually rise early or late?"

chapters.title: Chapter 106
chapters.content:
How Could You Expect Your Son to Do That?

"This—" Zisu didn't know what the Fourth Master meant, and was worried that a wrong answer might bring trouble on her young miss.

"Just tell me honestly. If your mistress normally rises late, let her sleep a while longer." Jiang Jiuxiao said mildly.

Zisu's heart relaxed.

So that was what the master meant.

She quickly replied: "Young Miss does like to sleep in — but Fourth Master, don't worry, from now on this servant will—"

"Just today, let her sleep in. Other days, as long as there's nothing pressing, let your mistress sleep as she likes. Tai-furen doesn't like daughters-in-law coming every day to pay their respects — only on the first and fifteenth of each month."

Zisu immediately agreed.

She was overjoyed for her young miss.

The master's face gave nothing away, but every word he spoke showed consideration for her young miss.

And Tai-furen only expected daughters-in-law to come for the first and fifteenth — what a rare and wonderful mother-in-law.

In how many of the capital's noble households did mothers-in-law use morning greetings as a way to put daughters-in-law through their paces?

After Jiang Jiuxiao had dressed, washed, and was ready, he picked up a book and sat reading by the window.

Zisu looked at the sky and decided her young miss truly could not sleep any longer.

She was about to go wake her when Qin Ruyin gave a soft murmur, sat up from the bed, and stretched a long, luxurious stretch.

What a good sleep.

The book in Jiang Jiuxiao's hands came to a halt.

His gaze drifted over.

"Young Miss — we must dress and wash quickly!" Zisu panicked and hurriedly called all the second-tier maids waiting outside the door in.

After a flurry of activity:

Qin Ruyin, wearing a brilliant red pomegranate-and-scrolling-vine brocade gown with gold threading, a matched set of purple crystal and garnet jewelry, stood bright and vivid before Jiang Jiuxiao.

Jiang Jiuxiao set his book down on the side table and looked her up and down.

"Very nice. Vivid colors suit you well."

Qin Ruyin hadn't expected a compliment.

She gave him a glowing smile and said: "Thank you for waiting, Fourth Master. Shall we go pay our respects to Mother and the elders?"

Jiang Jiuxiao nodded.

Qin Ruyin made a private comment in her head.

He was perfectly pleasant last night.

Today the ice-face was back.

And he was so strikingly handsome.

...

After Qin Ruyin followed Jiang Jiuxiao through the tea ceremony and met the family, she received a pile of first-meeting gifts.

The Jiang family had many descendants, and many small children of the younger generation — she gave out quite a few things as well.

For Jiang Jiuxiao's own blood nephews and nieces, her gifts were fine ones — prepared at two hundred taels' worth per person.

Jiang Jiuxiao had given her a betrothal gift of ten thousand taels, and she had originally intended to return six thousand to him.

But he had told Feng Mama to pass her a message in advance — no need to return it. The full ten thousand was his gift to her.

Since the man was so generous, out of respect for his feelings, she certainly couldn't treat his own nephews and nieces poorly.

Besides, she was spending his silver to play the generous one.

That said — she felt no psychological burden about it at all.

This man was her husband now.

Seeing her such generosity, her sisters-in-law were simultaneously pleased and faintly resentful.

They had been told Old Four's bride was from a modest family.

This was modest?

They had assumed that among her eighty trays of trousseau — aside from the palace gifts — most of it was for show.

But seeing her spend so freely, they understood: those trays must have been packed solid.

They couldn't be entirely blamed for their suspicion. The old matriarch had glanced at the trousseau list and then put it away in a box — they couldn't get a look at it if they tried.

...

After Jiang Jiuxiao escorted Qin Ruyin back to their courtyard, he was summoned to Jiang Tai-furen's Rong'an Hall.

Jiang Tai-furen had been notably less warm to him than to the new bride during the morning's tea ceremony.

Jiang Jiuxiao knew very well why his mother was displeased with him.

"Old Four — what did Mother tell you? Why won't you listen?"

Jiang Tai-furen didn't even invite him to sit — she launched straight into reproach.

"You're a grown man, so it doesn't matter so much for you. But do you know how difficult it is for a woman in the inner household?"

That morning, several of the distant cousin wives' thinly veiled jabs and snide remarks toward the Fourth Mistress had been too much for her — she had quietly given them a reprimand.

Fortunately the Fourth Mistress had been quick on her feet — unflustered and unashamed, she had simply turned and asked that pointed cousin's wife directly: how exactly did a distant cousin's wife come to know such a private matter between husband and wife?

Jiang Jiuxiao, in fact, had also followed up with a remark — saying he too was curious to know how a certain cousin's wife had come to know.

The bird that sticks its neck out gets shot. That cousin's wife, asked such a question, didn't dare open her mouth, and the others who'd been hoping to see Qin Ruyin embarrassed naturally didn't dare push further.

"The matter of not consummating — Mother won't blame Ruyin. Mother only wants a word with you!" Jiang Tai-furen glared at him. "Are you still not over that old business?"

Jiang Jiuxiao drew a slow, deep breath.

"Mother — it's not what you think."

"Still saying it's not? You brought Ruyin home and entered her name in the clan record — that means you accept her."

"Yet you won't consummate the marriage with her, and let people mock her behind her back. Why is that?"

"Mother truly cannot understand you anymore!" Jiang Tai-furen said in frustration — she had in truth never quite been able to understand this fourth son of hers.

As a note: the first time Jiang Jiuxiao married, he had not entered his first wife's name in the clan record.

In the Great Ying Dynasty's noble families, only the original principal wife's name was entered in the clan record.

For example, the First Mistress Fang was a second wife — even she could not be entered in the Jiang clan record, though her children could be.

The Jiang family's concubines, and children recorded under a legal wife's name — even those children could not be entered in the clan record.

In other words: if Jiang Jiuxiao had entered his first wife's name in the clan record, Qin Ruyin would have had no right to be entered.

The fact that her name was now in the Jiang clan record meant the Jiang clan recognized that Jiang Jiuxiao's original principal wife was she, and not the first woman.

"Mother — your son did hear your words. It's just that—"

"Just what?" Jiang Tai-furen cut him off. "You still can't let go of the old business, and you're still averse to contact with women?"

"No." Jiang Jiuxiao shook his head. "Let Mother let me finish."

"Say it then!" Jiang Tai-furen had dismissed all her attendants — with only the two of them present, there was no need to worry about being overheard.

"Mother doesn't know — Ruyin's monthly cycle hasn't come yet. She's still just a child. How could you expect your son to bring himself to do it?"

"Ah?" Jiang Tai-furen's eyes went wide. "Is that so?"

"Isn't it?"

"Is your son the sort of depraved and heartless person to do that?"

Jiang Tai-furen realized she had misunderstood her son and was a little embarrassed.

"Oh dear! That child — I never even thought of this. I assumed—"

Mother and son looked at each other and both felt the urge to laugh.

"And you're laughing!" Seeing him truly smile, Jiang Tai-furen couldn't help laughing and scolding him at the same time.

She then said: "It's my fault too — when I met Ruyin's mother, I was so occupied with everything, I forgot to ask her."

This was truly not the fault of the woman's side.

It was the Jiang family who had set the wedding date too hastily.

And the woman's side had been in that difficult situation at the time.

If the woman's side had deliberately raised this matter, she would probably have assumed they were trying to back out of the marriage.

"Never mind — your marriage has always been unlucky, and it wasn't easy to finally bring home a woman you were willing to marry, only for this to happen."

"Then I'll have to ask Mother to treat Ruyin like a daughter for now." Jiang Jiuxiao said.

Jiang Tai-furen laughed. "What else is there to do? Of course she'll be raised like a daughter first!"

...

In the Lingxi Hall of Jiang Third Master's household.

Jiang Third Master lay sprawled on the large daybed by the window, his face displeased.

Jiang Third Mistress Yin Shi came forward. "My Third Master — what's gotten into you? Who's upset you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 107
chapters.content:
Three Sisters-in-Law With Grudges of Their Own

"Yuan Niang." Jiang Third Master's gaze was frighteningly sinister.

"Sometimes I truly don't understand — Old Four and I are twins, born from the same womb. Why does he outshine me in every single way?"

"And Mother has always favored him most. From the time we were small, more of the family's resources were tilted toward him."

"Even when Father was alive, Father preferred him. Even Elder Brother deferred to him by a step."

Yin Shi gave a cold snort.

"Didn't I always say — since you and he are twins, it was Jiang Jiuxiao who absorbed your good fortune while still in Mother's womb. Of course his luck runs strong!"

Then she said with aggrieved sorrow: "And you always stop me from saying so!"

Jiang Third Master's heart was bitter.

Who would believe such a thing even if said?

And even if they did — what good would it do?

Could believing him mean he could replace Jiang Fourth?

Could it make him the head of the Ministry of Personnel at a young age — first among all Six Ministries?

Even in looks — Jiang Fourth was more strikingly handsome, seemingly a celestial being descended from the nine heavens.

"Before, I thought Old Four was just marrying a daughter of some minor fifth-rank official. But now his wife's family looks different entirely..."

Jiang Third Master covered his face with his hands.

"His fortune is inexplicably strange."

Jiang Third Mistress looked at her husband like this and felt a twinge of sympathy.

She went forward and took hold of his arm, trying to comfort him. "Third Master — let's not compare with him on any of that!"

Jiang Third Master looked at her, a flash of guilt crossing his eyes.

What he said came out full of apology: "I just feel I've let you down. Let you and our children down."

"I may have passed the provincial examinations with second honors, but this career of mine — to this day I'm still just a seventh-rank minor official. Yuan Niang, you are only a seventh-rank titled Lady."

"While she — that Qin woman — barely a teenager, and she's already the wife of the Great Ying Dynasty's Minister of Personnel. A second-rank Lady of Distinction!"

Jiang Third Mistress scolded him: "Third Master, what are you saying all this for? Who's comparing herself to Old Four's wife?"

"To tell the truth — the Qin woman is only a second wife. I am Third Master's original principal wife!" Jiang Third Mistress felt a pang of sourness in her heart.
