In truth — if comparisons could be made, which capital noblewomen didn't wish her title of Lady was higher?

And she didn't even have a full Lady's title yet — only a minor Titled Lady's honorific.

Jiang Third Master, seeing her say this, felt the darkness in his eyes deepen.

There was something his mother had strictly forbidden him and the other sons and their wives from mentioning.

Not that she didn't trust them — she simply feared loose lips among them or their natal family connections, which could cause trouble.

"Yuan Niang — there's something you don't yet know. In truth, when Old Four first married, he didn't enter that first woman's name in the clan record."

"Wh — Third Master, what are you saying?" Jiang Third Mistress was greatly startled. Those already large almond-shaped eyes widened further.

"Old Four's marriage this time is his first proper principal-wife marriage. The last one only had the ceremony — her name was never entered in the Jiang clan record."

Jiang Third Mistress: ...

She could barely maintain the gentle expression on her face. A few shades of something ugly showed at the corners of her brow.

How could that Qin girl have such good fortune?

"Third Master — is this truly certain?" Jiang Third Mistress looked at him.

Jiang Third Master nodded. "How could I say such a thing carelessly?"

Jiang Third Mistress's eyes also went dangerously dark. A great upheaval surged through her heart. She felt the heavens were truly unfair.

"Then — does Elder Sister-in-law know this?"

Jiang Third Master shook his head this time.

"Mother gave instructions long ago — none of us sons were to speak of it. Elder Brother, always so filial, wouldn't disobey Mother's words."

"That being so, Elder Sister-in-law probably doesn't know either." Jiang Third Mistress gritted her teeth.

A cold, cutting glint flashed through her eyes.

When Jiang Third Master looked, Jiang Third Mistress had already returned to her usual composure.

He said to her: "Mother at the time was worried about Old Four — he really did suffer a terrible blow, and after that kept his distance from all women."

"If you sisters-in-law found out Old Four hadn't entered that first one's name in the clan record, just think — which family with a daughter wouldn't try to get their hands on Old Four as their marriage prize?"

"Mother's concern was that the attention would be too much for Old Four at that vulnerable time — that's why she gave the seal-of-silence order."

Jiang Third Mistress answered aloud while laughing coldly to herself.

At bottom, the old woman was just too partial to Old Four.

She also guarded against them, these daughters-in-law, as if they were outsiders.

Did she really think her Old Four was such a precious prize everyone was after?

Even if the Fourth Master was truly the prize every family with daughters was after — so what?

She simply refused to accept it!

Why were Third Master and Old Four born twins from the same womb, yet the old woman made such a difference between them?

Back in the day, to support Old Four's studies, the old woman had exhausted every connection their late father had built to invite the best tutors for him. And what about her Third Master?

He had grown up like a wild weed in the Jiang family school.

And yet her Third Master had still made second honors on his own merit.

Yet in the old woman's eyes there was only Old Four — she gave her Third Master not the slightest regard.

On the matter of their careers, the old woman had been even more outrageously partial.

...

"Third Master — Old Four has been given three days of holiday for the wedding. Rest and relax properly. Don't overthink everything."

Third Mistress called her senior maid over and asked for a light blanket. "These past days you've been running around helping with all the preparations and you're tired. You also woke early this morning."

"Rest for a while. I'll go to Elder Sister-in-law's."

She thought a moment and explained to Jiang Third Master: "What with Old Four's wedding keeping everyone so busy, Elder Sister-in-law assigned all of us sisters-in-law various duties. Now that things are done, I have to hand back the management tokens."

Jiang Third Master nodded. He was indeed tired, and his mood was foul — he couldn't even read the official gazette.

After Third Mistress settled him into his rest, she brought two senior maids and the management tokens to Elder Mistress Fang's Shangshan Courtyard.

"Third Sister-in-law is here — take a seat." Jiang Elder Mistress Fang was still occupied and said to her: "I'll finish with this and come sit with Third Sister-in-law in a moment."

Jiang Third Mistress smiled pleasantly. "Elder Sister-in-law, go ahead with your work. Don't mind me. I'm only here to hand back the management tokens."

Jiang Elder Mistress thought privately: this Third daughter-in-law always had a reason beyond her stated reason when she came in person. Handing back management tokens didn't require a personal visit at all.

Let it go. Once she was done here, she'd listen to whatever the woman had to say.

Fang Shi suppressed her annoyance and continued managing the household.

Jiang Third Mistress watched her settle one matter after another in neat, methodical order, issuing management tokens one by one — and couldn't help a wave of private envy.

She had also learned proper household management from her mother and elder sister-in-law at home.

But as long as the Jiang brothers didn't divide their household, she would probably never have a chance to manage anything.

After Jiang Elder Mistress had dispatched the last matter, she smiled and asked: "Did Third Sister-in-law tire of waiting?"

"Not at all." Jiang Third Mistress cast a glance upward and said with a smile: "Coming here early today — I realize just how taxing Elder Sister-in-law's household management is."

Jiang Elder Mistress didn't take the remark at face value and only smiled.

Waiting for her to get to the point.

"Old Four's couple must give Elder Sister-in-law a proper thank-you — without you, their wedding couldn't have been done so beautifully!"

Jiang Elder Mistress frowned slightly, reached for her teacup, took a gentle sip, set it down, and then smiled. "What is there to say like that?"

"We're all one family. Elder Brother holds seniority — looking after the younger brothers and their wives is only right."

Jiang Third Mistress was smiling on the outside, laughing scornfully inside: these words sounded nice but deceived no one.

"Long Brother and Elder Sister-in-law are both capable and kind-hearted — we younger ones are all fortunate."

Jiang Elder Mistress thought privately: here she was flattering her. What was the woman after?

In the past, when she had come to find her, it was always either to ask for something or to get something.

She pressed down her inner irritation and continued listening.

"By the way, Elder Sister-in-law — there is one thing I don't know whether you know or not."

Jiang Elder Mistress thought: here it comes.

But her face showed only puzzlement. "I wonder what Third Sister-in-law means?"

"I only heard it as drunken rambling from my Third Master." Jiang Third Mistress made a show of mystery.

"Word is that when Old Four married the first time, that woman's name was never entered in the clan record. Elder Sister-in-law — did you know that? Is it true?"

Jiang Elder Mistress's mind gave a resounding thud.

Both her hands clenched tight.

Jiang Third Mistress had been watching her closely. She strained to hold it together — barely keeping the expression on her face from cracking.

She said, smile somewhat forced: "This matter — I've never heard our Elder Brother mention it."

Jiang Third Mistress seized the moment: "I didn't believe it at first either. But thinking about it — my Third Master said it when he was drunk, so maybe it was the truth coming out?"

"Elder Sister-in-law, I don't know about you — but when I heard it, my heart was like a cat scratching at it. I just had to know what happened with that first woman of Old Four's back then. How is it that he didn't enter her name in the clan record even after she died?"

"Elder Sister-in-law — has Long Brother really never once hinted at any of this to you? These men! Their mouths really are sealed! We're their closest people — the ones beside them in bed, the mothers of their children — and they still hide things from us. That shows they don't treat us as family at all."

Jiang Elder Mistress's composure gradually slipped.

"Third Daughter-in-law!" She spoke coldly, snapping the words: "What nonsense are you talking?"

Jiang Third Mistress made a show of clapping her own mouth. "Elder Sister-in-law, don't be angry — I just got too curious. I was a little angry at my Third Master too."

Jiang Elder Mistress said coolly: "These are all Old Four's private affairs. What is there for you to get angry about?"

Jiang Third Mistress saw this composed, virtuous Elder Sister-in-law finally starting to crack, and felt inwardly triumphant.

She simply didn't believe it.

Everyone said the Elder Master and this second wife were deeply devoted — everyone envied Elder Sister-in-law for having a mother-in-law who valued her, a husband who respected her, children who adored her. A perfect woman.

She wanted to see: now that Fang Shi knew the Qin girl couldn't be entered in the clan record the way she had been — would she still be that eight-faceted, flawlessly composed paragon?

And as for that Qin woman — she didn't believe a girl so young, already a second-rank Lady of Distinction, would be content to let a second-wife Elder Sister-in-law manage the household.

After Jiang Third Mistress left Shangshan Courtyard, Fang Shi's wet nurse tried to comfort her: "Young Miss — don't think too much. You know what Third Mistress is like."

"Mama, don't try to comfort me." Fang Shi waved her hand limply.

"I know Yin Shi is someone who thrives on chaos, and she didn't tell me all this out of any good intention — she came to stir up trouble and watch the spectacle."

"But Mama — I'm genuinely hurt."

While the mistress and her nurse were talking, a small maid outside announced: "First Mistress — the Fourth Mistress has come to see you."

Fang Shi's brow furrowed. She murmured to her wet nurse: "Why has she come?"

Fang Shi's wet nurse immediately said: "Young Miss — this servant thinks our new Fourth Mistress is a sharp one. Let's see what she's about before deciding."

Fang Shi's expression shifted uncertainly, then she gave a small nod.

"Yes. For now, I can only follow Mama's advice and see first."

She sighed — she hoped Old Four's wife wasn't a troublemaker.

Otherwise life in the Jiang family would be very difficult for her.

chapters.title: Chapter 108
chapters.content:
Her Husband Has Something on His Mind

After Qin Ruyin and Jiang Jiuxiao had completed the tea ceremony and met the family, the couple returned to Minglan Residence to change into everyday clothes.

Not long after, Jiang Tai-furen sent for Jiang Jiuxiao to come to Rong'an Hall.

When Jiang Jiuxiao returned, he brought back two thousand taels in banknotes.

He said they were from Jiang Tai-furen — a gift to her to prepare some presents and go sit with the Elder Mistress Fang at Shangshan Courtyard first.

When she returned from Shangshan Courtyard, Jiang Jiuxiao would take her directly to Rong'an Hall to accompany Jiang Tai-furen for the midday meal.

The two thousand taels were a supplement from the mother-in-law.

She also made clear that Qin Ruyin was not to refuse.

Her mother-in-law was personally spending her own silver to put Qin Ruyin in the position of the kind one — Qin Ruyin was certainly not going to refuse.

The very first rule of living in the Jiang family was this:

As long as her mother-in-law and Fourth Master stood on her side and did not damage her dignity, she would follow their lead without a second thought.

Of course, she would still judge for herself whether their lead was worth following.

At this moment, Qin Ruyin had already entered Jiang Elder Mistress Fang's Shangshan Courtyard with Feng Mama, Banjia, and Jiang Tai-furen's provided senior maid Baihé.

And Fang Shi's courtyard maid was just then reporting to her mistress.

"First Mistress — the Fourth Mistress is here. And... the Fourth Mistress has brought many gifts."

Fang Shi immediately exchanged a glance with her wet nurse.

Her wet nurse counseled: "Young Miss — this servant thinks our newly arrived Fourth Mistress has a head on her shoulders. Let's watch and see first."

Fang Shi's expression was uncertain, then she gave a small nod.

"Very well. For now let's follow Mama's advice and see first."

She let out a sigh and hoped Old Four's wife wasn't going to be difficult.

Otherwise her days in the Jiang family would not be easy.

...

Since Qin Ruyin was a new bride, a bride's first three days were considered the most honored.

She was the honored guest.

Jiang Elder Mistress Fang personally led her wet nurse and senior maids outside to meet her.

Seeing Qin Ruyin dressed in her brilliant red long gown — looking vivid and graceful and composed — she couldn't help an inward admiration.

"Fourth Sister-in-law has come — I'm sorry for not meeting you sooner. Please don't take offense."

Fang Shi's courtesies were always impeccable, making one feel as warmly at ease as a spring breeze.

She stepped forward and took Qin Ruyin's arm, looked her up and down smilingly, and praised: "Fourth Sister-in-law, how beautiful you are!"

Qin Ruyin saw that while Fang Shi was complimenting her, there was a faint hint of scrutiny concealed in her eyes, and she wasn't surprised.

Feng Mama had told her: what Fang Shi cared about most was her children, and second most was managing the household. Even Elder Master Jiang ranked after these.

Fang Shi knew what she wanted and knew what she could hold on to.

A woman this sharp and clear-headed would naturally regard her as a competitor.

After all — in the time when her own family's branch hadn't split yet, the Qin Second Branch had broken the rules. Not looking at seniority — only at who was stronger.

Fang Shi was probably afraid she might do the same.

After all — the man she had married, Jiang Fourth, was by far stronger than Elder Master Jiang.

"Elder Sister-in-law is too kind." Qin Ruyin said with a bright smile, and reached out to take Fang Shi's arm in return.

She addressed her as "Elder Sister-in-law."

Fang Shi was momentarily startled.

In this household so far, she was the only one who called herself "Elder Sister-in-law."

The others only called her "Elder Sister-in-law" in the general way.

The title "Elder Sister-in-law" had always been reserved for the first wife of Elder Master, who had passed away.

"Today I was going to go see Mother first — but Mother had Fourth Master tell me to come to your Shangshan Courtyard first."

"Both Fourth Master and I are so grateful to you and Elder Brother. It's thanks to both of you that our wedding went off so beautifully and with such dignity."

Fang Shi was somewhat taken aback by her directness.

And seeing Qin Ruyin put her before Elder Master Jiang, she was even more surprised.

This little girl...

She couldn't quite read her.

After all, Fang Shi was more than ten years her senior — she could have been her mother.

But she couldn't deny it: the things this girl said were genuinely pleasant to hear.

And at least from those words, she gathered that her mother-in-law and Old Four both acknowledged her own hard work and effort.

Fang Shi's wet nurse, listening nearby, also let a smile touch her aged face, and personally brought Qin Ruyin a cup of tea.

"Fourth Sister-in-law, please take some tea." Fang Shi's eyes held a more genuine warmth as she said: "We're all family here — no need to stand on ceremony."

"That's thanks to your and Elder Brother's kindness." Qin Ruyin smiled back. "Not every family avoids the kind of brother-against-brother feuding, you know."

Fang Shi paused again.

This girl spoke with such disarming frankness.

"What Fourth Sister-in-law says has some truth in it. But our Jiang brothers, though many, are united where it shows, and there would never be outright feuding among them."

As Elder Mistress of the Jiang household, Fang Shi would of course only say pleasant things.

Qin Ruyin wouldn't contradict her — though inwardly she was a touch skeptical.

She was newly arrived, but that didn't make her blind.

"Those things are beyond my management, and I wouldn't presume to think about them. In any case, with such a capable and kind Elder Sister-in-law watching over everything, I have nothing to worry about!" Qin Ruyin said, deliberately putting Fang Shi at ease.

Seeing Fang Shi's slight frown, she laughed softly — two little heh-heh sounds — and looked at Fang Shi. "Elder Sister-in-law, I really am one very fortunate person! You have to promise me — I'm going to rely on you to indulge my laziness!"

Fang Shi's brow smoothed, and she couldn't help a laugh.

She understood.

This girl was being clever and lighthearted all at once.

She was also giving her a hint.

A hint that she had no intention of competing for household management.

Thinking this, Fang Shi gave a private cold snort at Yin Shi.

What a petty schemer.

Old Four's wife being the clan-registered original principal wife — so what?

She didn't care about that.

She didn't care who Old Four's wife was.

As long as she didn't compete for management of the household.

As long as she was still the Jiang family's managing Elder Mistress.

Of course, if Old Four one day wanted to seize management of the household for his own wife's sake, then she wouldn't object either.

Just allow the First Branch to divide off on their own.

She was a woman with an independent streak — she only ever wanted to be the one in charge of her own home.

Qin Ruyin had very clearly noticed how visibly Fang Shi relaxed after hearing her last remark.

She understood: the hint had landed.

How pleasant it was to deal with intelligent people.

She also understood why her mother-in-law Jiang Tai-furen had a strong dislike for fools.

She had it herself, after all.

The mother-in-law sending her with gifts to visit Fang Shi first couldn't solve the fundamental issue.

That much the mother-in-law surely understood herself.

It was also, she thought, a test of how she handled the situation.

What Qin Ruyin was clear about: the only thing that would put Fang Shi's mind at ease was for Fang Shi to genuinely believe she had no designs on household management.

Managing a household was exhausting work — who truly wanted to hold on to it?

It was nothing but the face Fang Shi valued.

She herself wasn't married to the eldest — she had no obligation to prove her capability to anyone. She despised trouble above all things.

She had no desire whatsoever to manage this household.

With so many Jiang brothers and cousins, the constant problem of everyone feeling shortchanged and wanting more — that was a headache.

She not only had no wish to take Fang Shi's management role — she prayed Fang Shi would never drop the burden and walk away.

Besides — her mother-in-law Jiang Tai-furen was a sharp woman. The household manager she approved of — could she be bad at the job?

If Fang Shi one day truly stepped down, then it would be her turn.

The other sisters-in-law — their husbands held positions too low to command the respect of the full household.

When Qin Ruyin left Shangshan Courtyard, Jiang Elder Mistress Fang also gave her six bolts of the finest Xiaguang brocade as a return gift.

After all, Qin Ruyin's thank-you gift to Fang Shi had been worth no less than five hundred taels.

The six bolts of Xiaguang brocade couldn't match the value of Qin Ruyin's gift, but Xiaguang brocade was hard to come by.

Especially in the vivid scarlet and marigold shades — those were rarer still.

This was the specialty of Fang Shi's ancestral hometown.

Fang Shi had said she was in the full bloom of youth and nothing suited her better than bold, vivid colors like Xiaguang brocade.

Qin Ruyin carried Jiang Elder Mistress's return gift back to their own courtyard, where Jiang Jiuxiao was sitting reading on the large daybed by the window, waiting for her to return.

When she came in, he set the book aside and looked at her. "I didn't expect — you and Elder Sister-in-law could actually get along."

Qin Ruyin lifted her chin a fraction, rather pleased with herself. "Of course! Not only did we get along — Elder Sister-in-law specially gave me six bolts of the most sought-after Xiaguang brocade!"

Jiang Jiuxiao looked at that little self-satisfied air she had, and his mouth threatened to betray him — he covered it quickly with a loosely curled fist.

She had called her "Elder Sister-in-law."

That was as it should be.

The first Elder Sister-in-law had been gone for many years now. The living move on.

Fang Shi, though a second wife, had been diligent and dutiful for years, managing the Jiang household's inner court well enough.

She deserved the title.

He glanced at the trays the small maids carried — the colors were vivid and rich, indeed perfectly suited to her.

"Elder Sister-in-law is thoughtful. The Xiaguang brocade comes only from her ancestral hometown. The truly vivid pure shades are extremely hard to find."

Qin Ruyin understood.

Jiang Jiuxiao then said: "Elder Sister-in-law can be cold on the surface and hard to get through to — most people can't manage to get on her good side."

Qin Ruyin nodded. "I could see that — she isn't easy to handle."

Jiang Jiuxiao laughed.

"Ruyin handled it well."

"I was thinking the same — I'd like life to be a little easier for us going forward."

"Honestly, just say what you mean directly — I hate it when people bury things in their heart and scheme and calculate."

Jiang Jiuxiao's heart gave a slight lurch.

Had the girl overheard something from Elder Sister-in-law?

Why did it feel like she was hinting at him?

Qin Ruyin finished speaking and lowered her head to drink her tea.

"Ruyin—" He considered a moment, and called to her.

chapters.title: Chapter 109
chapters.content:
Newly Wedded — He Helps Her Choose Jewelry

Qin Ruyin had barely answered when Juhong's voice came from outside, announcing that Tai-furen's people had come to invite the Fourth Master and Fourth Mistress to Rong'an Hall for the midday meal.

"Let's go to Mother's first. If you want to know anything, just ask me directly."

Qin Ruyin stood as she nodded.

But she said: "And if I want to know what you were just about to say, Fourth Master?"

Jiang Jiuxiao: ...

She truly did ask whatever was on her mind.

He looked at the bright, vivid little girl for a moment, the corner of his lip curving slightly.

"What I was going to say is this: you, Qin Ruyin, are my Jiang Jiuxiao's registered-in-the-Jiang-clan-record original principal wife, wed by proper betrothal."

He said it, and kept his gaze fixed on her eyes — and saw a flash of astonishment cross them.

Qin Ruyin was of course astonished.

Jiang Jiuxiao was clearly remarrying as a widower — so why was he saying she was recorded in the Jiang clan record as his original principal wife?

In retrospect, her mother had once said with pity that since she was to be a second wife, even with the title of Lady, she couldn't be entered in the Jiang clan record.

Her mother had felt wronged on her behalf.

At the time, she had genuinely not minded.

She thought: as long as she lived well and had a good life while she was alive, that was enough.

But Jiang Jiuxiao was now telling her she was the original principal wife entered in his Jiang clan record.

After the astonishment came confusion.

She knew that his first wife had been married to him for several years — and had been brought in through proper betrothal with eight bearers, the full ceremony. By rights, a properly wed principal wife would be entered in the husband's clan record the very day of the marriage.

Now that she was the one recorded in the Jiang clan record, it meant Jiang Jiuxiao's first wife had never been entered.

What was the story there?

"Fourth Master — was your previous wife, Mistress Yao, never entered in the Jiang clan record when she married you? Otherwise it would never be my turn."

"This is a long story. Let's go to Mother's first. I'll tell you in full when there's time." Jiang Jiuxiao's expression grew a little grave.

Qin Ruyin saw this and asked no more, and simply nodded.

After a moment, Jiang Jiuxiao added quietly: "I'm telling you this today so you know — because I am aware that sooner or later this matter will get out. I don't want you to hear it from someone else."

"I'll follow your lead." Qin Ruyin nodded. "Don't worry — even if I hear something from others, I won't take it to heart, and I won't go asking around either. If there's anything I truly want to know, I'll ask you directly."

After coming to the Jiang family, Qin Ruyin had decided she would not proactively ask about Jiang Jiuxiao and his first wife.

That was a past she had not been part of.

It was Jiang Jiuxiao and his first wife's private matter.

It had nothing to do with her, and she chose to respect that.

But if something connected to his first wife's affairs touched her own interests in a way that needed clarification, she would ask Jiang Jiuxiao himself directly.

"Good." Jiang Jiuxiao was very satisfied with the girl's clear-minded reasonableness.

"Let's go see Mother first. We mustn't keep her waiting." Qin Ruyin smiled at him, then added: "Thank you, Fourth Master, for telling me yourself. I'm very pleased!"

Whether it was that Jiang Jiuxiao had chosen to tell her proactively, or that she truly was his clan-registered original wife — both were things to be pleased about.

Before, she had assumed being a second wife was a fixed reality, and that it was not within her power to decide whether or not she was entered in the clan record. Whether she minded or not, she couldn't change the outcome.

Better to take an unbothered attitude and simply live her life well.

This turn of events was an unexpected joy.

Who would willingly be a second wife when she could be an original principal wife?

As for whether Jiang Jiuxiao would ever tell her about his past with his first wife — that was entirely his matter.

She held to that same principle: as long as it didn't touch her own interests, she would not proactively go looking for answers.

No point in it — the woman had been dead for years.

"Fourth Master, wait a moment while I change into a more casual outfit." Qin Ruyin felt this one was too formal and wanted to swap into something simpler and more everyday.

Her mother, sisters-in-law, and sisters had all prepared plenty of new clothes for her. She could change three times a day for a month and never repeat.

Pretty new clothes were meant to be worn and enjoyed.

With so many new outfits available, she certainly wasn't going to leave them sitting at the bottom of a trunk — what a waste that would be.

Jiang Jiuxiao was already looking at her, considering, and then said calmly: "This looks very nice on you. No need to change."

"The hairstyle could stand to be something simpler." After a brief thought, he offered.

She had been going to call on the Jiang family's First Mistress — a formal visit, which called for a more elaborate hairstyle and more jewelry.

With more jewelry, the head grew heavy.

Jiang Jiuxiao's suggestion suited her exactly.

What Jiang Jiuxiao was thinking of — though she didn't know it — was the wedding night when he had removed the phoenix crown for her, and the way she had quietly endured its weight with such patience.

He thought she probably didn't much like heavy, elaborate head ornaments — which was why he made the suggestion.

Juhong came to pin up a simple cloud-flow bun for her.

Qin Ruyin told her to keep the jewelry simple too.

Juhong agreed and selected a few silver pieces inlaid with white jade. The jade was not large, but its luster was warm and translucent — it was nearly half-transparent, with an excellent sheen.

Jiang Jiuxiao looked and felt it was a little too plain — it would be overpowered by the bold, full-sleeve peony-vine red gown she was wearing.

He reached into her jewelry case and drew out a red-gem kingfisher-feather auspicious-cloud hairpin, and gently tucked it into the base of her cloud-flow bun himself.

"That's better." He looked at the girl in the bronze mirror, a faint smile at the corner of his lip.

Qin Ruyin also felt the hairpin he had chosen complemented her cloud-flow bun beautifully, and silently admired his taste.

She turned her head and looked at him standing behind her, breaking into a radiant smile.

Paired with her carefully made-up appearance, she was devastatingly beautiful — like all the flowers in a spring garden, blooming all at once in a single breathtaking moment.

Jiang Jiuxiao's heart quickened slightly, and he immediately looked down to conceal the upturned corners of his mouth.

Now he understood why his mother, upon seeing her for the first time, had come back home and promptly sought him out to declare that the Qin family's Sixth Young Miss was a beauty so striking she had made even an old woman like her forget herself for a moment.

She truly was beautiful.

...

Properly prepared, the newlyweds made their way to Jiang Tai-furen's Rong'an Hall.

Along the way, Qin Ruyin brought up with Jiang Jiuxiao the idea of building a small kitchen in their courtyard.

Their courtyard was called Minglan Residence.

Before she came, her mother and sisters-in-law had all speculated that the new couple's rooms would be set in the courtyard of Jiang Jiuxiao's first wife.

They imagined it would be one of the finest courtyards in the Jiang family.

After all, his first wife had come from a background so distinguished it was breathtaking.

The woman had been from the Yao family of the capital.

The Yao ancestors had produced four Grand Tutors — the highest of the Three Excellencies.

And the current Grand Tutor of the Great Ying Dynasty was Mistress Yao's own paternal great-uncle.

Mistress Yao was the eldest legitimate daughter of the Yao family's Second Branch — but had been raised at the knee of the First Branch's mistress.

Which made her essentially a daughter of the First Branch.

Mistress Yao had also been a renowned beauty of the capital in her day, though she had passed away in the full bloom of her youth.

However, the courtyard the Jiang family had arranged for Qin Ruyin was not the one Mistress Yao had occupied.

The day before the wedding, when Zisu led people to the Jiang family to set up the bridal bed, she had come back and told Qin Ruyin this.

That was how she learned: the courtyard where Mistress Yao had once lived was not one of the better-positioned courtyards in the Jiang family.

It was actually rather isolated, and some distance from the Jiang family's main court.

Whether the Jiang family had done this deliberately or there was some other hidden reason — she didn't know.

The courtyard she now occupied, Minglan Residence, had apparently been the one Jiang Jiuxiao lived in as a boy.

The courtyard was lovely — only there was no small kitchen.

After all, Jiang Jiuxiao was a man, and he paid little attention to food and drink.

He had grown up handsome but with an aloof, cold nature — he disliked young women coming near him and found young maids who secretly glanced at him tiresome.

His courtyard was staffed entirely with older matrons or manservants a few years older than himself.

With this sort of household, there was no reason to build a small kitchen.

He wasn't the kind of young nobleman raised in the lap of luxury, with a circle of maids and young servants attending to him — some wealthy young masters had their own courtyard kitchen as a matter of course, preparing everything separately from the main kitchen.

Jiang Jiuxiao agreed at once.

After a brief consideration, he also said to her: "The main kitchen's cook is reasonably skilled. If you don't mind, you don't need to go to the trouble yourself."

He knew she had a fondness for cooking.

The want for a small kitchen was almost certainly because she intended to put her own hands to work.

Qin Ruyin smiled and agreed.

Then she said to him: "Your stomach is poor and needs to be nursed. I'm not only thinking of my own appetite."

Jiang Jiuxiao looked at her, a glimmer of something warm in his eyes.

"I want to make you some stomach-nourishing remedial foods regularly. And even the most devoted fan of rich feasting eventually longs for simple congee and side dishes."

"Besides — Mother has been so good to me. In my spare time I'd love to bake pastries to present to her."

Flattering words cost nothing, after all.

And making simple pastries and dishes wasn't much effort.

Making medicinal food for him would please him, please those around him, and please the mother-in-law most of all.

Making pastries for the elders would earn her the reputation of a filial daughter-in-law.

Why wouldn't she?

She genuinely loved to cook her favorite dishes herself.

"I just don't want you to wear yourself out." Jiang Jiuxiao stopped walking to wait for her, then slowed his pace so they walked side by side.

"It won't wear me out. I hardly do everything in the kitchen myself." Qin Ruyin said honestly with a smile: "I don't have the ability for that!"

"The food you prepare is very good." Jiang Jiuxiao said, his gaze on her moving feet and the fluttering of her pleated skirt.

"I'm glad Fourth Master likes it!"

...

The newlyweds chatted all the way there.

The moment they arrived at Jiang Tai-furen's Rong'an Hall, Hua Mama came hurrying to receive them.

"Fourth Master and Fourth Mistress — Tai-furen has been looking forward to you all morning! Please come in at once!"

Jiang Jiuxiao gave only a slight nod.

Qin Ruyin smiled warmly and said to Hua Mama: "Thank you for coming out to receive us personally, Hua Mama."

Hua Mama said with a beaming smile: "Fourth Mistress flatters me too much!"

Qin Ruyin said a few more kind things.

Hua Mama was charmed, and led Qin Ruyin forward with even greater solicitude.

"Fourth Mistress — Second Mistress, Third Mistress, and Fifth Mistress are already here." Hua Mama gave Qin Ruyin a quiet word. "Today Tai-furen is hosting a family banquet especially to welcome Fourth Mistress."

"The masters are also all in the household, having taken holiday time for the Fourth Master's wedding. The men's banquet is in the garden hall."

Qin Ruyin had assumed today's midday meal was just Jiang Jiuxiao and her accompanying the old woman.

She had no idea it was going to be a full family banquet.

It was also her fault as a new bride for not knowing a thing.

And Jiang Jiuxiao had probably forgotten to tell her.

Jiang Jiuxiao, hearing Hua Mama's words, furrowed his brow.

His mother had only said to bring his new wife to accompany her for midday — not that it was a family banquet.

He glanced at Qin Ruyin.

Qin Ruyin felt a burning gaze and quickly looked back.

She saw Jiang Jiuxiao give her the smallest shake of his head.

She immediately understood.

It wasn't that Jiang Jiuxiao had forgotten to tell her this was a family banquet.

He hadn't known either.

With five sisters-in-law all gathered, there was probably going to be quite a performance.

After all — three women alone made a full drama.

She wasn't afraid.

She saw Jiang Jiuxiao say to Hua Mama: "Ruyin is a new bride — young and with a thin face. If Mother can't speak to certain things conveniently, please help Ruyin a little."

Hua Mama's aged eyes crinkled with delight at seeing their Fourth Master actually thinking to protect his new bride, and she agreed repeatedly.

She thought: if Tai-furen knew, she would definitely be so happy she couldn't sleep tonight.

Seeing Jiang Jiuxiao's expression still not quite right, Qin Ruyin also gave him the smallest shake of her head — telling him not to worry.

...

"Oh! Fourth Master and Fourth Sister-in-law are here! Fourth Sister-in-law, come sit down — sit at Mother's left hand! On a new bride's first three days, no one outranks you!"

Third Mistress Yin Shi was dressed in a pale violet silk short gown with a slate blue gold-threaded wrap skirt — rich, elegant, and composed.

Only the moment she opened her mouth, "composed" no longer applied.

Hearing her words, Qin Ruyin gave a polite, distant smile — and did not take the bait.

Seeing Qin Ruyin not rise to it, the smile on Yin Shi's face immediately faded considerably.

chapters.title: Chapter 110
chapters.content:
Deflecting Third Sister-in-Law's Provocation with a Feather's Touch

"Oh dear! Have I said something wrong? Why won't Fourth Sister-in-law say anything?"

Yin Shi smiled at Qin Ruyin — but the smile didn't reach her eyes.

Jiang Tai-furen's aged face had already gone cold.

Second Mistress Chen Shi, seeing the awkward atmosphere, immediately rose and smoothed things over: "Fourth Sister-in-law, come sit down!"

She reached out to take Qin Ruyin's arm, also guiding her toward the seat at Tai-furen's left.

On today of all days, with Qin Ruyin the new bride, the seat at Tai-furen's left by rights belonged to her.

Chen Shi had no interest in competing for this, and no objection whatsoever.

She was happy to play the good person.

After all, even the First Mistress Fang had to give way to the new bride today and take the seat at Tai-furen's right.

Qin Ruyin hadn't planned to be modest about it either.

But Jiang Third Mistress Yin Shi making a point of bringing it up was pure provocation.

She thanked Chen Shi first, and then in a warm tone addressed her: "Second Sister-in-law — I'm new here and young, and don't yet know many of the customs of our household."

Qin Ruyin stood without moving. "Third Sister-in-law just said that — and now I'm afraid to take the seat at Mother's side. I'm not singling you out — please don't take it to heart."

She only mentioned not yet knowing the household's customs — not general etiquette and propriety.

That was a pointed remark at Yin Shi.

Chen Shi understood perfectly that Yin Shi had overstepped and gotten her fingers burned. She simply smiled and sat back down.

Jiang Third Mistress Yin Shi pretended not to understand that Qin Ruyin was calling her out.

She answered with a trace of sugared sarcasm: "Our Jiang family doesn't have so many rules! Mother is the most gentle and kind of mothers-in-law — you'll see for yourself in time."

Still provoking.

The corner of Qin Ruyin's lips curved slightly. She replied: "Of course Mother is the kindest of mothers-in-law!"

"I knew that long before I married in — I'd actually met Mother twice before I ever came through the gates!"

Yin Shi's face stiffened.

She thought bitterly: this is a teenage girl?

Slippery as an eel. And she'd managed to get in a killing remark without seeming to try.

She and her Third Master had been engaged and married through a matchmaker — the old woman had never once visited her family before the wedding.

Only now with Old Four did everything become special.

Not only had the betrothal gift and ceremony been staggering, the old woman had personally visited the Qin family twice.

Didn't that show how much the Jiang family valued this match with the Qin family?

Didn't it show how much the old woman valued this new Fourth daughter-in-law?

None of the other Jiang daughters-in-law, except this one, had been given such treatment.

"That's right — Mother loves Fourth Sister-in-law most dearly. We all know it!" Yin Shi's smile stayed bright, though her teeth were nearly aching.

Qin Ruyin listened and nodded along affably, then deliberately swept her gaze over Yin Shi.

Then she looked at Second Mistress Chen Shi, then at Fifth Mistress Zheng Shi.

None of them could tell what Qin Ruyin was getting at.

Qin Ruyin then turned her bright, vivid gaze to Jiang Tai-furen and said with sweet complaint: "Mother — look! Third Sister-in-law is jealous of me about this!"

"You've raised your sisters-in-law and Fifth Sister-in-law so beautifully — every one of them soft-complexioned and glowing like celestial maidens. And they've had years and years more of your love and devotion than I have..."

"Mother — I don't care about anything else. Now that I'm here, you must love me more than you love my sisters-in-law and Fifth Sister-in-law! Otherwise these missing years and even decades of lost pampering — won't I have gotten the worst of the deal?"

Chen Shi, Yin Shi, and Zheng Shi were all thunderstruck.

Who talked to their mother-in-law like that?

Who calculated it that way?

But this girl had just called all of them celestial maidens...

"Yes, yes, yes! Mother promises!" Jiang Tai-furen was already laughing and nodding eagerly.

She was about to say more when the sound of the bead curtain rustling drew everyone's eyes.

Jiang Elder Mistress Fang herself lifted the curtain and stepped through.

She looked in with a smile. "Mother — this daughter-in-law just walked in and already heard Fourth Sister-in-law crying grievance. What has she lost out on?"

She glanced at Qin Ruyin: "Fourth Sister-in-law — what have you lost out on? Tell me and Elder Sister-in-law will make it up to you!"

"Oh — Elder daughter-in-law, you're here. Come and deal with this little mischief-maker Ruyin—"

Jiang Tai-furen, still beaming, relayed what Qin Ruyin had just said to Fang Shi.

Fang Shi heard her out and couldn't hold back a laugh.

She also cast a cool, mocking glance at Yin Shi.

She thought: Old Four's wife really had deployed the move of using a feather's touch to redirect a thousand-jin force with beautiful precision.

Yin Shi — who had always been the one to get in the first cut — had finally met her match.

Did she think everyone was a fool?

A woman whom Old Fourth had been willing to marry — could Yin Shi possibly have her under her thumb?

"In that case, Elder Sister-in-law can't possibly compensate you, Fourth Sister-in-law." Fang Shi put on a playfully stingy face.

"Mother's indulgences — Elder Sister-in-law also wants more of them. Elder Sister-in-law is stingy. I won't share yours!"

Fang Shi joined in the banter.

Jiang Tai-furen laughed until she was nearly folded in half.

She had just come to realize for the first time that her Elder daughter-in-law was also capable of cracking jokes.

The old woman was genuinely happy today.

After all, she had been braced for Yin Shi's provocation, and had all but accepted that this family banquet was likely to end badly.

Old women like her tended to love family harmony above all else.

She had improvised this banquet on a whim, out of the old woman's fondness for reunion gatherings.

When Yin Shi opened her mouth with that first remark, she had regretted it immediately.

Now it had turned out completely different from what she'd feared.

Old Fourth's wife was remarkable.

"Elder Sister-in-law — I would never compete with you for Mother's indulgences! I'm counting on Mother to pamper you too, so you'll have the energy to keep showing me kindness!" Qin Ruyin fired off another line.

Fang Shi was delighted — laughed until the fine lines at her eyes multiplied.

Second Mistress Chen Shi, Third Mistress Yin Shi, and Fifth Mistress Zheng Shi watched as these three — mother-in-law, eldest sister-in-law, and newest sister-in-law — settled into such easy warmth, and a shadow passed through all their eyes.

None of them had ever imagined that the First Branch and the Fourth Branch would get along.

They had every reason to think Fang Shi was putting on an act.

But none of them had ever before seen genuine laughter on Fang Shi's face and in her eyes like that.

If the First Branch and the Fourth Branch were not going to fight — and were in fact going to join forces — then wouldn't the three of them have even less of a fighting chance?

Qin Ruyin traded a few more quips with Fang Shi.

Jiang Tai-furen was laughing so hard she kept tipping forward and back.

Hua Mama and the other attendants around Jiang Tai-furen were all smiling so widely their eyes had nearly shut.

"A new bride's first three days, she is the most honored — that's the rule! And all of you went through the same. Now go sit down. Let Mother have a good look at you and give you a proper pampering."

Fang Shi saw the meal was about to be served. She pressed Qin Ruyin firmly into the seat at Jiang Tai-furen's left.

After Qin Ruyin was seated, Jiang Tai-furen smiled and said to Fang Shi: "Sit down too. Later, keep Mother company with an extra cup of bamboo leaf wine."

Fang Shi smiled and agreed, then took the seat to Jiang Tai-furen's right.

The mischief Yin Shi had tried to stir was dissolved just like that.

Yin Shi wouldn't let it go, and made to speak again after everyone was seated.

She was stopped by a single cool glance from Jiang Tai-furen.

"The meal is starting. Eating is done in silence — let us all sit properly for the meal, and there will be plenty of time to talk after."

The unspoken message was a warning to Yin Shi, who was still trying to make trouble.

Yin Shi heard it and understood, but was unconvinced.

The old woman was getting older by the day — nearly sixty now.

There would come a day when she could no longer manage everything and everyone.

And this new Fourth Mistress had just arrived — if she didn't put Qin Ruyin in her place now, was she supposed to wait until Qin Ruyin had established herself firmly before making a move?

Absolutely not.

She was determined to get justice for her Third Master.

Of the six women at the meal — six sisters-in-law — only Qin Ruyin ate with cheerful enthusiasm. The others all ate with no taste for it.

Even Fang Shi glanced from time to time with slight puzzlement at Qin Ruyin eating so happily and energetically.

This girl...

She couldn't quite decide whether she was truly carefree and innocent, or whether this was a deliberate display of composure.

And honestly — what an appetite.

She was a little envious, if she was being honest.

Jiang Tai-furen, seeing her eat so happily, felt her own appetite revive. The corners of her mouth came up.

One thing led to another: Jiang Tai-furen ended up eating a full bowl and a half of green-grain rice.

She normally could only manage half a bowl of green-grain rice at most.

Hua Mama was already mentally noting: from now on, if the Fourth Master was out at the yamen, she must find a way to invite the Fourth Mistress to come keep Tai-furen company for meals more often.

Yin Shi watched Qin Ruyin eat with that fine appetite and wrinkled her nose in contempt.

She ate with perfectly proper manners — but that appetite! Was she competing with piglets?

Did her mother Li Shi not teach her?

A young lady should not eat this much in company.

Second Mistress Chen Shi was lost in her own thoughts.

Fifth Mistress Zheng Shi was privately very envious.

No wonder this new Fourth Sister-in-law had such wonderful color in her face. The way she ate — now she understood.

If only her own eldest daughter had such a good appetite.

After the meal, Jiang Tai-furen invited the sisters-in-law to move to the large daybed by the window to sit and talk.

Yin Shi's eyes darted around and she immediately addressed Jiang Tai-furen: "Mother — there is one matter your daughter-in-law doesn't understand. I wonder if Mother might be kind enough to enlighten me?"

chapters.title: The Mother-in-Law Shields Ru-yin
chapters.content:
Qin Ru-yin sipped her tea in small mouthfuls and, hearing those words, smiled cheerfully at Yin shi.

She still hadn't given up.

The other women, seeing Yin shi preparing to make trouble again, all lowered their heads.

Chen shi and Zheng shi, the two other sisters-in-law, were there purely for the entertainment.

Fang shi was lost in her own thoughts.

Jiang Tai Furen had expected Yin shi to stir things up again — it came as no surprise.

Her old eyes swept across Yin shi's face and she said lightly: "Third daughter-in-law, you are being far too modest."

"How many things in this household could Third daughter-in-law possibly be unaware of? I dare say there are matters I myself would need to ask you to enlighten me on."

Yin shi knew the Old Madam was using this to warn her — to discourage her from asking questions that would put the Old Madam in an awkward position.

But she was determined to ask anyway.

Her eyes darted about, and Yin shi put on an exaggerated smile and said to Jiang Tai Furen: "Mother, you flatter daughter-in-law far too much!"

Then, shifting tone abruptly: "It's just that the matter daughter-in-law wishes to ask about is one she truly knows nothing of... Though of course it is good news. Very wonderful news indeed!"

With that, she turned her smiling gaze to Qin Ru-yin, who sat cradling her tea cup with an expression of perfect innocence.

"Fourth Sister-in-law, come to think of it, this happy news concerns you as well. Third Sister-in-law offers her congratulations in advance!"

The moment she said this, Fang shi snapped her head up to look at her.

Fang shi understood immediately what Yin shi was trying to get the Jiang Tai Furen to explain.

But Fang shi's expression darkened at once.

Fool — so impatient!

She was not the only remarried wife in this room. Fang shi herself was also a second wife brought in after the first.

Even the Jiang Second Madam, Chen shi, raised an eyebrow.

This Third daughter-in-law was truly too hasty.

Whatever the matter was, couldn't she at least wait until the Fourth Son and his new bride had been married three days before raising it?

She had to choose today of all days.

No one knew what trouble she was about to stir up.

Zheng shi glanced around at one and then another.

She was the youngest daughter-in-law, the lowest in seniority — it was not her place to speak.

She settled herself with the air of someone who had come to watch a show and sat perfectly still.

Qin Ru-yin, seeing Yin shi's remarks turning toward her once again, cursed inwardly.

But her face remained smiling.

"Thank you, Third Sister-in-law — you are really too kind! Fourth Master and I have only just been married, and you have already congratulated me several times."

She took a sip of tea from her cup before continuing: "I am quite embarrassed, truly."

Yin shi's punch had landed on cotton.

Not only had she gained nothing, she had strained herself so hard she suffered an internal injury from the effort...

She had been hoping Qin Ru-yin would ask why she was congratulating her again, so she could lead into what she really wanted to say.

But Qin Ru-yin simply refused to take the bait, and that left Yin shi having to bring it up herself — which would look all too deliberate.

Jiang Tai Furen, watching this, looked at Qin Ru-yin with a satisfied and tender expression.

This child was sharp. Her words were pointed, yet on the surface she gave offense to no one.

Still — this was her territory, and she was not about to let the Third daughter-in-law make this new bride miserable during the first days of her marriage.

"Third daughter-in-law, if you have a question, say it plainly. There is really no need to put ideas into Yin-niang's head. It is very unseemly!"

The moment Jiang Tai Furen's reprimand landed, Yin shi's face went white.

In front of her sisters-in-law — and a new bride no less — how could the Old Madam slap her face so directly?

To say outright that she was putting ideas into the new bride's head... how could she carry that?

"You were told to speak plainly — why are you now silent? Weren't you full of words just a moment ago?" Jiang Tai Furen's old eyes scrutinized Yin shi.

Yin shi had not expected the Old Madam to say something even worse.

That provoked her volatile temper.

"Mother, daughter-in-law talks a great deal because she wishes to be lively and show her filial devotion. If Mother does not like it, daughter-in-law will simply speak less from now on."

"Saying it like this, Mother will easily cause Fourth Sister-in-law to misunderstand daughter-in-law!"

"As for congratulating Fourth Sister-in-law just now — daughter-in-law truly meant it as a genuine congratulation!"

After saying all this, her face had already filled with the look of one deeply aggrieved.

Then she glanced at Qin Ru-yin, who was still cradling her tea cup with a serene smile, and felt fury rise in her.

Gritting her teeth, she turned to Jiang Tai Furen and demanded: "Daughter-in-law has heard that Fourth Sister-in-law's name has been entered into the Jiang clan registry... Mother, daughter-in-law wishes to ask — has our Jiang clan changed its rules?"

Jiang Tai Furen's gaze sharpened.

Yin shi ignored the warning in it.

She pressed on: "Truly, for Fourth Sister-in-law, this is a great joy. But as they say — one person's joy is another's sorrow."

"First Sister-in-law is also a second wife, and she has worked herself half to death for this household. Daughter-in-law holds her efforts in the highest regard!"

"First Sister-in-law has been kept in the dark... so daughter-in-law must speak up for her. Since the clan has changed its rules and a second wife may now be entered into the genealogy..."

Yin shi glanced at Fang shi and gave her a meaningful look, then dragged out her words with deliberate effect:

"Since Fourth Sister-in-law's name could be entered into the clan registry, First Sister-in-law, as the wife of the eldest son and the senior daughter-in-law, has even more right to be entered, doesn't she? Mother, am I not correct?"

Jiang Tai Furen understood everything perfectly.

For Yin shi to know of this matter, the Third Son must have told her.

That Third Son!

Jiang Tai Furen was furious.

But she showed nothing of it on her face.

She knew exactly what scheming little calculations Yin shi had in mind.

First, she was deliberately using this matter to drive a wedge between the First daughter-in-law and the Fourth daughter-in-law.

Second was her own nosy curiosity — she wanted to know why the Fourth Son had never entered his first wife Yao shi's name into the clan registry in the first place.

Third, with ill intent, she wanted to use the fact that the Fourth Son had been married before to make the Fourth daughter-in-law feel uncomfortable.

The Fourth daughter-in-law was a new bride, and a young one at that. If she had been the sort who couldn't weather difficulties, she would have fallen straight into Yin shi's trap.

A young girl with a thin skin — if she were the type to silently swallow her grievances, a seed of resentment would be planted from this day on, and along with it, a seed of future trouble.

"Third daughter-in-law, you truly disappoint me..."

Jiang Tai Furen had not yet finished speaking when Qin Ru-yin reached out and gently tugged on her arm.

Jiang Tai Furen immediately stopped and turned to look at her.

"Mother, the matter of Fourth Master and his first wife is something that passed many years ago. Yin-niang doesn't mind it at all — please don't trouble yourself over it either."

Then Qin Ru-yin turned to Yin shi: "Third Sister-in-law, did this really have to be raised today? Making everyone unhappy — is that what you wanted?"

"...Of course, I personally don't mind. I chose Fourth Master as a person, and I chose such a wonderful mother-in-law. Everything else is of little importance to me."

She then looked around at her sisters-in-law: "I came to this household hoping to live a peaceful life."

"But if anyone refuses to let me live in peace — I may be young, but I am stubborn by nature. As long as the fault is not mine, I am not in the habit of indulging anyone."

"I dare say this even in front of Mother, so let us wait and see! I have no wish to start trouble — but I am not afraid of it either!" With that, she fixed Yin shi with a pointed look.

Yin shi bit down hard and stared at Qin Ru-yin with humiliation.

The corner of Fang shi's lips curved almost imperceptibly upward.

Chen shi's gaze flickered.

Zheng shi wore an expression that was difficult to read.

Jiang Tai Furen gave a soft, satisfied clap. "Well said, Yin-niang! That is exactly the spirit I love in you!"

If she had been seven parts satisfied with the Fourth Son's new bride before, she was now ten parts satisfied.

There was no other reason — this girl truly reminded her of herself in her younger days!

She had given birth to so many children, and not one of them had a temperament quite so similar to her own in her youth.

So she felt her heart lean toward Qin Ru-yin just a little more.

The look she turned on the Third Madam Yin shi was anything but kind.

"Third daughter-in-law, you see? There are very few fools in this world waiting around to be outwitted. Put away those little schemes of yours!"

"Today I'll let things rest for Yin-niang's sake, but the Third Son is to stay behind."

Having said that, Jiang Tai Furen turned first to Fang shi: "First daughter-in-law, you have exhausted yourself these days managing the wedding banquet for the Fourth Son. Mother has had some restorative gifts specially prepared — please take them with you."

Fang shi smiled graciously in acknowledgment and offered her thanks.

Qin Ru-yin rose and curtseyed to Fang shi, again thanking Fang shi and the Jiang First Master.

Fang shi smiled and reached out a hand to lift her.

With a meaningful air she said: "Fourth Sister-in-law, there is no need to stand on ceremony with Elder Sister-in-law. If Fourth Sister-in-law wishes to live peacefully in our Jiang household, Elder Sister-in-law is glad of it too!"

Qin Ru-yin returned a bright, warm smile.

Jiang Tai Furen watched with a contented smile.

As long as the First daughter-in-law and the Fourth daughter-in-law had no great rift between them, the inner quarters of the Jiang family could not be thrown into disorder.

The others, no matter how many little calculations they harbored, would not be able to stir up any real storms.

She was not worried.

"Yin-niang, let your Elder Sister-in-law go and rest early. You stay here and keep this old woman company a while longer."

Qin Ru-yin curtseyed in gracious assent.

Jiang Tai Furen waved the other three daughters-in-law off. "All of you may return to your own courtyards!"

Yin shi had gained nothing today and had swallowed a stomach full of anger.

She was miserably aggrieved.

The Jiang Second Madam Chen shi gave the Fifth Madam Zheng shi a look, and the two of them hurriedly took their leave of Jiang Tai Furen.

They then pulled the stone-faced Yin shi away with them.

"Third Sister-in-law... what you said earlier about Fourth Sister-in-law — a second wife who has been entered into the clan registry — is it really true?" Zheng shi could not hold back and asked Yin shi as they walked.

Yin shi gave a cold snort. "Would I lie about something like that? If it were false, the Old Madam would have rebuked me on the spot!"

Zheng shi's heart gave a little jump. She turned to Chen shi: "Second Sister-in-law, you came into this household earlier than any of us. What exactly happened between Fourth Brother and that Yao shi back then?"

"It's been so many years and our household still treats it as a forbidden subject. Not that I'd say so aloud — I've always been rather curious myself!"

Seeing that Yin shi was also looking at her, Chen shi gave her a reproachful glance. "Fifth Sister-in-law entered the household later and wouldn't know — but you came in even before that Yao shi did."

"...Your channels of information have always been far sharper than mine. By rights you would know far more than I do. Why are you looking at me?"

chapters.title: The Jiang Sisters-in-Law and Their Private Calculations
chapters.content:
Yin shi looked defeated and gave a bitter snort. "Second Sister-in-law, if I knew what exactly happened between the Fourth Son and Yao shi back then, I would not have had to go and ask Mother myself today!"

"And Mother — with the new bride right there in the room, she didn't leave me a shred of dignity. Made me look like a complete fool, and all because she dotes on the Fourth Son. Utter favoritism!"

Chen shi frowned slightly. She had no patience for listening to the Third daughter-in-law go on about the Old Madam's favoritism.

The Fourth Son was that capable — if she were the Old Madam, she would be just as partial. Openly, brazenly partial.

Of course she would never say such a thing to Yin shi.

She simply thought the Third Son and his wife were not quite right in the head.

Always complaining the Old Madam showed favoritism, yet never pausing to think why.

How amusing.

Since Yin shi had presented herself so conveniently...

Chen shi lifted her tea cup and first said that she herself truly had no idea what had passed between that couple all those years ago.

Then she shook her head at Yin shi: "Third Sister-in-law, I don't mean to lecture you, but really... how could you choose today of all days to ask Mother about that matter?"

"You know perfectly well that Mother has always shielded the Fourth Son. His remaining unwed for so long has been a thorn in her heart."

"Now that thorn has finally been pulled out — naturally she will love the house and everything in it, and stand firmly behind the Fourth Son's wife. Why on earth would you pick today to make things unpleasant for her?"

"Hmph — I was not making things unpleasant for her. I was speaking up for Elder Sister-in-law." Yin shi refused to acknowledge what Chen shi had said.

Chen shi gave another quiet internal snort but showed nothing of it.

She shook her head. "You! Even if you were speaking up for Elder Sister-in-law — did you see any gratitude from her?"

Yin shi's expression was slightly sour.

She stubbornly held her ground. "I'm not asking for her gratitude! I simply felt sorry for her..."

"What 'sorry' and what 'not sorry' — whether it's Elder Sister-in-law or Fourth Sister-in-law, their days are certainly better than any of ours." It was Zheng shi who spoke up suddenly, in a quiet, distant tone.

Chen shi's gaze shifted faintly.

She then looked at Zheng shi with a smile. "Fifth Sister-in-law is still young, and for now you have only little Yun-jie'r. Once you've given birth to a son, then you'll know what 'not easy' really means!"

Chen shi herself had given birth to four sons.

She considered this unmatched among all the Jiang daughters-in-law.

Yet the Old Madam had never looked at her differently for having given the household four legitimate grandsons.

In the Old Madam's eyes, even Fang shi — a second wife brought in later, who had produced only one son — carried more face than she did.

On what grounds?

Even if Fang shi had given birth to two sons — she had only given birth to one, and yet held such a favored position!

Her eldest boy was the Jiang family's eldest grandson!

She admitted that these days it was the Fourth Son holding up the greater half of the Jiang household.

But the Fourth Son still had no children of his own — which meant his energy ought to be directed toward his nephews.

To speak plainly, she had felt a quiet sense of relief last night when the Fourth Son had not consummated the marriage with his new bride.

Her eldest boy was about to sit for the first round of the imperial examinations.

The old saying goes: a nephew is as good as a son to his uncle!

Since the Fourth Son still had no descendants, his energy ought to go toward her eldest boy.

But if the Fourth Son consummated the marriage and the new bride was lucky enough to conceive quickly...

Then the Fourth Son's energy would inevitably be directed toward his own wife and child.

The Third daughter-in-law was always complaining about the Old Madam's favoritism — it was simply that the Old Madam did not favor the Third Branch.

She was no less resentful that the Old Madam showed no favor to her Second Branch.

But when all was said and done, she could understand the Old Madam's partiality.

Whereas the Third Son and his wife had never understood it.

That was the difference between herself and Yin shi!

Hearing Chen shi's words, Zheng shi's eyes grew forlorn.

She wanted to give birth to a son too.

Four sons, just like Second Sister-in-law!

But she could not understand it — ever since giving birth to her first daughter, she had not been able to conceive again.

Thinking of her inability to conceive... her heart clenched.

Her Fifth Master was never home, as though he had been born and raised inside the army barracks.

She could not fathom it — originally it had been her Fifth Master who had refused another girl and insisted on marrying her...

Ah, never mind. That was something to think about later.

What weighed on her more immediately was her little Yun-jie'r.

Her Yun-jie'r was already three years old.

Yet she ate less than a kitten, and was sickly and listless all day long, thin and small.

Even children in other families who were just over a year old looked larger than her Yun-jie'r...

"Second Sister-in-law — Lin-ge'r will be sitting the imperial examinations next February, won't he? You really must pay careful attention." Yin shi said suddenly.

That struck Chen shi right at her most sensitive point.

She nodded vigorously. "Who says otherwise? My Second Master and I are both burning with anxiety trying to find a better tutor for Lin-ge'r!"

Yin shi's eyes darted about, and she made an exaggerated sound of surprise.

She then looked at Chen shi and said: "Second Sister-in-law, why are you and Second Brother fretting over this? This is exactly the kind of thing to bring to the Fourth Son!"

A shadow crossed Chen shi's eyes.

She lowered her gaze and said evenly: "My Second Master did speak to the Fourth Son about it. But the Fourth Son said Lin-ge'r has changed tutors too many times. He said that since he's gone through quite a few tutors without making much progress, the issue is probably not the tutors themselves..."

"Then what was the Fourth Son's meaning?" Yin shi's eyes darted. "What sort of logic is that? If the tutors aren't the problem, then surely it isn't our Lin-ge'r who is the problem?"

"Lin-ge'r's studies are actually quite reassuring at the moment. Naturally as his parents we want to see him advance even further..." Chen shi disliked Yin shi's tone, and her own tone cooled considerably.

"Now that you mention it, I'm not satisfied with Bai-ge'r's tutor either!" Yin shi acted as though she hadn't noticed and changed the subject.

She exclaimed to Chen shi: "Second Sister-in-law, you don't know this — I have had that tutor for two years and he is still only teaching Bai-ge'r the Thousand Character Classic. He hasn't even started the Analects yet."

Chen shi immediately became guarded.

She thought privately: That is because your son is slow, and what can the poor tutor do about it?

Unlike her Lin-ge'r — after teaching him the foundational texts, his tutor began on the Analects right away!

But aloud she said: "Bai-ge'r is still young! His tutor is quite skilled — laying a solid foundation first means that when the time comes to study more difficult material, he will soar!"

She then added to Yin shi: "I can see that our Bai-ge'r is a very clever child — he will do very well. You simply cannot rush him. As the saying goes, haste makes waste!"

"When my Lin-ge'r was starting out, his first tutor pushed him to move too fast. I always felt there was something lacking in the foundation... and I suspect it was that experience that caused trouble later, why he hasn't been making as much progress."

Chen shi said this to deter Yin shi from asking Jiang Jiu-xiao to find a good tutor for the Third Branch's Bai-ge'r.

Knowing Yin shi's temperament, if the Fourth Son found a famous tutor, she would certainly compete fiercely for a share.

Everyone loved to hear flattery — especially about their own children.

"Second Sister-in-law, is it really like that?"

"I thought our Bai-ge'r simply didn't have Lin-ge'r's gift for learning..." When it came to her own child, Yin shi revealed a wholly maternal tenderness.

Though she knew in her heart that her Bai-ge'r's aptitude for learning was indeed not equal to Second Branch's Lin-ge'r.

Her Third Master had also told her that haste makes waste, and had agreed that Bai-ge'r's tutor's approach was correct.

Her talk of changing tutors hadn't been entirely serious.

But if the Fourth Son really did find a renowned master scholar for the Second Branch's Lin-ge'r, she wouldn't fight for it outright — yet the Fourth Son would still have to be fair to everyone.

Seeing Yin shi ask in this way, Chen shi nodded immediately.

Then quickly shook her head: "Listen to what you're saying! Our Bai-ge'r is so clever — how could he have no gift for learning? I can see that once the foundation is solid, he will surpass all his elder cousins!"

Yin shi brightened at that and launched into boasting about her Bai-ge'r to Chen shi...

Chen shi listened and smiled along with hollow pleasantries.

Zheng shi sat listening nearby, inwardly cold with contempt.

Second Sister-in-law's scheming was so transparent, like Sima Zhao's ambitions — plain for all to see...

So what if Third Sister-in-law was pushy and competitive?

So what if she and Second Sister-in-law were supposedly close?

When it came to their own children's interests, who cared about any of that?

None of them were as good as the newly arrived Fourth Sister-in-law.

At least that woman said openly what she was thinking.

When she first heard Fourth Sister-in-law say those things, she had been displeased.

She felt that a new bride who had only just entered the household, speaking in such a way in front of her mother-in-law and sisters-in-law — how could she dare?

Even if she was the youngest daughter-in-law in terms of rank, Zheng shi had still entered this household several years before Qin shi.

At the time, she had thought the Fourth Master's wife simply relied on the Fourth Master behind her and didn't place any of her sisters-in-law in her eyes...

But now, looking at the Second and Third Madams, Zheng shi felt she'd rather deal with the Fourth sister-in-law.

"Second Sister-in-law, Third Sister-in-law — my little Yun-jie'r has been ill again these past few days and can't be without me for long, so I'll be heading back..."

Chen shi immediately urged her to go: "Fifth Sister-in-law, do go — Yun-jie'r needs you. Go take good care of her."

Yin shi, her cheerful run of boasting about her son interrupted by Zheng shi, pursed her lips and had nothing to say to Zheng shi.

......

In the flower hall, Jiang Tai Furen gave the Third Master a thorough dressing-down, then sent all her sons away.

She only instructed Jiang Jiu-xiao to come to Rong'an Hall in one hour to collect Qin Ru-yin.

Jiang Jiu-xiao agreed.

Jiang Tai Furen was satisfied.

She returned to her large daybed by the window and drew Qin Ru-yin over to talk.

"Don't take what your Third Sister-in-law said today to heart." Jiang Tai Furen took Qin Ru-yin's hand and gently stroked her soft fingertips.

"Your Third Sister-in-law has always had that tiresome temperament. She hasn't made much progress in all these years."

Jiang Tai Furen looked into Qin Ru-yin's eyes and said warmly: "Mother will also be honest with you — of all her daughters-in-law, the one Mother likes least is your Third Sister-in-law."

Jiang Tai Furen spoke plainly.

Qin Ru-yin could see it herself.

So she smiled and said nothing.

Everyone has their likes and dislikes. The chemistry between people depended on both temperament and character.

When temperament and character aligned, the relationship was easy. When they didn't, even the most virtuous person was difficult to be around.

She saw nothing wrong with her mother-in-law disliking Yin shi.

She didn't like her either.

Seeing Qin Ru-yin press her lips together in a smile, Jiang Tai Furen smiled too.

She went on: "That said — what she mentioned about your name being entered into the clan registry is indeed the truth."

Qin Ru-yin, seeing Jiang Tai Furen pause, nodded and said: "Mother, I already know about this — as it happens, Fourth Master told me himself today."

"Oh? Is that so?" Jiang Tai Furen was slightly surprised, and more than slightly pleased.

"The Fourth Son is a man who keeps things close to his chest. When he speaks with me, he usually waits for me to ask before he answers... For him to take the initiative to tell you — that is a good sign!"

Qin Ru-yin thought of what he had said, and told Jiang Tai Furen with a smile: "Fourth Master also said he didn't want me to hear about this first from someone else's mouth."

Jiang Tai Furen felt even more pleased.

This meant the Fourth Son was keeping the promise he had made to her.

Since he had brought Qin Ru-yin into the household as his wife, he would treat her well and live a good life with her...

A son having this kind of heart made her happier than any promotion he could ever receive!

After a moment's reflection, Jiang Tai Furen's old face broke into creases of delight, and she regarded Qin Ru-yin with even greater tenderness.

Holding Qin Ru-yin's soft little hands in both of hers, she asked: "Since the Fourth Son has already told you your name was entered into the Jiang clan registry, did he tell you the reason for it?"

chapters.title: Competing with Him for His New Bride?
chapters.content:
Qin Ru-yin shook her head. "Fourth Master hadn't had the chance to explain yet."

"So the meaning is... the Fourth Son was willing to bring it up on his own?" Jiang Tai Furen smiled.

Qin Ru-yin also smiled in reply: "Mother, I truly do not mind what passed between the Fourth Master and his first wife all those years ago."

"The late Yao-jia jiejie has been gone for nearly ten years. The departed are at rest — what matters is that those of us still living make the most of our lives."

She paused, then added: "Yin-niang knows that Third Sister-in-law was trying to sow discord with what she said today. But since I don't mind in the least, her attempts at stirring trouble are entirely pointless."

"I won't hide it from Mother — when Third Sister-in-law said those things just now, I was displeased."

"But what displeased me was simply that she harbored such unkind intentions in the first place."

"Mother knows that I came to the Jiang household hoping to live in peace. Third Sister-in-law behaves as though she won't rest unless the whole world is unsettled."

In front of her sisters-in-law, Qin Ru-yin had chosen to give Third Madam Yin shi one last shred of face and had not confronted her openly.

But if Yin shi dared to do it again, she would not be giving her that consideration.

She therefore made her position clear to Jiang Tai Furen as well.

"Mother, if Third Sister-in-law behaves this way again next time, Yin-niang will not be indulging her."

"Though Mother may rest assured — Yin-niang will certainly never provoke trouble without reason..."

Hearing this, Jiang Tai Furen did not reprimand Qin Ru-yin at all. She burst out laughing.

Excellent!

That was exactly as it should be!

Don't start trouble, but don't be afraid of it either!

She truly was the image of Jiang Tai Furen's own younger self.

Though in her own younger days, when she had sparred with her sisters-in-law, she had already been in her twenties.

She had grown bolder as she aged.

And after her children's father passed, she had been forced to hold the family together like a man, shielding the young children still in the household.

But how old was Yin-niang now?

And already this bold.

She had even made it clear beforehand in front of her mother-in-law.

Setting things out in the open like that — that was wisdom as well as courage.

Both brave and shrewd. No wonder she was the child raised by the Qin First Branch.

No wonder the Qin First Branch had been bold enough to take the Third Branch and split from the main Qin clan.

"Good! If she stirs things up again next time and tries to make trouble for Yin-niang, Yin-niang may freely put her in her place with words — Mother will be here to back you up!"

Jiang Tai Furen waved her hand. "As long as you have done nothing wrong, we have nothing to fear! And if Mother cannot hold things together on her own, there is still the Fourth Son!"

It was probably time, however, to let Yin-niang know about the matter of the Fourth Son's first wife before too long.

Just not right now — she had only just been married. Better to wait a few more days.

No need to frighten the young girl.

Qin Ru-yin leaned over and clung to her arm, acting spoiled: "Listen to Mother talk — Yin-niang isn't going off to war."

"As long as the sisters-in-law and Fifth Brother's wife don't come picking on Yin-niang, everything will be perfectly fine."

"Yin-niang only wants to take walks with Mother every day, sit in the sun, and drink tea..."

Jiang Tai Furen was so delighted that her eyebrows arched as high as they could go.

How wonderful!

Ever since she had grown older, one would think — sons and grandchildren filling the house, and one especially accomplished son — her life as an honored matriarch should be the envy of countless people.

Yet who could know that once the children grew up, and the grandchildren had their own parents to look after them, she felt as though no one needed her anymore... Such days were truly too lonely.

A loneliness that frightened her.

"It is settled then — from now on, come and keep this old woman company whenever you have time!" Jiang Tai Furen's eyes lit up with anticipation.

This young girl was a delight.

And since the Fourth Son had not yet consummated the marriage with her, she needed to help him keep her close properly.

"Of course — as long as Mother doesn't mind me!" Qin Ru-yin laughed and nodded.

Then, with excitement, she said to Jiang Tai Furen: "Yin-niang has already spoken to Fourth Master about building a small kitchen in Minglian Residence. When that's ready, Yin-niang will make delicious food for Mother!"

Jiang Tai Furen exclaimed her approval repeatedly.

Not only Jiang Tai Furen — even Nanny Hua could barely contain her beaming delight.

......

The Jiang brothers were walking along the covered corridor, chatting idly.

When they were about to go their separate ways, Jiang Jiu-xiao called out to the Third Master to stop.

"Third Brother, a moment."

The Third Master halted and turned. "Something the matter?"

"Go home and keep a better hand on your wife."

The Third Master's brows drew tight together and he fixed Jiang Jiu-xiao with a contemptuous glare.

"It was nothing but women's idle chatter — since when does the Fourth Son take it so seriously? That doesn't sound like you at all!"

"Third Brother, you know in your own heart what is really going on." Jiang Jiu-xiao looked at him evenly.

"If Third Brother and Third Sister-in-law truly feel aggrieved living in this Jiang household, there is a vacant magistrate's post in Yanling in Jiangnan. You could take Third Sister-in-law there and serve as the county magistrate."

The Third Master's teeth ground audibly.

"You want to drive me away?"

"Hardly. I simply see that Third Brother has grown increasingly discontented over the years, and in the capital..."

"Any position in the capital, even the smallest, is better than being a miserable county magistrate in some godforsaken backwater!" The Third Master furiously cut him off.

"You are now the President of the Ministry of Personnel — surely you know that even a minor capital official outranks his provincial counterpart by three grades?"

"I don't know what you're playing at. Instead of helping your brother as a younger brother should, you're trying to drive him away!"

The Third Master's years of suppressed resentment finally broke through.

His face was contorted with agitation, his voice loud.
