The maids and matrons tending the gardens along the corridor hurried away, terrified of hearing something they shouldn't and being sold off by the masters.

The Jiang household had always treated its servants well — on festivals and celebrations, monthly wages were tripled. With so many masters in the household, each having their birthday or a celebration, there were bonuses to be had every single month of the year.

No one wanted to leave such a household.

"The capital is thick with minor officials. By rights, Third Brother is not without ability — and yet have I seen you rise over all these years?"

"I told you long ago to go and gain some real-world experience in a local posting. Working your way up from there would be a far better investment than clinging to the capital."

"Besides, Yanling is the ancestral home of Third Sister-in-law's natal clan. Sending you to Yanling is doing you a kindness — don't be ungrateful."

"Yanling has also been a land of abundance for a thousand years. It is the kind of post that scions of great families fight tooth and nail to obtain. Securing it for you was no small matter."

Jiang Jiu-xiao was genuinely magnanimous toward his own blood brother.

And the Third Master was, in fact, Jiang Jiu-xiao's twin.

Though the two looked little alike.

Toward this Third Brother who had come into the world only half an hour before him, his feelings were inevitably different.

But whatever disagreements existed between brothers, they ought not to involve their wives.

The Third Madam Yin shi wanted to use his new bride as a stepping-stone — and behind that stood the Third Master's own intentions.

Otherwise, Yin shi would not have dared.

"However prettily you say it, it cannot hide the fact that you have always been unable to tolerate me!" The Third Master raged, his eyes red.

Jiang Jiu-xiao sighed and shook his head.

"Think it over carefully. And discuss it properly with Third Sister-in-law."

Having said that, Jiang Jiu-xiao said nothing more. He clasped his hands behind his back and strolled back toward Minglian Residence.

In Jiang Tai Furen's quarters, she was holding Qin Ru-yin's hand and speaking to her about the Third Master's inner demons.

"To be truthful, your Third Sister-in-law may be pushy and competitive, but she has never done anything truly wicked... She is someone whose entire mind is filled with only her own little family."

"If there is anyone in this world who cares most about the Third Son, even this old woman of mine comes after your Third Sister-in-law."

"Today Mother is very angry with your Third Sister-in-law, and she truly wants to give her a sharp scolding to wake her up — but...alas!"

Jiang Tai Furen shook her head and sighed. "Let us not speak of those two anymore — the more I say, the more vexed I become."

It was only now that Qin Ru-yin learned that the Third Master — Jiang Jiu-xiao's twin — had always harbored a deep envy of Jiang Jiu-xiao...

The gap between them was simply too vast.

From childhood, Jiang Jiu-xiao had been the kind of child every parent dreams of — gifted in every area and brilliant in all of them.

But the Third Master, despite being half of the same twin pair and the elder of the two, had been a child of ordinary talent from birth.

He had only his effort.

And he had indeed made every effort.

Through sheer determination, he had carved out his own path in the imperial examinations and emerged as a Second Division jinshi.

That was, in truth, quite a remarkable achievement.

Only — Jiang Jiu-xiao's brilliance was breathtaking.

The blazing light of the full moon and the faint glow of a grain of rice: the eyes of the world are naturally drawn to the blazing moon.

The Third Master's fault lay in his state of mind.

He could not escape his own inner demons.

And Third Sister-in-law Yin shi was fiercely protective of her husband by nature.

From what Jiang Tai Furen described, Qin Ru-yin concluded that Yin shi was someone entirely consumed by romantic devotion.

She charged ahead on the Third Master's behalf, fighting and grabbing for everything.

The Third Master hid behind her and enjoyed the fruits of her efforts.

This couple...

Honestly speaking, Qin Ru-yin found them both rather difficult to account for.

Of course, it was their own choice as a couple.

As an outsider, she had no business judging.

Only — they had better not parade themselves in front of her!

"Yin-niang, Mother tells you these things not because she wants you to keep yielding to that foolish pair... You handle things exactly as you see fit."

"Mother is simply giving you a picture of what that foolish pair are about. As for the First Branch and Second Branch — they have their own troubles too."

"As for the Fifth Son — he is Mother's youngest. Mother was already past thirty when she had him."

"Unfortunately, not long after his birth, his father took ill and lingered, and Mother was consumed with caring for his father and was unable to give him the attention he needed. He was left entirely in the care of his wet nurse."

"And so — though he is my youngest, he and Mother are the least close."

This was Jiang Tai Furen's greatest regret in life.

"When he came of age to discuss a match, he wouldn't listen to Mother and said he would only marry someone he chose himself."

"It was only the Fourth Son pressing him that finally led to a betrothal with the Zheng family Second Branch's third legitimate daughter."

"And then, after the betrothal was settled, he announced he was in love with the Zheng family Third Branch's second legitimate daughter — that is your Fifth Sister-in-law today..."

"Alas! That little wretch... The Fourth Son went to the Zheng family to apologize and suffered a great deal of humiliation on his account."

"Fortunately, the Zheng family agreed in the end." Jiang Tai Furen exhaled heavily.

"But that little wretch — after marrying your Fifth Sister-in-law, he still did not settle down. He spends at least half of every month away from home..."

Qin Ru-yin listened and felt just as troubled for Jiang Tai Furen.

Everyone had said Jiang Tai Furen had such good fortune.

Now she saw — the old proverb held true after all.

Every household has its own difficult scripture to read.

Qin Ru-yin offered some comfort to Jiang Tai Furen: "Mother, you have long since fulfilled your duties — it is high time you lived well for yourself!"

"Children and grandchildren will find their own path. Don't be a beast of burden for them... Besides, when it comes down to it, all the brothers and the Fifth Son have actually turned out quite well."

"They were born into a great and wealthy clan like the Jiang family, yet none of them strayed from the right path. As for the small frictions and disagreements among brothers — that is quite ordinary."

"Just think about it — even teeth sometimes bite the tongue. It happens. As long as things never escalate into a real rift, all is well."

That is just life.

Nanny Hua, listening to the side, nodded emphatically and said to Jiang Tai Furen:

"Tai Furen, look — doesn't our Fourth Madam know exactly what to say! What she says is so right and so sensible! You really should do as she says — stop worrying yourself over so much. Your children and grandchildren will find their own fortune. You being well and healthy is fortune enough for all of them!"

Qin Ru-yin nodded in agreement: "Mother, Nanny Hua is quite right! As long as you are well, that itself is the greatest fortune for all of us younger ones!"

The melancholy that had settled over Jiang Tai Furen opened up and brightened at once.

Just then, a little maid outside reported that the Fourth Master had come to escort the Fourth Madam back to Minglian Residence.

Jiang Jiu-xiao, tall and upright, lifted the bead curtain with his own hand and walked in.

Jiang Tai Furen looked at him with a hint of displeasure: "Why have you come so quickly? Did I not say to come and collect Yin-niang after one full hour?"

Jiang Jiu-xiao was somewhat taken aback.

Was his old mother... competing with him for his new bride?

chapters.title: Qin Ru-yue Is Despised by Her In-Laws — A Marriage That Becomes Estranged from the Very Start
chapters.content:
"Mother, your son waited the full hour before coming to collect her, exactly as you said." Jiang Jiu-xiao settled himself into a chair in the room without ceremony, lifting his robe to sit.

Jiang Tai Furen looked a little skeptical and checked the light outside. "Has a full hour really passed already?"

Nanny Hua smiled and said to her: "Tai Furen, it has been a little over one full hour since the Fourth Master left."

Jiang Jiu-xiao nodded. "Walking here took nearly a quarter of an hour."

He had actually walked rather quickly.

Jiang Tai Furen paid him no mind and simply held Qin Ru-yin's hand. "How strange — usually Mother feels the days crawl by so slowly. But today, chatting with you like this, look how quickly the time has passed!"

Qin Ru-yin's eyes curved with a smile, and she said: "Then Yin-niang will stay and keep Mother company a little longer."

Jiang Jiu-xiao looked at Qin Ru-yin with a quiet, lingering gaze.

Qin Ru-yin, however, did not notice.

It was Jiang Tai Furen who caught her son's glance, and her eyes lit up.

She immediately urged: "No, no — you two are newlyweds at the sweetest moment of your marriage. Hurry back to your own courtyard."

Even as she said it, Jiang Tai Furen was reluctant to let go, her fingers still stroking Qin Ru-yin's smooth, fine-skinned little hand. "...Yin-niang, come keep Mother company again tomorrow."

Nanny Hua watched with quiet amusement.

Looking at her mistress, one would think the Fourth Son hadn't married a bride for himself at all — it was as if she herself had acquired a beloved Fourth daughter-in-law.

Without even waiting for Jiang Tai Furen's instruction, Nanny Hua took it upon herself to escort the newlywed couple out of Rong'an Hall.

"It seems you and Mother got along very well." Jiang Jiu-xiao remarked to Qin Ru-yin on the way back to Minglian Residence.

Jiang Jiu-xiao stood at least six chi tall, with a pair of long, striding legs that moved swiftly.

Qin Ru-yin's height was not small by a woman's standards, yet beside Jiang Jiu-xiao she looked like a little sprout.

She naturally walked much slower than he did.

Jiang Jiu-xiao had always been slowing his pace to match her rhythm.

Even so, Qin Ru-yin still found it tiring to walk alongside him.

She had always quietly congratulated herself on having a pair of long, straight, shapely legs.

Now she let go of that vanity.

Her little legs, spinning like wind-fire wheels, were aching with the effort.

When Jiang Jiu-xiao spoke to her, she was already rather listless, and could only nod in reply.

Jiang Jiu-xiao frowned.

"Did Mother say something that displeased you?"

By rights, that shouldn't be the case.

He knew his old mother's temperament well enough. She and this young girl ought to get along very naturally.

"Of course not! Mother adores me." Qin Ru-yin immediately spoke up for Jiang Tai Furen, then negotiated with him: "Fourth Master, could you walk a little more slowly? My legs are short — I can't keep up..."

The Jiang estate, after all, had been expanded three times under Jiang Jiu-xiao's ownership and was of very considerable size.

Walking from Jiang Tai Furen's Rong'an Hall to Minglian Residence, even at a brisk pace, took well over a quarter of an hour.

The inner quarters did have palanquins available for the ladies when the distances were long.

But she felt she wasn't a woman with bound feet — walking fifteen or twenty minutes should be no trouble.

Besides, the Jiang estate's garden was beautifully crafted. The garden scenery, rockery, and plantings were all exquisite. Admiring them on the way lifted the spirits considerably.

Hearing her, Jiang Jiu-xiao looked at her in mild surprise, then looked down at his own feet...

He had thought himself attentive — he had already slowed his steps considerably to match her pace.

It seemed, then...

A grown man and a delicate young woman were simply not the same...

"Ah... right."

He slowed even further, and turned to look at her from the side.

"The path from Minglian Residence to Mother's quarters is quite long as well. In future when you come alone to keep Mother company, have the servants arrange a palanquin for you first."

Qin Ru-yin agreed.

She thought to herself: He is truly meticulous in his attentiveness! No wonder he can hold such high office.

Though if she were walking alone to the Tai Furen's courtyard, she would simply think of it as a stroll through the garden — it would not tire her feet like this.

Jiang Jiu-xiao, seeing she was clearly lacking her earlier energy and looked rather deflated, felt a pang of something he couldn't quite name.

So he stopped, and without further deliberation, turned and scooped her up in his arms.

Qin Ru-yin let out a startled cry.

On instinct, she threw both arms around his neck to steady herself.

She stared at him wide-eyed, her lovely face flushing instantly crimson...

Jiang Jiu-xiao, however, did not look at her. He fixed his gaze straight ahead and strode forward.

The maids and matrons attending Qin Ru-yin all bowed their heads and suppressed smiles.

By the time Jiang Jiu-xiao carried Qin Ru-yin back — before they had even reached Minglian Residence — the news had already spread throughout the inner quarters of the Jiang household.

Who had said the Fourth Master disliked women coming near him?

If that were true, why was he carrying the newly married Fourth Madam in his arms right now?

At the same moment, a person who had been quietly watching the Jiang household from the shadows also received word.

Prince An.

At this moment, Prince An was seated in a private room of the wine house closest to the Jiang estate.

"Jiang Jiu-xiao!"

He slammed the wine cup in his hand down hard.

Wine splashed everywhere.

The men beside him dropped to their knees in alarm.

Only the elderly Daoist seated across from him, dressed in his ceremonial robe, remained perfectly calm, flicking his horsetail whisk with unhurried composure.

He said to Prince An: "Your Highness, please be at ease. Whether or not Miss Qin has become Jiang Jiu-xiao's woman — as long as Your Highness keeps Miss Qin close, she will be just as beneficial to your prospects..."

"What if this King says he does not wish for her to become Jiang Jiu-xiao's woman?" Prince An clenched his fist, his expression dark as he looked at the old Daoist.

The old Daoist paused.

Could it be that the Prince had truly developed feelings for that Miss Qin?

That seemed unlikely.

He had been constantly at Prince An's side and knew very well that the Prince had only laid eyes on Miss Qin once.

But regardless, since the Prince had expressed this sentiment, he naturally had to nurture it.

"Your Highness, our people have sent word — the newlyweds did not consummate their marriage last night. We still have an opportunity..."

Before the old Daoist could finish, Prince An cut him off: "Opportunity? What opportunity?"

"The day of their wedding was the best opportunity! Yet that day I lost fifteen of my most formidable men, and still failed!"

"Now she is sheltered in the Jiang family's inner quarters... what opportunity remains?"

The old Daoist said quickly: "Your Highness, Miss Qin cannot remain in the Jiang family's inner quarters forever and never set foot outside..."

Prince An cut him off again.

"On the day of their wedding, I already flushed the birds from the grass! Though the Emperor did not blame me, and found a suitable scapegoat to erase all traces for me —"

"— do you truly believe that with the Emperor's suspicious nature, he holds no suspicions toward me?"

The old Daoist dared not answer this.

"Whatever else, there can be no bold moves again in the near future..."

Prince An gave a cold snort, and then instructed one of the men kneeling before him: "Go and send word to Wang Huai-mian — tell him to keep a close eye on that Qin woman of the Qin Second Branch!"

The attendant acknowledged and rose, slipping away to carry out the order.

The old Daoist thought for a moment and said: "Since Your Highness still intends to make use of Wang Huai-mian, the promise made to Qin shi must be fulfilled."

"Hmph. It is nothing more than letting Wang Shi-cheng climb half a step from his position as Chancellor of the National Academy — it is no great matter. There are suitable people at court to handle this for me."

"Before I entered the palace today, I had already made the arrangements. Barring any mishap, the Ministry of Personnel will have already issued the promotion document for Wang Shi-cheng." Prince An gave a cold smile.

The old Daoist frowned.

"Though the Chancellor of the National Academy in our Great Ying dynasty does not hold the real power he once did in former dynasties, it is a position some people can only dream of."

"Your Highness — the Wang family is so shortsighted. Building them up may well prove to be of very limited use..."

"No matter!" Prince An cut him off. "The Wang family is small. I have never had them in my sights. They do not deserve to be cultivated by me."

It was purely for the sake of that Qin woman who could have prophetic dreams.

On the day of the wedding, if his plan had succeeded, Qin shi would at this moment have been Jiang Jiu-xiao's wife.

Then Qin shi would have been of even greater value.

And the person he had wanted most would already be at his side.

What a pity...

A single wrong move, and the entire game was lost.

......

Qin Ru-yue had as she wished become Wang Huai-mian's wife.

Yet on the very first day after the wedding, Qin Ru-yue suffered greatly.

Lady Wang found her and Wang Huai-mian's wedding-day conduct mortifying, and made no secret of her dislike for the new bride.

She did not even bother to pretend otherwise.

And Lord Wang — a man known for his ostensibly gentle disposition — saw fit to reprimand his new daughter-in-law for her impropriety on their wedding day.

By custom, a father-in-law would not lightly reprimand a daughter-in-law — yet she had experienced it nonetheless.

She was still a new bride and had already earned her mother-in-law's displeasure and her father-in-law's reprimand.

Naturally, her sisters-in-law and distant sisters-in-law were either secretly laughing at her or already eagerly positioning themselves to put her down.

Even the husband who had said he would marry no one but her showed no particular joy after obtaining her.

At this moment he was still blaming her for a prophetic dream that had turned out to be inaccurate — accusing her of making him and the Wang family a laughingstock in the eyes of all the capital's great families...

But how was she to have known that Prince An would be so vicious as to try to switch the bride on her very wedding day?

"Second Master, please trust me — my prophetic dreams are certainly accurate! Before I left my parents' home, I had already verified them many times!" Qin Ru-yue said with distress.

"If they weren't accurate, why do you think my grandmother and father were willing to give me such a generous dowry?"

"Hmph!" Wang Huai-mian gave a cold snort, not even glancing up at her, his eyes fixed on the scroll in his hand.

Qin Ru-yue bit her lip.

At that moment the curtain moved, and Red Sleeve — the senior maid Qin Ru-yue had brought to the Wang household — entered with her face bright with excitement.

chapters.title: A Petty Person Reveling in Triumph
chapters.content:
"Second Master, Second Young Madam — wonderful news! My lord has been promoted! The Ministry of Personnel has just sent someone with the official promotion document..."

"Ah..." Qin Ru-yue let out an excited cry.

Wang Huai-mian leapt to his feet, his gaze blazing: "Is it true?"

Red Sleeve nodded again and again.

"Congratulations, Second Master! Congratulations, Second Master!" Red Sleeve was beaming.

She knew that her young mistress had entered the Wang household and immediately fallen into a precarious situation...

And now, at this critical moment, my lord had been promoted. Could anyone say this wasn't thanks to her young mistress?

She could only hope that the young master would feel how valuable the young mistress was, and treat her better!

If the young mistress was well, then they, who followed the young mistress, were also well.

Qin Ru-yue also collected herself.

After a look of approval at Red Sleeve, she instructed her: "Father's promotion is such joyous news — today everyone in Youluoyuan receives one hundred wen each!"

Wang Huai-mian saw her rewarding the courtyard's servants in celebration of his father's promotion, and was well-pleased.

He was always aloof and proud, and was not inclined to lower himself and make the first move toward his new wife.

"Second Master, didn't I tell you just now? As long as we serve Prince An, there will be nothing but good things for our household..."

"Mm... hmph!" Wang Huai-mian suppressed his delight and his urgent desire to go to the outer courtyard to find his father.

He could not go just yet.

His father had not moved at all in seven or eight years, and now a sudden promotion — someone had clearly worked behind the scenes.

Needless to say, he already knew who that someone was.

In that case, Qin shi had been right.

The prophetic dream she had, though somewhat at odds with reality, was correct that aligning with Prince An was not wrong!

At least not wrong for the Wang family.

Since Qin shi had already made a gesture of goodwill, he too needed to offer her some reassurance.

And besides, she was truly beautiful.

Having become a wife after being a maiden, she had grown even more beautiful...

Thinking this, a few threads of tenderness wove into his gaze as he looked at Qin Ru-yue.

He gave two false coughs and walked to Qin Ru-yue's side, taking her shoulder with a hand: "Madam is quite right. It isn't that this husband did not believe you. It's simply that last night was exhausting and my energy was a little low, so I may have been somewhat remiss toward Madam..."

"I hope Madam will forgive me..."

Hearing him speak such private words of a husband to his wife, Qin Ru-yue's lovely face flushed scarlet.

"Second Master, you..."

Seeing her adorably flustered — even more alluring for it — Wang Huai-mian felt a wave of emotion stir within him.

He deliberately leaned close to her ear and breathed a puff of air, then laughed lightly and teasingly: "We are husband and wife already — what is there to be shy about? Besides, everyone in this room is your people. Wasn't Madam last night quite..."

Qin Ru-yue pressed her hand over his mouth. "Second Master! In broad daylight..."

Wang Huai-mian winked roguishly, then said: "Very well — have someone attend me while I change my clothes. I must go to the outer courtyard to see Father."

Qin Ru-yue stepped back two paces, curtseyed, and with a smile instructed Red Sleeve and another senior maid named Moon Sliver to come attend him and help him change his clothes.

Lady Wang had by this time also received the good tidings from the outer courtyard.

Yet she was not nearly as excited and pleased as the young couple.

Though Lord Wang had indeed been promoted, it was by only half a grade — to the post of Grand Court of the Imperial Stud, a third-rank post.

It was a promotion, to be sure, and the position of Grand Court of the Imperial Stud was the head of its own department — an actual post with real authority, compared to the previous fourth-rank position of Chancellor of the National Academy.

But what was there to be pleased about?

The Chancellor of the National Academy — how prestigious and honored a position that was!

Among the literati, its prestige was considerable.

And the Grand Court of the Imperial Stud of the Great Ying dynasty specialized in managing the royal carriages and horses, as well as breeding horses and training warhorses.

Going from a distinguished and leisurely position to a demanding and complex one in a single step...

Lady Wang truly could not see the good in it.

And besides, breeding horses and training warhorses was hardly an unambiguously fortunate posting.

Wang Huai-mian went directly to the outer courtyard and straight to Lord Wang's study.

Lord Wang was cradling the document from the Ministry of Personnel and beaming with joy.

"Father!" Wang Huai-mian stepped in with eager strides.

Lord Wang saw him come and waved him over immediately. "Mian-ge'r, come — take a look!"

Wang Huai-mian read Lord Wang's promotion document, and his lips trembled with excitement.

"Father! Your son congratulates you — this time you've finally been appointed to a real post with substance!"

Lord Wang stroked his beard, laughing with unrestrained delight. "Yes — finally a post with real substance!"

"Only..." Wang Huai-mian still leaned toward positions that were both prestigious and wielded real authority.

He frowned slightly at his father: "Only, if this appointment had been to the Ministry of Personnel or the Ministry of Revenue, that would have been even better!"

"Aiya!" Lord Wang shook his head repeatedly. "You are still young. At this time, being appointed to head the Grand Court of the Imperial Stud is the very best possible posting!"

Wang Huai-mian looked at him in confusion. "Father, how so?"

Lord Wang stroked his beard and guided him through it: "If the Emperor were still in the prime of his years, this position would be little better than a sinecure."

"But now the Emperor is approaching the end of his years, and all the princes are grown — which means the question of succession is at hand..."

He left the rest unsaid, but Wang Huai-mian already understood.

Lord Wang, seeing his son so quick to grasp the implication, was very pleased.

He continued: "Whenever a great central dynasty like ours enters the twilight of an emperor's reign, the powerful kingdoms on the borders always begin to look with hungry eyes."

"Especially those to the north... Throughout history, there have been no exceptions."

"And at such times, the Grand Court of the Imperial Stud must prepare the finest horses in advance, training warhorses..."

"And war is the finest shortcut for those ambitious princes who wish to seize military merit and prestige..."

Wang Huai-mian's heart gave a sharp thud.

If his father was speaking this way, then Prince An's ambitions were... substantial indeed!

Otherwise, why would he have shifted their family — generations of scholars and literati — into a position overseeing all the horses and vehicles of the realm?

And vehicles were not only the supply wagons that accompanied armies on the march.

War chariots were also vehicles.

And the most important kind of vehicle in the Great Ying dynasty at that!

And their family, with its long tradition of scholarly prestige and high standing among the literati, could in future — if needed — be rotated back to a position of both prestige and real power...

Just thinking it through briefly, he was already thrilled.

Prince An having great ambitions was the best possible news!

It meant that Qin shi's prophetic dream was correct — by following Prince An, the Wang family could only advance further!

Lord Wang naturally knew that his rapid promotion owed to Prince An's intervention behind the scenes.

Since Mian-ge'r had already made covert contact with Prince An, even if on the surface they took no sides, the Wang family had no choice but to align with Prince An in private.

Once you place your stone, you play it without regret!

Word spread quickly throughout the capital's great families that Lord Wang had suddenly been promoted — transferred and elevated from the position of Chancellor of the National Academy to Grand Court of the Imperial Stud.

Many of the great family patriarchs were astonished.

There had not been the slightest whisper beforehand.

Some privately envied, others privately doubted.

Those who were truly perceptive could see which patron the Wang family had secretly backed, and they all privately thought Lord Wang was a fool. They quietly began instructing their own families to slowly distance themselves from the Wangs.

On the Jiang household's side.

Word of the Wang family masters' various reactions to Lord Wang's promotion quickly reached Jiang Jiu-xiao.

Under the laws of the Great Ying dynasty, an official was given nine days of leave for his own wedding.

Jiang Jiu-xiao would not be going to the office for those nine days.

Yet as the chief minister of an entire department, even without going to the office, certain matters still required his personal handling.

Documents requiring his decision were all sent to the Jiang household.

The document for Lord Wang's promotion was one he himself had signed.

An informant had been quietly placed in the Wang household several days earlier.

These arrangements were partly his own doing, but more the intent of the Crown Prince.

In truth, the Crown Prince, ever since the injury to his leg left him disabled, had become somewhat despondent.

On top of that, several of his sons had fallen gravely ill and died in succession. After the youngest of them also passed, the Crown Prince had at one point been so unable to see a way forward that he had considered surrendering that position altogether.

But as it happened — just a few days before he and Yin-niang formalized their betrothal — the Crown Princess was found to be three months along with a male child.

Because the Eastern Palace had kept it tightly concealed from the beginning, the early signs of the Crown Princess's pregnancy had been carefully hidden.

Even Wang Cheng-bin had been unaware.

With a son on the way, the Crown Prince at last found his resolve renewed.

He could not act only for himself — he owed it to the Crown Princess and the child she carried to secure a path forward.

This was his legitimate heir!

Of the three sons who had died before, one was born of the Crown Prince's principal concubine Lin Liang-di, one of concubine Li Liang-yuan, and the youngest of concubine Wang Liang-yuan.

After entering the Eastern Palace, the Crown Princess had given birth to two little commandery princesses and had not conceived again. Years later, this unexpected pregnancy — and a male child at that — was as though Heaven itself stood on the Crown Prince's side and had given him hope once more.

The Crown Prince had long known that Prince An was a whetstone that his Imperial Father was keeping on hand to sharpen him and his brothers against.

In the imperial family's contest for the throne, blood and ice always ran hand in hand.

Before the Crown Prince had made a firm and final decision to burn his bridges and fight, Jiang Jiu-xiao had not, as Wang Cheng-bin imagined, been doing his utmost to secure his succession.

He had always been observing.

His own strategy was, in truth, relatively passive: handle what comes, meet the stream with a dam.

Steering a great clan several hundred years old — the weight on his shoulders was far more than duty. Greater than duty was human lives.

One misstep, and every member of the Jiang main lineage would be annihilated.

Even the Jiang collateral branches would not escape ruin for generations.

This was why he had been striving so urgently to find a way to break the impasse.

The Crown Prince's current state was something he found reasonably satisfactory.

After Li Yi took his leave, Jiang Jiu-xiao rose and strolled back toward Minglian Residence.

Qin Ru-yin was reclining against the large chair by the window, reading a paperback volume.

Jiang Jiu-xiao walked toward her and asked: "What are you reading?"

Qin Ru-yin put the book away a little sheepishly.

"It's something my Second Brother found for me — it tells the story of a young man of wealth who by a twist of fate traveled through the northern frontier."

Jiang Jiu-xiao's lips curved slightly. "You enjoy books on local customs and travel writing?"

Qin Ru-yin nodded. "I do! I also like reading vernacular novels..."

Jiang Jiu-xiao's eyebrow rose a fraction.

That was refreshingly honest.

In families like theirs, young women were not supposed to read vernacular novels.

But he personally felt that when one's mind was tired, reading something like that to change one's thinking was perfectly all right.

The author writes freely, the reader reads freely.

"My outer study has some — go look whenever you're at leisure and feeling bored."

"You also read vernacular novels?" Qin Ru-yin stared at him in disbelief, her small mouth slightly open, looking a little silly.

Jiang Jiu-xiao nodded. "I do. Some of them actually have their merits."

He paused, then added: "But read fewer of those written by bitter, failed scholars about beauties who fall for a talented man and offer up both themselves and their fortunes for him..."

Qin Ru-yin had to work very hard not to burst out laughing.

What was this — a worried father lecturing his child?

But he was not wrong.

"Don't worry — even if I read them, I would never..." Qin Ru-yin's words were cut off by a commotion from the little maids outside.

"Third Madam... Third Madam, you cannot just walk into our Fourth Madam's inner chamber uninvited! Our Fourth Master is still inside!"

"Oh? Since when has your Fourth Master gone to the outer study?" Yin shi asked coldly.

"That would be Third Sister-in-law." Qin Ru-yin looked at Jiang Jiu-xiao. "She sounds very fierce — is she coming to pick a fight with me?"

"Not with you. Earlier I told Third Brother that he should take Third Sister-in-law and go to Yanling to serve as the county magistrate..."

Qin Ru-yin's eyes brightened. "Yanling? What a wonderful place! Yanling is one of our Great Ying dynasty's most fertile regions, isn't it?"

The Third Master was a minor seventh-rank official in the capital who hadn't moved an inch in years — he would genuinely be better off going to a local posting and serving properly as a county magistrate for a few years.

Three consecutive years of excellent evaluations, and he could be promoted by at least one and a half ranks.

"You know Yanling?" Jiang Jiu-xiao smiled faintly and nodded. "Yes, that Yanling."

"What a wonderful place! The people are prosperous, commerce is thriving, and it is exactly the sort of place where an official can build an excellent record of achievements."

Qin Ru-yin thought that if her elder brothers had taken the scholarly path, she would have been overjoyed to wake from a dream laughing if one of them could serve as county magistrate in Yanling!

Jiang Jiu-xiao sighed inwardly.

Even Yin-niang, a young girl, understood this logic, and yet his Third Brother was still furious with him.

Not daring to make his own move, he had covertly sent his wife to stir things up.

Never mind that Jiang Jiu-xiao was in the middle of his honeymoon.

"It seems Third Brother and Third Sister-in-law are not pleased."

Qin Ru-yin looked at Jiang Jiu-xiao's furrowed brow. "Fourth Master, this time again it is Third Sister-in-law charging ahead while Third Brother hides behind her... I suppose I'll have to be the one to deal with her."

"What do you suggest?"

Jiang Jiu-xiao's gaze turned ice-cold. "No need to be polite with her."

He then reached up and lightly touched her hair. "We have barely just been married, and already you must face all of this. I am sorry you have been put through this."

Then he reached into his robe and drew out a stack of banknotes, handing them to Qin Ru-yin: "This was originally for your personal spending this month — consider it an early apology. Tomorrow I'll have someone bring down more notes..."

He gave her a personal monthly allowance?

Wonderful! And he knew to spend his own money keeping his wife comfortable.

A model husband!

Qin Ru-yin smiled cheerfully: "Fourth Master, please put it in the drawer of my vanity table for me. I'll go and meet Third Sister-in-law!"

Jiang Jiu-xiao had said not to stand on ceremony — which meant no matter how she handled Yin shi, Jiang Jiu-xiao would stand behind her.

What did she have to worry about?

She had also given advance notice to her mother-in-law Jiang Tai Furen.

If Yin shi dared to come dancing in front of her again, she would not be lenient!

Yin shi, hearing the little maid say Jiang Jiu-xiao was inside, had already stopped dead in her tracks.

How could a sister-in-law barge into a younger brother's and sister-in-law's inner chamber uninvited?

The words she had blurted out left her looking quite uncomfortable.

Zisu lifted the bead curtain for Qin Ru-yin while Banxia supported her arm as she stepped out.

"Third Sister-in-law, what's the matter? You look rather fierce."

Qin Ru-yin came out and asked straightaway.

Then she instructed Zisu: "Third Madam has come as a guest — please escort Third Madam to the flower hall to sit."

Zisu acknowledged and walked to Yin shi's side, curtseying politely: "Third Madam, please follow this servant to the flower hall next door for tea and refreshments."

Yin shi looked at Qin Ru-yin.

She wasn't sure whether Qin Ru-yin was deliberately being proper by sending her to the adjacent flower hall rather than inviting her into the inner chambers — or deliberately keeping her at a distance.

Perhaps both.

She pressed her lips together and said nothing.

With a stiff face, she let Zisu support her arm and went to the adjacent flower hall.

Qin Ru-yin, supported by Banxia's arm, followed in unhurried steps.

After host and guest took their seats, the maids and matrons set out fragrant tea and refreshments.

"Third Sister-in-law looks displeased?" Qin Ru-yin made a gracious gesture of invitation. "No rush — let's talk in a moment. First have a cup of tea to cool your temper."

Yin shi gave her a long, searching look.

Without touching the tea, she asked Qin Ru-yin directly: "Since your Fourth Master has returned from the outer study to the inner quarters, did he say anything to you?"

Qin Ru-yin picked up her own tea cup, and hearing her ask so boldly, smiled.

"Third Sister-in-law, what kind of question is that? Do the private conversations between Fourth Master and me need to be reported to Third Sister-in-law?"

Yin shi's brow creased sharply. "That's not what I meant..."

"Then what did you mean?" Qin Ru-yin set down her cup and looked at her. "I have thought over and over again, and I have not offended Third Sister-in-law in any way."

"What Third Sister-in-law did at Mother's today — I won't bring that up."

"Why has she come to me again so quickly? And judging by Third Sister-in-law's expression, she is not here as a social call, is she?"

Yin shi, seeing Qin Ru-yin's words so razor-sharp — with nothing she could say in response, nothing she could accuse her of — looked even worse.

"Do you not know why I've come? Your Fourth Master wants to drive our Third Branch away!"

Yin shi's aggrievement surged to the surface.

She pulled out her handkerchief and began to blot at tears.

Crying as she dabbed, she recounted to Qin Ru-yin everything Jiang Jiu-xiao had said to her Third Master.

Qin Ru-yin looked at her. "Third Sister-in-law, you and Third Brother really ought not to mistake a kind heart for an ill one! In your honest opinion — is it truly so bad for Third Brother to serve as county magistrate in a fertile region like Yanling?"

"What — so Fourth Sister-in-law also wants to drive..."

"Stop right there. No one wants to drive you out of the Jiang family." Qin Ru-yin raised her hand in a cool, dismissive gesture, cutting Yin shi off.

"As long as the Third Branch commits no great wrongs, as long as you do nothing foolish that damages the family — I believe no one has the right to drive you away..."

Yin shi gave a grudging snort. "At least that sounds a bit more reasonable."

"Oh? My words are reasonable, but Third Sister-in-law's are not particularly so." Qin Ru-yin gave a perfectly unsparing reply.

Yin shi opened her mouth and for a long moment made no sound, her mind failing to keep up.

And she was half-furious besides.

"Third Sister-in-law, setting everything else aside — do you truly not know how many people are scrambling for that county magistrate post in Yanling?"

"My Fourth Master is now the President of the Ministry of Personnel. How many eyes are watching his every move? Do you think it was easy for him to secure that posting for Third Brother?"

"Third Sister-in-law also comes from an official family — you must know that for Fourth Master to seek advantages for his own kin in his position is a great taboo at court... and yet he did it for Third Brother anyway!"

"Does Fourth Master not bear any risk?"

"Furthermore, Fourth Master also told me — Yanling is precisely where Third Sister-in-law's natal family's ancestral home is located! That is yet another advantage."

"At the very least, if Third Brother goes there as county magistrate, your natal family can help shield him from many of the local power brokers..."

"If Fourth Master truly wanted to drive your Third Branch away, why would he go to such lengths to send you to Yanling? He could simply have tossed your Third Branch off to some frigid outpost in the northwest, or somewhere in the south ravaged by miasma — wouldn't that be far more effective?"

"You... you..." The face of Yin shi, still showing traces of beauty, went from green to white.

"Does Fourth Sister-in-law want to say I am vicious?" Qin Ru-yin smiled lightly.

"This only shows how magnanimous Fourth Master is, and how dearly he loves his brothers."

"If it were up to me, with a brother so troublesome and so failing to improve — I'd ship him straight to the wilderness so he could learn what real hardship means!"

"With a brother as generous and forgiving as Fourth Master, Third Brother and Third Sister-in-law ought to count yourselves lucky! What is there to make a fuss about? Does everyone in this household truly have to revolve around your Third Branch?"

Yin shi nearly fainted with rage.

"Third Sister-in-law, please don't faint — we are young people here, none of that sort of thing is done." Qin Ru-yin, seeing her eyes nearly flutter shut, called out sharply: "And don't go blaming me — I'm not afraid even if you do!"

Yin shi forced herself back to full wakefulness.

She had truly just been overwhelmed with a rush of blood to the head.

This wretched girl was not only brazen — her tongue was wickedly fast.

She truly said whatever she pleased!

She gave not a shred of face!

"All right, all right. Third Sister-in-law, no need to be angry — I was simply laying out the facts, with no ill intent."

"If Third Brother truly does not want to go and work in a local posting, then he should go find Fourth Master himself and say so plainly. Why hide behind Third Sister-in-law and expect her to fight every battle for him?"

"And Third Sister-in-law — I must also offer you some criticism! Have you never considered that precisely because you always charge out in front of Third Brother, he has lost the heart to face things on his own?"

Yin shi froze.

She stared at Qin Ru-yin wide-eyed. This was something no one had ever said to her before.

No one had ever told her...

"But..." she wet her lips, beginning to stammer. "But... if we went to Yanling, what would become of our children? Yanling may be fertile and rich, but it is still not the capital."

"Did I not say? Whether Third Brother goes to Yanling as county magistrate is not the real point — the real point is what he actually wants."

"And equally important — what do you, Third Sister-in-law, actually want?"

"Third Brother is a man — I cannot speak for him."

"But Third Sister-in-law — do you wish to step outside and be your own mistress, or do you wish to spend the rest of your life shut away in the back quarters of this great Jiang household?"

Qin Ru-yin asked Yin shi a question that cut straight to the bone.

"Father has his own wealth, Mother has hers, brothers and sisters have theirs... none of it compares to having your own." Qin Ru-yin reflected aloud, then lifted her tea and took a sip.

She had said what needed to be said, delivered the lecture that needed to be delivered — she had vented her feelings enough.

Yin shi was, after all, her sister-in-law.

The Third Master was Jiang Jiu-xiao's twin elder brother.

This was an unchangeable fact.

And if she and Jiang Jiu-xiao had children someday, that would make the Third Master and Third Madam those children's own Third Uncle and Third Aunt.

She still preferred everyone to get along in harmony.

Yin shi's temperament was hasty and competitive, but as Jiang Tai Furen had said — she had never done genuine harm.

Compared to the Second Madam Chen shi, her methods were far cleaner.

"My head is a mess — I don't know how to answer you..." Yin shi tried to compose herself, but her mind wouldn't cooperate.

Qin Ru-yin, seeing the bewilderment on her face, said: "Then Third Sister-in-law, go home and think it through properly. But don't coddle Third Brother so much."

"If Third Brother resents you for it, just tell Third Brother plainly — and tell him it was I who said it. If he refuses to accept that, let him come find Fourth Master himself."

Qin Ru-yin said her piece and waved Yin shi off. "Third Sister-in-law, please go."

Yin shi didn't even know how she found her way out of Minglian Residence.

When Jiang Tai Furen heard about all of this, she said to Nanny Hua with delight: "Goodness — I had underestimated Yin-niang! She has actually managed to hold that loose-tongued Yin shi in check!"

Nanny Hua marveled too: "Our Fourth Madam is truly remarkable — Third Madam is not someone an ordinary person could handle..."

While Qin Ru-yin was speaking with Yin shi, Jiang Jiu-xiao had come out of the inner chamber and settled onto the daybed by the window of the outer sitting room, reading.

His internal cultivation was deep, and his hearing sharp — he had caught every word of the exchange between Qin Ru-yin and Yin shi.

When Qin Ru-yin returned from the flower hall, he beckoned her over.

Qin Ru-yin walked over and asked: "Was I rude to Third Sister-in-law?"

chapters.title: Rude?
chapters.content:
Jiang Jiu-xiao shook his head.

His gaze was clear and bright, carrying appreciation and encouragement.

"I heard everything Yin-niang said to Third Sister-in-law — Yin-niang did very well." His manner was sincere.

"Only... what I want to say is this: Third Sister-in-law's temperament is stubborn, and however sensible your words were today, she is unlikely to change easily."

"In those first years after she married into the family, Mother also counseled her often — telling her she need not put herself at the forefront of everything on behalf of the Third Son, who is a grown man... To no effect."

"Eventually Mother said it so many times that Yin shi simply began to brush her off. Mother found it pointless — a daughter-in-law is not a daughter; you cannot hit her or scold her — and let her be."

"Therefore, if she comes to bother you again in future, you must be fiercer with her." Jiang Jiu-xiao advised.

Qin Ru-yin pressed her lips together in a smile. "Fourth Master thinks I wasn't fierce enough with Third Sister-in-law today?"

"You were not fierce at all today." Jiang Jiu-xiao shook his head, and said earnestly: "I know you were doing good by her and holding your temper the entire time."

Qin Ru-yin's eyes shone with a warm, bright feeling — the pleasure of being understood.

It was not that she wanted to be the magnanimous one.

It was simply that, as fellow women, she could see that for all Yin shi's outward pushiness and competitiveness, at her core she only wanted to live a peaceful life.

If given the choice, who would willingly become someone others found tiresome?

But she had already done what she could.

Who in this world truly had an easy life?

Was Mother-in-law Jiang Tai Furen's life easy?

Was Elder Sister-in-law Fang shi's life easy?

Was Second Sister-in-law Chen shi's life easy, with four sons?

Was Fifth Sister-in-law Zheng shi's life easy, married for years with only one daughter to show for it?

No one had it easy!

"It's just that with someone like Third Sister-in-law, meeting her kindness with kindness is precisely what makes her bolder..."

Jiang Jiu-xiao paused, and out of concern that his new bride might be bullied by the household's sisters-in-law, he added a few more words.

Qin Ru-yin took them all in.

Then she looked at him with a pretty, playful air. "If I truly do get fierce, Fourth Master, I'm afraid Third Sister-in-law won't be able to bear it. I am capable of saying absolutely anything."

"What if she can't take it and goes back to her own family to cry her grievances — and her family's elders come to find Mother to demand an explanation? Wouldn't that cause trouble for you and Mother?"

Qin Ru-yin looked at her Fourth Master with bright, sparkling eyes.

Jiang Jiu-xiao met that brilliantly luminous gaze and was momentarily caught off guard.

Realizing she was probing him, the corners of his lips lifted.

"Do not be afraid!" He said firmly. "I am here."

"But what if I truly go too far — what if I scold her too harshly?"

Jiang Jiu-xiao replied: "My only worry is that you are not fierce enough and get taken advantage of."

The corner of Qin Ru-yin's mouth curved high.

What more was there to say!

She suddenly lurched forward, launching herself toward Jiang Jiu-xiao.

Jiang Jiu-xiao's eyes went wide. Thinking she was about to fall, he instinctively opened both arms to catch her.

Qin Ru-yin tumbled squarely into his embrace.

Her two soft, tender arms circled his neck, and in a moment Jiang Jiu-xiao had absolutely no way to anticipate, she pressed her soft, rosy lips to his right cheek with a firm, cheerful "smack."

"Fourth Master, you are wonderful! I like you so very much!"

Qin Ru-yin finished and paid no mind to the fact that the person in question was rigid with shock and had been effectively turned to stone. She laughed quietly to herself.

To tell the truth — she had wanted to do this ever since the moment he lifted her red veil.

Not for any other particular reason.

It was just like how, in her previous life, she had been unable to resist the urge to kiss the soft, plump little arm of her best friend's three-month-old baby daughter.

Having ambushed someone, she was naturally a little frightened of what came next.

She had already quickly let go of Jiang Jiu-xiao and was covering a fake yawn with her hand.

She feigned a glance at the light outside and murmured: "Today has truly been exhausting."

Then, with forced composure, she walked over to the bead curtain and called out to Xinyi on the other side: "Xinyi, send a little maid to the main kitchen to check when the evening meal will be ready."

Jiang Jiu-xiao had by now recovered from his shock.

But he still felt a faint, lingering warmth where her lips had touched his right cheek.

He looked at her, his gaze deep and still, his thoughts unreadable.

After the evening meal, Qin Ru-yin took the initiative to say to him: "Fourth Master, if you are still not used to sharing a room with someone, please feel free to do as you wish."

She knew that beyond the inner quarters, he had his own courtyard in the outer compound, and his outer study was spacious too, fitted with a sleeping couch.

Nanny Feng had told her that in the past, when he was particularly busy, he often simply slept in the study.

Hearing her say this, Jiang Jiu-xiao's brow furrowed faintly.

Of course, he did not misconstrue her meaning. He knew she was respecting his choice.

She was not angry, and she was not making a scene.

Just like this — gentle, understanding, considerate.

But why, then, did he not feel entirely pleased?

He did not dwell on it, however, and did not attempt to correct or explain anything.

He gave a calm nod. "As it happens, there are some matters — I'll go to the outer courtyard first."

Qin Ru-yin smiled and nodded: "Of course, Fourth Master, as you wish."

After Jiang Jiu-xiao left Minglian Residence, Xinyi, who was tending to Qin Ru-yin, wore a look of unconcealed disappointment.

She couldn't help saying to her young mistress: "Young Miss, you and the Fourth Master are newlyweds — how could you send the young master away like that?"

Qin Ru-yin gave her senior maid a mischievous smile. "You wouldn't understand."

This was called: play hard to get.

Xinyi didn't understand, and there was nothing she could do about her young mistress.

Of course she also knew that her young mistress never acted without purpose — the young mistress was young in years but had plenty of ideas of her own.

She would just have to wait a little longer then.

For now, the important thing was to attend to the young mistress properly and make her comfortable.

Xinyi led the little maids and quickly, with nimble hands, began helping Qin Ru-yin remove her makeup, wash, and prepare for bed.

When Qin Ru-yin was getting into bed ready to sleep, there was another commotion outside.

Banxia was on night duty tonight.

Hearing Qin Ru-yin call for her, she quickly lifted the bead curtain and came in.

She curtseyed, her face breaking into a wide smile as she reported: "Young Miss, it's the Fourth Master's outer courtyard matrons — they're moving the Fourth Master's clothes trunks and book chests over here..."

Jiang Jiu-xiao was moving his everyday belongings to Minglian Residence?

He was planning to live here with her permanently?

Qin Ru-yin was suddenly wide awake.

Banxia saw another little maid coming to report and hurried back out.

After listening to the little maid's report, she slipped back through the bead curtain with delight, lowering her voice to tell her young mistress: "Young Miss — the Fourth Master is on his way too. He's almost at the moon gate to our courtyard..."

Qin Ru-yin gave her a smiling, mock-reproachful glance. "Why are you even more excited than I am?"

"Of course this servant is happy for Young Miss!" Banxia's eyebrows practically jumped with joy.

"Even if Young Miss and the Fourth Master haven't yet consummated the marriage — the Fourth Master treating Young Miss this well will make everyone in all those other Jiang courtyards who've been wagging their tongues positively sick with envy..."

Qin Ru-yin knew that Banxia had been outside and had heard some unpleasant gossip. There was a suppressed frustration she had been carrying.

Even though she had prepared her closest attendants mentally before they came to the Jiang household, once things played out like this, these senior maids were still outraged on her behalf.

"You lot... I've told you already — don't mind what other people gossip about. Rest assured, your young mistress will not suffer in this Jiang household."

Qin Ru-yin looked at Banxia seriously. "And I will not let any of you who came with me suffer either."

Banxia's eyes reddened at once. "As long as Young Miss doesn't suffer, that is all we servants could wish for — we are perfectly all right!"

Qin Ru-yin shook her head. "That won't do. You are all my people. If you suffer, it is as if I suffer. If someone gives you a hard time, it is as if they've given me a hard time..."

The sound of the bead curtain stirring interrupted the exchange between mistress and maid.

Nanny Feng herself had come.

"Young Miss, the Fourth Master's outer courtyard people have brought the Fourth Master's everyday things here to our courtyard — do you wish to have them arranged and put away?"

Qin Ru-yin was about to ask Banxia to bring her clothes over when Jiang Jiu-xiao's voice carried in.

"Don't get up. Lie still and rest. My things can sit in the flower hall for now — have someone arrange them properly tomorrow."

He entered in long strides, reached out, and pressed down on Qin Ru-yin, who had half-risen.

Qin Ru-yin heard this and laughed.

She said to Nanny Feng with a smile: "As Fourth Master says — arrange everything tomorrow."

Then she asked Jiang Jiu-xiao: "Fourth Master, shall I have someone attend you for your washing up?"

He disliked young maids attending him personally. Qin Ru-yin had specially arranged two older, capable, discreet matrons to be on hand in her courtyard.

If Jiang Jiu-xiao needed them, they would attend to him.

Jiang Jiu-xiao heard this and shook his head.

"I have already washed up in the outer courtyard." One glance, and Nanny Feng was smilingly steering Banxia out with her.

"I thought you had matters to attend to, and would rest in the outer courtyard tonight." Qin Ru-yin sat up again and moved to help him unfold the bedding he would use.

"Don't move — lie down properly. I'll manage it myself." Jiang Jiu-xiao said again.

Qin Ru-yin gave a mock-aggrieved look. "If Yin-niang doesn't even help Fourth Master spread his bedding, and Mother finds out when I go home to visit three days from now, she'll certainly scold me."

"She won't." Jiang Jiu-xiao looked at her steadily. "I will explain it to your mother."

Seeing him so naturally refer to her own mother as "Mother" along with her, the warmth in Qin Ru-yin's eyes deepened a little.

When the two of them lay down, Qin Ru-yin had only just closed her eyes when Jiang Jiu-xiao's large hand reached over and drew her to him — bedding and all.

"Hmm?" Qin Ru-yin gave a startled little sound. "Fourth Master?"

"Let us share a quilt. You are young — you tend to kick off the covers at night."

"Don't catch cold. After tomorrow, there is the three-day return visit to your parents... sleep now."

Having said that, he peeled away the bedding wrapped around her and tucked the young girl in her lotus-pink inner garment against him.

Qin Ru-yin lay in his broad, warm embrace and didn't dare move.

"Fourth Master, my sleeping posture is very proper... I really don't kick off the covers." Qin Ru-yin said, wondering if in this life her healthier body really did kick off the covers at night.

She suddenly felt a little less sure of herself.

"Mm." Jiang Jiu-xiao gave a vague acknowledgment.

"I... did I kick you last night?" Qin Ru-yin asked, a little embarrassed.

"No." Jiang Jiu-xiao shook his head.

"Sleep," he said again.

"Oh... all right." Qin Ru-yin closed her eyes, but could not stop the corner of her mouth from curling upward.

She thought she understood now.

Her sleeping posture was not actually poor.

It was more likely that he simply liked holding her while he slept.

According to Nanny Feng, his sleep quality had always been very poor in the past.

But seeing him so bright and sharp today, it seemed last night sleeping beside her had given him a very good night's rest.

That was a good sign...

After Qin Ru-yin's breathing settled into the soft, even rhythm of sleep, Jiang Jiu-xiao's tightly closed eyes suddenly opened.

He lowered his gaze and looked at the young girl sleeping peacefully in his arms, and also curved his lips in a smile.

Very good.

Tonight, he would sleep well again.

The next morning.

Qin Ru-yin woke late again.

Not quite as late as the sun standing three poles high, but past the hour when the Jiang household's masters ordinarily had their morning meal.

"Young Miss, the Fourth Master hasn't eaten yet — he's been waiting for you to wake up and says he wants to eat together with you." Ju-hong whispered to Qin Ru-yin as she helped her dress and arrange her hair.

"That won't do — from now on, if I sleep late, you must all encourage Fourth Master to go ahead and eat first. His digestion is poor, and eating at regular times is very important for him..."

"Young Miss, we didn't dare say anything... Nanny Feng even asked the Fourth Master to go ahead and eat, but even Nanny Feng couldn't persuade him..."

Qin Ru-yin found that odd and asked: "Why didn't you dare? Fourth Master may not like you coming close, but he would never be harsh with you."

Honestly speaking, Jiang Jiu-xiao's rank and standing were considerable, yet he was not one to order his servants about imperiously.

He simply spoke very little, which gave all the servants the impression that he was frightening.

In truth, he was not frightening in the least.

"Young Miss, please forgive us! The Fourth Master, he..."

"What is it with the Fourth Master?"

chapters.title: Give Him a Kiss
chapters.content:
"The Fourth Master is perfectly wonderful, isn't he?"

After she came to the Jiang household, Qin Ru-yin came to understand what it truly meant when people said rumors could kill, and how easy it was to slander a person but how hard to clear their name.

What manner of man did the gossip outside make Jiang Jiu-xiao out to be?

Every last one of those young lords and princes out there was not fit to even hold his shoes!

"Aiyo, Young Miss — the Fourth Master is wonderful, yes — wonderful to you..."

"As for us servants below, except for the older matrons and nannies, the Fourth Master has never once had a kind expression for us... How could we not be afraid?"

Ju-hong said this, but her face was wreathed in a deep, genuine smile.

She and her fellow maids who had come with their young mistress to the Jiang household had already spoken privately among themselves about their plans for the future.

The young mistress had told them early on as well.

When they were of age, she would find each of them a good match and let them go out and marry as proper wives.

None of them would stoop to be like those shameless, scheming creatures who set their sights on the master of the house...

The young mistress had also said that even after they had all married out, if they still wished to come back and serve her, they could return as household managers.

The young mistress was the wife of the President of the Ministry of Personnel! To serve as her household manager — what standing that would carry!

And those who had always been loyal to their young mistress, who had served her wholeheartedly — when they married out, they would be prized and cherished by their in-laws.

Whoever was foolish enough to want to be a concubine or a kept woman in the household was simply brainless.

With such a wonderful mistress, one who planned and provided for them all like this — if they still harbored such base thoughts, they would deserve to be struck by lightning!

......

In the Great Ying dynasty, a new bride was expected to wear at minimum a red upper garment for the first three days of marriage.

Qin Ru-yin wore today a long, fitted jacket of kesi silk brocade in a peonies-and-scrolling-vines pattern.

Paired below with a gold-speckled horse-face skirt in a shade of moonlit lotus.

Ju-hong coiffed her hair into a dangling tilt-bun and adorned it with a matched set of amethyst jewelry.

Dignified, yet warm and graceful.

When Jiang Jiu-xiao saw her freshly dressed, the corner of his mouth lifted.

No matter how she was dressed, this young girl always looked lovely.

After greeting him, Qin Ru-yin spoke to him first: "Fourth Master, from now on if you wake early, please go ahead and eat your morning meal without waiting for Yin-niang."

"It doesn't matter..." Jiang Jiu-xiao rose and moved a chair aside so she could sit. "I'm not hungry."

Qin Ru-yin's small face turned serious, and she tilted her head to look up at him: "Yin-niang will not allow you to say 'it doesn't matter'! If you wake early and don't feel hungry, you may have simply gone past the point of hunger."

Jiang Jiu-xiao blinked.

Qin Ru-yin continued to regard him with solemnity.

"Besides, your digestion is already weak. The most important thing is to nourish your stomach properly and eat at regular hours..."

This was the first time Jiang Jiu-xiao had seen her look so serious.

Knowing she meant it for his own good, a warmth rose in his heart.

On instinct he nodded in assent: "All right."

Nanny Feng, attending nearby, was quietly astonished.

In the past, even when the Tai Furen had both coaxed and scolded, the young master either said "it doesn't matter" or simply said nothing at all.

But with the young miss, the young master had simply and obediently agreed.

Nanny Feng then felt nothing but joy.

Whatever the young master had agreed to, he had never failed to follow through!

It was still the young miss's words that carried weight!

Who said the young master didn't like women? Clearly he liked the young miss very much!

Would he listen to her if he didn't?

After the young couple finished their morning meal and rinsed their mouths, they went to Rong'an Hall to pay their respects to Jiang Tai Furen.

Jiang Tai Furen had also woken early.

Word had already reached her that last night the Fourth Son had sent the daily-use belongings from his outer courtyard — even the entire trunk of his most beloved books — to Minglian Residence.

Having a wife truly made all the difference!

The old lady was so pleased she ate an extra bowl of green-stem rice porridge at breakfast.

All the longtime attendants were happy for her.

At this hour, Jiang First Madam Fang shi — having already dealt with the morning's household affairs — was already present in the Tai Furen's quarters.

The Jiang Second Madam Chen shi and the Fifth Madam Zheng shi were also already seated.

When Jiang Jiu-xiao arrived with Qin Ru-yin, only the Third Madam Yin shi had yet to arrive.

That was rather unusual.

Ordinarily, Yin shi was never the last to arrive for morning greetings to Jiang Tai Furen.

"All of you daughters-in-law have your own affairs to manage — there is truly no need for you to come and pay your respects every single day."

Jiang Tai Furen's old eyes swept in turn across Fang shi, Chen shi, and Zheng shi as she spoke.

Fang shi smiled pleasantly and said: "Mother, isn't it because Fourth Sister-in-law has just entered the household? It's her new bride period. She comes to keep Mother company every morning, and we sisters-in-law naturally want to come and accompany her too."

Chen shi also smiled and said: "That's right, Mother — a new bride is still shy. She needs all of us who came in earlier to be here with her, or it would feel awkward..."

Zheng shi just smiled and said nothing.

Jiang Tai Furen heard this and smiled, giving them all a word of praise.

She then turned to Fang shi: "First daughter-in-law, Yin-niang is returning to her parents' home tomorrow for the three-day visit. Has the return-visit gift been prepared properly?"

Fang shi replied immediately: "Mother, please be at ease — daughter-in-law has prepared Fourth Sister-in-law's return-visit gift perfectly! I even had a reliable person check it over three times. Not a single problem."

"Good!" Jiang Tai Furen nodded. "Thank you for the trouble."

Fang shi immediately rose and curtseyed: "Mother, you will shame daughter-in-law with such words — this is all daughter-in-law's rightful duty."

Chen shi glanced at Zheng shi with a smile, but finding Zheng shi in a daze again, felt it was dull and quickly looked away.

She let her gaze drift quietly over Qin Ru-yin.

Jiang Jiu-xiao had originally intended to pay his respects to his mother and then leave — after all, the room was full of women.

But then the Jiang Second Madam Chen shi suddenly spoke up: "Tomorrow is the day of Fourth Sister-in-law's return visit — will Fourth Brother be accompanying Fourth Sister-in-law home as well?"

Jiang Tai Furen's brow tightened.

Fang shi also looked at Chen shi in surprise.

This Second Sister-in-law of hers was always measured and circumspect — she never said what shouldn't be said, never asked what shouldn't be asked.

What had come over her today?

Ahh.

No wonder.

The Third Madam wasn't here.

Otherwise, it would have been the Third Madam who asked this.

"What a question, Second daughter-in-law! Of course the Fourth Son is accompanying Yin-niang on the return visit tomorrow!"

Jiang Tai Furen was terrified her Fourth Son might not accompany Qin Ru-yin, and immediately settled the matter.

She had been too caught up in her joy and had forgotten to ask the Fourth Son about this in advance.

People always said a mother knows her son best.

She was probably the person in the world who understood her Fourth Son best.

And even she couldn't always figure him out.

Chen shi had not missed the flicker of alarm in Jiang Tai Furen's old eyes. A cold light passed through her own.

The Old Madam's warmth toward the Fourth Son's new bride was genuine — not an act.

Seeing Jiang Tai Furen's sharp, warning gaze turn on her, Chen shi felt a stab of inner resentment.

But she still feigned obliviousness to Jiang Tai Furen's look and lowered her eyes, nodding: "How good then that Fourth Brother will accompany Fourth Sister-in-law on the return visit!"

"I meant nothing else by asking." Then she turned a smiling look on Qin Ru-yin: "Fourth Sister-in-law's family all dote on her — if Fourth Brother didn't accompany her tomorrow, her family might hold it against Fourth Brother."

Qin Ru-yin did not look at Chen shi. She only looked at Jiang Jiu-xiao: "If Fourth Master truly has urgent business to attend to, there's nothing to be done about it."

"My family are all sensible people — they wouldn't blame Fourth Master. Only... it would make Yin-niang's face look a little poor."

Saying it this way, she was already certain Jiang Jiu-xiao would accompany her.

Jiang Jiu-xiao said firmly: "I will naturally accompany you."

Jiang Tai Furen let out a quiet breath of relief, her old face creasing into smiles.

Fang shi also smiled at Jiang Tai Furen: "Mother, you may put your mind at ease now!"

"Indeed, now I can put my mind at ease!" Jiang Tai Furen smiled and nodded.

She then urged Jiang Jiu-xiao: "Fourth Son, go to the outer study and attend to whatever official documents from the office have been sent over. Come here to Mother's for the noon meal."

Then she smiled and beckoned Qin Ru-yin to sit beside her, taking her hand and saying to him: "Mother is keeping Yin-niang here to chat with her again today."

Jiang Jiu-xiao gave his acknowledgment.

He then turned and bowed to Jiang First Madam Fang shi and Jiang Second Madam Chen shi.

Zheng shi rose and curtseyed to him.

Jiang Jiu-xiao nodded in return.

Watching Jiang Jiu-xiao go out the door, Jiang Tai Furen cheerfully asked Qin Ru-yin whether she had slept well the night before and whether her morning meal had been satisfying.

Qin Ru-yin answered each question.

Hearing her answers, the warmth in Jiang Tai Furen's old eyes deepened.

"You are sleeping soundly and eating well here in our household — that puts Mother's heart at ease!"

Fang shi smiled along.

Chen shi thought privately: they were husband and wife sleeping under the same quilt in chaste innocence — what was there to be pleased about?

Zheng shi sat staring at the tight clasp of Jiang Tai Furen's hands around Qin Ru-yin's, her thoughts drifting somewhere far away.

Jiang Tai Furen was talking happily with Qin Ru-yin, forgetting all three other daughters-in-law were even there.

Then the call of a matron outside announced the arrival of the Third Madam Yin shi to pay her respects.

"Greetings to Mother. I hope Mother is well." Yin shi curtseyed, looking somewhat listless.

Jiang Tai Furen looked at her, startled by the dark circles beneath her eyes that even powder could not conceal. "Third daughter-in-law, what has happened to you? Why are your eyes so dark?"

chapters.title: The Fourth Master Obediently Agrees
chapters.content:
Seeing her other sisters-in-law all looking over, Yin shi felt embarrassed.

She could only make an excuse: "In reply to Mother — daughter-in-law got up to use the bathroom several times last night and didn't sleep well, and it has left her looking like this."

It was true that Yin shi had not slept well last night.

The business of getting up repeatedly to use the bathroom was a complete fiction.

Jiang Tai Furen thought briefly and understood.

She couldn't be bothered to fuss over her and said carelessly: "You must take care of your health. Go ahead and sit down."

"Yes." Yin shi curtseyed in thanks and sat in her usual seat.

Chen shi beside her quietly asked: "You can get dark circles like this just from getting up too many times?"

Yin shi was a little impatient.

She only said: "Second Sister-in-law, don't ask right now. Give me a few days and I'll tell you in full."

Chen shi lowered her gaze and said no more.

Fang shi glanced over at Yin shi again.

She was usually on the closest terms with Chen shi and had never turned such an impatient face toward her.

Since Jiang Tai Furen was keeping the newlywed couple for the noon meal, Fang shi and the others could not linger long. After exchanging pleasantries for a while, they rose and took their leave.

Jiang Tai Furen glanced at Yin shi and kept her behind.

"First daughter-in-law and the rest of you — you've been here a good while. All of you go back to your own business. Third daughter-in-law came a little later, so she can stay and keep me company a moment longer..."

Yin shi was startled and hurriedly tried to beg off: "Mother, daughter-in-law also has some things still unfinished in her own courtyard — might she also go first?"

Jiang Tai Furen glanced at her. "Today you don't need to rush — stay."

Yin shi dared say nothing more and curtseyed in acquiescence.

"Well then — tell me. What has really happened? Did you and the Third Son have a quarrel?" Jiang Tai Furen's old eyes bore steadily into Yin shi.

Yin shi's face froze in its awkward attempt at a smile.

Really now.

How could the Old Madam ask her this sort of thing right in front of the Fourth daughter-in-law?

Jiang Tai Furen was not acting without purpose.

After the Third Madam had gone to Minglian Residence the previous day and tried to get the upper hand over the Fourth daughter-in-law — only to be gotten the upper hand over instead — she had returned to her own courtyard and had a fierce quarrel with the Third Son.

"This is not a bad thing. You and the Third Son should have had a proper quarrel long ago." Jiang Tai Furen looked at Yin shi, shaking her head.

"The Third Son's tendency to shrink from anything difficult... how you have endured it all this time."

Yin shi went rigid.

She stared at Jiang Tai Furen in shock.

Was this woman truly being a mother?

Was she not grateful that this daughter-in-law had treated her son so well?

"Mother knows your heart. All these years you have been blameless in your devotion to the Third Son. Mother is grateful to you..."

"But think for yourself — since you have always charged ahead and handled everything in his place, has the Third Son made any improvement whatsoever?"

In the past, Jiang Tai Furen would never have spoken to a daughter-in-law like this.

After all, she was a mother — naturally she was more protective of her own flesh and blood.

She had thought that the Third Madam's devotion to the Third Son was his good fortune, and had not wanted to disturb that.

But the newly arrived Fourth daughter-in-law's way of speaking and conducting herself had made her understand something.

When an abscess has formed, you must be brave enough to lance it, press out the poison from within, and then apply medicine — and most of the time it will heal.

But if you are too afraid of the pain and only apply ointment to the surface of the abscess, you will never solve the problem at the root.

"Mother... you..." Yin shi's lips trembled with aggrievement. "Mother, is it that daughter-in-law wanted to do this? Wasn't it because Mother showed such favoritism?"

Qin Ru-yin finally glanced at this third sister-in-law.

In front of someone as upright as Jiang Tai Furen, speaking one's true feelings honestly was the only real way to resolve things.

All the fighting and grabbing Yin shi had been doing previously was precisely the wrong approach.

Though — in a household where the influential elder was the soft-hearted, easily swayed kind, fighting and grabbing would have had some use.

But then again, soft-hearted people who were easily swayed rarely built great things either.

If her mother-in-law had been that kind of elder, the Jiang household might not be what it was today.

On this side, Jiang Tai Furen drew a slow, deep breath — but did not grow angry.

She looked at Yin shi calmly and said in a gentle voice: "Then tell me — in what ways has Mother been unfair? Today I give you full leave to say everything on your mind."

Qin Ru-yin refilled Jiang Tai Furen's cup herself.

Then she refilled Yin shi's cup.

She then sat quietly to the side without a sound.

Yin shi glanced at Qin Ru-yin.

Qin Ru-yin said: "Third Sister-in-law, why look at me? You said Mother shows favoritism — and it's obvious to whom, isn't it? It can only be Fourth Master."

Hearing Qin Ru-yin say it so directly, Yin shi's face flushed.

Yet she stubbornly held her head up: "It isn't only Fourth Master."

"All right, then let me step out for a moment." Qin Ru-yin started to rise without any particular feeling about it.

But Jiang Tai Furen's hand pressed her down. "Yin-niang, sit down. There is no need to step out."

Then she said to Yin shi, who was still wearing a defiant look: "Since Yin-niang joined this family you have harbored grievances — you have always been looking for something to pick at..."

"Then let us lay it all out clearly, face to face — that is far better than having you two as sisters-in-law harbor bad feelings toward one another later."

Seeing Jiang Tai Furen speak this way, Yin shi had no choice.

She gritted her teeth and began to pour out her list of Jiang Tai Furen's alleged acts of favoritism.

"Let daughter-in-law not speak of First Brother and First Sister-in-law's side — Mother, your regard for First Sister-in-law, a second wife who came later, has always been so high..."

"As for Second Brother and Second Sister-in-law — in your eyes they are the great contributors to the Jiang family, for having given you four grandsons."

"As for Fourth Brother and Fourth Sister-in-law — there is no need to say anything. Everyone with eyes can see how partial you are to them!"

"And as for the Fifth Son — he is your youngest. You favor him in all things! When he went back on a betrothal, you had the Fourth Son go and make amends for his mess, and he still ended up marrying the woman he wanted."

Yin shi finished and dabbed at her genuinely bitter, aggrieved eyes.

"Only our Third Master — neither high nor low, wanted by no one, loved by no one. Even daughter-in-law and our boy and girl have no standing in your eyes!"

"And to say the Third Master and the Fourth Son are even twins — what is that worth? You treat Fourth Son so well and turn such a blind eye to our Third Master!"

"And you say you are not partial?"

Jiang Tai Furen listened to everything Yin shi said, then looked at her with a gaze of genuine compassion.

"So. All these years, this is how you have thought of me."

"And the Third Son thinks of me this way too?"

Yin shi stiffened her neck and said nothing.

Her expression already said everything.

"My child!" Jiang Tai Furen shook her head and sighed. "You have got yourselves locked inside a blind alley."

"The First Son and his wife, as the eldest branch, follow the customs of our Great Ying dynasty — as long as they have committed no great wrong, the Jiang family will pass to the eldest branch."

"After I am gone, the brothers may each set up their own separate households if they wish. It is simply the custom to keep the family together while the parents are living."

"In every great family, the eldest son and grandson are always given special regard."

"Mother hopes that after I am gone, the First Son and his wife will look after the rest of you younger ones — that is my own selfishness."

"The Second Son and Second daughter-in-law have many children, and naturally Mother asks after them more. But I have not given the Second Branch anything extra."
