"Even the New Year's red envelopes are the same for all grandchildren. And yet the First and Second Branches have more children than your Third Branch and the Fifth Son — that is simply a fact."

"And do I not give the Third Branch and the Fifth Son extra in return?"

"Truth be told — the Fourth Son and Yin-niang have only just married, and Yin-niang is still young. Mother also cannot bear the thought of her suffering the trials of childbirth so young."

"The Fourth Son, with his temperament, will also follow their natural course in the matter of children. When it comes to descendants — I am at peace, leaving it to fate."

"Think on it — does this not mean the Fourth Son actually has it the worst of all?"

"The Fifth Son is someone whom I, as his mother, have failed. All his elder brothers and sisters were personally raised by me when they were small."

"Only after he was born, his father fell gravely ill, and I was so occupied with nursing his father that I left him entirely to his wet nurses. So he and I are the least close."

"I naturally lean a little more toward him as a result — that, I admit!"

"But child — put yourself in my position for a moment..."

"If a son or daughter of yours were raised by a wet nurse and grew up with little closeness to you as a mother, would you not try in every possible way to make it up to them and draw them close?"

"And as things now stand — the First Son does not have the ability to carry the Jiang family forward on his own. That burden has fallen on the Fourth Son's shoulders instead."

"You and the Third Son both say I favor the Fourth Son. But think — among all these brothers, who could take the Fourth Son's place?"

"If any of them could take his place, Mother would favor that one just the same. What can I do — every child I have raised must rely on him!"

"What can I do when the entire great Jiang household must rely on him?"

"When it comes down to it — favoring the Fourth Son is favoring all the brothers whose prospects fall short of his!"

Yin shi stared wide-eyed.

In her heart she did not accept Jiang Tai Furen's reasoning.

She felt it was a sophistry.

Yet she could not find a word to refute it.

"Think it over carefully." Jiang Tai Furen looked at Yin shi with warmth. "And tell the Third Son what I have said. Let him think it over too."

Having said that, Jiang Tai Furen waved her hand at Yin shi. "You may go now."

"Fourth Master may not even want Mother's favoritism — if Third Brother could take Fourth Master's place, I believe Fourth Master would be genuinely relieved."

Qin Ru-yin rose and looked at Yin shi with calm, steady eyes.

Yin shi did not dare meet Qin Ru-yin's gaze.

Ever since the day Qin Ru-yin had spoken those words to her, she had not been able to look her in the eye.

Now she was even less able to.

This time, Jiang Tai Furen had Nanny Hua personally escort Yin shi out.

Yin shi's retreat was very nearly a rout.

After Jiang Tai Furen heard Qin Ru-yin's few words to Yin shi, a sadness rose in her heart.

Her Fourth Son!

All these years he had suffered!

Yet even she, his own mother, had expected more from him and depended on him more than she had worried over him!

It was Yin-niang...

She, his mother, did not worry over him as well as this new bride who had just married in!

Jiang Tai Furen's eyes reddened, and she began to speak to Qin Ru-yin of all the hardships Jiang Jiu-xiao had carried over the years.

She said she had let him down as a mother...

Qin Ru-yin squeezed Jiang Tai Furen's hand gently and shook her head: "You need not think of it that way."

"I believe Fourth Master must feel that with great ability comes great responsibility..."

"After all, the Jiang family is not a household of ordinary common people — it is such a great clan! Someone always has to stand up and carry it."

"Good child! The way you speak always brings such comfort..." Jiang Tai Furen said warmly. "No wonder the Fourth Son likes you!"

"Ah?" Qin Ru-yin blinked in surprise. "Fourth Master likes me? I didn't notice."

"Foolish child!" Jiang Tai Furen laughed.

But she said nothing more.

Some things were better left at a light touch. Saying too much would only do harm.

Qin Ru-yin did not take it to heart.

She thought — with a personality like Jiang Jiu-xiao's, how could he fall for a woman so quickly?

Even his first wife, who had lived in the Jiang household for four years, had never entered his heart — had she not?

Nanny Hua returned after seeing Yin shi out.

Jiang Tai Furen asked: "How was Third daughter-in-law? Was she all right?"

"In reply to the Tai Furen — Third Madam appeared to have worked something out. Her spirit and bearing were quite different from before."

"You're flattering me again." Jiang Tai Furen gave Nanny Hua a reproachful look. "Can a person's nature change that quickly?"

Then she said to Qin Ru-yin: "Your Third Sister-in-law has always been this pushy and competitive — she was like this even growing up in her maiden home. It was shaped over a lifetime. Changing it will be very difficult."

Qin Ru-yin smiled and offered comfort.

"Mother — not necessarily. Sometimes a person changes when a single remark strikes them just right, or when a single event shifts their heart. It can happen just like that."

The mistress and daughter-in-law were talking happily when Jiang Jiu-xiao lifted the bead curtain and came in without waiting for a maid to announce him.

He entered and immediately bowed to Jiang Tai Furen: "Mother, your son cannot stay for the noon meal today..."

He had not even finished the sentence when Jiang Tai Furen grew tense. "Fourth Son — has something happened?"

chapters.title: No Wonder the Fourth Son Likes You!
chapters.content:
A son holding high office was a point of pride.

Yet the slightest stir, the smallest shift in the wind, was enough to make an old mother's heart clench with fear.

"Someone from the Eastern Palace has come to the household... Your son must go to the palace immediately."

"What great matter is this? You are still only on your second day as a newlywed..." Jiang Tai Furen grew anxious.

Jiang Jiu-xiao, seeing how worried his old mother was, said gently to reassure her: "Mother, please be at ease — your son will go and come back quickly. It is nothing serious."

He then looked at Qin Ru-yin: "Yin-niang, stay here and keep Mother company. There is no need to worry either."

Qin Ru-yin agreed.

She thought to herself: The love parents have for a child is not something that goes away simply because someone says not to worry.

But what she said aloud was: "Fourth Master, go to the palace without concern. Mother has me here with her. Only... take care of yourself at every step!"

She paused, then added: "Whatever hour, whatever place — please remember always that Mother and I are here at home waiting for you!"

Jiang Jiu-xiao looked at her for a long moment, then nodded.

A feeling he had never experienced before rose in his heart.

So... this was what it meant to have a wife?

Watching Jiang Jiu-xiao's departing figure, the worry in Jiang Tai Furen's eyes deepened.

Qin Ru-yin offered her reassurance once more.

Jiang Tai Furen shook her head. "Do you see? Your Third Brother and Third Sister-in-law say I am partial to the Fourth Son."

"But the higher the Fourth Son climbs, the more my heart trembles for him... And truth be told, every one of his brothers owes something to the Fourth Son!"

"If not for the Fourth Son bearing the burden ahead of them, how could they live such a comfortable, wealthy life?"

Qin Ru-yin thought: having a mother-in-law who understands reason is a genuine blessing — it made all of Jiang Jiu-xiao's efforts for this family worthwhile.

"Very well — let us not speak of those things anymore. I don't want to frighten Yin-niang." After catching a signal from Nanny Hua, Jiang Tai Furen understood, and immediately cut the subject short.

Then she turned to the matter of Qin Ru-yin's return visit the following day.

"Tomorrow when you return home, Mother has had your Elder Sister-in-law prepare the public household's return-visit gifts. But Mother also has a private gift of her own — something to give your mother..."

Qin Ru-yin smiled and said: "You needn't be so formal — whatever Elder Sister-in-law has prepared for my return visit will certainly send me home in grand style!"

"The public household's gifts are the public household's. Mother's is Mother's own heartfelt gesture." Jiang Tai Furen patted the back of Qin Ru-yin's hand lightly. "I am simply letting you know in advance — you are not to refuse."

The Second Branch's Feiluan Courtyard.

It was now the noon meal hour.

Feiluan Courtyard, because the Second Master was joining Chen shi for the noon meal, had fetched the food from the main kitchen earlier than usual.

The Second Master, for his part, made no pretense of the custom of not speaking at the table.

He chatted with Chen shi while they ate.

"I've been hearing the servants gossip — they say Mother is very fond of the Fourth Son's new bride?"

Chen shi served him his food and smiled in reply: "My Second Master — is this not perfectly obvious? Do you need to hear it from the servants?"

The Second Master put on a proper face and said: "You know perfectly well — your Second Master has never cared to involve himself in these inner-quarter matters."

Chen shi sighed inwardly.

She thought: Second Master, you may not care for inner-quarter matters, but it is your poor wife who suffers for it!

Truth be told, the Second Master's prospects, among the Jiang brothers, were the weakest.

Even the youngest, the Fifth Son — though no scholar — had taken the military path. He now held a sixth-rank military post, serving in the Imperial Guard Bureau.

That was one rank higher than the Third Son, who had passed the imperial examinations and earned a Second Division jinshi.

The First Son, though only a Third Division graduate, now held a senior-fourth-rank post with actual authority.

Among the Jiang brothers, only the Fourth Son could surpass him.

Only her Second Master: neither successful in letters nor in martial affairs.

It was still the Fourth Son who had pulled strings so he could serve as a private secretary to the current Prefect of the Capital, Lord Li.

He handled legal and tax affairs on the Prefect's behalf.

Other matters were handled by a second private secretary.

A private secretary held no official rank or position.

And yet her Second Master considered himself a man of considerable refinement and pride.

Speaking of refined pride — he was the only one among the Jiang five brothers who had taken concubines...

Thinking of this, dark shadows swept through Chen shi's eyes.

And moreover, among all the sisters-in-law in the household, she was now the only one — besides the newly arrived Fourth Madam — without a formal imperial title.

But the Fourth Madam's second-rank title would likely be conferred within a few days.

That would be one rank higher than even the Old Madam's title.

In those years, the late Master Jiang had risen to the third rank before he passed.

The Old Madam had received her third-rank title by virtue of his position, and so the sons no longer needed to petition for a separate title for her.

At this moment, she would almost have preferred the Old Madam had no title at all...

Then that Qin shi's second-rank title would have had to defer to the Old Madam instead.

Noticing his wife had gone quiet, the Second Master felt a flicker of awkwardness.

"You should also make more effort to go and see Mother — visit her more often, and say more of the kinds of things old people like to hear..."

Chen shi's hand, which had been placing food in his bowl, stilled for a moment.

Then she smiled and replied: "Second Master, it isn't that daughter-in-law doesn't wish to go to Mother's — it's that Mother prefers peace and quiet, and doesn't like her daughters-in-law coming too frequently..."

"Then why does Mother like the Fourth Madam so much? She leaves her to stay for the noon meal every day?" The Second Master frowned.

Chen shi nearly couldn't stop herself from slamming down her chopsticks.

But she held it in.

She smiled: "Fourth Sister-in-law is still a new bride — she's only been married two days! When I was a new bride, aside from the day of my return visit, Mother also kept me for the noon meal for a full six days!"

The Second Master had no memory of this.

He looked at Chen shi with vague bewilderment. "Is that so?"

Chen shi wanted to splash the soup in his face.

Her ability to maintain composure was still commendable.

She nodded with a smile. "Of course!"

Then she said: "This is Mother's established custom — every daughter-in-law when she is a new bride is kept by Mother for a few days over the noon meal."

"I see..."

"Those servants are gossiping — they say the Fourth Son and his new bride haven't yet consummated the marriage. What is the story behind that?" The Second Master asked again.

Chen shi rolled her eyes in silence.

Hadn't he said he didn't care to involve himself in inner-quarter affairs?

So many questions today!

"Fourth Master, about this matter, daughter-in-law also doesn't know the reason..."

"But from what Mother seemed to indicate, it was her own idea — something about Qin shi being too young, and asking them to wait a little longer before consummating."

The Second Master set down his chopsticks.

He looked at Chen shi and shook his head. "Mother was desperate for the Fourth Son to marry — her hair has gone much whiter from the worry. How could she possibly see Qin shi as too young and forbid them from consummating the marriage?"

He paused, then frowned again. "Besides, Qin shi is already sixteen — it's not as if she's a girl who has only just come of age."

"Hmm... I expect the Fourth Son has some real problem of his own, and Mother is deliberately covering it up for him and for Qin shi."

Chen shi frowned and said with some discomfort: "That, daughter-in-law truly does not know."

"You! Learn something from Qin shi! Whatever the case, Mother is willing to cover for Qin shi — which means Qin shi has won Mother's favor. You should find ways to please Mother more, so Mother will give our Second Branch more advantages."

"Mother — that person — when she likes someone she likes them with her whole heart, and when she dislikes someone she dislikes them entirely. Black and white, no middle ground..."

"You must find ways to win more of Mother's favor, and then Mother will give our Second Branch more, won't she?"

Chen shi: ...

Utterly speechless.

Did she even need him to tell her these things?

"You are not the one saying Mother is covering up for the Fourth Son?" She couldn't quite hold herself back.

She was not like the Third Madam Yin shi — completely devoted to her husband as if he were her entire world.

The Third Son at least had his books, and was an official, however modest his post.

What was her own husband?

Besides — she had given birth to four sons. Surely at least one of them would be worth relying on?

She did not need to revolve her whole world around her husband!

Her imperial title could only come from her sons now!

"Mm-hmm..." the Second Master, put on the spot, was displeased.

He gave his wife an annoyed look.

"Your temper — stop being so sharp all the time. Be softer. Mother likes..."

"Second Master! Since you know what Mother likes, you as her son should go and win Mother's affection yourself!"

"Think about it — a mother prefers to have her own son win her affection... or an outsider daughter-in-law?"

The Second Master, stung by the retort, slammed his chopsticks down.

"I say one word, and you throw ten back at me! Where has your gentle and virtuous manner gone — the one you show the world?"

"Yes, daughter-in-law is not gentle or virtuous enough. Second Master, go find your two gentle and virtuous beautiful concubines!"

Chen shi also cast down the chopsticks she had been using to serve him food.

She picked up her own and sat down, then began to eat entirely on her own.

The Second Master stared at her, seething.

"You! Impossible to reason with!"

"Only women and petty people are hard to manage..."

"Yes, yes! Second Master, you have become a sage. If Second Master has finished his meal, please attend to whatever business you have. Daughter-in-law would like to eat now!"

After snapping that reply, Chen shi ignored him entirely.

The Second Master's face had gone green. He flicked his sleeve and turned to leave.

"Second Madam — how could you drive the Second Master away like that? This month the Second Master has only come to your courtyard four times... Alas!"

Chen shi's old wet nurse looked at her with pained concern.

Chen shi gave a cold laugh: "I am past the age of worrying. I've already given him four sons. What do I fear?"

"Am I supposed to rely on that good-for-nothing who can't cut it in either letters or martial arts?"

"I often think — who among us wasn't once young and bright and pure, like Qin shi?"

"But when you marry a selfish man who amounts to nothing — don't you end up worn down into something less than human?"

Chen shi couldn't eat either. She sat there, tears sliding silently down her face.

Then a matron lifted the bead curtain and entered.

"In reply to the Second Madam — the Fourth Madam has come to call on you."

"Qin shi?"

Chen shi immediately took her handkerchief and dried her eyes, composed herself as though nothing had happened, and told her wet nurse: "Nanny, help me touch up my powder."

Once she was presentable, she rose to go and receive Qin Ru-yin.

chapters.title: A Quarrel Between the Second Master and His Wife
chapters.content:
Qin Ru-yin came into Feiluan Courtyard with her senior maid Banxia and a few attendants.

This was the first time she had come to the Second Branch's quarters.

The interior of Feiluan Courtyard was clean and well-arranged.

Though not as lavishly furnished as her own Minglian Residence, it had a quiet and warm atmosphere.

Chen shi welcomed her with a composure that looked as though nothing had happened.

She was smiling as she welcomed Qin Ru-yin inside.

Qin Ru-yin had brought several items of food that her own small kitchen had prepared.

"Second Sister-in-law, I was bored in my courtyard with nothing to do — so I came to impose on you for a while. And I also brought some new recipes I've been trying. If Second Sister-in-law doesn't mind them being humble, please try some."

Chen shi heard the words "my own small kitchen" and felt a sharp prick somewhere inside — but showed nothing.

On the surface she was warm and generous: "Fourth Sister-in-law is too kind! You troubled yourself to bring things to eat — how could I mind? Come, come, sit down."

The two sisters-in-law sat down in the flower hall.

The maids served tea.

"Does Fourth Sister-in-law mind the heat? There's a cool breeze in my garden — shall we go sit in the pavilion?" Chen shi asked.

"Certainly — Second Sister-in-law leads the way." Qin Ru-yin readily agreed.

So Chen shi led Qin Ru-yin out through the verandah and into the garden.

Feiluan Courtyard's garden was smaller than that of Minglian Residence, but the plantings were meticulous and the flowers were in full bloom.

They settled in the gazebo.

A breeze swept through, carrying with it the fragrance of flowers — it was indeed several degrees cooler than indoors.

"Second Sister-in-law's garden is beautifully kept." Qin Ru-yin looked around with genuine appreciation.

Chen shi smiled lightly. "It's nothing much. Not worth comparing with the scenery in Fourth Sister-in-law's Minglian Residence — I've heard the garden there is truly magnificent."

"The garden is nice, but too large." Qin Ru-yin laughed. "I honestly preferred something smaller and more intimate, like Second Sister-in-law's."

Chen shi looked at her.

This Fourth Sister-in-law — sometimes she really didn't know what to make of her.

When she spoke sharply she was startlingly direct. When she spoke warmly she was genuinely warm. And she had clearly come today with every intention of being agreeable.

Was she here to win her over?

Or simply passing the time?

"Fourth Sister-in-law, the Fourth Master has gone to the palace — aren't you worried, staying at home?" Chen shi asked.

"A little." Qin Ru-yin didn't deny it. "But worrying won't help — better to go visiting and distract myself. Second Sister-in-law's company is the best distraction."

Chen shi heard this and felt the prick again.

She was a sharp woman. She could tell that Qin Ru-yin was not flattering her — she meant it quite naturally.

"Fourth Sister-in-law gives me too much credit." Chen shi smiled.

Qin Ru-yin looked at the flowers blooming in the garden and said quietly: "Second Sister-in-law, I heard — Second Brother's four sons are all very outstanding."

Chen shi paused.

"They're all right. The eldest is the most promising." She smiled.

"Second Sister-in-law raised four outstanding sons — that truly isn't easy." Qin Ru-yin said sincerely.

Chen shi was quiet for a moment.

Then she said: "It was not easy. But... it was worth it."

Qin Ru-yin seemed to hear something beneath those words.

She did not press further.

She reached out and broke off a bloom from a nearby branch — a small white flower — and held it in her fingertips.

"Second Sister-in-law, I came today partly because I wanted to get to know you better."

"We've all come into this family from outside — we're the people who have to manage things in this big household together. It would be much easier if we understand each other a little."

Chen shi looked at her.

Qin Ru-yin returned her gaze openly and without guile.

Chen shi's expression was unreadable for a moment.

Then she laughed — genuinely, for the first time.

"Fourth Sister-in-law is quite refreshing."

Qin Ru-yin smiled. "I just say what I think. If Second Sister-in-law finds it too blunt, please forgive me."

"No." Chen shi shook her head. "I find it... rather agreeable."

She looked at Qin Ru-yin for another moment.

Then she said, almost to herself: "When I was a new bride here, I wish someone had spoken to me this plainly."

Qin Ru-yin did not say anything to that.

She only smiled gently and offered Chen shi one of the pastries she had brought.

"Please try one — I made these myself. They're a recipe I came up with, and I'm not sure if they suit Second Sister-in-law's taste."

Chen shi accepted it.

She took a small bite.

The flavor was delicate and not overly sweet — exactly to her liking.

"It is very good." She said, and meant it.

"Fourth Sister-in-law has real talent."

"Flattery — I just enjoy fiddling around in the kitchen." Qin Ru-yin laughed.

The two women sat for a while longer.

The conversation was light — about flowers, about cooking, about the children.

Nothing pointed. Nothing loaded.

Just two women talking.

When Qin Ru-yin finally rose to leave, Chen shi walked her to the gate of Feiluan Courtyard.

"Fourth Sister-in-law." Chen shi called out just as Qin Ru-yin was about to step away.

Qin Ru-yin turned.

Chen shi seemed to consider something for a moment.

Then she said, simply: "Come again sometime."

Qin Ru-yin smiled. "I will."

She turned and walked away, Banxia falling into step beside her.

Chen shi stood at the gate for a long moment after Qin Ru-yin disappeared around the bend.

Then she turned and went back inside.

Her wet nurse was waiting anxiously.

"Second Madam — how did it go? What was the Fourth Madam like?"

Chen shi was quiet for a moment.

Then she said: "She is... not what I expected."

Her wet nurse blinked. "Good or bad?"

Chen shi sat back down in the garden and looked at the flowers.

"Harder to say than I thought."

She picked up the remaining half of the pastry Qin Ru-yin had given her and took another bite.

Still good.

She chewed slowly and thought for a while.

Then, for the first time in a long while, she felt something in the tight knot inside her chest ease, just slightly.

Just slightly.

But it was something.

chapters.title: Telling Her the Reason the Marriage Was Not Consummated
chapters.content:
On the first day after her wedding, Qin Ruyin had paid her respects to Jiang Dafuren, Madam Fang.

Now, on the second day, she followed the proper order and called upon Jiang Erfuren, Madam Chen.

After accompanying Jiang Tafuren through the midday meal, the old matriarch briefed her on matters concerning the Second Branch before sending her off to Feiluan Yuan, where Madam Chen resided.

Though Madam Chen was surprised by the visit, she quickly recovered her composure. A new bride had come to pay her respects—she, as hostess, could hardly afford to be lacking in courtesy.

When Hua Momo escorted Qin Ruyin out of Rong'an Hall, she pulled her aside and murmured a few words from the heart. They were about Madam Chen.

As the person closest to the old matriarch, Hua Momo was still, at the end of the day, a servant. There were things she dared not say too plainly.

But Qin Ruyin understood.

Madam Chen's methods ran far deeper than she had imagined. She was nothing like the gentle, virtuous, non-meddlesome woman she appeared to be on the surface.

The meaning in Hua Momo's words was a warning: tread carefully when making idle conversation with Madam Chen. Do not fall into her verbal traps without realising it, and do not say things that ought not be said.

……

Madam Chen came out through the moon gate to receive her.

She watched with a warm smile as Qin Ruyin approached, accompanied by Feng Mama and the head maidservant Xinyi. Behind them came six servants carrying trays laden with gifts of every description.

Madam Chen's smile deepened considerably.

When Qin Ruyin had called upon First Sister-in-Law Madam Fang, the old matriarch had subsidised the visit with two thousand taels of silver, letting Qin Ruyin select gifts from her own belongings. Now, visiting Madam Chen, the old matriarch had given her another two thousand taels in banknotes—specifying that she was to prepare gifts herself for her calls on the Second, Third, and Fifth Branches.

Of course, since the Fifth Branch was the youngest, it was proper for Madam Zheng of the Fifth Branch to call on Qin Ruyin first, with Qin Ruyin returning the visit afterwards.

Once she had made the rounds among her sisters-in-law, the old matriarch would personally escort her to pay respects to the elder aunts and senior female relatives.

When Jiang Tafuren had offered her the two thousand taels that morning, Qin Ruyin had politely declined. But the old matriarch had taken her hands and said, "Consider it this old woman making amends to the Fourth. Hold it on his behalf." The regret in her eyes was plain, and Qin Ruyin had not had the heart to refuse any further. To set the old woman's mind at ease, she had accepted.

Naturally, the gifts for the Second Branch could not be on the same scale as those for the First Branch. But they were still perfectly respectable.

"Fourth Sister-in-Law, you're here! Why bring all of this when you're just paying a visit?" Madam Chen smiled and exchanged a peer's greeting with Qin Ruyin.

Qin Ruyin replied with polite modesty: "Oh, it's nothing special—just some fabric for Er Sao and the nephews to have a few outfits made."

There were also brushes, ink, paper, and inkstones for the boys' studies, but she left that unsaid.

Madam Chen had noticed them, too.

She was genuinely pleased—not merely because they were fine things, but because she sensed that this new Fourth Sister-in-Law, though plainspoken, had a sincere heart. The gifts were carefully directed at her and her children, and were clearly of good quality.

Indeed, Qin Ruyin had brought nothing extra for Jiang Erlang. She had tucked in two bolts of men's brocade among the fabrics—but that was all. As a younger sister-in-law, it would have been improper to bring gifts specifically for her husband's brothers. It was also a matter of propriety.

Madam Chen had quarrelled with Jiang Erlang earlier that day—a row that the two of them had managed to keep from spilling over into outright ugliness. She had just told her wet nurse with great bravado that she could not rely on Jiang Erlang, that he was a useless wretch. But after driving him away with her biting sarcasm, the unease in her heart had not fully lifted.

Qin Ruyin's arrival was not unwelcome. At least there was someone to talk to.

Something had also gone wrong with Madam Yin lately, and Madam Chen had stopped expecting her to come by for company.

Qin Ruyin herself had not intended to linger. She had come to pay a brief call and leave a gift—nothing more. But when she rose to take her leave, Madam Chen stopped her with a genuine invitation to stay.

It seemed she truly meant it, and Qin Ruyin could hardly insist on going.

"Fourth Sister-in-Law," Madam Chen said, "I don't mean to be nosy, but I did happen to hear a bit of gossip, and I wanted to ask you… why wasn't the marriage consummated on your wedding night?"

Qin Ruyin was momentarily stunned.

Of all her sisters-in-law, she had imagined that the one most likely to ask such a blunt question would be Madam Yin of the Third Branch. She had not expected it to come from Er Sao, Madam Chen.

Madam Chen felt a touch of awkwardness herself after the words were out. Seeing Qin Ruyin stand there in silence for a long moment, she began to regret her impulsive curiosity.

When all was said and done, they were both women, and she genuinely felt for Qin Ruyin's situation on that wedding night. In her view, if the marriage went unconsummated, the man barely noticed—but it was the woman's dignity that suffered.

She was no saint. But she would not stoop to wounding someone over something as significant as this.

"That is… Fourth Sister-in-Law, if you'd rather not say, you needn't! It doesn't matter!" Madam Chen said hastily. "Just consider it Er Sao speaking out of turn. Please don't take it to heart..."

But Qin Ruyin smiled.

She could feel that Madam Chen's words were genuine. After all, Madam Chen had asked to her face—which, if anything, spoke to simple, uncomplicated curiosity. That, at least, was open and honest. Far better than whispering behind her back.

And she had no qualms about telling her own sister-in-law why the marriage had not been consummated. As long as she herself did not mind, no one could use it to hurt her. Now that her mother-in-law and husband both knew the reason and had chosen to respect her—had taken her side—she had even less reason to mind if her sisters-in-law knew as well. It was better this way. It would spare them the trouble of wild speculation.

"Since Er Sao has asked, of course I'll tell her," Qin Ruyin said with a smile. "The reason is quite simple: I haven't had my monthly cycle yet."

"Ah?"

Madam Chen was dumbfounded.

She had imagined many possible reasons. She and her husband had even speculated today that perhaps the Fourth really did have some unspeakable problem—after all, rumours had been circulating outside for quite some time.

She had never imagined that the unconsummated wedding night was due to Qin Ruyin's own situation. The girl hadn't even had her first monthly cycle yet…

My goodness…

The Fourth was a full-grown man in his prime.

He truly should not have consummated the marriage...

"No wonder!" Madam Chen was quick to understand, and said sincerely, "In that case, the Fourth was absolutely right not to consummate the marriage on the wedding night."

The little lass hadn't truly come of age yet.

Then she frowned.

"Has Fourth Sister-in-Law been examined by a physician who specialises in women's ailments?" Madam Chen asked.

She herself had given birth to four sons—not a single daughter. In her heart, she had always had a soft spot for sweet, gentle little girls, and had once longed to have a daughter of her own. But as the years passed, she had grown increasingly disenchanted with Jiang Erlang. She could not bear to share a bed with him; she could barely stomach sharing a meal.

She had felt some jealousy toward Qin Ruyin before. But now that she knew this "secret," that jealousy simply dissolved.

Seeing her ask such a question, Qin Ruyin's smile grew warmer.

"Thank you for your concern, Er Sao. While I was still at home, my mother and sisters-in-law arranged for physicians who specialise in women's ailments to examine me..."

"And what did they say?" Madam Chen pressed.

"Nothing is wrong. It's simply that the women in my mother's family tend to start their cycle late. My mother herself did not have hers until she was nineteen by the old reckoning, and both my sisters were also late."

Qin Ruyin paused, then smiled again: "Er Sao also knows that my betrothal to the Fourth came about rather unexpectedly. At the time, my mother could hardly bring up such a matter of her own accord, and the family on this side had too many other things to attend to… so it ended up this way."

She spoke with ease and grace, as if chatting with her own sisters at home.

Madam Chen nodded knowingly.

"Put like that, it is indeed understandable."

But then she thought of Qin Ruyin's eldest sister, Rujin, who had been married for several years without conceiving a child, and her gaze drifted briefly to Qin Ruyin's abdomen.

She said nothing more on the subject.

Qin Ruyin pretended not to notice Madam Chen's glance at her belly.

She smiled and sipped her tea.

Madam Chen felt a touch of embarrassment herself and only offered a mild reminder: "Just take care of yourself. Being a daughter-in-law is nothing like being a pampered guest in your own home."

Qin Ruyin thanked her.

She glanced at the sky again.

But Madam Chen still showed no intention of letting her go. She launched into the matter of her eldest son Lin-ge's studies.

Qin Ruyin offered a few complimentary remarks.

Before calling on Madam Chen of the Second Branch, Jiang Tafuren had briefed her on the four nephews of the Second Branch. The eldest, Lin-ge, was an exceptionally gifted student—not at all like his father in that regard, but very much like his maternal uncles, Madam Chen's brothers.

Madam Chen's family background was not among the most distinguished, but her three legitimate brothers and two half-brothers were all diligent scholars. That was the source of her confidence when she called Jiang Erlang a useless wretch in front of her wet nurse. Still, she was a married-out daughter—whatever resources her family had were naturally directed first toward her nephews. And no matter how well-read her brothers were, the highest-ranking among them held only a senior fourth-rank post, which could not begin to compare with the Fourth's network and connections.

When Madam Chen raised the subject of changing Lin-ge's tutor in front of her, Qin Ruyin felt no irritation. She understood the universal anxieties of parenthood—she had been through much herself. She had personally benefited enormously from dedicated study, and at her core, she admired scholars and wanted others to have the chance to learn properly. For she knew from experience that genuine, committed study could truly transform a person's fate—especially for children from humble families at the bottom of society.

Pity that in the feudal dynasty of Da Ying, the vast majority of such children could not even afford to go to school.

Still, if a child wanted to change tutors, there ought to be a reason given.

And so Qin Ruyin gently asked Madam Chen why she wanted to change Lin-ge's tutor.

"Lin-ge has a talent for scholarship, and my husband and I want to find the finest tutor possible for him. Yes, we've changed tutors rather frequently, I know. But Fourth Sister-in-Law, we are not the sort of people who look for more while they already have enough. It is only that after the first tutor—Old Chu—brought Lin-ge to a certain level, the boy stopped progressing. That's why we grew anxious to find someone new. But every tutor since has been painfully slow to show results. The only thing beyond doubt is that Lin-ge's foundations were laid very well. Even your Fourth has often praised him for that."

That was different from what she had told Madam Yin of the Third Branch earlier...

"Er Sao, you yourself have said that the Fourth does not advise changing Lin-ge's tutor so frequently. I would think that if he made such a recommendation, he must have his reasons," Qin Ruyin said, looking at Madam Chen calmly. "After all, the Fourth is a person who truly cares for his nephews and nieces."

Madam Chen understood from this that Qin Ruyin had no intention of acting as a go-between with the Fourth. But she remained composed and did not hold it against her—only smiled ruefully and said: "We parents are anxious. Next year Lin-ge is to sit for the preliminary examination!"

Qin Ruyin thought for a moment, then said, "But even when it comes to changing a child's tutor, surely it can't be settled by you and Second Brother making the decision on your own?"

"Hmm?" Madam Chen looked surprised. "Isn't that for us as parents to decide?"

Qin Ruyin shook her head with a smile. "It is Lin-ge who is doing the studying, not Er Sao and Second Brother. Surely you should ask the child himself whether he wants to change tutors!"

"Hm… come to think of it, when we changed Lin-ge's tutors, we never once asked what Lin-ge himself thought..."

Madam Chen looked at Qin Ruyin with some bewilderment. "Fourth Sister-in-Law, you mean—I should ask Lin-ge first?"

Qin Ruyin did not give a direct answer. She only said carefully, "I've been thinking—you've changed Lin-ge's tutors seven or eight times now. And yet the boy has never made much real progress. Which means there's a good chance that the tutor Lin-ge liked the most—or the one best suited to him—was the very first one, Old Chu."

Madam Chen's eyes went wide…

chapters.title: Er Sao Asks a Favour; Ruyin's Advice
chapters.content:
This was a possibility neither she nor her husband had ever considered!

Not only had she and her husband never thought of it—no one around them had, either, except for this newly arrived Fourth Sister-in-Law. Not even a man as brilliantly perceptive as the Fourth had ever raised the point with her husband.

Qin Ruyin understood why. In a feudal society, filial piety reigned supreme. The higher the family's standing, the greater the authority of the paternal line. Parents always believed they were acting in their children's best interests. How many enlightened parents actually thought to consult their children?

Putting herself in Lin-ge's position, she found it rather suffocating.

She imagined the boy must have liked that first tutor best of all—that young Chu was his favourite. But as a child, he could not stop it from happening, and he hadn't even dared to tell his parents that he wanted to keep Old Chu...

"Fourth Sister-in-Law... do you think I should really ask Lin-ge whether he wants to change tutors?" Madam Chen, at this moment, was a flustered mother without a compass, and she had instinctively made Qin Ruyin her anchor.

Qin Ruyin said seriously, "My suggestion would be for Er Sao to speak with Lin-ge in private first. With a gentle manner. And... it would be best not to mention any of this to Second Brother just yet. After all, he is the boy's father, and fathers can least bear to see their children push back against them."

Madam Chen felt this was absolutely true!

Never mind her husband—hadn't her own father been exactly the same way? And the brothers in her family? The eldest and the third among her husband's brothers were no different with their own children.

Madam Chen did not realise that as these thoughts came to her, her teeth were clenched very tightly.

"Alright! I understand. I'll find a quiet moment to have a proper talk with Lin-ge... Thank you so much, Fourth Sister-in-Law! Truly, you've woken me right up!"

Qin Ruyin smiled and waved a hand. "Er Sao needn't thank me. I married into the Jiang family because I genuinely want to live a good life here. The children—Lin-ge and the rest—may be only a few years younger than me, but they still have to call me Fourth Auntie. So I ought to treat them as I would my own nieces and nephews at home. That is the right spirit for a harmonious and flourishing household."

"Of course," Qin Ruyin added, looking at Madam Chen, "I haven't actually been much help."

"This much I can offer: if Er Sao speaks with Lin-ge and discovers the real issue, and if a new tutor does turn out to be needed, I'll mention it to my husband."

"But I should also say plainly from the start—if the Fourth cannot find a tutor well-suited to Lin-ge, Er Sao and Second Brother should not blame us for it."

Madam Chen was already deeply grateful.

"The fact that Fourth Sister-in-Law is willing to say all this already helps our Second Branch enormously! How could we ever resent you or the Fourth?"

"That would make us ungrateful wretches."

Whether they turn out to be wretches or not is entirely up to the two of you, Qin Ruyin thought.

She only smiled and said, "Er Sao, it's getting late—I really must return to Minglan Ju. I still have things to put in order there."

This time Madam Chen made no effort to detain her.

After all, Lin-ge would be dismissed from his studies shortly, and she was eager to find him and ask her questions.

……

Madam Chen personally walked Qin Ruyin to the moon gate of Feiluan Yuan and urged her to come by and chat often in the future.

Qin Ruyin readily agreed.

However calculating Madam Chen might be, as long as it was not directed at her or the people she cared about, there was no need to worry. If Madam Chen turned out to be truly malicious, of course she would cease to be close to her. But judging by today's conversation, the woman was not beyond redemption.

……

After seeing Qin Ruyin off, Madam Chen immediately instructed her trusted head maidservant, Chunyu, to go and wait outside Lin-ge's study in the outer courtyard. The moment his tutor dismissed him, she was to bring Lin-ge straight to Feiluan Yuan.

Once Chunyu left, Madam Chen paced restlessly back and forth.

Her wet nurse urged her to sit, have some tea, and collect herself—but she paid no attention.

Her wet nurse finally said, "Miss, what if the Fourth Madam's guess turns out to be wrong?"

"Right or wrong, what she said is certainly possible," Madam Chen replied. "Otherwise—we've changed tutors so many times. Why hasn't Lin-ge made any real progress?"

"Besides, the Fourth's wife is barely any older than Lin-ge himself. Perhaps she understands children his age?"

Her wet nurse nodded at this and said, "Miss, from what we've gathered… the Fourth Madam was cherished and spoiled by her closest family at home. It's quite possible that the Master and Madam of the Qin household consulted her about decisions that affected her."

"Very likely!" Madam Chen's eyes lit up.

"If the Fourth Madam can really help resolve the matter of Lin-ge's tutor, I shall have to thank her properly!"

After saying this, she turned to her wet nurse and asked, "Momo, from what you saw today—do you think our Fourth Madam truly only wants to live peacefully in the Jiang household?"

The wet nurse thought for a moment, her expression turning solemn. "The Fourth Madam has only just arrived, so this old servant cannot say for certain. But I will say this—I have never seen the Fourth Madam act anything like the current First Madam, or Third Madam, or Fifth Madam did when they first came to this household."

"She seems entirely without ambition to compete for anything..."

Madam Chen heard this and felt something she could not quite name stir in her chest.

She understood what her momo meant. Had she herself not arrived at this household with "great ambitions" of her own? She and this little Fourth Sister-in-Law were nothing alike!

After a long silence, she sighed: "If our Fourth Madam is truly as she says, then Madam Fang has struck the greatest fortune!"

"What a lucky woman she is..."

Her wet nurse tried to comfort her: "Miss, don't think too much about all that. As long as you hold on to your four sons and live well, you'll have far more blessings in your old age than the First Madam!"

"Just look at the old matriarch—so many sons, all of them capable. How splendidly she shines, how well she is provided for!"

When her wet nurse brought up Jiang Tafuren, a flicker of contempt crossed Madam Chen's eyes.

She snorted softly: "As for our Tafuren—she may not be as splendidly provided for as you say, Momo."

Her wet nurse did not dare respond to that.

She glanced at the sky and smiled. "Miss, Lin-ge should be here soon."

And indeed, before the words were fully out, they heard a little maidservant announce outside:

Lin-ge had arrived.

Behind him came Madam Chen's head maidservant, Chunyu.

Lin-ge was thirteen years old now. He stood a little taller than Madam Chen herself.

He wore a robe of creamy white Hangzhou silk, and despite his young age, his features were extraordinary—one could only call them breathtakingly refined.

He looked like Jiang Erlang. And among his brothers, Jiang Erlang's looks were second only to Jiang Jiuxiao's.

In his younger days, he had been a beautiful man.

When Madam Chen was a girl and negotiations for the match were underway, she had disguised herself in a maidservant's clothes and sneaked a look at him through a parted curtain. She had been won over in an instant.

Now Madam Chen deeply regretted that decision.

To say she had been seduced by his looks in her youth, and was now left to swallow the consequences alone...

……

The handsome young man was pleasant enough to look upon, but between his brows hung a dense cloud of gloom.

There was nothing of the liveliness and cheerfulness one would expect from a boy in his teens.

He was subdued in a way that did not suit a young man his age.

When she saw her eldest son, Madam Chen was filled with warmth.

She beckoned him to come to her side.

Lin-ge bowed and paid his respects, then did as he was told—but throughout, the expression on his face did not shift by a single shade.

It was as still and flat as standing water.

"Today..." Madam Chen had meant to ask how his studies had gone. But remembering Qin Ruyin's advice, she changed her words.

"Did anything unpleasant happen to you today?"

At that, Lin-ge's expression shifted—just slightly.

A look of surprise crossed his handsome face.

Then he shook his head.

"This child, why so few words in front of his own mother?"

Under ordinary circumstances, Madam Chen would have already shown her displeasure.

But today, she kept Qin Ruyin's words close in mind, and resolved to try—to be a mother who thought things through from her child's point of view.

She said the words with a smile.

Lin-ge registered only a brief flash of surprise, then returned to his usual expression.

"I had the kitchen prepare the sweet cakes you love. Have a little first..."

Lin-ge's brow furrowed.

Sweet cakes...

His mother had not let him have sweet cakes in years—not since childhood, when he had eaten too many and spent a night writhing with the pain of a rotting milk tooth.

He remembered: on the occasion of his twelfth birthday, he had quietly told the eldest daughter of the First Uncle's family that he wanted sweet cakes. She had secretly brought some from her husband's home and hidden two pieces away for him.

But one of the servants had reported it to his mother. Upon learning of it, his mother had scolded him soundly and then aimed her biting sarcasm at Elder Cousin until the girl was in tears...

After that, he never touched sweet cakes again.

Not just sweet cakes—he gave up all pastries and confections entirely.

"My dear boy... why are you looking at your mother like that?" Madam Chen, disconcerted by his gaze, shifted uncomfortably.

"Mother... why have you suddenly given me sweet cakes?" Lin-ge looked at her, his eyes as impassive as ever.

"Mother just... well, you're older now. You're not a little child losing your baby teeth anymore. There's no harm in having a little something you enjoy now and then."

Lin-ge shook his head. "Thank you for the thought, Mother—but I... don't eat sweet cakes anymore."

"Hmm?" Madam Chen was taken aback. "You don't eat them? Why ever not?"

Lin-ge paid no attention to her reaction and did not answer her question.

He said calmly: "If Mother has nothing more to instruct me, I will go back to my rooms to study."

"Wait!" Madam Chen felt a sudden pang of alarm.

In that moment, she realised something terrifying.

When her Lin-ge was with her—his own mother—the two of them bore no resemblance to a mother and son.

Once, she would not have given this a second thought. She might even have been pleased, thinking her eldest son was composed and steady beyond his years—a touch of his Fourth Uncle's bearing. A child who would accomplish great things!

But today, after what Qin Ruyin had said, she finally understood...

She was frightened.

"Lin-ge, wait. Your mother has something to say to you..."

"Then Mother may speak, and I will listen." Lin-ge said, devoid of any feeling, regarding her with the same placid stillness as always.

chapters.title: Jiang Jiuxiao Came Back Too Late
chapters.content:
Madam Chen's heart ached with a pain both sharp and sour.

But she forced herself to betray nothing.

Wearing her most tender expression, she reached out and gently smoothed the hair at Lin-ge's brow, then tried to take his hand—to draw him to sit beside her.

Lin-ge stepped back, swiftly.

"Lin-ge..." Madam Chen looked at her eldest son with startled eyes.

"Mother, I am grown now," Lin-ge said, his voice cool and measured. "I will sit on my own."

Madam Chen drew in a long breath, forced herself to smile, and nodded. "All right."

She then instructed her head maidservant, Chunyu: "Go to the main kitchen yourself and ask them to prepare a few of Lin-ge's favourite dishes. I will have him stay for the evening meal tonight."

The words had barely left her mouth when—before Chunyu could even respond—Lin-ge said: "Mother, there is no need. I still have to get back early to study..."

Madam Chen cut him off: "Lin-ge, have you truly no time even to dine with your mother?"

Lin-ge pressed his lips together and said nothing.

He was, after all, still a boy in his teens. Confronted by his mother's accusing tone, he did not know how to respond.

"I did not mean to reproach you. Only—reading is important, but surely we mother and son ought to find a moment to share a meal... Lin-ge, it has been nearly a month since we last ate together, has it not?"

Lin-ge thought to himself: If it was just the two of us dining together, it had not been nearly a month. It had been close to a year.

But he had long since given up hoping.

"Today your Fourth Auntie came to call on me. She said some things. She said a mother should try to see things from her child's point of view, and a child should likewise try to understand the parents'. She also said that parents and children need to understand each other better..."

At this, Lin-ge's eyes stirred.

His new Fourth Auntie—the young, small one, freshly arrived—had said these things to his mother? And his mother had taken them to heart?

Thinking about it again, Fourth Auntie was not much older than he was himself, so it was possible she could see things from a child's perspective. But his mother... could she truly have listened?

He was not sure he believed it.

When Elder Cousin had given him sweet cakes, she too had been thinking from a child's point of view—considering what he wanted.

And what had his mother done?

If his mother had truly taken Fourth Auntie's words to heart, it was probably only because Fourth Auntie stood behind the Fourth. And his mother did not dare to offend the Fourth.

Elder Cousin, on the other hand, was merely a married-out daughter of the Jiang family. Her husband was ordinary, and her position in this world precarious. The current First Madam treated her decently enough, but only on the surface. As for First Uncle...the less said, the better.

Elder Cousin was kind-hearted, and yet pitiful.

She had always been there for her brothers and sisters—and yet not a single person looked after her. And his mother had hurt someone as good as that.

Lin-ge gave a cold inward laugh.

Elder Cousin was not the only person his mother had hurt. Her calculations ran far and wide. Was there anyone she did not factor into her schemes?

Even he himself—her own eldest son...

She was so consumed with his academic performance, cared so much about his prospects—was it not all so that she could rely on him in the future? And for the sake of that, she had not once thought about what he, her son, actually felt. Every time a tutor failed to show dramatic improvement within two months, she would rush to demand that his father arrange a new one...

"Lin-ge, if you don't want to dine here with me tonight, then it doesn't matter," Madam Chen said, forcing herself to stay calm, still maintaining her composure with great effort.

Inside, she was shaken to her core. She had not even realised, until now, how completely estranged Lin-ge had become from her.

"But do stay and sit a while. There is something I want to ask you—what you think about changing tutors."

Madam Chen had no choice but to say what she had wanted to say from the start.

"I defer to whatever Mother decides," Lin-ge replied flatly.

"I have no thoughts on the matter."

Such passive, deflecting indifference.

Madam Chen felt another twist of pain.

"Lin-ge, do you miss your very first tutor—old Master Chu?"

She had run out of other approaches.

She was desperately trying to close the distance between herself and her son, but the way he was responding left her with no way in. She thought again of what Qin Ruyin had said, and asked exactly that.

And indeed—Lin-ge trembled.

He lifted his eyes and stared at his mother with disbelief.

Madam Chen felt a small surge of hope at that reaction.

Perhaps Fourth Sister-in-Law was right after all.

"Lin-ge, I won't hide anything from you," Madam Chen said, watching him, keeping her voice as gentle as she could, terrified of causing him to pull away further.

"Earlier today your Fourth Auntie came to visit, and I asked her to speak to your Fourth Uncle about finding you a new tutor. But she asked me why we had been changing tutors so frequently. Her view is that more tutors is not necessarily better—that a good match between teacher and student also matters a great deal. She suggested that perhaps, if none of the tutors you've had since can match the first one—if you never quite caught up to where you were with Master Chu—then the teacher you liked best, and who suited you best, might very well be Master Chu himself."

"Lin-ge, is that how it is?"

A tremor ran through Lin-ge deep inside.

But his stubborn nature would not let him speak.

What did it matter, hearing this from his mother now? Master Chu had long since been dismissed. He had no idea where the man was these days…

"Lin-ge, if you say nothing, I can only take it to mean that this is the case," Madam Chen said, helplessly.

Lin-ge lowered his head. "It is whatever Mother says it is. I need to go back to my studies."

"All right. Go back and make sure to eat a proper meal. I'll have the kitchen send over all your favourite dishes." Madam Chen watched her son.

Lin-ge did not look at her. He dipped his head in a bow, arms folded. "Thank you, Mother. I take my leave."

Madam Chen watched him go.

The moment Lin-ge's silhouette disappeared behind the bead curtain, she collapsed forward onto the small lacquered side table and wept—broken, without restraint.

"Lin-ge... my Lin-ge... he must hate me—his own mother..."

Her wet nurse tried to comfort her: "Miss, there is no need to grieve like this. I truly do not think Lin-ge hates you. He is simply... too well-behaved for his own good."

Madam Chen wiped her tears, and a new resolve slowly hardened in her gaze. "This matter of Lin-ge... I think I need to speak with Fourth Sister-in-Law again."

"But Miss," the wet nurse said with some worry, "will the Fourth Madam be willing to help you think through something like this? She was kind enough to say what she did today—and I think she was partly afraid that you would find her interfering."

After all, their Miss had not been particularly warm to the new Fourth Madam from the start.

The Fourth Madam, sharp as she was, must have noticed.

Standing there in attendance, she had seen it clearly—the Fourth Madam had chosen her words with great restraint when speaking with their Miss.

It frustrated her. Had she known from the beginning that this new Fourth Madam was so openly honest in her character, she would have urged Miss to draw close to her sooner...

"Momo, don't worry about that. I have no intention of harming Fourth Sister-in-Law. At most, I may have felt... envious of her good fortune in becoming the Fourth's wife as his first and principal bride, not a secondary one. And she's young enough to be my daughter. There is no real conflict of interest between us."

She paused, then pressed her lips together: "I have not treated her the way Madam Yin tried to—scheming to control her from the first day. Fourth Sister-in-Law is perceptive, and she is kind. She will understand my feelings as a mother."

The wet nurse sighed inwardly.

In her heart, she thought: Miss and the Fourth Madam have virtually no relationship to speak of. One cannot simply expect someone else to intuit one's suffering without prior warmth between them.

But Miss was the child she had nursed from infancy and raised to adulthood. When she had grown old and her own son had listened to his wife, turning against her and treating her with contempt—and her grandchildren had followed suit—it was Miss who had found out and taken her back.

From that day on, she had stayed beside Miss.

She would say the unsayable—she had come to consider Miss the only true child she had ever had in this world.

And so she would always stand on Miss's side.

She made up her mind, quietly, to pay Lin-ge a visit—to speak with him.

If she could, she hoped Lin-ge might win the Fourth Madam's genuine affection.

After all, their Miss had more than just Lin-ge to think about. She worried that if the rift between mother and son could not be healed, it would become a lasting problem.

Back in his own courtyard, Lin-ge sat motionless by the window, a book in his hands but not a single word entering his mind.

He wanted very much to find his Fourth Uncle. But he also knew that the Fourth was newly married, and he did not wish to disturb him.

……

Minglan Ju.

Before the midday meal, Jiang Jiuxiao had left Jiang Tafuren's Rong'an Hall—without even staying to eat—saying he needed to make a trip to the palace. He told the old matriarch and Qin Ruyin that it was nothing serious and that he would be back soon.

Yet the hour for the evening meal came and went, and Jiang Jiuxiao had still not returned to the residence.

Qin Ruyin was beginning to worry.

"Miss, please go ahead and eat your dinner first. The dishes have been reheated twice already—any more and they'll be spoiled." Zisu stood beside her, trying to coax her.

Qin Ruyin sat at the dining table, her chin propped in both hands. "Your master said he'd go and come straight back before noon. It's well past the evening hour now, and he still isn't back. How am I supposed to eat?"

Zisu comforted her: "Miss, please don't worry. The Master is careful and prudent in everything he does. Nothing will go wrong."

Just then, Feng Mama—whom Qin Ruyin had sent to gather news—returned.

"Miss, the Fourth is still inside the palace gates. Something of considerable magnitude appears to have occurred in the palace... but please do not worry, Miss—the Fourth is safe inside the palace. Nothing will happen to him!"

Feng Mama glanced at the untouched table of food and added: "Miss, please go ahead and eat first. Otherwise, when the Fourth finds out..."

Qin Ruyin shook her head. "I truly cannot eat. Feng Mama, all of you have also worked hard today—go and eat your own meals first."

Then she told Zisu: "Leave a bowl of egg and tofu custard. Have the rest cleared away."

She had already passed the point of hunger; now, looking at the full spread on the table, she found she had no appetite at all.

A bowl of egg and tofu custard to settle her stomach would be enough.

Zisu resigned herself to the situation, exchanging a look with Feng Mama. Feng Mama gave a small shake of her head.

Once they stepped away, Feng Mama said to Zisu: "The dishes on that table have turned—our Miss can't eat any of that. Zisu, you go now and post someone at the main kitchen. Ask them to keep a cook on standby. When Miss is hungry, they can prepare something fresh then."

Zisu lowered her voice: "Feng Mama, the main kitchen isn't our own private kitchen. Will the cooks there really agree to that?"

Feng Mama let out a cool huff. "Would they dare not agree!"

Zisu's eyes narrowed. "Right! It's not as if our Miss can't afford to have fresh food made. If needed, we'll just pay them—"

"No need for payment," Feng Mama said, waving her hand. "Just send someone over. Those people have eyes for status—they'll be falling over themselves to stay and cook for our Miss."

Zisu smiled. "Understood! I'll do as Feng Mama says!"

If Feng Mama spoke with such certainty, she must know what she was doing.

The truth was, everyone in the Jiang household, from top to bottom, had long since learned not to underestimate their Miss. And nothing could be better news than that.

……

By the time Jiang Jiuxiao returned to Minglan Ju, it was the beginning of the hai hour.

He walked into the inner chamber and saw Qin Ruyin—a small, curled-up figure, hands propped on the little side table of the cool divan, eyes closed, her head nodding...

His refined, handsome face grew still.

chapters.title: Just Like That, Her First Kiss Was Gone
chapters.content:
Then, moving without a sound, he stepped forward, bent down, and lifted the small, curled figure into his arms.

Such a light, soft little thing...

Qin Ruyin jolted awake in an instant, nearly crying out in alarm.

But Jiang Jiuxiao spoke first, his voice gentle: "Ruyin, don't be afraid. It's me. I'm back."

At once, Qin Ruyin was wide awake. "Fourth? You're back? What time is it?"

"Just past the beginning of the hai hour," he replied.

"This late? Are you all right?" She struggled to get down, but Jiang Jiuxiao would not allow it.

"I'm fine. Don't worry." He carried her toward the elaborately carved thousand-craft canopy bed.

"You should have gone to sleep long ago. Why did you wait so late?"

"You hadn't come back—how could I not worry..." She paused, then thought to ask: "Have you sent word to Mother yet? She must still be awake, fretting over you!"

"I already had Li Yi go and report to her personally. Don't worry."

Seeing Qin Ruyin visibly relax, he frowned. "I had wanted to send word to you in the palace... but there are too many watching eyes inside, and it is truly inconvenient to act out of the ordinary..."

"Don't! The palace is dangerous—you cannot afford to misstep even slightly. Just keep yourself safe—that is all that matters!" Qin Ruyin was so alarmed she reached up and covered his mouth with her hand.

"Mother and I will wait for you at home peacefully."

Jiang Jiuxiao felt the warm, soft pressure of her small hand against his lips, and his heartbeat surged unexpectedly. The tips of his ears went hot.

He stared down at the little figure in his arms, momentarily lost.

Qin Ruyin, meanwhile, said: "Put me down, please... you haven't eaten dinner yet, have you?"

She called for Zisu to come in.

"Zisu, go to the main kitchen yourself and ask them to make a bowl of chicken-shred noodles, and two light side dishes."

Zisu entered to find the Master holding her Miss in his arms, and immediately dropped her gaze, not daring to breathe.

Qin Ruyin gave her instructions; Zisu obeyed and hurried out.

Qin Ruyin then told Jiang Jiuxiao: "Zisu already had someone sent to the main kitchen to wait. A cook was kept on standby especially."

"It's quite late, though, so you shouldn't eat too much. Have just a little to get by."

Jiang Jiuxiao was indeed hungry.

He had come straight home the moment he left the palace, without eating a single bite.

In fact, he had gone without his midday meal as well—starving through two meals in a row.

His stomach was not strong; hunger always made it worse. He bore it without showing it on his face.

He had gone without two meals before—endured it, and then it passed. And in those times, he had returned to his own courtyard in the outer wing, or his study, to face it alone, in silence.

But now, he had married her...

Everything was different.

He found, just now, that he could no longer endure the sensation of two missed meals.

This change was precisely the kind he had most resisted—even feared—before.

"Have you eaten your dinner?" Jiang Jiuxiao asked her, his voice softer than he even realised.

"I have," said Qin Ruyin, nodding.

She did not mention that she'd only managed a bowl of egg and tofu custard.

But she truly wasn't hungry. She would not have let herself go without for no reason.

Even if it was late, a little something to tide herself over would not hurt—one could always think of it as a late supper.

Jiang Jiuxiao smiled. "Good. That's how it should be. Once my holiday leave is over, I will often be coming home late. You should eat when it is time to eat, and rest when it is time to rest. Do not wait for me."

Qin Ruyin heard the gravity in his voice and nodded seriously.

That had been her intention, too.

But today he had been inside the palace far too long without any news, with no way for her to find out what was happening. The worry and anxiety were inevitable.

She would not want to have just married him only for him to meet with some accident in the palace.

Jiang Jiuxiao saw her nod obediently, and the corners of his lips curved upward.

"You don't need to play the virtuous and dutiful wife in the Jiang household," he added, looking at her earnestly.

Qin Ruyin laughed.

"Where did that come from? I'm not exactly virtuous and dutiful to begin with."

Jiang Jiuxiao tilted his head and looked at her. "I see you heading precisely in that direction."

Qin Ruyin was surprised.

How had he noticed?

"I think you've misread me," she said with another laugh.

"If you don't believe it, you'll see for yourself the moment you take a concubine. You'll discover just how un-virtuous I actually am."

"A concubine?" Jiang Jiuxiao's brow contracted. "Who said something to you?"

Then a thought struck him, and his eyes grew sharp and cold in an instant.

"Was it Second Sister-in-Law?"

"Ah—no, no, no!" Qin Ruyin waved her hands frantically. "No one said anything to me! I did visit Er Sao today, but she only talked about Lin-ge..."

Jiang Jiuxiao set her gently on the bed.

With his arms suddenly empty, his chest felt strangely bereft...

He stood for a moment, staring at his own hands, then composed himself and looked at Qin Ruyin squarely.

"Mother loathes it when men take concubines. Father never took one in his life. I despise having a back courtyard full of women—messy, foul, and without dignity. Of all my brothers, only Second Brother has taken two concubines—and even those were women he first kept secretly as mistresses outside the home. When Second Sister-in-Law discovered them, she herself arranged to have them formally brought in as concubines."

Jiang Jiuxiao made no effort to spare his second brother's reputation.

It was evident he held him in very low regard.

"Ruyin, listen carefully. I don't need you to be that kind of virtuous woman. Don't model yourself after Second Sister-in-Law. She thinks what she did was generous and magnanimous—taking the initiative to bring in the mistresses her husband had been keeping outside. She thinks he would be grateful to her for it. But he is not."

"I would never learn from Er Sao!" Qin Ruyin laughed so hard she nearly lost her composure. "You said it yourself—no concubines!"

"Of course," said Jiang Jiuxiao, with solemn gravity.

"If you did want to take one," Qin Ruyin continued cheerfully, "that's fine too—just give me advance notice. Don't do what Second Brother did, keeping a woman on the outside. That respects neither me as your wife nor those beautiful women outside."

Jiang Jiuxiao looked at this little figure discussing the matter of concubines with the casual ease of someone talking about other people's affairs entirely, and something unpleasant stirred in his chest.

"I would never—"

"Don't say it so absolutely yet. Given your position, the future is truly hard to predict," Qin Ruyin cut him off.

Then she smiled: "Besides, I'm not the sort to cling and cause a scene. If you do wish to take a concubine, simply give me a letter of dissolution and we will part ways."

"You can rest assured—my family will not blame you for it. They would all understand your circumstances..."

Jiang Jiuxiao suddenly bent forward, both hands closing around her small hands where they rested atop the coverlet. "You've thought all of this through already—long before it was necessary?"

Qin Ruyin, entirely unaware that danger was approaching, sat up and nodded at him.

"Of course! I—"

Jiang Jiuxiao did not know whether it was the pain of his empty stomach clouding his mind, or whether he had been provoked by the girl's breathtaking ease and nonchalance.

In that moment, without thought or reason, he caught her two slender wrists in one hand, wrapped the other around her waist, and pulled her into his arms.

His lips sealed over that small, chattering mouth.

Qin Ruyin went utterly still, eyes wide and staring upward. She did not dare breathe.

In truth, she could not breathe.

Mercifully, Jiang Jiuxiao pulled back almost at once.

Because Zisu's voice came from beyond the bead curtain: "Miss, the Fourth's dinner is here."

Jiang Jiuxiao rose, one hand clasped behind his back.

He looked at her and asked: "Will you have a little more as well?"

Qin Ruyin's head was spinning, and words failed her entirely. She could only shake it.

Jiang Jiuxiao let the hand behind his back curl into a tight fist, then said in a warm voice: "Then I'll go and have a bite."

Qin Ruyin nodded, again and again.

Once he had gone into the outer room to eat, she buried her face in both hands.

Good heavens! What had just happened?

He had kissed her?

He had kissed her on the lips?

He had actually kissed her on the lips?

Was this still the composed and steady Jiang Jiuxiao she knew?

Jiang Jiuxiao, alone with his dinner, found his own thoughts in disarray.

He had... what?

Then the thought came: she is his wife. A little closeness between husband and wife is perfectly natural.

With that reasoning, the upward curve of his lips refused to be suppressed.

He ate quickly—the entire bowl of chicken-shred noodles, spotless, and the two small dishes nearly as clean.

Finished, he went swiftly to the washroom to wash up and change.

When he returned to the inner chamber wearing a fresh robe of lake-green silk, Qin Ruyin startled—as if stricken with a fright—and instinctively burrowed beneath the soft coverlet, pulling it over her head.

Jiang Jiuxiao's gaze deepened. He crossed the room in a few long strides.

He gently drew down the coverlet she had pulled over her head.

Then he exhaled softly. "Don't be afraid of me. I had no intention of frightening you. I just—"

Qin Ruyin cut him off hastily, the flush on her face still not faded.

But she forced herself to appear unbothered.

"Fourth, what are you saying? We are husband and wife. What you did was not inappropriate, and there is no need to reproach yourself."

She was, she thought, completely terrified.

She was an absolute novice with no experience whatsoever!

Across two lifetimes, this was her first kiss.

And then there was the grudging indignation.

Was it really going to go like that—her first kiss, just... gone so splendidly?

She hadn't even properly savoured the moment before it was over.

Well. Let it go.

When she and Jiang Jiuxiao had grown a little closer, she would find a way to...

"I know you're afraid. And I am so many years your senior. But between husband and wife, there are things that must eventually be—"

The awkwardness was unbearable. "Mmm, yes, I know—please—stop." She cut him off and burrowed back under the blanket.

Heavens above. The embarrassment was truly mortifying.

In that moment, she found herself thinking: at least with someone you chose yourself, this kind of closeness wouldn't feel so awkward. Surely?

And this old fellow kept talking, kept going on and on.

As expected—too great an age difference truly meant a generation gap...

"All right, I'll stop. Come out from there—you'll give yourself trouble if you smother yourself like that."

"You have to promise not to say that kind of thing again! At least—not tonight!" Qin Ruyin's voice came from inside the coverlet, muffled and indignant.

Jiang Jiuxiao looked at this creature—adorable, wilful, unable to bear even a single word about the intimacies of married life—and let out a deep, silent laugh.

"All right. I promise. Not tonight."

Qin Ruyin did not catch the trap buried in those last two words, and only then did she emerge from the coverlet—only to fall directly into a warm embrace.

chapters.title: Return to the Maiden Home
chapters.content:
"I'll hold you as we sleep," Jiang Jiuxiao said to her.

The words were ordinary enough, yet Qin Ruyin felt her heart give a startled leap before the warmth of them settled in. She felt her face grow hot.

Across two lifetimes, she had never had anyone hold her as she slept—not as an intention, not as a comfort.

In the depths of her heart, she yearned for this kind of simple, uncomplicated tenderness.

What came out of her mouth was: "Fourth... I'm not a child."

Jiang Jiuxiao gave another low laugh. "Then humour me. I can only sleep well when I'm holding you."

He was telling the truth. Qin Ruyin knew he was not a man who deigned to lie, and this confirmed what she had long since suspected: he truly did sleep better with her in his arms.

Perhaps, she thought, they were two of a kind.

A strange tenderness rose in her heart.

Jiang Jiuxiao settled them both into bed, tucked the covers neatly around the two of them, and then—with that settled—made no further overtures.

"Ruyin, something of great consequence happened in the palace today. The Emperor has been poisoned..."

Qin Ruyin had just closed her eyes, ready to sleep, when Jiang Jiuxiao spoke.

She gave an involuntary shudder beneath the coverlet.

The Emperor had been poisoned?

Heavens above!

She had once naively assumed that the brutal and bloody power struggles of ancient imperial courts existed only in dramatic productions—invented to move the story along.

She had never imagined they could come to life right in front of her...

"How could the Emperor have been poisoned?" Even her voice trembled slightly.

She was truly shocked.

"Is the Emperor... all right?"

The reigning Emperor of Da Ying, whose reign title was Guanghui, was the twenty-third ruler in the dynasty's history. He was a monarch of revival—known for his ability to identify and deploy talented men, and for his genuine concern for the welfare of his people. Under his diligent and benevolent rule, Da Ying had achieved relative peace and prosperity: so long as natural disasters did not strike, most ordinary people had food and clothing enough.

Such a capable and humane ruler—and he had been the target of a poisoning plot?

"The poison has been drawn from the Emperor's body. The one who ordered it has not yet been identified—the Imperial Guard has been deployed in full force..." Jiang Jiuxiao's voice was grave and measured.

"If something like this has happened, the court is bound to be a bloodbath. You—"

Qin Ruyin was afraid for him.

Jiang Jiuxiao patted her back gently in reassurance. "Don't worry about me. By the time the Emperor was found, his mind was still clear. He immediately issued a verbal decree summoning several people into the palace—the Crown Prince, myself, and Wang Chengbin were all called in."

Qin Ruyin understood.

This meant the Emperor trusted the Crown Prince and those who supported him.

In the most perilous moment, the Emperor had turned to the faction aligned with the Eastern Palace...

She asked nothing more.

She understood what must not be said.

When it came to the imperial family's most closely guarded secrets, it was wisest not to ask too many questions.

Whatever Jiang Jiuxiao chose to share, she would receive. No more, no less.

It surprised her, in truth, that he was willing to share even this much with her. Her father, for all his deep love for her mother, rarely spoke of court affairs at home.

And yet Jiang Jiuxiao was willing to tell her something as weighty as this—a secret at the very heart of the imperial house. And she had only just married him.

"Ruyin, you know this now, but even when you return to your family tomorrow, please don't mention it to your mother and the others."

After a moment's reflection, Jiang Jiuxiao continued: "As for Mother—if she asks, you may mention it briefly. If she doesn't bring it up, there's no need for you to raise it with her either."

Qin Ruyin agreed immediately.

"I hadn't intended to tell you all this—I was afraid of frightening you." His arm around her tightened slightly.

Qin Ruyin said quickly: "Don't worry. I'm not afraid. I trust you, Fourth."

At these words, Jiang Jiuxiao looked down for a moment at the slight figure nestled in his arms, and the corners of his lips lifted.

"Mm." He made a sound of acknowledgement.

Then, slowly: "I've thought it through. Given the position I'm in, and the role the Jiang family plays, our household will not be a peaceful one. And you are my wife—you will be the first target. Those who cannot move against me will come for you instead."

"Today's incident with the Emperor proves that certain people can no longer contain themselves. From here on, all manner of dangers are likely to follow in quick succession."

"I understand," Qin Ruyin replied at once. "I'm not afraid."

Then, with real concern: "Do you have enough people around you privately? If not, I have some savings in my trousseau—take it. Go find a few more men who are skilled in martial arts and can be trusted as guards."

Jiang Jiuxiao's eyes brightened, and his lips curved.

"A man of my standing, taking money from a young girl's trousseau? Don't worry. I've been quietly cultivating my own people for some time now. The Jiang family must be able to defend itself, and I must be able to protect the people in it."

"Now that you are my wife, you are the person closest to me. I will have people stationed around you in close protection. Do not feel that there are too many unfamiliar faces, or that it is troublesome. Even in the future, if you absolutely must leave the house, my personal guards will accompany you at all times..."

He gave many instructions. Qin Ruyin accepted them all.

She was deeply grateful for his protection.

In her previous life, it was her failing body that had kept her under the constant shadow of death. No one understood the preciousness of life better than she did.

She wanted to live—long, safely, and happily.

And he—her new husband—was willing to spend everything he had to guard her life and keep her safe.

She thought, and then she said something in concern for him.
