"I'll stay inside the residence and go out as little as possible, so I'll be fine. But you're different—you must be especially careful. Even on the ordinary days when you go to morning court and return from the ministry, make sure to add more guards..."

Qin Ruyin offered her careful reminder.

To put it plainly: the Jiang family were loyalists to the throne. That they had stood unshaken for hundreds of years meant every generation before them had been men of extraordinary ability. Now that burden had fallen to Jiang Jiuxiao—which meant he, too, was staking his life for the family's continued standing. And all those connected to the Jiang family rose or fell together.

The Qin family had entered into a marriage alliance with the Jiang family—and so they, too, were on the same boat.

Even if the Qin family had not wished to be on that boat—who among the cunning old foxes in the court who worked in the shadows would believe them?

Her father had also told her privately: following the Jiang family as loyalist ministers to the Emperor was the most suitable path the Qin family could hope to find.

And in her previous life, the Jiang family had lost that battle.

But in this life, with her fourth younger sister, the path forward for Jiang Jiuxiao had surely changed in ways she could not yet see.

Just as on the wedding day, when Anwang had plotted in the shadows to switch the bride—and Jiang Jiuxiao had thwarted it entirely.

"Mm, I know." Jiang Jiuxiao leaned down and pressed his lips briefly to her forehead.

Qin Ruyin felt the spot where he had kissed her go warm in an instant.

"That... Fourth, the dream that my fourth younger sister told you—was it useful to you and the Crown Prince?"

Qin Ruyin changed the subject.

In the dim amber candlelight, warmth gathered in the depths of Jiang Jiuxiao's gaze.

Seeing that she had finally asked, he did not conceal it.

"Yes. Very much so. And all because of you and Fourth Sister."

Qin Ruyin said: "I didn't do anything. It was all Fourth Sister's contribution."

Jiang Jiuxiao shook his head. "That's not how it should be put. Without you, how would the Jiang family have known about Fourth Sister's dream?"

He paused a moment, considering, then spoke again.

"Some of what came out of the investigation is too complicated to discuss right now. But after some time has passed, I'll tell you whatever you wish to know."

Qin Ruyin nodded.

"It's late. We also need to rise early tomorrow for the return visit. Let's rest now." Jiang Jiuxiao, seeing her quietly acquiescent...

……

The following morning, Qin Ruyin woke up late again.

Jiang Jiuxiao had let her sleep.

He was accustomed to rising early for morning court and had long since formed the habit. When the head maidservants were anxious enough to go in and rouse Qin Ruyin, he stopped them.

He even stepped to the door and told Zisu with a frown: "Let your Miss sleep her fill. If the return visit runs late, I'll answer to her parents myself. Stop hovering and peeking through the door."

Zisu was so frightened her heart was pounding, and she retreated several paces from the inner chamber door.

It was only when Qin Ruyin's family sent her eldest and second brothers to escort her back that Jiang Jiuxiao went in and woke her himself...

It was not a fixed custom for a bride's family to send her brothers to bring her home for the return visit. But families of standing who wished to show that they valued their daughter would make the gesture of sending their own kin to receive her.

There was also this: some mothers-in-law who were displeased with the new bride would deliberately prevent the son-in-law from accompanying the bride home—and the family sending their own people to fetch her was a way to preserve both the bride's and the family's dignity.

"Oh my goodness, Fourth... you got up so early—why didn't you wake me?"

He had even said the night before that they needed to be up early for the return visit.

He had been up early. She, on the other hand...

Once Qin Ruyin realised the sun was already high in the sky, she scrambled to jump straight out of bed.

But before her feet could touch the ground, Jiang Jiuxiao reached out with both hands and caught her firmly.

"The floor is cold—how can you leap out of bed without putting your stockings on first?"

He watched the lively, flustered little figure—rushing about and still finding time to reproach him—and his eyes were full of smiles.

"There's no rush. Your Second Brother and Third Brother happen to be here in the residence today. I've already had word sent out—they're being received and entertained in the outer courtyard."

Qin Ruyin was momentarily taken aback.

To have Jiang Erlang and Jiang Sanlang personally come out to welcome and accompany her brothers—that was no small courtesy.

"Second Brother and Third Brother are entertaining the two brothers-in-law while you get ready. Take your time, no rush."

Jiang Jiuxiao had even had the kitchen send breakfast over.

"I won't eat breakfast—there's no time!" Qin Ruyin called out as she hurried through washing up.

"There is time," Jiang Jiuxiao said, his voice unhurried. "Allow me to accompany you for a bite."

"Didn't we agree—you should eat your morning meal first thing when you get up? You can't go about with an empty stomach..."

"And neither can you," Jiang Jiuxiao said, quietly and without sternness, yet in a way that left no room for argument.

"Fine—then I'll eat. But from now on, every morning after you get up, you must have your breakfast too—even if it's just a simple bowl of chicken-shred noodles..."

"All right," Jiang Jiuxiao agreed.

Qin Ruyin was satisfied.

With time short, the morning meal was kept simple.

Jiang Jiuxiao asked for just two bowls of chicken broth noodles.

Once they were ready, Jiang Jiuxiao accompanied Qin Ruyin to the front courtyard.

Qin Ruyin, dressed and made up in her finest, was reunited with her two brothers.

Da Ge and Er Ge studied their little sister carefully.

They saw her: rosy, glowing, full of spirit and vitality.

Both brothers exhaled with quiet relief.

By the look of her, she had not suffered in the Jiang household—and the Jiang family had not made things difficult for her.

Their father and mother would finally be able to set their hearts at ease.

After the exchange of greetings, Jiang Jiuxiao explained to the two brothers-in-law:

"Please forgive us, brothers-in-law. I had an unexpected matter arise last night and had to leave the residence. Ruyin waited very late for me before she could sleep, so I hadn't the heart to wake her early this morning. Hence we are late. I ask for your understanding."

Jiang Erlang and Jiang Sanlang, standing nearby, both looked up at Jiang Jiuxiao.

This Fourth Brother of theirs... had personally come out, arranged for the two of them to receive and entertain the visitors, and was now addressing his brothers-in-law with such courtesy.

It seemed the Fourth truly was looking after this new wife of his...

Da Ge and Er Ge exchanged a glance with their little sister.

Then the two brothers together bowed toward Jiang Jiuxiao.

Da Ge said: "You are too courteous, brother-in-law. Ruyin was not well as a child—our mother always let her sleep in. She's grown up with the habit. We only hope that as she grows a little older it will improve. Please be patient with her in the meantime..."

Jiang Jiuxiao corrected the form of address.

"We are family now. There's no need for such formality, brothers-in-law. Just call me brother-in-law—or by my courtesy name—whichever you prefer."

Da Ge and Er Ge exchanged a smile.

Then both said in unison: "Brother-in-law."

Jiang Jiuxiao nodded with a smile.

Then he told the brothers: "Don't worry on our account. Ruyin being able to eat and sleep well is a great blessing. It's a very good thing—no need to change it!"

He then invited the two brothers-in-law to share his carriage.

Da Ge and Er Ge thanked him and politely declined.

Jiang Jiuxiao thought about it and realised that today, as newlyweds, they ought to be especially careful going out—so it was perhaps better that the two brothers-in-law declined.

The Qin family's carriage led the way.

The Jiang family's carriage followed in the middle.

A third carriage behind carried Qin Ruyin's attendants.

And behind that, several more carriages bore the lavish return gifts the Jiang family had prepared for Qin Ruyin.

One of those carriages was loaded with gifts the old matriarch had specifically prepared for Qin Da Furen, Madam Li.

The journey began smoothly.

But when the carriages reached a busy street corner, they came to a sudden halt.

Qin Ruyin's heart lurched—and Jiang Jiuxiao immediately drew her into his arms, his voice tender: "Don't be afraid. Nothing will happen."

But his eyes, sharp as a hawk's, swept the surroundings.

Then he spoke clearly into the carriage: "What has happened at the front?"

The coachman answered at once: "Replying to the Master—Li Yi has dismounted and gone ahead to investigate. From what can be seen at present, it appears two carriages from noble households have collided..."

Jiang Jiuxiao told Qin Ruyin: "Don't worry. Nothing will happen. Today before we set out, I had twice the usual number of hidden guards stationed to travel with us in shadow."

Qin Ruyin felt her nerves settle.

But the two households' guards were each refusing to give way, and spectators had gathered three deep around them, making the road impossible to pass. The carriage was forced to stop on the stone-paved street.

Jiang Jiuxiao was not the sort to invoke his rank and authority to bully his way through, so they waited.

After roughly a quarter of an hour, Li Yi returned.

He stood beside the carriage window and reported: "Replying to the Master and Fourth Madam—it is the carriage of the Young Lord of Yong'an Marquis Household that has collided with the carriage of the Young Lord of Jingnan Duke Household. The bystanders have already been dispersed, and our carriages may proceed."

"These two families..." A glint flickered in Jiang Jiuxiao's eyes.

"Li Yi, stay sharp. Let us proceed."

Li Yi answered respectfully.

The carriage moved forward smoothly.

"Do you think something about this is off?" Qin Ruyin, seeing Jiang Jiuxiao with his brow still slightly knit, ventured to ask.

Jiang Jiuxiao was unwilling to let her sit in boredom, so he told her something of the two households whose carriages had collided.

The Yong'an Marquis and the Jingnan Duke's families were old enemies.

In this generation, the Young Lord of Yong'an Marquis and the Young Lord of Jingnan Duke had also come to blows over a girl—a courtesan—they had both fallen for.

The Yong'an Marquis family had risen through military merit and still commanded considerable prestige in the army.

The Jingnan Duke's household, by contrast, was in decline—the current Duke coasting entirely on the grace of his ancestors, holding the title of Jingnan Duke by hereditary succession alone.

In a fight between a young man trained in combat from childhood and a decorative vase propped up only by his family's former glory, the outcome was entirely one-sided.

In that previous brawl, the Young Lord of Jingnan had been beaten badly.

And the Young Lord of Jingnan was the Duke's only son—raised as a precious treasure. Since that incident, the enmity between the two families had deepened further.

"The Young Lord of Yong'an is remarkably handsome and an exceptional martial artist—a pity he is inordinately dissolute." Jiang Jiuxiao shook his head, the look in his eyes carrying a trace of something like regret.

Though it was not entirely regret for the young lord's reckless ways.

At times, dissipation was the best cover of all.

A marquis's heir from a military family who was too exceptional would keep many people awake at night... The frontier was at peace, so the Young Lord of Yong'an had no choice but to carry on in that dissolute manner.

That was the real source of Jiang Jiuxiao's regret.

"If these two families' carriages collided, it was either deliberate or someone arranged it from the shadows."

Qin Ruyin immediately understood what he meant.

Though she found it hard to believe a person would be so brazen.

"Didn't he receive a reprimand from the Emperor last time? Does he still dare to stir trouble in secret?"

"There's a saying: the wilder the storm, the more precious the fish. The more dangerous the moment, the bolder he acts. Even if he did this—as long as there's nothing to grab hold of on the surface, suspicion alone counts for nothing. Besides, the Emperor may not necessarily believe it was him. The Emperor... he has always had great confidence in his own judgment."

Qin Ruyin understood.

The Emperor of Da Ying was a virtuous ruler—but virtuous rulers had their flaws as well.

The Emperor's flaw, it seemed, was overconfidence...

A glimpse of this could be seen in the fates of his sons in her previous life.

"If he only had the carriages of those two families collide, what could he hope to achieve?" Qin Ruyin asked.

She truly could not work out the purpose.

"Probing," said Jiang Jiuxiao, with two quiet words.

He explained: "He is probing. Testing how many people I have arranged in shadow to protect you when you leave the house... If I had deployed no one, the consequences would be something neither of us could bear."

Qin Ruyin found the feeling deeply unpleasant.

The sensation of being a creature watched and studied by a predator.

She desperately wanted Jiang Jiuxiao to get rid of that repulsive man sooner.

But she could not put undue pressure on him.

She pressed her lips together and said nothing.

Jiang Jiuxiao gently patted her back.

He had plans in motion, plans he could not yet speak of openly.

For the rest of the return visit journey, aside from the incident with the Yong'an Marquis and Jingnan Duke household carriages, everything went smoothly.

Even Da Ge and Er Ge merely assumed the collision of two noble families' carriages at a busy street corner was an accident.

They had no idea that in the shadows, Jiang Jiuxiao's hidden guards had already engaged in an intense, silent battle with several figures of mysterious origin—and won.

Not even Qin Ruyin knew.

……

When the carriages arrived at Zijing Hutong and came to a halt, Jiang Jiuxiao stepped down first.

Then with one hand he lifted the carriage curtain, and the other he extended into the carriage.

Qin Ruyin gathered her deep red ceremonial skirt in one hand and placed the other in Jiang Jiuxiao's large palm.

Jiang Jiuxiao closed his fingers gently around her slender, jade-green ones, and helped her down.

Inside the main gate, all the members of the Qin family who were Qin Ruyin's peers had already gathered to receive them.

After the exchange of greetings, Qin Ruyin and Jiang Jiuxiao were escorted through to the inner residence to pay their respects to Qin Da Laoye and Qin Da Furen, Madam Li.

Once the newly married couple had paid their respects to the elders, Jiang Jiuxiao was ushered away by Da Ge and the others to drink tea and converse in the outer courtyard.

Qin Ruyin was surrounded by the womenfolk.

Madam Li gripped her youngest daughter's hands tight, her eyes unwilling to leave her face for a single moment.

She looked at her: dressed in her deep red ceremonial clothes, hair pinned up in the style of a married woman, small face rosy and smooth, eyes bright and full of life.

One glance told her the girl had not suffered in her husband's household.

The great stone in her chest finally rolled aside.

Da Sao, Lin Xi, led the other women away, leaving mother and daughter to speak in private.

"Is your husband treating you well? And your mother-in-law?"

Though Madam Li could see for herself that Qin Ruyin had been well these past days, she still needed to hear it from her daughter's own mouth before she would be truly at peace.

"Mother, please don't worry. My mother-in-law likes me very much, and the Fourth is quite good to me." Qin Ruyin spoke sincerely.

Her eyes were full of smiles.

Madam Li pressed her hand to her chest. "Thank the ancestors! Thank goodness, thank goodness!"

But in the next moment she studied Qin Ruyin's face more closely, then leaned in and whispered: "You and your husband haven't... consummated the marriage yet. He didn't get angry, did he?"

"Ah? Mother, how did you know?" Qin Ruyin was surprised.

Madam Li shot her a look. "Child! Your mother has been through it herself—can't I tell?"

Then, with a slightly awkward expression, she said: "When I married your father, we didn't consummate our marriage on the wedding night either..."

Qin Ruyin covered her mouth and laughed.

Given how devoted her father was to her mother, she had more or less guessed as much.

But her parents' private matters were not something a younger family member could pry into uninvited.

"Goodness, you child—heartless girl, what are you laughing at?"

Madam Li had no idea what to do with her.

"I took the initiative and told the Fourth myself. After that, he didn't bring up consummating the marriage," Qin Ruyin told her mother honestly.

Madam Li nodded in relief. "Your husband is a good man! Thank goodness!"

"I was so worried about exactly that—if he had forced himself on you, you would have suffered terribly."

"When the Qin family of Shunyi Hutong was arranging your father's marriage—do you know why that old woman chose me? She had no good intentions. First, because I hadn't had my monthly cycle by the age of eighteen, she thought there was a very good chance I would never be able to bear children, and she wanted to cut off your father's line. Second, she thought that at eighteen I hadn't yet truly come of age, and that I would suffer terribly on the wedding night—and might never be able to conceive even if I could, after such suffering. Again, all to cut off your father's line. In truth, your mother was worried that the same fate might befall you. That's why I told you before you left—if it came to the worst, you could tell your husband yourself."

"As it turned out, everything has gone well! Thank the heavens!" Madam Li clasped her hands together again.

Qin Ruyin comforted her: "Mother, you truly needn't have worried."

Madam Li shook her head. "You are the child I carried for ten months. How could I not?"

Qin Ruyin changed the subject and began talking of other things.

Madam Li suddenly broke into a smile. "Today is also the day your cousin of Shunyi Hutong returns home for her return visit. You have no idea—ever since that Madam Tong came back to the Shunyi Hutong Qin household, things have been quite lively over there!"

Qin Ruyin remembered a remark her second elder sister had made in passing—and her eyes glinted.

chapters.title: Return to the Maiden Home (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Madam Tong, after all, came from a family of a hundred-year standing, and she had more than enough methods at her disposal.

Even after she had been sent to the countryside, and even though Qin Laotaitai and Qin Mingjie's mother and daughter had deliberately suppressed her people—transferring anyone loyal to her away from positions of influence, and even selling off many of them—it had not stopped Madam Tong from swiftly reassembling her network of loyal servants after returning from the country estate.

Madam Tong understood with perfect clarity that now that she had returned, she and Qin Laotaitai's faction had entered a fight to the death.

So she had stopped being frugal with money and goods. Previously, when there had been no open break with Qin Mingjie and his mother, she had always found ways to make them spend their own silver while protecting her own. Now, with her mind made up, she resolved that anything that could be solved with money would be solved with money.

As long as she was willing to spend, there was no shortage of capable people willing to work for her.

She had had Qin Mingjie's concubine Ruiniang investigated down to the bone.

And indeed, she had turned up something remarkable.

When Madam Tong learnt that it was Qin Laotaitai who had arranged for Ruiniang to be brought in as Qin Mingjie's concubine, she inwardly wanted to strangle the old woman with her bare hands—though outwardly she continued to maintain the performance of a dutiful daughter-in-law.

What Madam Tong had uncovered was this: Ruiniang had not, from the very beginning, been a simple courtesan. She was a woman deliberately cultivated and placed in the pleasure houses for a particular purpose by someone with an agenda.

When Madam Tong tried to pursue the trail further—to find out who was behind Ruiniang—the trail suddenly went cold.

Even when she personally returned to her family's residence in the capital and enlisted the help of her own kin to investigate, she could dig no deeper.

Her eldest brother warned her plainly: the trail had been severed, and that meant someone had deliberately cut it. He told her to stop investigating, lest she bring fire down on herself.

Madam Tong was not willing to let it go.

But in front of her elder brother, she promised to comply.

When she returned to the Qin household from her family's residence in the capital, she said nothing of Ruiniang's suspicious origins to anyone. She had no intention of alerting the enemy.

Instead, she quietly sent a trusted agent south to Jiangnan to find more girls of Ruiniang's sort—younger, prettier—and bring them back.

If Qin Mingjie resented her, his principal wife, for being plain and dull, and claimed she did not understand him—then she would buy him several young and beautiful girls to keep him company, to be his blushing companions over wine and verse.

Did Ruiniang, that vixen, think she could enjoy his exclusive favour?

Not while the principal wife still had a say in the matter.

Even with all these arrangements made in secret, Madam Tong could not sleep peacefully. In the quiet of deep nights, her heart felt as if it were being roasted over a fire.

The resentment she bore toward Qin Mingjie and his mother had changed her beyond recognition.

She was suffering. And she had no intention of letting them live in comfort either.

In recent days, Madam Tong had been using the matter of Ruiniang to cause trouble three times a day, throwing the household into chaos.

On the surface, she flatly refused to acknowledge Ruiniang as Qin Erlang's concubine.

Her reasoning was simple. As Qin Erlang's principal wife, the matter of taking a concubine was hers to decide. Since she—the principal wife—had never agreed, had never drunk the concubine's ceremonial tea, Ruiniang had no status whatsoever.

A woman brought in from outside—from a place of ill repute—could be beaten to death without consequence.

Ruiniang, knowing Madam Tong's family was powerful and that even Qin Mingjie's exclusive favour could not protect her, was terrified out of her wits.

In her anxiety and dread she wept day and night, and the child in her womb could not be held—she miscarried.

When Qin Mingjie heard the news of Ruiniang's miscarriage, he stormed directly into Madam Tong's courtyard, dismissed all her attendants, and came to blows with her.

In a single moment of lost control, he very nearly strangled Madam Tong with his own hands.

It was only because their youngest son happened to come to pay his respects to Madam Tong—and found something terribly wrong—that he burst into the inner chamber and pulled Madam Tong back from the edge.

After feeling Qin Mingjie's murderous intent directed squarely at her, Madam Tong seemed to age ten years in an instant.

She no longer harboured any hope, not even a shred, for Qin Mingjie or his family.

She had deadened her heart completely.

She also came to understand why her former daughter-in-law, Sun Shi, had been so determined to take her two children and leave.

She had once resented Sun Shi—resented her for making her eldest son, Qin Rong, lose face before the world, and for taking away her two eldest grandchildren.

But now, looking at this father and son who were one and the same—both capable of destroying the household for the sake of a vixen woman—she suddenly stopped resenting Sun Shi.

She even felt grateful that Sun Shi had taken her two eldest grandchildren away.

Whatever they had lost by growing up without their biological father, remaining in the Qin household would have cost them far more.

Madam Tong had come to understand a great many things.

But the rage of nearly being strangled to death by Qin Ronggong was not something she could simply swallow.

Consumed by hatred, she sent someone back to her family home to report what had happened—but the messenger was intercepted by Qin Laotaitai's people.

Qin Laotaitai summoned Madam Tong to Shouhe Tang, and using Madam Tong's children as leverage—especially her most beloved youngest son, the very one who had just saved her life—she forced Madam Tong to choke down her anger at nearly being killed.

To protect her youngest son's future, Madam Tong had no choice but to promise Qin Laotaitai she would stop sending word back to her own family.

But Madam Tong demanded compensation from Qin Laotaitai and Qin Mingjie in return.

Qin Laotaitai, who had been hemorrhaging money and goods over recent days and had grown ever more tight-fisted, not only refused to compensate Madam Tong—she mocked her.

With no compensation forthcoming, Madam Tong's resentment deepened further.

……

Today was also the day Qin Ruyue returned to the Qin household for her return visit.

Wang Da Ren had recently been promoted, and Wang Huaimian had returned to being gentle and attentive toward Qin Ruyue.

Since she had come back for the visit, he accompanied her.

Qin Mingjie, with his newly promoted father-in-law Wang Da Ren in mind, looked upon the new son-in-law Wang Huaimian with greater favour than before.

He placed more and more stock in Qin Ruyue's prophetic dreams as well.

He had, however, since found out that it was this very daughter who had secretly sent word to the Tong family—which had resulted in Madam Tong being brought back from the country estate.

At the time, he had been furious enough to blow his beard and roll his eyes, intending to give her a thorough scolding the moment she came back for her visit.

But now, weighing everything, he chose not to make an issue of what Qin Ruyue had done.

Privately, he hoped she would have more prophetic dreams—about his future and the future of his sons.

And so he wore a somewhat ingratiating air around Qin Ruyue.

Madam Tong had also learned that it was her youngest daughter's doing that had gotten her brought back from that miserable place in the country.

And the very moment her youngest daughter had married into the Wang family, the father-in-law had been promoted.

Though, in Madam Tong's view, the position of Guozijian Jijiu—Rector of the Imperial Academy—was illustrious and honourable for its cultural prestige, but the new position offered far more tangible power and advantage.

On balance, she thought the promotion very well-chosen.

And so she behaved with ever greater warmth and affection toward her youngest daughter.

……

Qin Ruyin, hearing all of this from her mother, widened her eyes in astonishment.

"What a mess it all is!"

Then she asked her mother: "How has all of this—things that surely should not be spoken of outside—managed to get out? That means Madam Tong, now that she has returned from the country estate, has simply stopped caring about keeping up appearances?"

Madam Li let out a cold laugh.

"All of that was reported back to us by your father's informant planted inside that household."

Qin Ruyin smiled. "Father is always so thorough and careful about things like this. And it's a good thing too—who knows what trouble that side of the family might stir up next, and what they'd try to drag us into..."

Madam Li nodded vigorously.

Then she said: "Madam Tong isn't quite so foolish as all that. On the contrary—now that she has finally resolved herself to act, she is truly going for the throat. She wants to take the full management of the household away from Qin Laotaitai, once and for all!"

Qin Ruyin understood her mother's meaning.

After all, for more than twenty years Madam Tong had presided over the household of Shunyi Hutong—yet real authority had always remained firmly in Qin Laotaitai's hands. Madam Tong had gone along with it because, as long as Qin Laotaitai and Qin Mingjie saw fit to give her the benefits of the position, she had not pressed for the power itself.

……

At this moment, inside the Qin household of Shunyi Hutong.

Qin Ruyue and Wang Huaimian had kowtowed to Qin Laotaitai and Qin Mingjie and his wife.

Qin Mingjie then had Qin Ronggong take his brothers and escort the new son-in-law to the outer courtyard for tea.

Qin Laotaitai kept Qin Ruyue behind to talk.

Madam Tong also stayed.

Qin Laotaitai did not want Madam Tong there, and frowned: "You are the household mistress. Today is a big day—the new son-in-law has brought Yueniang back for her return visit. There is much to be attended to. You go along now!"

Madam Tong replied with pointed sweetness: "Old Tai Tai, and who was it just yesterday who said that I've been away in the country so long I've forgotten how to manage a household, and suggested I hand over my duties?"

Qin Laotaitai's expression fell.

Qin Ruyue was also taken aback.

She had only been gone a few days, and yet what had happened at home?

In her heart, she naturally sided with her birth mother.

She thought for a moment, then asked Qin Laotaitai: "Grandmother, what has happened? Why say something so harsh?"

Since Wang Da Ren's smooth promotion, Qin Ruyue's confidence in her identity as the reborn woman had returned. And with her father smiling and clearly satisfied with her today, she felt even more emboldened.

In front of Qin Laotaitai, she became a little presumptuous.

Qin Laotaitai had not expected to be questioned so bluntly by her granddaughter, and her face immediately darkened.

"Yueniang, you are a married woman now. What happens here in your maiden home is no longer your concern. It is too complicated to explain to you—just stay out of it!"

Qin Ruyue smiled without showing any annoyance. "You're right, Grandmother. I am a Wang family person now. My only concern is the Wang family from here on."

Qin Laotaitai, thus neatly checked, looked even more displeased.

Madam Tong, standing to one side, felt a fierce surge of satisfaction.

She gave Qin Ruyue a look of approval.

Then she said to Qin Laotaitai in her most sugary, barbed tone: "Old Tai Tai—you can't expect the horse to run hard and also refuse to let it eat properly, and then find fault with the horse on top of it all. That's too heartbreaking."

Qin Laotaitai quickly took Qin Ruyue's hand and said: "Yueniang, your grandmother didn't mean it that way. It's only that ever since your mother came back from the country, it's as if she's become a different person, and the household is in chaos..."

"Let your grandmother explain it all to you properly!" Qin Laotaitai looked at Qin Ruyue expectantly.

Qin Ruyue merely smiled, and said to Qin Laotaitai: "Grandmother, my mother managed the household very well. You praised her for it all those years. And even the time she was sent to the country—it was her taking the blame on behalf of this family. You ought to be more patient with her."

She paused, paying no mind to Qin Laotaitai's expression.

She put on the manner of someone not wishing to meddle in her maiden family's affairs, and glanced as if casually at the sky.

"Hmm? Today is also the day Sixth Sister is returning for her return visit! Our First Branch and Third Branch may have broken off the family register, but the bloodline between us can never be changed. Sixth Sister's husband is still a cousin to the people here."

"Grandmother is still Sixth Sister's grandmother as well... Why hasn't Sixth Sister brought her new husband to kowtow and pay respects to Grandmother?"

chapters.title: The Second Branch Is a Mess; the Reborn Woman Schemes Again
chapters.content:
Qin Laotaitai's old eyes flickered as she looked at Qin Ruyue with an expression of great satisfaction.

Yueniang was right!

She had nearly let the matter slip her mind entirely.

Madam Tong, too, caught on in that instant.

Lately the household had been turned upside down, and she had not had the heart to pay attention to what was happening in the First Branch of the Qin family.

But she had not been without information—she had heard the servants' gossiping more than once, and all of them spoke with envy of how the First Branch, having broken off the family register, was growing more and more prosperous...

Hearing it made her burn with indignation.

Qin Laotaitai paid no further mind to Madam Tong's presence, and summoned someone to ask for a detailed account.

She, too, had kept people watching the Qin household in Zijing Hutong...

The three generations of women listened to the report and found their expressions turning collectively unpleasant.

"Hmph! Look at that—the sixth girl really is a lucky creature. The Jiang family truly does think highly of her—not only did the esteemed Jiang Sijia, the Minister of Personnel himself, accompany her for the return visit, but the gifts they prepared are so plentiful!"

Qin Laotaitai's tone carried a sharp undercurrent of sourness.

Madam Tong, hearing this, felt something twist uncomfortably in her chest as well.

And when she thought of her own Yueniang...

What a pity!

On the wedding day she had already swallowed so much humiliation—and now the Wang family had treated her Yueniang with such indifference!

Today's return visit gifts from the Wang family—what a miserable, paltry display!

She did not even want to speak of it.

Twenty catties of ceremonial pork, two large carp, two chickens and two ducks...

And beyond that, just some boxes of pastries and a few catties of dried goods...

That was it!

Was that supposed to be a return visit gift?

Even the down-at-heel distant relatives who came to sponge off her household every year-end did not show up with so little.

And she could not even speak ill of the Wang family.

The moment she did, someone was there to defend them—saying the Wang family was honourable but not wealthy, that they could not be expected to provide extravagant gifts, that what mattered was that the proprieties were observed.

"My goodness! One cannot compare people directly; one cannot compare goods directly. Set them side by side, and our Yueniang's husband's family truly leaves one at a loss for words!"

Qin Laotaitai thought of the return visit gifts her own true-blooded granddaughter's husband had brought, and shook her head helplessly.

Qin Ruyue's face had been passable enough a moment ago, but hearing her grandmother's complaint, her eyes darkened until they might have dripped.

On one hand she was envious and resentful of the Jiang family's regard for Qin Ruyin.

On the other, she could not help thinking back to her previous life.

In her previous life, when she had returned home for her visit, Jiang Sijia—that Jiang Si—had not accompanied her back to the Qin household...

That had given her no end of grief back at her maiden home, and even her closest companions had secretly laughed at her.

True, the return gifts the Jiang family had prepared for her were still decent—a full cartload of good and substantial things...

But compared to Qin Ruyin's four cartloads of return gifts now? They looked like a bad joke.

And this was not even the most galling part.

What she could least forgive was this: in her previous life, after Qin Ruyin had married Wang Huaimian, her mother-in-law's return gift for Qin Ruyin had been far more lavish than the one given to her.

In her previous life... the Jiang family had not treated her as well as they treated Qin Ruyin.

In this life... the Wang family did not treat her as well as they had treated Qin Ruyin, either.

What did that leave her with?

……

"Old Tai Tai, Yueniang is right. That side may have separated the family registers—but the bloodline cannot be changed!"

"If that side has any manners, the sixth girl should have brought her new husband here to kowtow and pay respects to you!" Madam Tong still referred to Qin Ruyin as "Sixth Girl," even though the First Branch had long since broken off the family register.

It was as if by calling her that, she maintained the illusion that the First Branch was still as it had been in years past—under her thumb, living in her shadow, unable to breathe a free breath without her say-so.

Oh, those were the days!

She truly did not want to lose that.

If only she had not been sent to that wretched country estate by Qin Mingjie—if she had still been here—she would never have let the First Branch break off so easily.

And the Third Branch had gone along with them...

Now, in this Qin household, the Fourth, Fifth, and Sixth Branches were all sheltered under that old hag's protection. Who still took her, the household mistress, seriously?

At least if the Third Branch had stayed, she would have someone she could manage!

Now she was like a general without an army. Even if she wanted to assert her authority, there was no one left to assert it over.

"Grandmother, I agree with my mother," Qin Ruyue said, sniffing.

Her gaze went dark and flickered several times. Qin Ruyue continued to say to Qin Laotaitai: "Although the two households have broken their family ties, Sixth Sister is special... She should return to two homes. The fact that she brought her new husband to visit the maiden family first means she remembered to come here, too. Otherwise, Grandmother, how could you justify expecting them to come pay respects here?"

Qin Laotaitai's old eyes spun with calculation. After a pause, she said: "By right that should be so—but does your sixth sister even know this propriety?"

Qin Ruyue saw that her words had moved her grandmother and pressed further, saying to Qin Laotaitai: "Grandmother, perhaps Sixth Sister does know this propriety. And the Jiang family as well—otherwise, why would the Jiang family have prepared such generous return gifts? They must have been divided into two portions: one for Zijing Hutong, and one for our household."

Qin Laotaitai's heart stirred at that, and a cold, calculating smile crept across her aged face.

Madam Tong's eyes glinted with a thought.

She said with studied sweetness: "It's just as Yueniang guesses! Which household of any standing prepares four cartloads of return gifts for a new bride? It stands to reason they are divided—one for Zijing Hutong, one for our household..."

Qin Laotaitai heard this and let out a cold inward huff.

She had not forgotten the enormous quantities of silver and fine things the First Branch had wrested from her. She had not let go of that grievance.

And now—regardless of whether the Jiang family had truly prepared two sets of gifts or not—she would proceed as if they had.

She would bite off a piece of flesh from the First Branch's husband and wife.

She would make that pair of husband and wife understand her, this old woman, and know that she was not someone to be trifled with.

"By rights, it should be this way. Family registers separated or not—blood ties cannot be cut. Whoever is of the same generation as Yueniang in Zijing Hutong... hm, including the Sixth Girl... must still call this old woman Grandmother!"

"Indeed, is that not so?"

Madam Tong laughed inwardly, but on the surface she nodded in agreement, thinking: let this old hag go and make trouble for the First Branch couple.

Taking the opportunity, she followed up: "Old Tai Tai, are we to wait here for Sixth Girl to bring her new husband over to pay respects to you, or shall we send someone to notify them?"

"Wait a while." Qin Laotaitai, having made up her mind, settled into a state of composed self-possession.

"First, have people go out and spread the word—say that the Sixth Girl is filial, that she came to Zijing Hutong first, but has not forgotten this old woman her grandmother... Say she will bring her husband, Lord Jiang, to come kowtow and pay respects to her grandmother before the noon meal. Have people spread it especially near Zijing Hutong—this old woman does not believe they would dare not come and pay their respects!"

Madam Tong could not help but feel a grudging admiration.

When it came to this sort of small, vicious manoeuvre—the kind that made you sick to your stomach without quite crossing a line—the old hag still had the edge on her.

She herself would never have thought so quickly to use such a petty trick to achieve her aim.

Qin Ruyue, too, had a new respect for her grandmother.

With this method, even if Qin Ruyin was unwilling to come, she would have no choice.

Would she dare refuse and let the charge of unfilial conduct fall on her? And would her new husband, Jiang Si, dare be labelled unfilial as well?

If he earned a reputation for lack of filial piety, how was he supposed to carry on as the Minister of Personnel?

As long as Qin Ruyin brought Jiang Si to kowtow and pay respects, they could hardly come empty-handed.

And once Jiang Si had come and bowed before her grandmother, everyone who was watching Jiang Si would understand.

Jiang Si still acknowledged the Shunyi Hutong household.

Jiang Si still recognised this family as relatives.

If that were so, her father and brothers would benefit from it in their careers as well.

And the Wang family, too, related by marriage—perhaps they would also receive some quiet advantages.

After all, Jiang Si was the Minister of Personnel—the man who presided over the appointments of officials throughout the land!

……

Zijing Hutong, the Qin household.

The dishes for the feast welcoming the son-in-law had just been brought out.

Qin Da Laoye and Qin Da Erlang were personally keeping Jiang Jiuxiao company at the table.

But then Ning Shu came in with a grave expression to report something to Qin Da Laoye.

By the time he heard out the last part, Qin Da Laoye's brow was deeply furrowed.

At the same time, in the inner courtyard, Qin Da Furen, Madam Li, had also received the news.

"Outrageous! That old hag from Shunyi Hutong is deliberately picking a fight!"

Madam Li shot to her feet, bristling with such ferocity she could have torn the woman apart with her bare hands.

Da Sao, Lin Xi, and Er Sao, Meng An, hurried over to calm her.

Elder Sister Rujin and Second Sister Ruxiu both sat there, their faces cold.

"Quite a scheme!" Second Sister Ruxiu, ever the quick-tempered one, said through clenched teeth.

Elder Sister Rujin thought for a moment, then spoke to Madam Li: "Mother—by rights, we have separated the family register. We need only treat that side as ordinary relatives from here on out. They have done something this despicable, and what they are after is not to manipulate Little Sister—it is to manipulate her husband."

"That is precisely it! The malice in it!" Madam Li was so furious she broke into a cold sweat.

Lin Xi and Meng An looked at each other.

The two sisters-in-law both understood: this was a thorny situation.

If Little Sister brought her new husband to Shunyi Hutong, that side would have the leverage over them.

If they did not go, the Shunyi Hutong side would surely spread even uglier rumours to defame Little Sister and her new husband.

If it were left to Madam Li's wishes, they would not go, and simply ignore it.

But she understood that this was not a matter a woman of the inner household could settle unilaterally.

"Ruyin, what do you think about this?"

"I certainly don't want to go," Qin Ruyin said, making no bones about it. "That would be walking straight into their trap, wouldn't it?"

"But if we don't go, it will surely affect my husband's reputation."

"Perhaps Mother could send someone to the outer courtyard to ask Father first—to see what he and my husband have decided together?"

chapters.title: On the Art of Making People Sick
chapters.content:
Qin Ruyin took her mother's arm and gave a slight shake of her head. "There is no need to send someone to the front courtyard. If he has made a decision, he will have already sent someone here to inform us."

Madam Li's eyes grew more worried.

Da Sao, Lin Xi, asked Qin Ruyin: "Ruyin, do you mean to say that your husband, the Jiang Master, has no intention of going to Shunyi Hutong?"

"Mm." Qin Ruyin nodded.

Of course not.

Why should they go to Shunyi Hutong? And give them that much face?

Qin Ruyin had guessed rightly.

In the front courtyard, Qin Da Laoye had asked Jiang Jiuxiao's thoughts on the matter.

Jiang Jiuxiao replied with measured composure: "Father-in-law, please do not worry. Now that our household and the Qin household of Shunyi Hutong have separated family registers, it is entirely at your discretion whether you and your sons mark the three annual festivals with a courtesy call or not. And as for Ruyin and her sisters-in-law who are married out—it is their choice whether they acknowledge that side as relatives. No one can compel it."

His words had barely landed when Da Ge and Er Ge and the youngest, Jinlang, all brightened at once.

Of course!

This was not so difficult to resolve.

Even within ordinary family clans, married daughters not keeping up relations with their own uncles' households was entirely common.

How much more so when the two households had fallen out and separated family registers entirely.

Qin Da Laoye's brow remained slightly furrowed. "We certainly do not want to put the two of you newly-weds in that position, nor have you treated shabbily. My only concern is the effect on you, Jiuxiao, in court—"

Jiang Jiuxiao rose and bowed in response. "Thank you for your concern, Father-in-law. But please rest assured—this matter will not affect me."

"There is no law or precedent that requires two households which have formally separated their family registers to continue behaving as relatives."

"As for why the separation was conducted the way it was—with open quarrelling—it was because that household went too far. If anyone in the court tries to make an issue of it to attack me, I have my own answer to give..."

Qin Da Laoye, hearing Jiang Jiuxiao speak these words with perfect equanimity, felt something ease in his chest.

"It occurs to me that Mother-in-law and Ruyin in the inner courtyard may also be anxious about this matter. Father-in-law, would you be so kind as to have someone inform them?—so that Mother-in-law, Ruyin, and all the sisters-in-law and elder sisters may be at ease."

Qin Da Laoye nodded several times.

He was satisfied.

The Jiang son-in-law had asked him to send word to the inner courtyard—no doubt because he was concerned that Ruyin might be worried.

Qin Da Laoye thought as much, then at once gave the order for someone to go to the inner courtyard and inform Madam Li and Qin Ruyin that there was no need to go to Shunyi Hutong.

"The Jiang son-in-law is truly decisive!" Madam Li said sincerely, upon hearing what the messenger from Qin Da Laoye brought back.

It was, in truth, an acknowledgement that Jiang Jiuxiao had backbone and was dependable.

Elder Sister Rujin smiled and said to Madam Li: "That goes without saying! At his age, to become the youngest Minister of Personnel in all of Da Ying, he must be firm and resolute in all things."

Everyone nodded and murmured their agreement.

Once they had all settled their minds, they turned to teasing Qin Ruyin.

The room filled with warmth and laughter.

When the laughter subsided, Qin Ruyin turned to Feng Mama, who was always close at hand.

"Feng Mama, find a few nimble people and quietly spread some information outside as well. Something along these lines: how the Qin household of Shunyi Hutong once bullied our family... and why the family of my maternal grandfather's side mobilised in their entirety from Xianyang to escort me to Beijing for the wedding—what was the ostensible reason, and what was the true reason behind their resolute support for our separation? And why did we insist on it?"

Qin Ruyin gave Feng Mama a quick blink.

"My father made a promise when he parted ways with that side of the Qin family—he would not go out of his way to spread word of Qin Laotaitai's dirty secret about misappropriating my grandmother's dowry. But that doesn't stop sharp-eyed people from speculating on their own."

Feng Mama smiled and agreed.

Their Miss had not taken the initiative to announce anything.

She was only guiding others to speculate for themselves.

For someone of Feng Mama's background—a seasoned operative—this sort of small task was far beneath her full capabilities.

She received the order and said to Qin Ruyin: "Miss, leave it to this old servant. This kind of small matter will be handled so cleanly that even the court's Imperial Guard couldn't trace it back."

Her mistress's lord had personally added people to protect Miss and handle private matters on her behalf.

This task would be managed without a trace.

After the noon meal, Madam Li had wanted to continue chatting with her youngest daughter—but Rujin and Ruxiu shooed her off to take her afternoon rest.

"Mother, Da Sao and Er Sao have both gone back to their own rooms to rest with the children. You should go rest properly as well!"

Qin Ruyin also agreed that her mother should nap, for Madam Li was in the habit of resting after the midday meal. And today, because of her return visit, her mother had been up far earlier than usual.

She worried that without the nap, her mother might be troubled by headaches by mid-afternoon.

Madam Li thought it over—with all three daughters present, they could have a proper talk without her there to make them guarded—and so she listened to her daughters and went to rest.

"Hah—the little girl is married now and running her own household. One can see it just in the way she speaks and carries herself—so different from when she was still a young miss!"

Ruxiu, all smiles, took Qin Ruyin's hand and looked her up and down.

"Tell Second Sister the truth—what were you saying to Feng Mama just now?"

"Hmm?" Qin Ruyin feigned innocence. "Nothing much—I was just giving her a few reminders about some things."

"You, girl—do you think you can fool your second sister? I saw you—when you were giving Feng Mama her instructions, your eyes were absolutely shining!"

Ruxiu was not suspicious that her little sister was up to anything bad.

Even if she was up to something, she was delighted by it.

She would far rather her little sister be scheming against other people than have other people scheming against her little sister.

Elder Sister Rujin said to Ruxiu: "Stop interrogating Ruyin—doesn't everyone have their secrets? Besides, you have a secret right now that you haven't told Ruyin."

She thought for a moment, then laughed.

"Actually, so do I!"

"Aha! Second Sister—quickly now, tell me all your secrets!" Qin Ruyin grabbed at Ruxiu's sleeve.

Rujin moved to shield Ruxiu, laughing and saying to Qin Ruyin: "Ruyin, your Second Sister is expecting again."

"Oh my goodness!" Qin Ruyin released Ruxiu's sleeve at once, and with great delight, offered her congratulations.

Ruxiu's pretty face flushed crimson, and she shot her elder sister a glance of mock reproach.

Rujin laughed: "You—three children and still not knowing to be more careful. Ruyin didn't know you were expecting, so she was pulling and tugging at you. What if that had startled the child?"

"Of course, of course! Elder Sister is right! Second Sister—you're our most precious person right now. I didn't know, and that grabbing and pulling could easily have startled the little nephew or niece inside—"

"Ah?" Rujin blinked in surprise.

Ruxiu looked at Qin Ruyin with bright, hopeful eyes. "Ruyin, did you just say this child I'm carrying is a little niece of yours?"

Qin Ruyin had spoken without thinking and was momentarily taken aback.

She had just said without thinking that Second Sister was carrying a little niece.

In this feudal age, of course people preferred boys.

"Second Sister..."

"Don't look at me like that—I love little girls! Soft and sweet little girls are so lovely!"

Ruxiu pulled Qin Ruyin into a hug. "Best of all if she comes out exactly like you—all mischief and cleverness!"

Qin Ruyin relaxed. "I just said it without thinking—it might not be right!"

"People say that what you let slip is the most truthful," Rujin comforted Qin Ruyin. "Don't worry—your second sister genuinely prefers raising a daughter."

Qin Ruyin pressed her palm to her forehead.

She suspected Ruxiu had been scared enough by her lively little boys.

"Children are what fate brings—you get what you're given, and you love them all!" Qin Ruyin said earnestly. "None of us should favour daughters over sons or sons over daughters."

"Very well said!" Rujin laughed, looking at Ruxiu. "And you should not favour daughters over sons—otherwise our eldest nephew will be heartbroken."

Caught in a gentle scolding from elder sister and little sister both, Ruxiu could only admit defeat. "Fine, fine! I will not favour daughters over sons. You may both rest easy!"

Once the sisters had finished laughing, Rujin asked Qin Ruyin about how she had been getting on in the Jiang household.

Ruxiu sat down and listened seriously.

"The eldest sister-in-law in the Jiang household is intelligent and composed, though a little fond of power—but that doesn't matter. I have no desire to compete with her for power. She is the First Branch's wife, the head of the Jiang household. As long as she does not come after me, I am perfectly willing to get along peacefully with her."

After she finished speaking of the First Sister-in-Law, both Rujin and Ruxiu nodded in agreement.

"From how the old matriarch values the First Madam, one can tell—the First Branch will always be the First Branch. As long as they don't commit a serious fault, no one can ever surpass them," Rujin observed.

Ruxiu added: "In all these respectable households in Da Ying, things are the same way. As long as the First Branch doesn't make a grave mistake, even if they're rather mediocre, no one can take away their right of succession."

Rujin thought for a moment and said to Qin Ruyin: "Ruyin—if you're ever unhappy in the Jiang household, the answer is simple: separate into your own household."

Ruxiu agreed: "Elder Sister is right. Your brother-in-law seems a man of reason and decisiveness. I can't imagine him letting you be bullied in the Jiang household."

Qin Ruyin smiled. "He wouldn't. My Third Sister-in-Law has twice tried to make trouble for me—not openly, but covertly—and Jiang Jiuxiao went and gave his Third Brother a talking-to all the same."

"I knew that Third Sister-in-Law of yours was not going to be easy!" Ruxiu said, knitting her brows.

Qin Ruyin quickly and lightly patted her hand. "Second Sister—you need to keep your heart cheerful at all times. The child you're carrying will be all the more beautiful for it. Don't get stirred up over people who have nothing to do with us..."

Rujin agreed with what Qin Ruyin said.

Ruxiu laughed.

"I'm not angry! Since your brother-in-law has already stood up for you, what is there to be angry about?"

"We were all so worried about you before—and it was you who insisted on marrying into the Jiang family. Now it seems you really did marry well!"

Ruxiu cheered up again.

Rujin smiled too, and then asked Qin Ruyin: "And what about your Second Sister-in-Law? Looking at her, she seems the most calculating of them all—wouldn't she be the more difficult one to handle?"

"My Second Sister-in-Law—she has four big sons to keep her busy, and plenty to worry about!"

She paused and said seriously: "I reckon that as calculating as she is, she's calculating for her four sons' sake. Jiang Erlang is someone she can't rely on—and if she wants to plan for her sons' futures, she is the very last person who ought to make an enemy of me."

"As for the Fifth Sister-in-Law—she's barely twenty. Though she's not much older than me, she carries herself with great self-possession, quiet and unassuming... Too soon to tell much about her yet."

Before Qin Ruyin had even finished speaking, a servant came to announce from beyond the bead curtain:

"Third Madam, all three, the Old Tai Tai from Shunyi Hutong has come to our residence..."

"Ha!" Ruxiu nearly laughed herself to anger.

She exclaimed: "Now that is really something! She's quite the nerve—even by the standards of an elder, she's a long way from respectable. The family registers are already separated, and she still comes running to our door?"

Then she asked the servant: "Aside from her—who else has come with her to our household?"

chapters.title: Qin Laotaitai Comes Running
chapters.content:
"No need to ask—that old woman is all bluster and no courage. She wouldn't dare come to our household alone," Qin Ruyin said with a huff.

"Exactly right," Ruxiu said with contempt, giving a firm little nod.

"That old woman is just that sort—all bark, no bite. You stay here in the Zhongyu Xiuge that Mother had prepared for you, Second Sister. I'll keep Ruyin company and we'll go deal with that lot ourselves."

Qin Ruyin nodded repeatedly, looking at her second sister: "Second Sister—I know you want to see the fun too, but you're carrying a little one now, the most precious person in our family! You can't risk any unpleasantness from that crowd!"

Seeing her little sister speak so charmingly, Ruxiu laughed.

"All right—I won't go to watch the fun then. I'll behave!"

Elder Sister Rujin smiled warmly and smoothed her hair—just as she had done when they were children.

Madam Li had barely fallen asleep when the aggravating news reached her.

She was deeply annoyed.

Suppressing her fury, she said: "Truly shameless! They won't leave us in peace—throwing aside all dignity entirely!"

Lin Xi and Meng An, who came hurrying to help her dress, urged her: "Mother, today is a joyous day for our household. Don't let people who are nothing to do with us ruin your mood!"

Madam Li drew a long breath and nodded to her two daughters-in-law.

"Let the servants help me dress. You two sit down and rest—you've only just coaxed the little ones to sleep, and you're tired enough..."

Lin Xi and Meng An exchanged a glance and smiled.

To have a mother-in-law who cherished her daughters-in-law like this was a fortune earned through lifetimes of virtue.

Whatever credit their husbands might deserve—it was their parents-in-law who deserved it more!

"Mother—we love serving you. Please don't send us away..." Meng An said, playing the part of a petted daughter.

Lin Xi, ever the composed eldest daughter-in-law, could not help but adopt a small daughter's playful manner in front of her mother-in-law.

"Exactly! Mother—we'd love nothing more than to serve you every day, to dress you up prettily and show you off. That's what makes us truly happy!"

With two daughters-in-law making her laugh, all the anger Madam Li had felt was gone like smoke in an instant.

Whatever came, she would face it!

Was she afraid of that old hag and Madam Tong—two old vipers?

In truth, it was not only Qin Laotaitai who had come from Shunyi Hutong.

Qin Ruyue and Wang Huaimian had come with her.

And behind them, Qin Mingjie arrived with his eldest son, Qin Ronggong.

Qin Laotaitai stood at the gates of the Zijing Hutong Qin household, flanked on either side by Madam Tong and Qin Ruyue.

She looked up at the imposing vermilion lacquered gate, and envy showed on all three women's faces—Qin Laotaitai, Madam Tong, and Qin Ruyue alike.

"Just look at this... such a grand gate! It would hold its own against a marquis or duke's mansion. The First Branch has really done well since they separated." Madam Tong could not contain the sourness overflowing in her heart, and made it her business to sow the same seeds of resentment in Qin Laotaitai.

She deliberately moved close to Qin Laotaitai's ear and said in a lowered, mocking voice:

"Old Tai Tai—back then, with not a cent of the late First Tai Tai's dowry in hand, the First Branch people walked around with their tails between their legs in our household."

"And now look—the First Branch got their hands on all those good things, and they've soared! Had you just handed things over properly at the time, even if the Wei family had come to make trouble, what could they have done about it? Used the late Master's name to divide things out early, and none of this would have happened."

Ha! If not for this old hag stirring up trouble, and being too greedy—getting herself caught by the First Branch couple—how could she have let them separate so easily?

And for all those years, that shrew Madam Li had scraped by under her thumb—now she had become a household mistress in her own right!

She must be laughing in her dreams.

And the Third Branch—that shadow of a man had apparently bought himself a little house in the capital and gone off to live comfortably. And those two useless boys of his were now being personally tutored by Qin Da Laoye...

The more Madam Tong thought about it, the more her stomach turned.

Qin Laotaitai nearly rose to the heavens with indignation, and hissed: "You make it sound easy! As long as the Wei family still has that dowry list, and they're willing to stand up for the First Branch, how could we have—"

Madam Tong gave a cold laugh. "That depends on who steps forward to deal with it. If my own family were to intervene—Old Tai Tai, do you think the Wei family has as many connections at court as my family does?"

Qin Laotaitai fell silent, her expression very unpleasant.

Qin Ruyue had her own agenda and did not wish for her grandmother and mother to begin quarrelling among themselves before they had even stepped inside.

She shot Madam Tong a warning glance. Madam Tong's eyes flickered—and she, too, said no more.

Qin Ruyue then guided Qin Laotaitai's attention by murmuring gently: "Grandmother, all of that is past. Let us not speak of it... Your granddaughter sees it this way—you are the senior, the elder. You say that after one comes of the same generation as Yueniang in Zijing Hutong, would they not open the main gate to receive you?"

Qin Laotaitai, diverted, gave a cold huff. "Well, that rather depends on your great-uncle's filial piety!"

Madam Tong arched a brow and said with deliberate provocation: "Child, your great-uncle is of course going to open the main gate for your grandmother! After all, your great-uncle must still address your grandmother as 'Mother'!"

"Has separating the family registers made him stop even acknowledging a mother? If your late grandfather had any awareness from the beyond, he would be lifting the lid off his own coffin to climb out of his grave..."

Qin Laotaitai detected the sarcasm in Madam Tong's words and, forcing herself to keep her temper, said: "Old Erlang's wife—what kind of talk is that? It is your late father-in-law you're speaking of. He is not something you may take out and joke with."

"What's more, your late father-in-law has long since passed. How can you speak of him in such an improper way?"

Madam Tong rolled her eyes, gave a cold laugh, and ignored her.

If you truly cared so much for your late father-in-law's dignity, how could you ignore his dying instructions—privately seizing and refusing to return the First Wife's million-tael dowry? All because of you, the late master's reputation in the main Qin family clan has collapsed entirely.

And thanks to Qin Mingjie—that miserable wretch—being despised and scorned by the Qin main clan: it was her own sons who suffered, unable to hold their heads up before the main clan.

Insufferable!

Madam Tong still burned with resentment, still convinced: had the old fool told her from the start about the hundred-thousand taels' worth of goods, she would have gone to her own family long ago to think of something—and the Wei family's people would never have come to the capital in the first place...

Qin Laotaitai was nearly knocked off her feet by Madam Tong's attitude.

But she had no choice but to swallow her anger. This was no time to begin infighting—they were about to step through that gate.

She could not have her own people brawling at someone else's doorstep before they had even gone in.

"Yueniang, tell your grandmother and mother to stop making a scene. It doesn't look right—two women of the household quarrelling at someone else's front door. This is not how people of breeding behave," Wang Huaimian said, suddenly tugging at Qin Ruyue's sleeve and murmuring in her ear.

From the outside, it looked like a young couple sharing an intimate whisper.

Qin Ruyue's strikingly beautiful face went red and then white by turns. She looked at her husband in disbelief.

"My lord—how... how can you say that?"

"They... they are also your grandmother and mother!"

Wang Huaimian pressed his lips together, his face a mask of poorly concealed displeasure. "Of course, of course—Yueniang is right. All the same, we cannot lose face out here, can we?"

He truly regretted following Qin Ruyue and coming here.

He had thought he might get a chance to meet the newly appointed Minister of Personnel in person—something to make his peers envious, even if he was not of the man's faction.

But watching his in-laws—this mother and grandmother-in-law pair—making such a scene in front of the younger generation, bickering in the open at someone else's front door without a shred of dignity, he knew he should not wade into this muddy water.

"My lord, do not worry—the voices are low, only we nearby can hear. No one else can." Qin Ruyue tried to reassure him. "My maiden family has come to this state—it's all the First Uncle's family causing trouble. There's nothing to be done about it—now that the First Uncle has such a powerful son-in-law as the Minister of Personnel, we can't afford to make enemies of them... I've come this time for your sake, my lord. After all, you will have a career in officialdom, and if we can't win over Jiang Si's favour, the least we can do is say hello—isn't that right?"

"Yueniang, you're quite right—I was impatient," said Wang Huaimian. He was perfectly pleased to hear Qin Ruyue say she was always thinking of him—but in his heart, he held her in-laws in even lower regard now.

What's more, now that his father had risen to the same rank as his father-in-law, he had lost whatever deference he once felt for Qin Mingjie.

So he answered Qin Ruyue in vague, placating terms—while inwardly he had already made up his mind.

He put on a remorseful, gentle expression and whispered to Qin Ruyue: "I know you mean well, Yueniang—it's only that I'm suddenly struck with terrible stomach pains... Must be that your brothers plied me with too much wine, and now my stomach is all wrong."

"If that is the case, would you not need a privy urgently?" Qin Ruyue looked around hastily. "If your stomach is acting up, we'll need to get through this gate quickly, so you can find a privy—"

Wang Huaimian cut her off with an expression of acute distress.

"I fear it's already too late for that... I'll have my page boy take me to the nearest privy right away!"

"Please make my excuses to the elders, Yueniang." And without waiting for Qin Ruyue to react, he hoisted his robe hem and turned and walked briskly away.

Qin Mingjie and Qin Ronggong, who had been coming up behind them, gaped at the sight of Wang Huaimian hurrying off with a pained expression—clearly in no mood to stop and explain.

Qin Mingjie's face darkened as he came to stand before Qin Ruyue and said under his breath: "What is wrong with the Wang son-in-law? He ran off without even a word of greeting—what is the meaning of this?"

Qin Ruyue was mortified.

But she remembered what Wang Huaimian had said just before he left—that it was her brothers who had poured too much wine into him and upset his stomach—so she turned and laid the blame on Qin Ronggong.

"It's Elder Brother, too—did you and Second Brother and Third Brother ply my husband with drink? Now you've made him ill with stomach pains, and naturally he has no time to greet Father."

"I never urged him to drink more—knowing his capacity was limited, I only offered the polite gestures—" Qin Ronggong was completely bewildered.

Qin Mingjie frowned. "Indeed, he didn't drink that much. But his constitution is weak, and stomach trouble from wine is possible..."

Before the words were even out of Qin Mingjie's mouth, the great main gate of the First Branch Qin household slowly swung open.

At the sight of the main gate opening, Qin Ruyue's beautiful eyes darkened.

The Qin household's head butler, Ning Shu, came out to receive them.

After the exchange of pleasantries and greetings, he began guiding Qin Laotaitai and the others—not toward the main gate, but toward the side entrance.

"One moment!" Qin Laotaitai had been rather pleased when she saw the main gate swing open, thinking: even so, the First Branch dares not be unfilial toward her.

A steward coming out to receive her was perhaps less than ideal—but being led to the side entrance?

That was outrageous!

chapters.title: Wang Huaimian Flees the Scene
chapters.content:
Ning Shu met her protest with the very same composure he had always displayed: completely unruffled.

"Old Tai Tai, please do not take offence. The main gate of our household is only opened for the grandest occasions. Today, Master Jiang and our Miss have returned for the family visit—it is on their account that the main gate has been opened. Your esteemed party arriving at this time is no doubt a further honour, but per our household's customs, side entrance reception of guests is standard practice—there is no intent to diminish you. Please do come through with us."

Qin Laotaitai turned puce.

This old butler could be infuriating.

Everything he said was impeccably proper. He had even placed the credit for the open main gate on Jiang Jiuxiao—leaving her not a single foothold to complain from.

Madam Tong made no outward comment, but inwardly she was enormously gratified.

Well-handled indeed.

How could Madam Li ever have been so easy to bully before? Just look at the people around her now!

Qin Mingjie, who had spent his life scheming, immediately understood what was happening.

He stepped forward and spoke in low, soothing tones to Qin Laotaitai: "Mother, let us not hold anyone up—let us go in."

Qin Laotaitai was not actually thick-headed. She simply could not swallow this.

At last, she suppressed her displeasure and followed Ning Shu through the side entrance.

Madam Tong and Qin Ruyue exchanged a glance.

Qin Ruyue had not forgotten that Wang Huaimian had absconded. But she had no choice for now—she forced herself to follow the group inside.

……

Madam Li came out and received them in the outer reception hall of the main house.

Her expression was controlled—not so as to give them any advantage, but not so chilling as to be overtly hostile.

Behind her stood Rujin and Ruxiu, her two daughters.

Naturally, Qin Ruyin was also present.

The two groups faced each other.

Qin Laotaitai scanned the room for Jiang Jiuxiao. His absence annoyed her.

"I would like to pay my respects to the new son-in-law. Have someone inform him to come."

Madam Li replied without inflection: "My son-in-law is occupied entertaining his brothers-in-law at the moment. Old Tai Tai is welcome to take tea and wait."

"He is in the same household!" Qin Laotaitai's face fell. "Just have someone call him over—how long can that take?"

Madam Li only smiled pleasantly and instructed a servant to serve tea.

Qin Laotaitai's heart simmered. She looked at Qin Ruyin.

"Sixth girl—you haven't lost your manners toward your grandmother, have you?"

Qin Ruyin met her gaze evenly and said with great courtesy: "Grandmother, your granddaughter's respects."

And she dipped her head slightly in acknowledgement—nothing more.

She did not bow. She did not go forward to support the old woman's arm.

Qin Laotaitai's expression shifted several times.

She had expected a warm, solicitous greeting—exactly the kind this girl had always given her. And yet here was this girl, standing her ground, perfectly mannered but utterly unmoved.

In the past, Qin Ruyin would have gone forward to take her arm. Would have called out to her warmly. Would have offered her the best seat.

All of that—gone.

Madam Tong looked on with something close to admiration.

She herself had been unable to produce this manner when she first entered the Qin household. This girl was something else entirely.

"Sixth girl," Qin Laotaitai said at last, with manufactured gentleness, "come and sit with your grandmother."

"Old Tai Tai is kind, but there is someone who must sit closest to you." Qin Ruyin smiled and let her eyes move to Qin Ruyue.

"Yueniang is your own granddaughter. She should sit beside you."

Qin Ruyue had been watching this exchange with complicated feelings.

She was acutely aware of how Qin Ruyin's behaviour had changed.

In their childhood and youth, Sixth Sister had always been gentle and yielding around Qin Laotaitai—going forward, supporting her, and always, always giving way.

But today every instinct of deference was gone—replaced with something quiet and immovable.

Qin Ruyue knew it was because Sixth Sister had Jiang Jiuxiao behind her now. She had backing.

But she still felt something unpleasant about it.

She sat down beside Qin Laotaitai as indicated.

The conversation that followed was stilted and full of undercurrents.

Qin Laotaitai tried several times to draw Jiang Jiuxiao's name into the conversation—his position, his prospects, his connections.

Madam Li deflected each attempt without giving an inch.

Qin Laotaitai noticed that Qin Ruyue's husband was not present and asked after him with feigned concern.

Qin Ruyue explained that Wang Huaimian had been unwell.

Qin Laotaitai made appropriate noises of sympathy.

The unspoken tension in the room had been simmering for some time when Ning Shu appeared at the doorway and quietly informed Madam Li that the Master Jiang had come.

Madam Li's eyes brightened.

Qin Laotaitai also straightened in her seat.

Jiang Jiuxiao entered.

He was exactly as Qin Laotaitai had heard—tall, composed, bearing a quiet authority that immediately made one feel the room had contracted.

He greeted Madam Li with a slight bow. Then he turned and looked at the assembled group from Shunyi Hutong.

His gaze was not hostile. It was not particularly warm.

It was simply measured.

"This must be the Old Tai Tai from Shunyi Hutong," he said, addressing Qin Laotaitai. "My wife's grandmother."

He offered a bow appropriate to the generation—courteous, nothing more.

Qin Laotaitai looked up at him and felt, for the first time, a small tremor of something she would not name.

"Son-in-law," she began, working to make her voice warm and familiar. "I have heard so much about you. Today I came specially to meet you—"

"Old Tai Tai is kind," Jiang Jiuxiao replied, unhurried. "I believe the distance is considerable from Shunyi Hutong. You must be tired."

His words were entirely pleasant. They offered nothing.

Qin Laotaitai understood, in that moment, that she had come all this way and achieved nothing.

Not one inch of ground.

She had expected nervousness, or deference, or at least some trace of wanting to please her. There was none of that.

There was only this: a man who was perfectly courteous, who had paid her exactly the respect her generation merited—and not a fraction more.

Madam Tong, seated slightly apart, was quietly, privately, impressed.

Qin Ruyue watched.

She looked at Jiang Jiuxiao, and then she looked at Qin Ruyin.

Qin Ruyin was sitting calmly, her hands folded in her lap, a small smile on her face.

She was not performing anything.

She was simply at ease.

And looking at her, Qin Ruyue felt the old familiar burn—that terrible, familiar ache that she could not explain and could not extinguish.

It had always been this way.

Even now.

Even here.

After sufficient tea had been drunk and pleasantries exchanged that satisfied the minimum requirements of propriety, Qin Laotaitai attempted one more time to extend the visit.

"We have not come all this way to sit for just a moment. Surely we might stay for the noon meal—"

Madam Li replied with perfect serenity: "Old Tai Tai's kindness is appreciated. But today's meal has already been set—it is in honour of our son-in-law and daughter's return visit, and the arrangements have been made to count exactly the family members present. I'm afraid we could not properly host additional guests at this short a notice. It would not do justice to Old Tai Tai's position."

The dismissal was so gracefully phrased that Qin Laotaitai could not take offence at a single word of it.

And yet dismissed she was.

She rose.

The party from Shunyi Hutong took their leave.

Ning Shu escorted them out through the side entrance.

Qin Laotaitai walked out with her chin high—but as the gates of the Zijing Hutong Qin household closed behind her, she knew, with deep and settled certainty, that she had not won.

Not today.

Madam Tong, at her side, said not a word.

Neither did Qin Ruyue.

For once, there was nothing to say.

……

Inside the Qin household, Jiang Jiuxiao returned to the outer courtyard.

Qin Ruyin looked after the retreating backs of the Shunyi Hutong party until the gate closed.

She turned and met her mother's eye.

Madam Li let out a long breath—and then, suddenly, laughed.

"Well," said Madam Li, "that's done with."

Qin Ruyin smiled.

"It's done with," she agreed.

And that was all there was to it.

chapters.title: The Qin Old Matriarch's Family — Envy, Jealousy, and Resentment
chapters.content:
Qin Mingjie's face darkened as well. He halted his steps and snapped at Uncle Ning in a low growl: "Old Ning, you wretched slave! What does my elder brother think he's doing?"

He had already been simmering with displeasure after the First Branch of the Qin family split from the clan and bought such a grand and imposing residence.

He thought to himself — that Qin eldest truly had the luck of the heavens, with a mother who had left behind such a lavish dowry.

If he had managed to reclaim that lavish dowry, it would all have been his!

And a mansion this grand would have been his too!

He had nowhere to vent his anger, and when he saw the main gate swing open, his mood had lifted slightly — but the moment he saw Uncle Ning leading them toward the side gate, he erupted.

Uncle Ning turned around at the sound. Neither angry nor aggrieved, he looked at Qin Mingjie with a calm, unruffled expression and asked mildly: "What seems to be the matter, Lord Qin? If you don't wish to go in and see my master, then please, feel free to leave......"

"Who said we don't want to see him?" the Qin Old Matriarch said coldly. "My Mingjie holds a higher official rank than your master, and I am his elder, besides."

"Does splitting from the clan mean he can simply stop recognizing me as his legitimate mother? It already lacks proper etiquette that his legitimate mother should arrive and be greeted only by an old servant rather than the master himself — and now we're being led through the side gate?"

Uncle Ning was largely unbothered by Qin Mingjie's words.

But when this old matriarch opened her mouth, Uncle Ning nearly choked on a laugh of outrage.

Fortunately, his cultivation of composure was exceptional. He merely let his expression cool.

"Madam Qin speaks in jest. How could this still be framed as a matter of a legitimate mother? Now that the two families have separated clans, if you wish to maintain ties as relatives, you may. If not, you part ways cleanly."
